al-ain/al-maqam.tutorsIntro: The tutors here work on assessed components rather than on general content coverage: internal assessment design in the sciences and mathematics, Extended Essay process coaching, Theory of Knowledge argument structure, and the written and practical components at IGCSE.

intro.heading: The parts of the course with no lesson attached
paragraphs: Al Maqam lies on the southern side of Al Ain, past the oasis belt, on the road out towards the mountain and with the main university campus close at hand. It is a district of larger plots and newer housing where families have often chosen space and a quieter street over being five minutes from a school gate. Children travel into the city's central school cluster, and older siblings frequently study at the university nearby, which makes this one of the few districts where a Diploma student has an undergraduate in the house.

The request that arrives from here more than any other concerns the assessed work that sits outside the taught timetable. Every programme has it. The Diploma has internal assessments in every subject, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition, the Group 4 project and CAS. The Middle Years Programme ends with the Personal Project. IGCSE has coursework or practical components in several subjects. All of it is marked, none of it has a weekly lesson, and most of it is supervised by a teacher carrying twenty other supervisees.

That structure produces a very particular failure. A student who is organised, well taught and perfectly capable arrives at the week a draft is due with nothing written, because nothing in their week ever said write it. The school set a deadline in October, the student noted it, and then eight weeks of lessons, tests and homework happened in between with no scheduled hour for the one thing that had no lesson. This is not a motivation problem. It is a calendar problem with a predictable shape.

The second failure is about criteria. Internal assessments are marked against published criteria, labelled by letter, each carrying a defined number of marks. Students routinely produce work that is strong on the criterion they find interesting and silent on two others, then cannot understand why the mark is mid-range. Reading the criteria with the marks attached, before starting, changes the piece that gets written. It is the cheapest single intervention available on the Diploma and almost nobody does it early.

The third is limits. Every written component has a word or page limit, and exceeding it has consequences that vary by component and by subject. Students write long because they are anxious, and then cut badly under time pressure, losing the structural clarity the criteria reward. Knowing the limit at the planning stage produces a different plan, and a different plan produces a better piece of work than any amount of editing at the end.

Everything described here is delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE and nobody will be sent to an Al Maqam address; that service exists only in India. On coursework the format is an advantage rather than a compromise, because a draft, a data file and a criteria sheet can all be on screen at once, which is awkward at a dining table and impossible across a desk.

al-ain/al-maqam.programmesIntro: Al Maqam households sit mainly on the IB continuum and the British route. Each programme is described below by its assessed components rather than by its philosophy, because the components are what this page is about.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level, each with an internal assessment marked by the teacher against published criteria and externally moderated. Alongside them sit three core components: the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge, and CAS. Internal assessment generally carries twenty to thirty per cent of a subject grade, which makes it the largest single piece of work most students have ever been marked on.
programmes.countryNote: A Diploma student travelling into central Al Ain from Al Maqam has a long day, and the core components compete with that journey for the same evenings. Schools here set internal deadlines that tend to cluster, so two internal assessments and an Extended Essay draft can land in the same fortnight unless the year has been mapped backwards from those dates.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, converted to a 1-7 grade. The programme closes with the Personal Project, an extended independent piece with its own criteria and its own supervisor. It is the first time most students manage a long deadline themselves, and it is excellent preparation for the Extended Essay if it is taken seriously.
programmes.countryNote: The Personal Project is the component Al Ain families most often underestimate, partly because it carries no examination and partly because it falls in a year already crowded with other things. Students who treat it as a rehearsal for Diploma coursework arrive in Year 12 with a genuine advantage over those who did it in a fortnight.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: Mostly terminal papers, with practical or coursework components in several subjects and an alternative-to-practical route in the sciences where laboratory assessment is not taken. Each component has its own mark allocation and its own conventions, and the practical papers reward specific trained habits rather than general scientific ability.
programmes.countryNote: Which science route a school enters a student for matters a great deal and is often not explained to families. The alternative-to-practical paper tests reading apparatus, identifying variables and handling real result tables, all of which are coachable without laboratory access, and students in Al Ain frequently sit it without ever having practised one.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: Papers carry nearly all the weight, with practical assessment in the sciences and coursework in a minority of subjects. The step from IGCSE is mainly in how much of an answer has to be constructed from scratch, and in how much independent reading is assumed rather than set.
programmes.countryNote: Some Al Ain campuses continue to A Level rather than the Diploma, which means fewer assessed components outside the timetable but a heavier reliance on the student's own question practice. Families switching between the two routes at sixteen should understand that the coursework load is genuinely different, not merely differently named.

al-ain/al-maqam.subjectsIntro: Requests from Al Maqam cluster around subjects whose internal assessment or practical component is doing the damage. Each entry below names the component and the recurring mistake rather than restating the syllabus.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The exploration is where this subject is won or lost outside the papers. Students choose a topic that sounds impressive and cannot be modelled with the mathematics they have, then produce a description of someone else's work. Topic selection is the session that matters most, and it belongs early.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Explorations here fail on data rather than on mathematics: a dataset too small for the test applied, or a statistical procedure used without its assumptions checked. Reflection and personal engagement are the criteria most often left thin, and both are easy to plan for in advance.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Internal assessments founder on investigations with no genuine independent variable, or on a research question too broad to answer in the available pages. Uncertainty handling and evaluation are the criteria that separate a mid mark from a high one, and both are coachable without a laboratory.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The common failure is an investigation that produces a straight line and no analysis worth writing about. Error propagation, graph choice and a genuine evaluation of method are where the marks are, and students who plan for those criteria design a better experiment in the first place.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Statistical treatment is the recurring weakness, together with research questions that cannot be answered with the equipment available. The Group 4 project also lands in this subject most often, and students rarely understand that it is assessed on collaboration and reflection.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Commentaries need articles chosen for the theory they permit, not for how interesting they are. Each commentary has a tight word limit, and students who choose a broad article write an overview that touches three concepts shallowly rather than one properly.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The research project requires a real organisation, genuine data and a defensible research question. Students pick an organisation they cannot get information from, discover it late, and then write around the gap. The feasibility check is a twenty-minute conversation that saves a term.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral is assessed on a global issue and two extracts, and it fails on structure rather than on insight. A student who arrives with observations and no argument will not reach the higher bands however well they read the texts.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition of three objects. The essay fails when it becomes an opinion piece, and the exhibition fails when the objects are chosen before the prompt is understood. Both are argument-structure problems rather than knowledge problems.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words on a self-chosen research question in a chosen subject, with a supervisor and a reflection process. Most failures trace back to a question that is either unanswerable or answerable in four hundred words, and that is decided in the first fortnight.

subjects.name: Sciences at IGCSE (0620, 0625, 0610 and Pearson equivalents)
subjects.description: The practical or alternative-to-practical component carries real marks and is rarely practised. Reading apparatus diagrams, identifying variables and processing an untidy result table are trainable skills, and they are the difference between a predicted and an actual grade.

subjects.name: MYP Personal Project
subjects.description: Assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting rather than on the product itself, which is the opposite of what most students assume. A beautiful outcome with no process evidence scores poorly, and a modest outcome with rigorous documentation scores well.

regions.name: Zakher
regions.note: The neighbouring southern belt, similar in character, with large plots and long bus runs. Enquiries from both districts share the same coursework problem and the same shortage of evening hours to put it in.

regions.name: Al Mutaredh
regions.note: North towards the oasis, older and more settled. Diploma families there have usually been at the same campus for years, which means they know the internal deadline pattern and can plan against it.

regions.name: Al Jimi
regions.note: The central school concentration and the destination for most buses out of this district. The internal deadlines that drive this page are set by campuses in this cluster.

regions.name: Al Khabisi
regions.note: Central and often on the same route. Transition enquiries dominate there while coursework enquiries dominate here, which reflects how long each population has been in the city.

regions.name: Asharej
regions.note: East of the centre with a strong university-linked population. Families there and here share the useful advantage of an older sibling who has written a long piece of work recently.

regions.name: Falaj Hazza

regions.name: Al Towayya
regions.note: North, beside the main hospital campus. Shift-working households there face the same component deadlines with a less predictable week to fit them into.

regions.name: Hili
regions.note: The northern edge, a long run from here across the city. Enquiries from there concentrate on examination technique rather than on coursework, which is a different problem with a different fix.

al-ain/al-maqam.modesIntro: Three patterns cover coursework support, and they differ by where in the component's life they sit. All three run one-to-one over live video, with the draft and the criteria on screen at the same time.

modes.title: A design session before anything is written
modes.description: The highest-value hour available on any assessed component, and the one families book last. The research question, the method, the feasibility and the criteria are examined before a word exists. A question that cannot be answered in the available pages is identified here rather than in March, when the only options left are bad ones.

modes.title: Draft review by questioning
modes.description: The student brings their own draft and the tutor asks about it: what this paragraph is doing, which criterion it serves, why this claim follows from that evidence. Nothing is typed into the document and no replacement text is supplied. The student leaves knowing what to change and does the changing themselves, which is the only version of this that is permissible.

Deadlines cluster, and the clustering is predictable. Seeing it in September is the difference between a planned year and three emergencies.

sections.heading: The components nobody timetables, and who is actually responsible
paragraphs: Start by writing down every piece of assessed work your child owes this year that does not have a weekly lesson attached to it. For a Diploma student in Year 12 that list usually runs to six internal assessments at various stages, an Extended Essay with a supervisor, a Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition, a Group 4 project and a CAS record. For a Year 11 student in the Middle Years Programme it is the Personal Project plus subject criteria work. For an IGCSE student it is practical or coursework components in several subjects.

Then write down who is responsible for each one. The answer, in almost every case, is the student, with a supervisor who checks in. That is by design: these components exist to assess independent work, and a supervisor who did more would be compromising the assessment. The problem is that nobody states the arrangement plainly to the family, so parents assume the school is managing the schedule and the school assumes the student is.

The consequence is the single most common Diploma crisis in this city. A capable, organised student reaches the week a draft is due with nothing written, because at no point did their week contain an hour whose purpose was writing it. Lessons, homework, tests and a long bus journey filled every hour that was scheduled, and the only unscheduled work was the work that mattered most. Blaming the student for this is both unkind and inaccurate.

The table sets out the components with their supervision arrangements and the characteristic point of failure for each. It is worth going through it with your child and marking which rows are genuinely in hand. In practice the rows that are not in hand are usually the ones with the most distant deadline, which is exactly the wrong way round and entirely human.

sections.heading: Internal assessment criteria, by letter, with the marks attached
paragraphs: Internal assessments are not marked holistically. They are marked against criteria, each labelled by a letter, each carrying a defined number of marks, and each assessed independently of the others. A student can write something genuinely interesting and score in the middle because two criteria were barely addressed. This is the most consequential thing a Diploma student can understand about coursework, and almost none of them understands it before the first draft is returned.

The practical implication is that criteria should be read at the planning stage, with the mark allocations visible, and the plan should allocate space in proportion. If a criterion carrying a quarter of the marks concerns evaluation of method, then evaluation of method needs planned space rather than whatever is left at the end when the word count is nearly gone. Students do the opposite: they write the parts they enjoy at length and compress the criteria they find difficult.

The second implication concerns the criteria students consistently neglect. Across subjects, the ones that go thin are reflection, evaluation and personal engagement, because they feel like padding to a student who thinks the mathematics or the data is the real work. They are not padding; they carry marks, and they are the easiest marks on the component to secure because they require honesty rather than brilliance.

The table below is written generically on purpose, because the exact criterion letters, counts and mark allocations differ by subject and are set by the current subject guide. Confirm the figures against the guide your child's school holds before planning against them. What does not change is the principle: find the letters, find the marks, allocate space accordingly, and do it before writing rather than after.

sections.heading: Word and page limits, and what exceeding them costs
paragraphs: Every written component has a limit, and most students treat it as a target to approach from above. The anxious instinct is to write long and cut later, which produces a piece whose structure was designed for a different length and whose cuts fall wherever cutting is easiest rather than where it is least damaging. Planning to the limit from the start produces a better piece of work, and it is a free decision made in the first session.

The published upper limit for the Extended Essay is four thousand words, and for the Theory of Knowledge essay sixteen hundred. Subject internal assessments are usually governed by page counts rather than word counts, with ranges set in the subject guide; mathematics explorations and science investigations both sit in the low-to-mid teens of pages in most current guides. Economics commentaries and the Business Management research project each carry their own tight limits.

The figures above are the widely published ones, and they should still be confirmed against the current subject guide your child's school holds, because limits are revised between syllabus cycles and the school's copy is the authoritative one. This project does not reproduce awarding-body documents, and it does not publish IB dates at all, because the IB's own site could not be checked programmatically. Treat any tutoring page that states a limit without that caveat with mild suspicion.

What a limit should change is the plan. A four-thousand-word essay has room for roughly five substantial sections and no room for a literature review that was interesting to write. A sixteen-hundred-word essay has room for two knowledge arguments properly developed, which is why students who attempt four end up with four assertions. Deciding the section structure and its word allocation before drafting is the whole technique, and it takes twenty minutes.

sections.heading: The internal deadline calendar, counted backwards
paragraphs: Schools set internal deadlines for coursework, and those deadlines are the ones that actually govern a student's year. They exist because teachers need time to mark, moderate and upload, and they therefore sit well before any external date. A family planning against an external examination window rather than against the school's internal calendar is planning against the wrong document, and will be surprised twice.

The clustering is the part worth anticipating. Because every subject's internal assessment has to be marked in the same term, schools tend to place drafts and finals in the same few weeks, and the Extended Essay reflection sessions land in among them. The result is a fortnight in which a student owes three substantial pieces of work and has the same number of evenings as any other fortnight. That fortnight is visible in September and invisible in January.

Counting backwards is the fix, and it is arithmetic rather than inspiration. Take each internal deadline, subtract the time the work genuinely needs, and put the start date in the calendar as an event rather than an intention. A science investigation needs its design approved, its data collected, a false start absorbed and a write-up drafted: that is weeks, not a weekend, and the weeks have to be real ones with hours in them.

This is also where an honest conversation about external dates belongs. Cambridge and Pearson publish their timetables and key dates, and those can be worked from: the Cambridge March 2027 series, for example, had final entries due on 27 November 2026 for an examination period of 3 February to 4 March 2027. IB session dates are deliberately absent from this page, because none has been verified from the IB itself, and a wrong examination date would be a genuinely harmful thing to publish.

sections.heading: Practical work and the Group 4 project when lessons are online
paragraphs: A fair question arrives from every science family: if the tutoring happens over video, how does practical work get supported? The honest answer is that practical work happens at school, in the school laboratory, under the school's supervision, and that is where it should happen. What a tutor can do is everything around it, and that turns out to be most of the marks.

Design is the first part. An investigation that produces no analysable variation cannot be rescued by good writing, and the commonest internal assessment failure in Al Ain is a method approved late and never interrogated. Working through the design before the laboratory session means the student arrives knowing which variable they are controlling, what range of values will produce a usable graph, and how many repeats the analysis will need.

Analysis is the second and larger part. Uncertainty propagation, graph selection, curve fitting, statistical testing and the honest evaluation of limitations are all screen work, and they are where the higher criteria marks live. A student can share a spreadsheet of their own results and work through the processing with a specialist watching, which is considerably more useful than doing it alone at eleven at night.

The alternative-to-practical paper at IGCSE deserves separate mention because it is routinely neglected. It is a written paper about practical work, testing whether a student can read an apparatus diagram, identify variables, spot a flaw in a method and process an untidy result table. All of that is trainable on paper with marked feedback, and students in this city regularly sit it without having practised a single one. The Group 4 project, similarly, is assessed on collaboration and reflection rather than on the science, and the reflection is the part nobody documents until it is too late.

sections.heading: Theory of Knowledge: an essay and an exhibition, both unlike anything else
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge is the component students find hardest to get help with, because it looks like a subject without content and therefore like a subject that cannot be taught. It has content: it has a structure, a vocabulary, and a set of moves that an argument has to make. What it does not have is material to memorise, which is why students who are strong at memorising find it uncomfortable.

The essay fails in a predictable way. A student takes a prescribed title, forms an opinion, and writes an opinion piece with examples attached. What the assessment wants is a knowledge argument: a claim about how knowledge is produced or justified in a particular area, supported, then tested against a counterclaim, with the implications drawn out. The difference between those two pieces of writing is structural, and it can be taught in a few sessions with a plan and a counterargument.

The exhibition fails differently. Students choose three objects they like and then try to attach a prompt to them, which produces three paragraphs explaining why an object is interesting. The assessment wants the prompt understood first and objects selected because they illuminate it, with each object's link to the prompt made explicit. Choosing in the right order is most of the work, and it takes one conversation.

On both components the tutoring boundary is the same as everywhere else and worth repeating here because this is the component where the temptation is strongest. A tutor may teach the structure of a knowledge argument, question the student's claim, point out that the counterclaim is a restatement rather than an opposition, and explain what each assessment band asks for. A tutor may not write the essay, supply paragraphs, or compose the argument for the student to reproduce.

sections.heading: What coursework support costs, and what it must never include
paragraphs: Published market figures first, in AED and attributed. EdFlik advertises online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour, Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, TutorChase shows AED 270, the Bestimate rate survey puts specialist IB and IGCSE work at AED 200 to 450 and above, and BartyED publishes AED 650. Those are the market's own numbers, not an IB Gram price list.

Coursework support prices differently from weekly subject tutoring because it is not weekly. The pattern that works is a small number of sessions placed where they change the outcome: one design session before anything is written, one or two draft reviews, and a final conversation about the criteria the student has still not addressed. Four sessions placed well beat twelve placed badly, and they cost a third as much.

There is a tier in this market that should be avoided entirely, and it is not defined by price. One page ranking for these searches sells completed internal assessments at a published figure. That is not an expensive tutoring service; it is a different product, and the product is a malpractice finding waiting to be issued. The student is the person who carries it, and at Diploma level the consequence can extend to the whole diploma.

The useful question to ask any provider is therefore not what it costs but what happens to the document. If the answer involves anyone other than the student typing in it, the service is one to decline regardless of the price. If the answer is that feedback is spoken, questioned and acted on by the student, the price is worth comparing against the published bands above.

sections.heading: A school supervisor and a tutor on screen: who does what
paragraphs: Families worry, reasonably, about whether bringing in a tutor undermines or duplicates the supervisor's role. It does neither when the division of labour is clear, and understanding that division is also how a family avoids the awkward situation of a student receiving contradictory advice from two adults a fortnight before a deadline.

The supervisor owns the formal process. They approve the research question, hold the required reflection sessions, confirm the work is the student's own, and submit it. They are the only person who can authorise a change of topic or sign off a declaration. Nothing a tutor says overrides them, and where their advice conflicts with a tutor's, the supervisor's view is the one that governs because they are accountable for the submission.

A tutor owns neither process nor product. What a tutor can do is spend time the supervisor does not have: interrogating a research question for scope, reading criteria with the student and asking which sentence serves which criterion, working through data processing, and questioning a draft paragraph by paragraph. A supervisor with twenty supervisees cannot do that, and is not expected to.

The table sets the two roles out explicitly, which is worth having if only so a student can answer the question honestly when a supervisor asks what help they have had. That question should be easy to answer, and if it is not, the help was the wrong kind. IB Gram holds no approval or accreditation from any awarding body or regulator, operates no UAE premises, and makes no claim to any relationship with your child's school.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, in practical detail
paragraphs: The rule is short: a tutor may teach, explain, question and review, and may not write, draft, complete or edit to completion an internal assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay, Personal Project or any coursework. What makes it useful is applying it to the situations that actually arise, because most breaches are not cynical. They happen at eleven at night, two days before a deadline, when someone helpful suggests a sentence.

Here are the practical lines. Explaining what a criterion asks for: fine. Reading a paragraph and asking what it is doing: fine. Saying that a conclusion does not follow from the data: fine. Dictating the improved conclusion: not fine. Typing into the document: not fine. Supplying a model paragraph on the same research question for the student to adapt: not fine, however it is labelled. Restructuring the essay yourself and sending it back: not fine.

The same applies to family help, which is worth saying in a district where many students have an undergraduate sibling nearby. A sibling explaining referencing conventions or how to read a journal article is useful and permitted. A sibling drafting a section is a breach, and the assessment rules do not distinguish between a paid tutor and a relative. The student signs a declaration that the work is their own, and that declaration means what it says.

Materials follow the same logic. Official syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the awarding bodies and are cited and linked rather than reproduced. The working material is what the school has legitimately issued. IB Gram publishes no self-assessed rating or success statistic, claims no regulator or board approval, and holds no UAE office. Where this page states a figure it names who published it, and where a date could not be verified it is left off.
bullets: Spoken feedback on the student's own draft is the boundary
A supplied model paragraph on the same question is a breach

process.title: Collect every internal deadline in writing
process.description: Not the external examination window, which is months later, but the dates your child's own school has set for drafts, finals and reflection sessions. Those dates govern the year. Written down together, they reveal the fortnight where three components collide, which is visible in September and invisible by January.

process.title: Read the criteria with the marks attached, before writing
process.description: Find the criterion letters for the component, find how many marks each carries, and allocate planned space in proportion. Students write at length on the parts they enjoy and compress the criteria they find difficult, which is precisely backwards. Twenty minutes here changes the piece of work that gets produced.

process.title: Test the research question out loud
process.description: Say the question and then try to answer it in two sentences. If that is possible, it is too narrow. If a term of work would not settle it, it is too broad. If the data or equipment needed does not exist within reach, it is not feasible. Each of those failures costs weeks when found late and minutes when found early.

process.title: Book the design session before the laboratory session
process.description: An investigation that produces no analysable variation cannot be saved by good writing. Working through the method first means the student arrives at the laboratory knowing the controlled variable, the range of values that will give a usable graph and the number of repeats the analysis needs.

process.title: Review drafts by questioning, and keep the typing with the student
process.description: The student brings their own draft, the tutor asks what each section is doing and which criterion it serves, and the student leaves with their own list of changes. Nothing is typed into the document. That is both the rule and, as it happens, the method that produces the better second draft.

whyPoints.title: The untimetabled components are treated as the real problem
whyPoints.description: Most pages about tutoring assume the issue is content coverage. In this district it is more often a piece of assessed work with no weekly lesson attached, a distant deadline and a supervisor carrying twenty others. Naming that lets the support go where the marks actually are instead of adding another content hour.

whyPoints.title: Criteria are discussed by letter, with marks attached
whyPoints.description: Internal assessments are marked criterion by criterion, independently, with defined mark allocations. A student who knows which criterion carries a quarter of the marks writes a different piece of work. Nobody in this market publishes criterion-level detail, which makes it both the most useful and the most neglected thing to explain.

whyPoints.title: Limits are published with a check-the-guide warning
whyPoints.description: Word and page limits shape a plan rather than a final edit, so they are tabulated here. They are also revised between syllabus cycles, so the page says plainly that the authoritative version is the subject guide your child's school holds, rather than presenting a number as permanent fact.

whyPoints.title: The deadline map comes from your school, not a template
whyPoints.description: Internal deadlines differ by campus and they are the ones that govern the year. The planning session collects your own school's dates and counts backwards from them, which is why it identifies the specific fortnight where two components collide rather than offering generic advice about starting early.

whyPoints.title: The supervisor's authority is respected explicitly
whyPoints.description: The supervisor approves the question, holds the reflection sessions, confirms authenticity and submits. Where their advice differs from a tutor's, theirs governs, because they are accountable for the submission. Saying so prevents the worst version of this situation, which is a student receiving contradictory instructions near a deadline.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line is applied to real situations
whyPoints.description: Not a policy paragraph but a list: explaining a criterion is fine, dictating a conclusion is not, a supplied model paragraph on the same question is a breach, and family help follows the same rule as paid help. Breaches happen late at night under pressure, so the lines are drawn in advance.

faqs.question: Why does my organised child arrive at a coursework deadline with nothing written?
faqs.answer: Because nothing in their week ever said write it. Assessed components outside the timetable have no weekly lesson, so every scheduled hour goes to lessons, homework, tests and a long bus journey, and the only unscheduled work is the work that carries the most marks. The deadline was noted in October and the next eight weeks contained no hour whose purpose was that piece of work. It is a calendar problem with a predictable shape, not a motivation problem, and the fix is putting start dates in the diary as events.

faqs.question: How much of a Diploma subject grade does the internal assessment carry?
faqs.answer: Generally twenty to thirty per cent depending on the subject and level, with the rest in terminal papers. That makes it the largest single piece of work most students have ever been marked on, and it is marked by the teacher against published criteria before external moderation. The practical consequence is that a strong paper performance cannot fully compensate for a weak internal assessment, and that the hours spent on it should be proportionate to the weight rather than squeezed into whatever time is left.

faqs.question: What does it mean that an internal assessment is marked criterion by criterion?
faqs.answer: It means the marks are awarded in separate boxes rather than for an overall impression. Each criterion has a letter, a description and a defined number of marks, and each is assessed independently. A student can produce something genuinely interesting and land mid-range because two criteria were barely addressed. Reading the criteria at the planning stage, with the mark allocations visible, and allocating space in proportion is the single most consequential thing a Diploma student can do with twenty minutes.

faqs.question: Which criteria do students most often leave thin?
faqs.answer: Reflection, evaluation and personal engagement, almost universally. Students treat them as padding because they believe the mathematics or the data is the real work, so those sections get written in the final hour as a short list of apologies. They carry real marks and they are the easiest marks on the component to secure, because they ask for honesty about what went wrong rather than for brilliance. Keeping a short running log during the work makes them straightforward to write properly at the end.

faqs.question: Does exceeding the word limit on the Extended Essay actually matter?
faqs.answer: Enough that it should shape the plan rather than the final edit. The published upper limit is four thousand words, and writing long then cutting produces a piece whose structure was designed for a different length, with cuts falling wherever cutting is easiest rather than where it does least harm. Four thousand words has room for roughly five substantial sections. Deciding that structure and its word allocation before drafting is the technique, and limits should still be confirmed against the current subject guide your school holds.

faqs.question: How many knowledge arguments should a Theory of Knowledge essay contain?
faqs.answer: Two, developed properly, is the shape that works within the published sixteen-hundred-word limit. Students attempting four end up with four assertions and no development, which is the commonest reason a capable student scores poorly. The essay also fails when it becomes an opinion piece with examples attached: what is wanted is a claim about how knowledge is produced or justified in an area, supported, then tested against a genuine counterclaim with the implications drawn. That is a structural skill and it can be taught.

faqs.question: How should my child choose objects for the Theory of Knowledge exhibition?
faqs.answer: After understanding the prompt, not before. The standard failure is choosing three objects the student finds interesting and then trying to attach a prompt to them, which produces three paragraphs explaining why an object is interesting. The assessment wants the prompt understood first and each object selected because it illuminates that specific prompt, with the link made explicit rather than implied. Getting the order right is most of the work on this component, and it takes one conversation rather than a course.

faqs.question: If lessons are online, how can anyone help with laboratory work?
faqs.answer: The laboratory work happens at school under the school's supervision, which is where it belongs. What a tutor can support is everything around it, and that is where most of the criteria marks sit: interrogating the method before the session so the student knows the controlled variable, the range of values that will give a usable graph and the repeats the analysis needs, then working through uncertainty propagation, graph selection and evaluation afterwards with the student's own spreadsheet shared on screen. That is considerably more useful than doing the processing alone at eleven at night.

faqs.question: What exactly is the alternative-to-practical paper testing?
faqs.answer: Whether a student can read an apparatus diagram, identify independent and controlled variables, spot a flaw in a described method, and process an untidy table of real results. It is a written paper about practical work, and every one of those skills is trainable on paper with marked feedback. Students in Al Ain regularly sit it without having practised a single one, which is why a predicted grade and an actual grade can diverge for reasons that have nothing to do with how well the student understands the science.

faqs.question: Why did my child score poorly on the Group 4 project when the science was fine?
faqs.answer: Because the Group 4 project is not assessed on the science. It is assessed on collaboration and on personal reflection about the collaborative process, and almost nobody documents either while it is happening. Students complete the investigation, enjoy it, and then have nothing to write about how the group made decisions, what went wrong between them and what they themselves contributed or learned. Keeping brief notes during the project days is the entire fix, and it takes minutes rather than hours.

faqs.question: Is the MYP Personal Project really worth taking seriously?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a reason students find counterintuitive: it is assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting rather than on the quality of the product. A beautiful outcome with no process evidence scores poorly and a modest outcome with rigorous documentation scores well. It is also the best available rehearsal for the Extended Essay, which arrives two years later and works the same way. Students who treat it as a fortnight's work arrive in Year 12 without ever having managed a long deadline.

faqs.question: Does bringing in a tutor undermine my child's school supervisor?
faqs.answer: Not when the division is clear. The supervisor owns the formal process: approving the research question, holding the required reflection sessions, confirming the work is the student's own and submitting it. Nothing a tutor says overrides that, and where advice conflicts the supervisor's view governs because they are accountable for the submission. A tutor spends the time the supervisor does not have, interrogating scope, reading criteria against the student's own draft and working through data. A supervisor with twenty supervisees cannot do that and is not expected to.

faqs.question: My older child is at university here and helps with drafting. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It can be, and the rules do not distinguish between a relative and a paid tutor. A sibling explaining referencing conventions, showing how to read a journal article or talking through an idea is useful and permitted. A sibling drafting a section, restructuring the essay or supplying paragraphs is a breach of the authenticity declaration your child signs. In a district where university siblings are common this is worth saying plainly, because the help is offered with good intentions and the consequence falls entirely on the younger student.

faqs.question: Can a tutor show my child a model answer on the same research question?
faqs.answer: No. A model paragraph written on the student's own research question for them to adapt is a breach however it is labelled, because what the student submits would then not be their own work. Explaining what a criterion asks for, reading a paragraph and asking what it is doing, and saying that a conclusion does not follow from the data are all legitimate. Dictating the improved conclusion, typing into the document or restructuring the piece and sending it back are not. The test is whether anyone other than the student composes text.

faqs.question: How many sessions does coursework support actually need?
faqs.answer: Fewer than families expect, placed well. One design session before anything is written, two or three on data analysis once results exist, one or two draft reviews a fortnight before each internal deadline, and a final criteria check. Four to six sessions placed at those points achieve more than twelve spread evenly, and cost a third as much. The expensive version is weekly coursework support from September, which mostly funds conversations about work that has not started yet.

faqs.question: Why does this page quote Cambridge dates but no IB dates?
faqs.answer: Because the Cambridge and Pearson dates were read from the boards' own published documents and the IB dates could not be. The IB's site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and publishing one would mean passing on an unverified number. Cambridge's March 2027 series, by contrast, is documented: final entries 27 November 2026, examinations 3 February to 4 March 2027. For IB dates, ask your child's coordinator.

al-ain/al-maqam.closingHeading: Bring the deadline list and the criteria sheet
al-ain/al-maqam.closingBody: The fastest route to something useful for an Al Maqam family is the list of internal deadlines your child's school has set and the criteria sheet for whichever component is closest. From those we can tell you what has to start this month, which fortnight is going to collide, and whether a design session or a draft review is the hour worth buying. Nothing is written for a student here and nothing is typed into a document, because the student is the only person who carries a malpractice finding. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, no home visits are sold in the UAE, and IB Gram holds no regulator or awarding-body approval of any kind.

al-ain/al-mutaredh.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work from marks rather than from impressions: component weightings, mark schemes, and the specific questions where a student's score is being lost. Most requests from this district are Diploma mathematics and sciences and IGCSE sciences in an examination year.

intro.heading: A grade is a conversion, not a measurement
paragraphs: Al Mutaredh is one of the older established districts of Al Ain, west of the centre near the oasis and the city hospital, with mature streets and large walled plots. Families here have often been at the same campus since primary, know the staff, and have a decade of report cards in a drawer. That long relationship produces a particular kind of enquiry: not panic, but a settled suspicion that something is not adding up, usually built on a grade that has sat at the same number for three years.

The suspicion is almost always well founded, and the reason is structural. A grade is not a measurement of your child. It is the output of a conversion: raw marks on individual components, weighted together, then mapped onto a grade using thresholds set after the examination has been sat and marked. Two students with the same grade can have reached it by completely different routes, and the grade itself tells you nothing about which route either of them took.

That is why a report card is a poor basis for a tutoring decision. It reports the output of a conversion and discards the input. A 5 in chemistry might mean a strong paper performance dragged down by an internal assessment, or an adequate internal assessment propping up a weak paper, or a consistent middling performance across everything. Those three situations need completely different work, and no amount of looking at the number distinguishes them.

The same logic applies to the documents families trust most. A predicted grade is a professional estimate made for an administrative purpose, not a prophecy. A forecast grade submitted to an awarding body is a formal requirement with a deadline, not a target. A mock result is a measurement of a student's performance on one paper under conditions that are never quite the real conditions. Each of those is useful if you know what it is for, and misleading if you do not.

This page therefore works in marks. It sets out what to ask for instead of a report card, how the raw-mark-to-grade conversion actually operates and why last year's threshold is not this year's, what predicted and forecast grades are, what mocks measure, and how to convert a target grade into a target mark per paper so that progress becomes something you can check rather than something you feel. It then covers results day and the resit arithmetic honestly.

One thing is stated at the outset and repeated later: nothing on this page or on this platform promises a grade. No tutor can, and a provider that offers one is making a claim it cannot keep. What can be offered is a clear account of where marks are being lost, the work that addresses it, and a way of measuring whether the work is having an effect. Delivery is one-to-one over live video; IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE.

al-ain/al-mutaredh.programmesIntro: Families in Al Mutaredh are mainly on the British route and the IB continuum. Each programme is described below by how its marks are assembled into a grade, which is the mechanism the rest of this page depends on.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Each subject produces a grade from 1 to 7, assembled from written papers and an internal assessment that generally carries twenty to thirty per cent. Those subject grades are totalled across six subjects, with additional points available from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, to produce an overall diploma score. Every stage of that is a conversion with its own thresholds.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in Al Ain are frequently in small sets, which has one specific consequence for marks: there are fewer classmates to compare against, so a student's sense of their own standing is based on a handful of data points. That makes external reference material, meaning past papers marked to the published scheme, more important here than in a large cohort.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: Grades come from terminal papers, weighted by component, with tiering in several subjects capping the available range. Raw marks are converted using thresholds determined for that specific series, which is why the same paper mark can produce different grades in different series.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge publishes a key-dates schedule for each series. For the March 2027 series, final entries were due 27 November 2026, forecast grades 27 February 2027, examinations ran 3 February to 4 March 2027, results reached Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates followed in late June. Those dates are the skeleton of any mark-based plan.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: Component marks are converted to uniform marks in some structures before aggregation, which is why a strong paper can offset a weak one more effectively here than families expect. Pearson's modular arrangement permits unit resits; Cambridge's International A Level can be staged across series.
programmes.countryNote: The resit arithmetic is genuinely different between the two structures, and it is the single most useful thing to understand before results day rather than after it. A family that knows in April which units could be retaken in which series makes a calm decision in August instead of a rushed one.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each scored out of eight, with the four totals converted to a 1-7 grade using published boundaries. This is the clearest example of the conversion principle: a student can score well on two criteria and poorly on two and land mid-band, and the grade alone will not say which.
programmes.countryNote: In a district where families have been at the same school for years, middle-years grades tend to be read as a trend line. They are better read criterion by criterion, because a flat grade across three years often conceals one criterion that has never improved and three that have.

al-ain/al-mutaredh.subjectsIntro: Requests from this district are usually about a specific component rather than a whole subject. Each entry below names where the marks concentrate and which part of the conversion a student is losing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Method marks are awarded for visible justified steps, so a student who works mentally loses marks on questions they answered correctly. The exploration carries its own criteria and is marked separately, which means a weak exploration can hold down a strong paper performance.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistical and modelling questions award marks across setup, execution and interpretation. The interpretation mark is lost most often, which means a student can be strong at the mathematics and still score in the middle of the range.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Calculations are marked in steps, so presentation determines whether partial credit is available when a final answer is wrong. The internal assessment is marked against separate criteria, and the two sources of loss need completely different work.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Units, significant figures and explanation sequencing account for a large share of lost marks, none of which indicate weak understanding. The practical skills component is marked to its own criteria and is frequently the lowest-scoring part of a strong student's profile.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command terms decide this paper more than content knowledge. A student who answers explain as describe loses roughly half the available marks on those questions, which can account for an entire grade across a full paper.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram marks are discrete and recoverable: axes, labels, shift and new equilibrium are each creditable. Evaluation marks require a judgement supported by the analysis already given, and are not awarded for a new argument in the conclusion.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Multi-step questions award marks at each stage, so stopping at the first unfamiliar part forfeits the marks that follow. Working through whole papers rather than topic sheets is what trains a student to keep going and collect those.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and qualitative analysis carry the mark weight. Structured working converts a wrong final answer into partial credit, which over a full paper is often the difference between two grades.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: The practical or alternative-to-practical paper is a discrete component with its own mark allocation and is rarely practised as a paper in its own right. That makes it the most commonly underperformed component in a strong student's profile.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 and Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: High content volume with marks distributed widely, which rewards breadth of recall under time. Diagram labelling and experimental design are small discrete mark pools that students routinely leave on the table.

subjects.name: English First Language and English A
subjects.description: Marked against level descriptors rather than point-by-point, which changes the strategy entirely: the work is on reaching a higher band for the whole response rather than collecting individual points. Students rarely have the descriptors explained to them.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Business Management
subjects.description: Explicit mark tariffs with application to supplied case material required for the higher marks. Generic textbook answers score the lower band consistently, which produces exactly the flat grade pattern this page is about.

al-ain/al-mutaredh.modesIntro: Three patterns follow from a mark-based diagnosis, and which one applies depends on where in the conversion the marks are being lost. All three are one-to-one over live video.

modes.title: A mark audit before any teaching
modes.description: One session that takes the last two marked papers and works out where the score actually went: which component, which question types, which error categories. The output is a breakdown and a target mark per paper rather than a target grade. Families who do this frequently discover the work needed is narrower and cheaper than they expected.

modes.title: Component-specific work
modes.description: Teaching aimed at a single component rather than a whole subject: the practical skills paper, the interpretation marks in a statistics question, the evaluation band in an essay. Components have their own mark pools and their own conventions, and treating them separately is why this approach moves scores faster than general revision.
bullets: One component at a time, with its own mark pool identified
Practice drawn from that component only, marked to the scheme
Reviewed by whether that component's score has moved

modes.title: A results-day plan prepared in advance
modes.description: A short block before results are released, mapping what each plausible outcome triggers: a remark request, a unit resit, a full re-entry, or a changed university plan. Decisions made before the envelope is opened are better than decisions made in the twenty-four hours afterwards, which is when most of them are currently made.

sections.heading: What a report card does not tell you, and what to ask instead
paragraphs: A report card is designed to communicate a summary to a parent in a small space, and it does that job. What it cannot do is tell you where marks were lost, which is the only information a tutoring decision actually requires. The grade is the output of a conversion and the conversion discards the detail. Asking a school for the detail is both reasonable and usually straightforward, and almost nobody does it.

The three documents worth requesting are the component breakdown for the most recent internal examination, the marked paper itself with the annotations on it, and the current internal assessment mark where one exists. With those three, a diagnosis takes twenty minutes. Without them, the first month of tutoring is spent reconstructing information the school already holds, which the family pays for twice.

The breakdown matters most. A chemistry grade of 5 that comes from a strong paper and a weak internal assessment needs coursework work. The same 5 from an adequate internal assessment and a weak paper needs examination technique. The same 5 from consistent mid-range performance everywhere needs content consolidation. Three different programmes of work, one identical number on the report, and no way to distinguish them without asking.

In a district where families have a decade of reports in a drawer, there is a second useful exercise: look for the flat line. A grade that has not moved in three years is rarely a plateau in ability. It is usually one component that has never been addressed, or one error category that nobody has ever named. Flat lines in a long run of reports are the most diagnosable pattern in a child's school record and they almost never get examined.
bullets: Request the component breakdown, the marked paper and the coursework mark

A flat grade across years usually means one unaddressed component
Twenty minutes of the right documents beats a month of guessing

sections.heading: From raw marks to a grade: how the conversion actually works
paragraphs: A student sits components. Each produces a raw mark. Those raw marks are weighted according to the published component weightings for that subject and level, aggregated, and then compared against thresholds to produce a grade. The thresholds are determined for each individual series, after the papers have been sat and marked, taking into account how the cohort performed and how demanding that particular paper turned out to be.

Two consequences follow, and both surprise families. The first is that a given raw mark does not correspond to a fixed grade. If a paper is harder than usual, the thresholds move down; if it is easier, they move up. That is the mechanism working as intended, because it protects students from being penalised for sitting a difficult version of a paper. It also means last year's threshold is a guide to this year's and not a promise about it.

The second is that weightings matter more than families assume. A component carrying a small share of the grade cannot rescue a weak performance in a large one, however well it is done, and a component carrying a large share will dominate the outcome. Working out which components carry the weight in your child's specific subject and level, from the published subject guide or specification, is the arithmetic that tells you where an hour of work is worth most.

A note on documents. Awarding-body specifications, subject guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. They are cited and linked rather than reproduced on this site, and no threshold figures are published here, both because they are the boards' property and because a threshold from one series applied to another is actively misleading. Ask the school for the relevant documents; they hold them legitimately.

sections.heading: Predicted grades, forecast grades and what each is for
paragraphs: Three different things get called a prediction and they do different jobs. A school's predicted grade is a professional estimate used for university applications and internal planning. A forecast grade is a formal submission to the awarding body with its own deadline, used in the board's own quality processes. And a target grade is an aspiration set by the school. Families routinely treat all three as the same number with the same meaning, which produces avoidable arguments.

The forecast grade has a hard date attached, which is the easiest way to see that it is an administrative instrument rather than a motivational one. For the Cambridge March 2027 series, forecast grades were due on 27 February 2027, with the examination period running 3 February to 4 March 2027 and results reaching Cambridge Direct on 13 May. The school is obliged to produce a defensible figure by that date, based on the evidence it holds at the time.

This is why the useful question about any prediction is what evidence it rests on. A prediction built on two mock papers and a coursework mark is a different animal from one built on an impression of classroom performance. Asking the question politely and specifically tends to produce a more considered answer, and occasionally it produces a revision, because the person answering looks at the evidence again in order to reply.

What a prediction is not is a ceiling or a floor. Students exceed and undershoot predictions in both directions every series, and the distribution is wide. Using a prediction as a reason to stop working, or as evidence that a target is impossible, misreads what the number is. The appropriate use is as a planning input: it tells you roughly where the student currently stands, which is useful precisely because it is approximate.

sections.heading: Mocks: what they measure and what they do not
paragraphs: A mock is a real measurement of something, and it is worth being precise about what. It measures a student's performance on a particular set of questions, marked by a particular teacher, under conditions that approximate but do not reproduce the examination. It is the best single predictor most families have access to, and it is routinely both over-read and under-used.

Over-read, because a single mock result is one data point with considerable noise around it. A student who was unwell, or who happened to meet two topics they had just revised, or who sat a paper set deliberately hard to prompt effort, produces a number that does not generalise. Treating one mock as a verdict is the commonest overreaction in an examination year, and it tends to trigger the purchase of three subjects' worth of tutoring at once.

Under-used, because the script contains almost everything worth knowing and most students never look at it again. A mock paper is a full diagnostic: it shows which components scored, which question types failed, where the timing collapsed and which error categories recurred. Going through a mock script line by line, a fortnight after results, is among the highest-value hours available in an examination year and it costs the price of one session.

The practical approach is to use mocks as a trend with a diagnosis attached rather than as a judgement. Two mocks and a set of class assessments give a usable trend. The script from each gives the diagnosis. A student who knows that eleven of their lost marks came from unfinished questions and nine from command-term errors has a plan. A student who knows only that they got a 4 has a worry.

sections.heading: Turning a target grade into a target mark per paper
paragraphs: The single most useful change a family in this district can make is to stop targeting grades and start targeting marks. A grade is downstream of a conversion the student does not control. A mark is the thing they actually produce, on a specific paper, in a specific room. Converting one into the other takes twenty minutes with the published component weightings for the subject and level, and it changes how a student revises.

The logic runs like this. Find the component weightings in the subject guide or specification the school holds. Work out the total marks available in each component. Take the student's most recent marks on each. Then work out what an additional handful of marks on each paper would do to the aggregate. The number that comes out is almost always smaller and more achievable than the student imagines, which has a measurable effect on how they approach the work.

The second part of the exercise is identifying where those marks are cheapest. Discrete mark pools are the easiest: diagram labels in biology, units and significant figures in physics, the setup and interpretation marks either side of a statistical calculation, the structure marks in an essay band. A student can gain several marks a paper from those alone without learning any new content, which is why a mark audit so often reduces rather than increases the work required.

No part of this guarantees anything, and it is worth saying so directly rather than in small print. No tutor can promise a grade, a score or an improvement, and anybody who does is selling something they cannot deliver. What this method offers is a target the student can see, a way of checking whether the work is moving it, and an honest answer when it is not. That is a different and better product than a promise.

sections.heading: Results day, remarks and the arithmetic of a resit
paragraphs: Results day decisions are usually made badly, and the reason is timing rather than judgement: the options have deadlines, the deadlines are short, and nobody has read them in advance. A family that spends one hour in the spring mapping what each plausible outcome would trigger makes a calm decision in August. A family that starts reading on results day makes a rushed one.

The published dates give the shape. Cambridge released results for the March 2027 series on Cambridge Direct on 13 May 2027, with certificates in late June. Pearson sent June 2026 International GCSE results to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson runs series in May or June and in November each year, and Cambridge in June and November, so the next entry opportunity is never far away.

The options differ in what they can achieve. A review of marking checks whether the mark scheme was applied correctly; it does not re-mark generously, and it can move a result down as well as up in some arrangements, so it is worth requesting through the school with a clear reason rather than on general disappointment. A unit resit, available in Pearson's modular structures, replaces one component. A full re-entry in a later series replaces the whole subject result and requires the whole subject to be prepared again.

The arithmetic that matters is what each option costs in time against what it can plausibly change. A review of marking on a component two marks below a threshold is a reasonable request. A full re-entry to move a grade by one when a university offer does not require it is usually a poor use of six months. These are judgements, and they are much easier to make with the component breakdown in front of you, which brings this page back to where it started.

sections.heading: What this work costs, and the hour that moves a mark
paragraphs: Published market figures, in AED and attributed, because most pages in this market provide none. EdFlik advertises online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour; Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; TutorChase shows AED 270; the Bestimate rate survey puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and specialist IB and IGCSE work at AED 200 to 450 and above; BartyED publishes AED 650. None of those is an IB Gram price.

For the work this page describes, the relevant distinction is not price but whether the hour involves a mark scheme. An hour of content re-explanation is useful for a student who has missed a topic and does nothing for a student whose marks are being lost to timing, command terms or a weak internal assessment. The tiers that mark work to the published scheme and name error categories are the ones that move the kind of marks described here, and they sit in the upper published bands.

A mark audit is also the cheapest useful hour available, and it frequently reduces the total spend. Families arrive expecting to book three subjects and leave with one component identified, a target mark and a six-session plan. That is a worse commercial outcome for a tutoring platform and a better one for the family, which is the trade a page like this has to be willing to make in order to be worth reading.

Two questions to put to any provider. Is the figure per hour or per session, since a sixty-minute hour and a forty-five-minute session at the same price are different products. And does the session include marking the student's own work against the published scheme, because that is the activity this entire page depends on and it is not universal at any price point.

sections.heading: Delivery from a central district, and the in-home comparison
paragraphs: Al Mutaredh is close to the school belt, so in-home tutoring is more practicable here than in the outlying districts, and families asking about it deserve a straight answer. It exists, it is advertised at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, and for a younger child who needs an adult present it solves a genuine problem. What it does not solve is the specialist question, because the people who teach a given Higher Level syllabus in this city already have full timetables.

IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE, and nobody will be sent to an Al Mutaredh address; home visiting is offered only in India. UAE lessons are one-to-one over live video, with the student sharing their own marked script or working on screen while the tutor applies the mark scheme to it in real time. That specific activity is actually easier on a shared screen than across a table, because both people can see the scheme and the script at once.

There is a second practical advantage for the work on this page. Marked scripts, error logs and per-component targets persist after the session, so a parent can see the diagnosis rather than receive a summary of it at the door. In a household that has a decade of report cards and no component breakdowns, having something concrete to look at is a change in itself.

Neither format is universally better and the table says so. A child who will not engage with a screen is better served by an adult in the room. A student whose marks are being lost in a specific component, where the work is script review and scheme application, is better served online, and the money saved on travel buys additional sessions in the term that decides the result.

sections.heading: No promises, no invented numbers, no claimed approvals
paragraphs: A page about marks has an obligation to be clear about what cannot be offered. No tutor can promise a grade, a score, a points total or a specific improvement, and no honest provider offers one. Outcomes depend on the student's work, the paper they meet, the cohort they are measured against and the thresholds set for that series, and none of those is under a tutor's control. A provider that promises an outcome is making a claim about things it does not decide.

The same applies to statistics. This site publishes no success percentage, no satisfaction figure, no average score and no student headcount, because a number without a sample, a date and a method is not information. Several providers in this market publish self-assessed ratings, and at least one shows two different review totals on the same page. Where this page quotes a figure, it names who published it and when.

On status: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the labour ministry, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. It operates no office, centre or branch in the UAE. It is an independent tutor-matching platform, and any provider in this market describing itself as approved for tutoring should be asked to produce the permit or centre number behind the claim.

On materials and dates: awarding-body specifications, subject guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are cited and linked rather than reproduced, and no threshold figures appear here because a threshold from one series applied to another misleads. The Cambridge and Pearson dates used on this page come from the boards' own published documents. No IB examination dates appear anywhere on this site, because none has been verified from the IB itself.
