process.title: Bring two pieces of marked school work
process.description: Not a report card. Two actual marked papers or assessments, with the teacher's annotations visible. Within twenty minutes those show whether the loss is content, command terms, timing or presentation, and that distinction decides everything that follows. A report card says a grade; a marked paper says why.

process.title: Identify the error categories before teaching anything
process.description: The first session sorts lost marks into categories: command term misread, no method shown, ran out of time, no application to context, no supported judgement. Most students have three or four recurring categories and no idea they are recurring. Naming them converts vague anxiety into a short list of fixable habits.

process.title: Audit the study week and write the budget down
process.description: Count the hours genuinely available after travel, mandatory-subject homework and fixed commitments, then allocate them by method rather than by subject. Replacing rereading with marked question practice is usually the largest single improvement available, and it costs nothing but a change of habit.

process.title: Run weekly marked practice, with the scheme visible
process.description: The student answers under time, the tutor marks against the published scheme while they watch, and they disagree about borderline points. That argument is where the learning is. An error log carries forward so each session has a target rather than a topic.

process.title: Switch to whole papers after mocks
process.description: In the final term the unit of work becomes a complete paper, correctly timed, reviewed immediately while the student can still recall their reasoning. This is the pattern that converts a mock grade into a better final one, and it needs a long block rather than a weekday hour squeezed between other things.

whyPoints.title: The gap is named rather than blamed on the school
whyPoints.description: Close individual marking does not scale to a class of twenty-five, and that is arithmetic rather than a failure of teaching. Saying so plainly lets a family aim private support at the one thing the school genuinely cannot provide, which is usually cheaper than the broad package they were about to buy.

whyPoints.title: Sessions are built on schemes and tariffs
whyPoints.description: Work starts from the published mark scheme and the marks in brackets, because that is where credit is decided. A student who can read a tariff as an instruction and recognise a command term has gained something that improves every paper they sit, in every subject, for the rest of their schooling.

whyPoints.title: Independent study is budgeted in hours
whyPoints.description: The study week is counted, written down and allocated by method, with rereading replaced by retrieval and timed practice. Two students with the same timetable produce different grades because of what happened in the evenings, and the evenings are the part nobody has ever been taught to manage.

whyPoints.title: Progress is measured by error category
whyPoints.description: An error log records what type of mark was lost, not just how many. That turns progress into something visible: four marks lost to the same category last month and none this month is evidence, where a general feeling that lessons are going well is not.

whyPoints.title: Thin local supply is handled rather than hidden
whyPoints.description: Al Ain has fewer resident subject specialists than the capital, and the northern districts are a drive from most of them. Online matching removes the geography, and where no UAE-based specialist covers a subject that is disclosed before any booking rather than discovered later.

whyPoints.title: The coursework line is explicit
whyPoints.description: Marking a student's own answer is coaching. Dictating the improved version for them to copy is not, whatever it is called. That distinction protects the student, who is the only person who carries a malpractice finding, and it is stated before a family has to ask about it.

faqs.question: My child understands the work in class and still does badly in tests. Why?
faqs.answer: Because understanding content and scoring marks are different skills, and only the first one gets taught at scale. Examiners award credit against command terms and against a tariff, so a four-mark question wants roughly four separate creditable points. A student can write a fluent, correct paragraph containing two of them and score two. That is not a knowledge gap and rereading the chapter will not fix it. What fixes it is answering questions under time, having them marked against the published scheme, and seeing exactly which point earned credit and which did not.

faqs.question: Why does the teacher not mark my child's work this closely already?
faqs.answer: Arithmetic rather than unwillingness. A teacher with a full specification and a set of twenty-plus students can deliver content, check understanding across the group and set practice. Marking every student's answer closely enough for them to see which creditable point they missed, then watching them attempt a similar question with that in mind, is individual work and does not scale to a class. Recognising that changes the question from whether the school is good enough to which part of the job your child is currently doing alone and unmarked.

faqs.question: What is the difference between describe and explain in a science paper?
faqs.answer: Describe wants the features or the sequence without causes. Explain wants a causal chain, in order, with the links actually made. The most common and most expensive error at this level is answering explain as describe: the student writes accurately what happens, never says why, and collects roughly half the marks. It feels like a hard subject and it is a vocabulary problem. Four questions and a mark scheme in one session is usually enough for a student to see their own habit, after which practice has a target.

faqs.question: Why did my child lose marks on an evaluation question they answered well?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the judgement arrived with new material attached. Evaluation marks are awarded for a conclusion that follows from the analysis already given in the answer. A student who introduces a fresh argument in the final sentence gets no credit for it, because nothing in the answer supports it. It is a structural habit rather than a thinking problem, and it is quick to correct once named. The same pattern costs marks in economics, business, biology and every essay-based subject your child sits.

faqs.question: How long should an answer be for the marks available?
faqs.answer: Treat the number in brackets as an instruction. One mark wants one point and then silence. Two marks want two separate points, or one point with development. Four marks want four distinct points or two developed ones, written so the separation is visible to a marker. Six marks in a case-study subject usually want theory plus application to the material supplied. The relationship is not exact across every board, but it is close enough to be the single most useful rule a student can take into a paper.

faqs.question: How do I work out how much time to spend per question?
faqs.answer: Divide the paper's duration by its total marks, which at this level usually gives somewhere around a minute to a minute and a half per mark. Then check your child's actual pace on a timed paper against that budget. Students who have never done this division have no way of knowing they are forty per cent over on question two, and the first they learn of it is an unfinished paper and a grade that misrepresents what they know. Timing is invisible in class because class work is rarely timed.

faqs.question: How many hours of independent study should a Year 11 student do?
faqs.answer: Ten to fourteen a week across all subjects is a workable range in an examination year, rising after mocks, but the split matters more than the total. A student doing six hours of rereading will be beaten by a student doing three hours of question practice marked against a scheme. Count the hours genuinely available after travel, mandatory-subject homework and fixed commitments before allocating any of them, because an ambitious plan built on hours that do not exist is abandoned by October and leaves nothing behind.

faqs.question: Is rereading notes really that ineffective?
faqs.answer: It is the most common study method and among the least productive, because recognising material feels like knowing it. Retrieval practice, which means closing the book and answering questions before checking, is harder, feels worse and produces far more. Add timed question practice on the weakest paper and a short weekly review of errors already made, and you have three activities that between them do more than any amount of highlighting. The uncomfortable part is that the effective methods feel less pleasant, which is why students avoid them without guidance.

faqs.question: Can you give us past papers to work through at home?
faqs.answer: Official papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the awarding bodies and are not ours to hand out, so we cite and link the official source and work with whatever your child's school has legitimately issued. There is rarely a shortage through the school. The folder is not the valuable part anyway: what converts a paper into marks is sitting it under time, marking it honestly against the scheme, categorising the errors and then working on the category that cost most. Most students do the first step and none of the others.

faqs.question: Why can my child not just mark their own work?
faqs.answer: Because self-marking awards credit for what the student meant rather than for what they wrote, which is precisely the error that lost the mark. A student who knows the answer reads their own partial response as complete. Watching someone else apply the scheme to that answer, and arguing about a borderline point, teaches more about the examination than reading the syllabus does. After a few months most students can mark themselves reasonably, and that independence is one of the better outcomes of this kind of work.

faqs.question: What is an error log and is it worth the trouble?
faqs.answer: It is a running record of what type of mark was lost rather than how many. The categories are few and stable per student: command term misread, method not shown, ran out of time, no application to the context, no supported judgement, arithmetic slip. Once a student can see that four of last week's lost marks were the same category, the next session has an obvious target. It also makes progress visible to a parent, which a general feeling that lessons are going well does not.

faqs.question: Our week crosses the Buraimi border. Does that complicate tutoring?
faqs.answer: It complicates scheduling and nothing academic. The syllabus does not change at a border: a Cambridge candidate sits the same paper and the same mark scheme applies whichever side they slept on. What helps is agreeing a pattern that reflects the real week rather than an idealised one, and building the flexibility in before it is needed. Online delivery suits this situation particularly well, because a lesson continues regardless of which address the student is at. Do check with the school which centre holds the examination entry and which zone timetable applies.

faqs.question: Does the tier of tutor actually change what happens in the hour?
faqs.answer: Substantially. At the budget end, roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour as published by Tutopiya and EdFlik, the hour is usually homework help and content re-explanation. At AED 150 to 200, as Unitors publishes for IGCSE and IB, you generally get content plus topic question practice. At AED 200 to 300 and above, which is where TutorChase's AED 270 and the Bestimate specialist band sit, the hour contains timed questions marked live against the scheme with error categories named. Only the last of those addresses the gap this page describes.

faqs.question: Can a tutor in Hili come to the house instead?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram, which sells no home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. In-home tutoring does exist in Al Ain generally, advertised at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included. The practical difficulty on the northern edge of the city is supply: there are fewer resident subject teachers here than in the capital, and Hili is a drive from the central districts where most of them live. For a specific Higher Level subject the local list is often empty.

faqs.question: Is marking my child's answer and then showing a better version allowed?
faqs.answer: Marking the answer and discussing why credit was or was not given is coaching and entirely proper. Dictating an improved version for the student to copy into assessed work is not, even when it is described as modelling. The line matters most on coursework: a tutor may teach the skills, explain each criterion and question a draft the student wrote, but may not write, draft, complete or edit it to completion. The student carries any malpractice finding, and at Diploma level that can reach the whole diploma.

faqs.question: How quickly should we expect to see the marks move?
faqs.answer: Technique changes faster than content, which is the encouraging part. Command term errors and tariff misreading often improve within four to six weeks of marked weekly practice, because they are habits rather than knowledge. Timing improves once a student has sat three or four properly timed papers. Content gaps take longer and depend on how much is missing. Nobody can promise a grade, and anyone who does is making a claim they cannot keep, but error categories disappearing from a log is evidence you can look at yourself.

al-ain/hili.closingHeading: Send the marked paper, not the report card
al-ain/hili.closingBody: If your child understands the work and the marks do not show it, the fastest route to an answer from Hili is two pieces of actual marked school work with the annotations still on them, plus the subject, level and board. From those we can usually name the error categories in one session and tell you whether weekly marked practice would change the outcome or whether something else is going on. Sometimes the honest answer is that the school has it covered and the study week is the problem, in which case we will say so. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, no home visits are sold in the UAE, and IB Gram holds no regulator approval of any kind.

intro.heading: The Diploma is an arithmetic problem before it is a studying problem
paragraphs: Most Al Ain families arrive at the question of Diploma tutoring with a worry rather than a number. A report says a child is working at a five in two subjects and a four in a third, the school has mentioned predicted grades, and the total on the page does not obviously connect to the university offers being discussed at home. The most useful thing an IB Diploma tutor in Al Ain can do in the first conversation is turn the worry into arithmetic, because the Diploma is unusually transparent once the structure is visible.

Here is the structure. Six subjects, each graded one to seven, give a maximum of forty-two points. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are graded A to E and combine in a published matrix worth up to three further points. The maximum total is forty-five. The Diploma is awarded at twenty-four points or above, provided a set of further conditions is also met, and those conditions are where results are lost by students whose totals look adequate. A candidate can reach twenty-six points and still not be awarded the Diploma.

That matters in Al Ain specifically because the city's Diploma cohorts are small. Option blocks are tight, a subject may run with a handful of candidates, and a teacher may be covering three courses. None of that is a criticism of the schools; it is arithmetic about cohort size. What it means practically is that a student here has less room to switch subjects or levels mid-course than a student in a large Dubai cohort, so decisions made in the first term of Diploma year one carry further.

The timeline is the other half of the picture, and it runs in a direction parents do not expect. A meaningful share of the subject total is settled by internal assessment completed months before the written papers, and the Extended Essay is largely finished before the final year's teaching ends. By the time most families start looking for a tutor, part of the total has already been decided. The hours that move the most points are the ones nobody is asking for yet: the weeks when an internal assessment method is being chosen and when the Extended Essay research question is still negotiable.

What follows is the arithmetic in full. Where the points come from, the published conditions that can withhold a Diploma, how the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix works, how to read a target total backwards into per-paper targets, the bilingual Diploma, what Al Ain's small cohorts do to Higher Level choices, what a two-year plan costs at published market rates, and the retake and remark routes. Confirm every IB regulation with your school's coordinator or on the IB's own site; this page explains structure, it does not replace the official documents. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, and IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE.

al-ain/ib-diploma-tutor.programmesIntro: The Diploma is the page's subject, but two neighbours shape the decisions around it: the Career-related Programme and the courses route within the IB itself, and the International A Level alternative that several Al Ain schools offer instead.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Higher Level courses carry more teaching hours and an extra paper in most subjects. Internal assessment contributes typically twenty to thirty per cent of a subject grade, with the balance from written papers sat in a single session.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain's Diploma cohorts are small, so option blocks are the binding constraint rather than the student's preferences. A combination such as Higher Level Physics with Higher Level Economics may be unavailable locally not because the school objects but because both run in the same block. Ask each Al Ain school for its current block structure before the Year 11 decision, not after.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme courses
programmes.description: Individual Diploma subjects taken for certificates without attempting the full Diploma. A student takes the same courses, sits the same papers and receives the same one-to-seven grades, but does not need to satisfy the award conditions. Universities treat certificates less consistently than the full Diploma, so this route needs checking against specific entry requirements rather than assumed.
programmes.countryNote: This route occasionally rescues an Al Ain student whose school cannot timetable a required subject combination, or for whom a compulsory second language is a genuine barrier. It is worth discussing with the coordinator early rather than in the final year, because moving onto a courses route late can waste a year of teaching.

programmes.name: International A Level
programmes.description: Three or four subjects, no compulsory core, longer and narrower papers. Suits a student with a settled direction and one weak area that the Diploma would not allow them to drop, typically a second language. The Ministry of Education's British-track equivalency route is written around Advanced and Advanced Subsidiary Levels, which some UAE families weigh heavily.
programmes.countryNote: Several Al Ain campuses run A Levels rather than the Diploma, so the choice between the two usually involves changing school in this city. That makes drive time a real variable alongside the academic fit, particularly for households in Zakher or Al Yahar where the run into the centre is already long.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The IB's middle-school framework, assessed against four criteria per subject group rather than by examination. Its habits transfer directly to Diploma internal assessment and the Extended Essay, which is why students arriving from a strong MYP background usually handle Diploma coursework better than those from a purely examination-based system.
programmes.countryNote: Several Al Ain schools run a middle-school programme and then move students onto international GCSE papers rather than continuing to MYP Year 5. A student arriving at the Diploma from Extended IGCSE rather than MYP Year 5 typically needs more support on the first internal assessment and less on examination technique.

al-ain/ib-diploma-tutor.subjectsIntro: Below are the Diploma courses Al Ain families most often ask for, with the component that decides the grade in each. Where a subject's internal assessment carries a large share, that is the component tuition should start with.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The course that accounts for most Al Ain enquiries. Higher Level uses differentiation inside the first term and assumes rapid algebraic manipulation. Marks go on unjustified steps and on calculator work presented without the setup. The mathematical exploration is twenty per cent of the grade and is frequently started too late to be assessed well.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led, with heavier technology use and a gentler algebraic load. It is the right course for a large share of students who are placed in Analysis and Approaches by default, and the honest conversation about which course fits is worth having before the first term rather than in January.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and extended organic mechanisms are where Higher Level separates from Standard. The commonest error is a sign convention rather than a calculation. The scientific investigation is marked on method quality and uncertainty treatment, not on whether the result came out neatly.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics with calculus-adjacent reasoning, plus uncertainty propagation that most students meet for the first time here. Graph gradients quoted without units and conclusions drawn without reference to the uncertainty range are the recurring losses in both papers and internal assessment.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the challenge rather than conceptual difficulty, and command terms decide more marks here than in any other science. Outline, explain, discuss and evaluate carry different tariffs, and writing a discussion for an outline question costs time without earning credit.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen textual analysis, comparative essay work and an individual oral built around a global issue. Students with strong IGCSE First Language grades often underperform in the first paper, because directed writing and unseen analysis of a writer's choices are different skills with different success criteria.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides more marks than prose quality. The internal assessment requires three commentaries on published news articles within strict word limits, and the commonest fault is an article too old or too broad to support the required analysis. Higher Level adds a quantitative paper that rewards practice rather than reading.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study papers reward applying a named tool to the stimulus rather than describing the tool. The Higher Level pre-released case study rewards preparation begun months early, which is among the most efficient uses of tuition hours anywhere in the Diploma.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An assessed essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition of three objects with commentaries. Students lose marks by writing about the topic rather than about how knowledge in that area is produced and justified. It feeds the core points, so an E here is a condition failure rather than a low score.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A four-thousand-word independent research essay in a chosen subject with a supervisor. The research question decides the achievable grade more than the writing does, which is why the most valuable supervision happens before any drafting. As with Theory of Knowledge, an E is a condition failure.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the international curriculum for the groups the regulator specifies, and separately examinable at Diploma level. Al Ain students sometimes move between first-language and acquisition streams between IGCSE and the Diploma, and the two are assessed against entirely different criteria.

al-ain/ib-diploma-tutor.regionsIntro: Al Ain is spread out, and for Diploma students the practical slot is late, because coursework work benefits from an unbroken block after the school run and after homework has been attempted.

regions.name: Al Jimi
regions.note: Central and close to several campuses, with short school runs. A half past four start is realistic, which allows a second slot for a sibling on the same evening.

regions.name: Asharej
regions.note: Near United Arab Emirates University, so households often include academic staff with a clear view of what a local university entry profile actually asks for. Evening slots compete with campus commitments.

regions.name: Falaj Hazza
regions.note: South-west, with campuses running both the Diploma and A Levels within a short drive, so the Year 11 decision between qualifications is genuinely live in these households.

regions.name: Zakher
regions.note: Southern villa belt with long runs into the centre. A seven o'clock video slot works here where a visiting arrangement would collapse on the first week of heavy traffic.

regions.name: Al Mutaredh
regions.note: Older central district by the Al Ain Oasis. Families here frequently have a Diploma student at one campus and a younger child on IGCSE papers at another.

regions.name: Al Muwaiji
regions.note: Western and heavily Emirati, with high demand for Arabic alongside Diploma subjects. Two separate language streams in one household is common here.

regions.name: Al Towayya
regions.note: Near the hospital campus, where parental shift rotas shape the week. A fixed weekly online slot survives a rota change; a visiting arrangement does not.

regions.name: Hili
regions.note: Northern Al Ain near the Buraimi crossing, with some households crossing the border daily. An earlier fixed slot proves more reliable than a late one here.

al-ain/ib-diploma-tutor.modesIntro: Diploma support takes three shapes over two years, and the useful one changes as the course progresses. All three are delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time.

modes.title: Weekly subject support across two years
modes.description: A fixed slot in one or two subjects, usually the Higher Level courses carrying the most risk, running alongside the school's scheme of work rather than ahead of it. The focus alternates between content and technique, and shifts decisively towards past papers from the start of the final two terms. Most Al Ain families start with one subject and add a second only if evidence justifies it.

A written note after each session listing what was covered and set
Reviewed against marked school assessments, not on a monthly cycle

modes.title: Internal assessment and core supervision blocks
modes.description: Scheduled feedback points on the subject internal assessments, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, timed to the school's own internal deadlines rather than to ours. The tutor reads the student's own drafts, questions the method, and names the criterion the work is being marked against. These are the hours that move the most points per hour spent.
bullets: Research question and method questioned before any drafting begins
Feedback mapped to the published criteria, criterion by criterion
Every submitted word remains the student's own work

modes.title: Final-term paper intensive
modes.description: A block in the last ten to twelve weeks built entirely around timed past papers, worked in the order the student will sit them and marked against official mark schemes. Targets are set per paper rather than as one overall grade, because a Higher Level grade is a weighted sum of components and the components respond to different work.

sections.heading: Where the forty-five points actually come from
paragraphs: Six subjects, each graded one to seven, give forty-two points. Three subjects are taken at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, and both levels are graded on the same one-to-seven scale, so a seven at Standard Level is worth exactly as many points as a seven at Higher Level. That single fact changes a lot of planning conversations in Al Ain, because families frequently assume Higher Level grades count for more. They do not count for more in the total; they count differently in the award conditions and in university offers.

The remaining three points come from the core. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are each graded A to E, and the pair combines through a published matrix that awards nought to three points. The matrix is not symmetrical and it is not intuitive: two B grades award fewer points than an A paired with a B, and certain combinations award nothing at all while still satisfying the conditions. Those three points are frequently treated as a rounding error by students and they are the difference between a thirty-four and a thirty-seven offer.

Each subject grade is itself a weighted sum. Most Diploma subjects comprise two or three written papers plus an internal assessment worth roughly twenty to thirty per cent. The practical implication is that no subject grade is a single thing to be improved; it is three or four components that respond to different work. A student losing marks on Paper 1 multiple choice and a student losing marks on the internal assessment have nothing in common except the grade on the report.
The table lays out one worked profile, so the relationship between subject grades, core points and total is visible in a single place. The numbers are an illustration, not a prediction.

sections.heading: The conditions that can withhold a Diploma at twenty-six points
paragraphs: Twenty-four points is the floor for the Diploma, and it is a necessary condition rather than a sufficient one. The IB publishes a set of additional requirements that must all be satisfied, and a candidate who misses any one of them is not awarded the Diploma regardless of the total. This is the part of the system that produces the worst surprises in July, and it is almost never explained to parents at the start of the course.

The requirements concern the distribution of grades rather than their sum. There are minimum point totals from the Higher Level subjects and from the Standard Level subjects taken together. There are limits on how many low grades a candidate may hold, and a single grade one in any subject is disqualifying on its own. The Creativity, Activity, Service requirements must be completed. Neither Theory of Knowledge nor the Extended Essay may be graded E. And any finding of academic misconduct removes the award independently of everything else.

What this means for tutoring priorities is counter-intuitive but important. For a student in the middle of the range, the hour spent lifting a weak Standard Level subject from a three to a four can matter more than the hour spent lifting a strong subject from a six to a seven, because the first removes a condition risk while the second only adds one point. An Al Ain family planning a two-year budget should know which of the two situations their child is in, and the answer is readable from the report.

sections.heading: The core matrix, and why three points are worth more than they look
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are each graded A to E, and the pair is converted into nought to three points through a published matrix. Students treat the core as the part of the Diploma that does not count, because it has no subject grade attached, and that reading costs Al Ain candidates points every session. Three points is the gap between many conditional offers. It is also, hour for hour, the cheapest part of the Diploma to improve, because almost nobody competes for those marks seriously.

The Extended Essay is the more controllable of the two. Its achievable grade is decided largely by the research question, which is set long before any writing happens. A question too broad to answer in four thousand words, or one whose evidence cannot be obtained from Al Ain, caps the grade before the student has written a sentence. Supervision at the question stage, questioning scope and feasibility, is worth more than any amount of feedback on a finished draft. This is the clearest case in the whole Diploma of effort placed in the wrong month.

Theory of Knowledge is harder to coach and still responsive. The essay is written on a prescribed title and the failure mode is consistent: students write about the subject matter rather than about how knowledge in that area is produced, justified and contested. The exhibition requires three objects with commentaries connecting them to a prompt, and the commonest loss is an object chosen for interest rather than for the specific knowledge question it illuminates.

The matrix below is the published shape of the conversion. Treat it as an illustration of structure and confirm the version applying to your child's session with the coordinator, since the core's assessment model has been revised more than once.

sections.heading: Reading a target total backwards into per-paper targets
paragraphs: A target of thirty-eight points is not actionable. Nobody studies for thirty-eight. What is actionable is a target per subject, then per component within the subject, then a statement of which specific question types that component rewards. Working backwards in that way is the main thing a Diploma tutor should do in the first fortnight, and it is why the first session should involve more reading of the student's marked work than teaching.

The arithmetic is straightforward once the components are visible. If Chemistry at Higher Level comprises three papers and an internal assessment worth around twenty per cent, then a student sitting at a five with a weak internal assessment and solid papers has a different route to a six than a student with a strong internal assessment and a weak Paper 2. The first needs supervision on method and uncertainty; the second needs timed extended-response practice. A generic request for Chemistry tutoring produces the wrong one about half the time.

The second half of working backwards is the calendar. Internal assessments are completed long before the papers, the Extended Essay earlier still, and the school sets internal deadlines ahead of the IB's upload dates. Counting backwards from the examination session therefore produces a sequence in which the coursework work happens first and the paper work last, which is the opposite of how most families schedule tuition. They start with subject revision in year two and discover the coursework marks were settled in year one.

sections.heading: Al Ain's option blocks, and what a small cohort really costs
paragraphs: Al Ain is 130 kilometres inland from the capital and its private-school set is considerably smaller than Abu Dhabi island's. For the Diploma, that translates into three concrete constraints. Option blocks are tight, so desirable subject combinations collide. Some subjects run with very small candidate numbers, which means a teacher may cover three courses and the depth of subject-specific support available inside the school is thinner. And the less common languages and Higher Level sciences are the first things to be unavailable.

None of that is a reflection on teaching quality, and it is not solved by changing school, because the next school has a similarly small cohort. What it does mean is that the Year 11 decision should include a specific question that few families think to ask: which subjects ran at Higher Level in the last session, and with how many candidates. A school that ran Higher Level Physics with four candidates last year may not run it at all this year, and a student who built a university plan around it discovers that in September.

The second practical consequence is that a student who finds themselves in the wrong mathematics course has less room to move than a Dubai student would. Switching from Analysis and Approaches to Applications and Interpretation partway through year one depends on there being a class to move into at a compatible time. Where there is not, the student continues in a course that does not fit, and that is a predictable source of grade-one and grade-two risk. The answer is to make the course decision properly before year one rather than to rely on being able to correct it.

Where the school cannot timetable a subject at all, two routes exist and both are worth raising with the coordinator early: taking the subject as a Diploma Programme course for a certificate alongside a reduced Diploma, or self-teaching with supervision, which is demanding and should not be entered into casually in a subject with an internal assessment component.

sections.heading: What a two-year Diploma plan costs at published market rates
paragraphs: Published UAE tutoring rates vary by a factor of ten and most pages competing for this search print no AED figure at all. The bands below come from providers' own published pricing and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. They describe the market, not IB Gram's price list, and they are here so an Al Ain quote can be judged against something checkable.

Budget online tutoring from university students is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150 to 300, where Unitors publishes IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. In-home one-to-one with travel runs roughly AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at 200 to 500. IB and IGCSE specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named tutoring reaches AED 650, as BartyED publishes. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year support. Monthly packages in the market include AED 799 for eight online sessions.

Two years is where the arithmetic becomes real. A single weekly hour in one subject across both Diploma years, at the mid-market monthly estimate, is a materially different commitment from a ten-week intensive before the papers, and the two buy different things. The pattern that tends to produce the most points per dirham is uneven rather than steady: coursework supervision blocks in year one and early year two, where a small number of hours can move two or three points, then a concentrated paper intensive in the final term. A flat weekly hour for twenty-four months, with no coursework focus, is the commonest way Al Ain families spend more and gain less.

For context on household education spending, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under an economic incentives package. That is a Dubai measure and does not apply to Al Ain fees, but it is a useful reminder that school fees dominate the household education budget and tuition is the smaller, controllable line. IB Gram publishes no rate card here; the next step is a trial lesson at no charge once a tutor has been matched, then a quote against the actual course and level.

sections.heading: Remarks, retakes and the November route
paragraphs: Results arriving below expectation open three distinct routes, and they operate on different clocks. The first is a remark, properly called an enquiry upon results, requested through the school within a deadline set by the IB. It is a re-evaluation of marking rather than a second attempt, and it is most worth requesting where a component mark sits just below a boundary and is inconsistent with the student's other components in that subject. Your coordinator advises on whether a case exists; the deadline is short.

The second is a retake of individual subjects in a later session. The UAE sits the May session, and a November session also exists, so a candidate may retake in a session after the original attempt rather than waiting a full year. Retaking changes the planning question entirely: the student is no longer being taught a course, they are being prepared for specific components, often while already at university or on a gap year. Internal assessment marks usually carry forward, which is worth confirming with the coordinator, because it means the retake work is paper work.

The third route is to proceed without the full Diploma using subject certificates, where the university offer permits it. Universities treat certificates less consistently than the full Diploma, so this is a question for the admissions office concerned rather than for a school or a tutoring page. Al Ain families with local university plans are better served asking the institution directly, because published requirements change between cycles.

No specific IB session or results date appears on this page. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, which means any date published on a tutoring page is secondhand, and a parent planning travel or a retake entry around a date that turns out to be wrong has a real problem. Check ibo.org or your school's coordinator, and treat both as more reliable than any aggregated calendar.
bullets: Enquiry upon results is a marking review, not a second attempt, and the deadline is short

sections.heading: Delivery, coursework limits and what is not claimed
paragraphs: Lessons for UAE families are delivered one-to-one over live video, at Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service available only in India. For Diploma work the format earns its place on the merits: a student's own marked Paper 2 script, the subject guide and the official mark scheme can all be on a shared screen at once, and the specialist on the other end may be the only person available anywhere who teaches that exact Higher Level option. In a city with small cohorts, that is the practical difference rather than a convenience argument.

Where Al Ain has a UAE-based specialist for the course, that is the first match offered, because shared school context and time zone are genuinely useful. Where no UAE-based specialist is free at the level needed, which happens most often in Higher Level sciences, Higher Level Computer Science and the less common languages, the match comes from the wider tutor pool teaching at Gulf Standard Time, and that is said before any lesson is booked. No competing page in this market discloses a coverage limit, which is not the same as not having one.

The line on coursework is firm and worth stating plainly, because this search returns providers who cross it. Internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay must be the student's own work. A tutor may teach the underlying content, question a method, read a draft the student wrote and point at the criterion it is being marked against, and help plan backwards from the school's deadlines. A tutor may not supply text, structure written for the student, or a finished piece. Academic misconduct removes the Diploma award independently of every point total on this page, which makes this the single most expensive corner a family could cut.

Finally, what is not claimed. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International or Pearson, and there is no IB Gram office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE. No grade, score or university place is promised by anyone here, no statistic appears without a named source, and no IB subject guide, past paper or mark scheme is distributed as a download. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the Ministry's own service, with fines and penalties under the applicable laws for anyone tutoring without one.

Coverage limits are stated before booking, never after payment

process.title: Send the subject list with levels, and one marked script
process.description: Six subjects with Higher and Standard Level marked, plus one recent marked paper or internal assessment draft. The subject list shows where condition risk sits; the script shows which component is losing marks. Together they make the first conversation diagnostic rather than exploratory.

process.title: Work out the condition position before the point target
process.description: Check the Higher Level and Standard Level minimums and the low-grade limits against current working grades. A student at condition risk and a student chasing a higher offer need opposite priorities, and the report usually makes clear which one you are dealing with.

process.title: Fix the coursework calendar first
process.description: Map the internal assessment deadlines, the Extended Essay checkpoints and the Theory of Knowledge dates from the school's own calendar, counted backwards. Those hours move the most points and they expire. Paper preparation can be scheduled around them; the reverse does not work.

process.title: Meet the matched tutor for a trial lesson at no charge
process.description: One introductory session once a tutor is matched to the named course and level, with nothing charged and no card needed to book it. The signal to watch for is whether the tutor reads the marked script and names a component, or begins teaching content without establishing where the marks went.

process.title: Review at assessment points, not on a calendar
process.description: Review after each marked school assessment, after the mock window and after each internal assessment feedback round. Reviewing monthly means reviewing at moments when nothing has been assessed, which produces impressions rather than evidence and keeps a wrong diagnosis alive for longer.

whyPoints.title: The arithmetic before the advice
whyPoints.description: Points, conditions and component weightings come first, because they determine which hour is worth buying. A target total with no per-component breakdown behind it produces effort in the wrong places and a plan nobody can check.

whyPoints.title: Condition risk treated as the priority it is
whyPoints.description: A single grade one, a missed Higher Level minimum or an E in the core withholds the Diploma whatever the total. Lifting the lowest grade usually matters more than lifting the highest, and that is the opposite of how most tuition is sold.

whyPoints.title: Coursework hours placed where they count
whyPoints.description: Internal assessment and the Extended Essay are settled long before the papers, and the research question decides more than the drafting does. Supervision at the question stage is the highest-return work available in the whole Diploma.

whyPoints.title: Al Ain's cohort size taken seriously
whyPoints.description: Tight option blocks, subjects running with a handful of candidates and thinner in-school subject depth are facts about a smaller city. They change what a student can correct mid-course, which is why decisions before year one carry more weight here.

whyPoints.title: Rates with sources attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED band is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it and kept separate from anything IB Gram charges. Three of the six pages competing in this market publish no price at all and two quote in a currency UAE families do not use.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Academic misconduct removes the award independently of any point total, so nothing a tutor contributes ever appears in a submitted piece. Teaching, questioning and criterion feedback on the student's own drafts is the whole of what is offered.

faqs.question: Where do the 45 Diploma points actually come from?
faqs.answer: Forty-two from six subjects, each graded one to seven, and up to three from the core. Three subjects are taken at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, and both are graded on the same scale, so a seven at Standard Level is worth the same points as a seven at Higher Level. The core points come from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, each graded A to E, combined through a published matrix. Each subject grade is itself a weighted sum of two or three papers plus an internal assessment worth roughly twenty to thirty per cent.

faqs.question: What are the conditions that stop a Diploma being awarded at all?
faqs.answer: Twenty-four points is the floor, and several further requirements must all be met: minimum point totals from the Higher Level and Standard Level subjects, caps on the number of low grades, no grade one in any subject, completion of the Creativity, Activity, Service requirements, no E grade in Theory of Knowledge or the Extended Essay, and no finding of academic misconduct. A candidate can reach twenty-six points and still not be awarded the Diploma. Confirm the exact current wording with your school's coordinator, who holds the authoritative version for your child's session.

faqs.question: How are the three core points awarded for the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: Both are graded A to E and the pair converts to nought to three points through a published matrix. The matrix is not symmetrical: an A paired with a B awards more than two Bs, and some combinations award nothing while still satisfying the award conditions. An E in either is a condition failure regardless of the points. Students treat the core as the part that does not count, which is why those three points are available cheaply to anyone who takes the Extended Essay research question seriously a year in advance.

faqs.question: How many of the 45 points are decided before the written papers?
faqs.answer: A substantial share. Internal assessment carries roughly twenty to thirty per cent of most subject grades, and those pieces are completed and submitted months before the examination session. The Extended Essay is usually finished before the final year's teaching ends, and Theory of Knowledge earlier still. Added together, a meaningful part of the total is settled before the first paper is opened, which is why families who start tutoring in the final term find that some of the available points have already been allocated.

faqs.question: What does one grade boundary actually move in the Diploma total?
faqs.answer: One point, which sounds trivial and frequently is not. A single point moves a thirty-four to a thirty-five, and conditional offers are routinely set at specific totals. More importantly, where the boundary crossed is in a weak subject, it can also remove a condition risk, which is worth far more than a point. The practical move is to find which component in which subject sits closest to a boundary and work on that one, rather than spreading effort evenly across six subjects.

faqs.question: My child is sitting on 31 points - what is a realistic target?
faqs.answer: Thirty-four or thirty-five within a year is a reasonable working assumption if the gap is diagnosable, and the diagnosis matters more than the ambition. Two points from the core, if currently at one, are usually the cheapest. One grade in a subject where a single component is clearly behind is the next cheapest. A target that requires three subjects to rise at once in the final term is not a plan. No tutor can promise a particular total, and anyone offering one is selling something other than teaching.

faqs.question: Which Higher Level subjects are hardest to timetable in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Higher Level sciences beyond the most popular one, Higher Level Computer Science, and the less common languages. The cause is cohort size rather than school policy: a subject attracting four candidates may not run at all, and two desirable Higher Level courses frequently sit in the same option block. Ask each Al Ain school which Higher Level subjects ran in the last session and with how many candidates, in writing, before the Year 11 decision. A university plan built on a subject that does not run is a serious problem to discover in September.

faqs.question: Do UAE universities look at the Diploma total or the Higher Level grades?
faqs.answer: Usually both, with subject-specific requirements attached, and the detail varies by institution and by programme. A medical or engineering pathway typically specifies Higher Level subjects and minimum grades within them as well as a total. Al Ain families have a major national university inside the city and several other institutions nearby, and each publishes its own requirements, which are revised between cycles. Ask the admissions office directly rather than relying on a school summary or a tutoring page, including on how subject certificates are treated.

faqs.question: How many Diploma subjects should a student get tutoring in at once?
faqs.answer: One or two, in almost every case. Three concurrent subjects usually means three hours a week on top of a Diploma workload that already includes coursework, and the result is less independent study rather than more support. The exception is a short, intense block in the final term where the work is timed papers rather than new content. Start with the subject carrying the most condition risk, verify from the next marked assessment that it has moved, and add a second only on that evidence.

faqs.question: What does Diploma tutoring cost in Al Ain for a two-year plan?
faqs.answer: Judge any quote against published market bands. Unitors publishes IB tutoring from AED 200 an hour and IGCSE from AED 150; TutorChase publishes AED 270; Bestimate's rate table puts specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with monthly estimates of AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year support at a weekly hour. Across two years the pattern matters more than the rate. Coursework supervision blocks plus a final-term paper intensive usually buys more points than a flat weekly hour sustained for twenty-four months.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start Diploma tutoring in the second year?
faqs.answer: Not too late to gain points, but the available points have changed. By the second year much of the internal assessment is submitted or near submission, and the Extended Essay may be finished, so the hours remaining are paper hours. That is still worth doing and can move two to four points across the subjects where timing and command terms are the losses. What cannot be recovered late is coursework quality, which is the honest reason to start supervision in year one rather than the second.

faqs.question: Can a November retake repair a low Diploma total?
faqs.answer: It can repair individual subject grades. The UAE sits the May session and a November session also exists, so a candidate can retake specific subjects in a later session rather than waiting a full year. Internal assessment marks usually carry forward, which should be confirmed with your coordinator, and that makes retake preparation almost entirely paper preparation. Before entering a retake, ask whether a remark is the better route: an enquiry upon results reviews the original marking and the deadline for requesting it is short.

faqs.question: What is a bilingual Diploma and is it worth aiming for in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: A bilingual Diploma is awarded where a candidate's subject combination meets the IB's published language conditions, broadly involving two languages studied as Language A or a Language A plus a subject from another group taught in a second language. In Al Ain, where many students have strong Arabic alongside English, it is more achievable than families realise and it signals genuine academic bilingualism to admissions offices. Whether it is worth engineering a subject choice around depends on the universities being targeted. Ask your coordinator which combinations at your school would satisfy the conditions.

faqs.question: What may a Diploma tutor do with coursework, and what is off limits?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the content, question a method or a research question, read a draft the student has written and name the criterion it is being marked against, explain what a criterion descriptor requires, and help schedule work backwards from the school's deadlines. A tutor may not supply text, write structure for the student, or hand over a finished piece. Academic misconduct removes the Diploma award regardless of the point total, so this is the most expensive possible shortcut. Every submitted word stays the student's own.

faqs.question: Is Theory of Knowledge support available alongside the six Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is frequently the most efficient hour in a plan, because almost nobody competes seriously for core marks. The work is structural rather than content-based: showing a student how to write about how knowledge in an area is produced and justified, rather than about the area itself, and helping choose exhibition objects that genuinely illuminate a prompt. The essay must be the student's own writing throughout. An E in Theory of Knowledge is a condition failure, so this is also risk management, not only point-chasing.

al-ain/ib-diploma-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the conditions, then the components
al-ain/ib-diploma-tutor.closingBody: Before any tutoring decision, do two pieces of arithmetic. Check the award conditions against your child's current working grades, because a condition risk outranks a point target every time. Then break the weakest subject into its components and find out which one is actually losing the marks, since a grade is never a single thing to improve. Send us the subject list with levels, one marked script and the school's coursework deadlines, and we will start there. Lessons are one-to-one over live video at Gulf Standard Time; home visits are an India-only service and are not offered anywhere in the UAE. Confirm every IB regulation with your school's coordinator, who holds the version that applies to your child's session.

al-ain/ib-dp-chemistry-hl-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed here teach Diploma Programme Chemistry at Higher Level for students in Al Ain and the wider Emirate of Abu Dhabi. Matching happens against a named unit and a named deadline, so the trial lesson starts on the mechanism or the calculation that is actually blocking progress.

intro.heading: Two walls, and how far away the next one is
paragraphs: Higher Level Chemistry does not get steadily harder. It has two distinct walls, and knowing which one a student has hit decides everything about the plan. The first is organic mechanism work in Reactivity 3, where a course that rewarded careful memorisation suddenly rewards reasoning about electron movement. The second is the mathematics folded into energetics, kinetics and equilibrium, where a student who is comfortable with chemistry discovers that the limiting factor is logarithms, rearrangement and the confident handling of negative signs.

A parent in Al Ain searching for an IB DP Chemistry HL tutor is usually describing a symptom from one of those two walls without knowing which. The report says effort is good and results are inconsistent. Mock marks swing between papers. The student says they understand the lesson and cannot do the homework. Those are the same three sentences for both walls, which is why the first useful hour of tutoring is diagnostic rather than instructional, and why a trial lesson spent watching a student attempt two past-paper questions aloud is worth more than a syllabus overview.

The structural facts of the course are fixed and worth knowing early. Higher Level Chemistry runs to 240 guided teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level. The content is organised into two halves, Structure and Reactivity, each carrying three units. Assessment is two written papers plus one scientific investigation marked out of 24 and worth a fifth of the grade. A data booklet is supplied in the examination, which changes what is worth committing to memory and what is worth practising until it is automatic.

Al Ain adds a supply constraint rather than a syllabus one. The city sits in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi and its private schools are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. The inland private-school set is considerably smaller than the capital's, and Higher Level sciences are where a smaller set shows: combined HL and SL teaching groups, a single Chemistry specialist carrying both, and HL-only material delivered in compressed blocks late in DP2.

Against that, what a tutor can honestly offer is specialisation and scheduling, not proximity. Teaching here is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not run in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we provide only in India. For a Chemistry HL student in Al Ain the practical effect is that the tutor is chosen for having taught the current guide and marked investigations against the current criteria, rather than for living within a twenty-minute drive of Al Khabisi.

The rest of this page is arranged around the two walls. It sets out how the six units are built and where the Higher Level extensions sit inside them, separates what the examination hands a student from what they still have to know, explains how the investigation marks are won at the design stage rather than in the writing, and gives the AED market bands with their sources named. The regulatory and equivalency material sits near the end, because those are decisions a family takes once while the teaching plan changes every fortnight.

al-ain/ib-dp-chemistry-hl-tutor.programmesIntro: Four starting points bring an Al Ain family to Chemistry HL tutoring. Each has a different realistic window, and the notes name what usually has to be fixed first at each one.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Chemistry, Higher Level
programmes.ageRange: Ages 16-19 · DP1 and DP2 · 240 guided hours
programmes.description: The full Structure and Reactivity content with the Higher Level extensions, two written papers and the scientific investigation. The Higher Level additions are not an extra unit at the end; they are extensions inside existing sub-topics, including Born-Haber cycles, Gibbs free energy, rate equations and order of reaction, buffers and pH curves, electrochemical cells, and the substitution and addition mechanisms.
programmes.countryNote: In an Al Ain school a Higher Level Chemistry set of six or eight students is normal, and it is frequently taught in the same room as the Standard Level set. The HL-only extensions are the part that suffers: they get compressed into the last two terms, and a student who misses a fortnight through travel or illness has no second pass at Reactivity 3.4 at school.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Chemistry, Standard Level
programmes.ageRange: Ages 16-19 · DP1 and DP2 · 150 guided hours
programmes.description: The same six units without the Higher Level extensions, shorter papers, and the same investigation worth 20%. Standard Level students who later need Higher Level for a medicine, pharmacy or chemical engineering application face a real catch-up, because the extensions are threaded through every unit rather than sitting in one block that can be bolted on.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain students sometimes begin at Standard Level because an HL set did not run in their year group, then find a university course expects Higher Level. Where the school can accommodate a switch, the first term of DP1 is the only comfortable window. We will say when a switch has stopped being realistic rather than sell sessions against it.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences, Years 4 and 5
programmes.description: MYP Sciences is assessed on four criteria and rewards investigation design and scientific communication. Diploma Chemistry rewards quantitative fluency: moles, concentration, limiting reagents, percentage yield and the algebra behind equilibrium and rate. The gap between the two is a mathematics gap far more often than a chemistry gap.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain students arriving into DP1 from an MYP set, a British Year 11 or a CBSE Class 10 cross the same gap. The pre-Diploma summer is the cheapest time to close it, and six to eight sessions on mole calculations, unit conversion, logarithms and rearrangement removes most of the first-term shock.

programmes.name: Chemistry Extended Essay and investigation supervision
programmes.description: A Chemistry Extended Essay needs a research question that can be answered with school laboratory access and a reagent list a school will actually approve. Supervision means process coaching: testing feasibility, checking the chemistry is measurable, questioning the uncertainty treatment, and giving criterion-referenced feedback on drafts the student has written.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain schools vary widely in what laboratory time and reagent access a Diploma student can get outside lessons, and that is the constraint that kills more Chemistry Extended Essay questions than anything else. Checking it in week one, before a question is fixed, is the single most useful thing an outside tutor can do.

al-ain/ib-dp-chemistry-hl-tutor.subjectsIntro: The grid below treats the Chemistry Higher Level course as a set of tutoring targets rather than a contents page. Each entry names what the unit assesses and the specific way Al Ain Higher Level students tend to lose marks on it.

subjects.name: Structure 1: Models of the particulate nature of matter
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with extensions at HL
subjects.description: The nuclear atom, electron configurations, the mole and ideal gases. Marks go missing on mole calculations where the limiting reagent is never identified, on gas law questions answered in the wrong units, and at Higher Level on ionisation energy trends explained by assertion rather than by shielding and nuclear charge.

subjects.name: Structure 2: Models of bonding and structure
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with formal charge and resonance at HL
subjects.description: Ionic, covalent and metallic models and the move from models to materials. Higher Level adds formal charge, resonance and the sigma and pi description of bonding. Students who learned shapes as a list rather than from electron-domain reasoning lose marks as soon as a question gives an unfamiliar species.

subjects.name: Structure 3: Classification of matter
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with transition metals at HL
subjects.description: Periodic trends and the classification of organic compounds by functional group. Higher Level extends into the d-block, coloured complexes and the behaviour of transition metals. This unit is the bridge into organic chemistry, and a student weak on functional group recognition carries that weakness straight into Reactivity 3.

subjects.name: Reactivity 1: What drives chemical reactions
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with Born-Haber and Gibbs at HL
subjects.description: Enthalpy changes, energy cycles, fuels, entropy and spontaneity. Higher Level adds Born-Haber cycles and Gibbs free energy. Almost every lost mark here is a sign error or a direction error rather than a chemistry error, which makes it unusually responsive to short, targeted tutoring.

subjects.name: Reactivity 2: How much, how fast, how far
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with rate equations and Kc work at HL
subjects.description: Amount of chemical change, rate, and extent of reaction. Higher Level adds rate equations, order of reaction, the Arrhenius relationship and quantitative equilibrium work. This is the unit where the mathematics wall appears most clearly: the chemistry is understood and the logarithms are not.

subjects.name: Reactivity 3: What are the mechanisms of chemical change
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with full mechanism work at HL
subjects.description: Proton transfer, electron transfer, electron sharing and electron-pair sharing reactions. Higher Level covers pH curves and buffers, electrochemical cells and electrolysis, and the substitution, addition and organic redox mechanisms. The single largest block of HL-only marks in the course sits here.

subjects.name: The data booklet as a skill
subjects.description: The booklet supplies constants, bond enthalpies, electrode potentials, characteristic infrared absorptions, proton nuclear magnetic resonance shifts and much else. Students who have never practised finding a value under time pressure lose marks to navigation rather than to chemistry, and this is trainable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Paper 1B data analysis in Chemistry
subjects.description: The data-based section asks students to process unfamiliar experimental results: read a titration curve, extract a rate from a graph, assess uncertainty, and judge whether the evidence supports a claim. It rewards technique over recall and is routinely left untrained until the last month.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation in Chemistry
subjects.levels: SL and HL, 20% of the final mark
subjects.description: One report of up to 3,000 words marked out of 24. Chemistry investigations fail more often on data sufficiency than on ambition: a reaction that gives three usable data points cannot carry the Data analysis criterion, however interesting the question behind it was.

subjects.name: Chemistry Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent investigation with its own criteria and its own supervision rules. Laboratory access and reagent approval decide feasibility more than the chemistry does, and both need checking in the first fortnight while the research question can still change.

sections.heading: Which of the two walls has your child hit?
paragraphs: An IB DP Chemistry HL tutor in Al Ain is almost always being hired to deal with one of two failures, and they need opposite treatments. The mechanism wall appears when the course moves from describing reactions to explaining them. A student who succeeded by learning reaction lists finds that Higher Level questions present unfamiliar molecules and expect the mechanism to be reasoned from electron density. No amount of additional memorising fixes this, which is why the student's effort rises and the marks do not.

The mathematics wall appears in Reactivity 1 and Reactivity 2. Gibbs free energy, Born-Haber cycles, rate equations and equilibrium constants all demand confident rearrangement, logarithms and sign discipline. The chemistry in these questions is often simple; the algebra is not, and a student who hesitates over rearranging an equation under examination pressure will lose the marks even though they understand the chemistry perfectly when it is spoken aloud.

Telling the two apart takes one diagnostic hour. Give the student an unfamiliar organic question and a Gibbs calculation, and watch which one they can start. If the mechanism stalls at the first arrow, the work is electron-density reasoning and functional group fluency. If the calculation stalls at the rearrangement, the work is mathematical and can be fixed faster than most parents expect. A student who stalls on both needs the mathematics first, because the energetics work is a prerequisite for making sense of why reactions go at all.
bullets: Mechanism wall: effort rises, marks stay flat, unfamiliar molecules cause a freeze
Mathematics wall: the chemistry is explained correctly aloud and lost on paper
Both walls present identically in a school report, which is why diagnosis comes first
If both are present, fix the mathematics first; energetics underpins the rest

sections.heading: Structure and Reactivity: how the current guide is built and where the HL extensions sit
paragraphs: The current IB Chemistry guide replaced the older core-and-options structure with six units split across two halves. Structure covers the particulate nature of matter, models of bonding, and the classification of matter. Reactivity covers what drives chemical reactions, how much and how fast and how far they go, and the mechanisms by which they happen. The Higher Level course is not a seventh unit; it is a set of extensions threaded through all six, which is exactly why a late switch into Higher Level is harder than it sounds.

The table below maps the units to their Higher Level extensions and to the planning question a parent actually has: how much tutoring time does this extension usually take for a student already secure on the Standard Level material underneath it. Those hour estimates are our own teaching experience in one-to-one sessions rather than a published IB figure, and a student weak on the prerequisites will need more.

Reading across the table shows why Reactivity 3 dominates Higher Level Chemistry tutoring in Al Ain. It holds pH curves and buffers, electrochemical cells and electrolysis, and the full set of organic mechanisms, and it is taught last. A student who arrives at it with shaky functional group recognition from Structure 3 is trying to learn mechanism reasoning and the vocabulary it operates on at the same time, in the term when the investigation deadline also lands.

There is one more consequence worth drawing out for a small Al Ain Higher Level set. Because the extensions are threaded rather than blocked, a teacher carrying both levels in one room often delivers the Higher Level material as additional work set alongside the shared lesson. That is a reasonable solution to an impossible timetable, and it means the Higher Level content is the part most dependent on a student working independently. One-to-one sessions tend to earn their place by holding that independent portion open rather than by repeating the shared lesson.

sections.heading: The data booklet: what the examination gives you and what it does not
paragraphs: A Chemistry student sits both written papers with a data booklet in front of them, and almost nobody treats that as a skill to practise. It changes the whole economics of revision. Bond enthalpies, standard electrode potentials, characteristic infrared absorption ranges, proton nuclear magnetic resonance chemical shifts, constants and the periodic table are supplied. Memorising them is wasted effort. Knowing where each one sits, and finding it in seconds while a clock runs, is not wasted effort at all.

What the booklet does not supply is the reasoning. It gives an electrode potential but not the decision about which half-cell is oxidised. It gives an infrared range but not the interpretation that a broad absorption around that range indicates a hydroxyl group in an alcohol rather than a carboxylic acid. It gives constants but not the rearrangement that puts them to use. The booklet is a reference, and the marks sit entirely in the chemistry a student does after looking something up.

The practical implication for a tutoring plan in the final months is direct. Sessions spent reciting values are sessions wasted. Sessions spent on timed navigation, on the definitions and conventions that are not supplied, and on the interpretation steps the booklet cannot do for the student, are the ones that convert into marks. The table below is the division a student should be able to draw themselves by the spring of DP2.

A simple exercise makes the point faster than any explanation. Hand a student a past-paper structure determination question with the booklet closed and time how long it takes to answer. Hand them a second one with the booklet open and no time limit. If the second answer is right and the first is wrong, the gap is navigation and nothing else. If both are wrong in the same way, the gap is interpretation, which takes longer and needs teaching rather than drilling.

sections.heading: How Higher Level Chemistry is assessed, and what a school report is not telling you
paragraphs: Higher Level Chemistry is assessed through two written papers and one internal investigation. Paper 1 carries 36% of the grade and splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section. Paper 2 carries 44% and holds the structured and extended-response questions. The scientific investigation carries 20%. A school report describing Chemistry as satisfactory is usually describing performance on Paper 2 style questions, because that is what classroom tests look like. The data-analysis section and the investigation together account for a substantial share of the grade and are often untested at school until late.

That matters for how hours are allocated. The investigation is 20% of the final grade, marked out of 24 by the school and moderated by the IB, and the student controls the conditions entirely. Moving an investigation from 13 to 19 marks is both achievable and permanent. Moving a Paper 2 grade by the same amount in the same number of weeks is considerably harder, because it depends on two years of accumulated fluency rather than on one piece of work done carefully.

The second asymmetry is Paper 1B. Data analysis in Chemistry means reading titration curves, extracting rates from concentration-time graphs, handling uncertainty and judging whether evidence supports a claim. It is a small, trainable skill set. Four or five sessions on it move more marks than the same hours spent on general content review, and almost no school revision programme separates it out, because school revision is organised by unit and the examination is not.
