sections.heading: Choosing a Chemistry investigation that can actually generate data
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is one report of up to 3,000 words marked out of 24 across Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation. In Chemistry the most common way to lose marks is decided before any chemistry happens: the chosen reaction cannot produce enough usable data under the conditions a school laboratory permits. A question about an interesting reaction that yields four points on a graph will not carry the Data analysis criterion regardless of how well the report is written.

There are three practical filters. Can the student get the reagents, and will the school approve them? Can the independent variable be varied across at least five values with repeats, inside the laboratory time available? And is the dependent variable measurable with the equipment on hand, to a precision that makes the differences real rather than noise? An outside tutor is useful here precisely because they will ask these questions coldly in week one, when the question can still be changed, rather than sympathetically in week six when it cannot.

The table below sets out investigation types that recur in UAE schools and what usually goes wrong with each. None of these is forbidden; several produce excellent reports when the method is designed properly. The point of the table is that the design decision is the mark-bearing decision, and it is taken at the start.

Evaluation deserves a separate warning, because it is the criterion where UAE students most consistently leave marks behind. The criterion asks for weaknesses belonging to this method and improvements that would actually address them. A sentence about human error, or about running more repeats, describes every experiment ever performed and earns little. A sentence naming the burette reading precision, the volume it put in doubt, and the effect that had on the gradient at the low-concentration end earns the mark and takes no more words.

sections.heading: Practical work, and what online Chemistry tutoring can and cannot replace
paragraphs: Chemistry is a practical subject and it is fair to ask what a screen can do about that. The honest answer has a clear boundary. Hands-on laboratory work belongs to the school, which has the equipment, the reagents, the risk assessments and the supervision. Nothing delivered online substitutes for standing at a bench and running a titration. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE either, so there is no in-home laboratory alternative on the table; teaching here is online, one-to-one, over live video, with in-home tutoring offered only in India.

What online work does well is the part of practical chemistry that is actually assessed. Method design, variable control, uncertainty treatment, graph choice, processing raw data into something that answers the question, and evaluating a method against its own weaknesses are all paper-and-screen skills, and they are what the investigation criteria reward. A tutor and a student annotating the same data set in real time, with the tutor asking why a point was discarded, is a better use of an hour than watching a demonstration.

The table below splits the practical requirement into what the school supplies, what online tutoring can genuinely help with, and what it cannot. Being explicit about the third column is the point: a parent paying for support deserves to know where its limits are rather than discovering them at the deadline.

One practical habit is worth adopting early in Al Ain, where laboratory access outside lessons varies a great deal between campuses. Rehearse the procedure in a session before the laboratory slot, with the student talking through each step and the expected observation. Students who do this waste far less of their limited bench time, and they come back with data that can be processed rather than with a set of readings taken in the wrong order. The session costs an hour and frequently saves a whole laboratory booking.

sections.heading: Chemistry HL, UAE university routes and Ministry equivalency
paragraphs: Higher Level Chemistry is a stated requirement for a large share of medicine, pharmacy, dentistry and chemical engineering routes, which changes what tutoring is for. A student who needs a 6 to hold an offer and a student who needs a 4 to pass the Diploma should not be sold the same plan. The first usually gains most from Paper 1B technique, command-term precision and mechanism fluency; the second gains most from securing Structure 1 and Reactivity 1 so that the rest of the course stops compounding.

Equivalency is separate from a university's own admission requirements, and no tutoring provider performs or guarantees it. The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among those five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test.

For the IB, no points threshold should be taken from any tutoring page. The source reporting the Ministry's clarification set out the British and American tracks and stated no IB figure, so the IB position must be confirmed on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority. Al Ain families applying locally should also read the programme's own entry requirements at United Arab Emirates University, Al Ain University or a capital institution, which can sit above the equivalency floor for the same subject.

sections.heading: The honesty boundary on Chemistry coursework
paragraphs: Two components must be entirely the student's own: the scientific investigation and, where chosen, the Chemistry Extended Essay. The school supervisor signs an authenticity declaration for both. A tutor who crosses that boundary creates an academic misconduct exposure for the student that is far more serious than a disappointing mark, and some providers in this market openly sell completed coursework, which is a malpractice trigger rather than a service.

The legitimate space is wide. A tutor can teach uncertainty propagation on a different data set entirely. They can ask whether a reaction will produce enough points to plot. They can read a student's own draft and name the criterion a paragraph is failing and the reason. They can mark practice questions, drill mechanism reasoning, and refuse a research question that cannot work. All of that is teaching and all of it is permitted under IB rules.

The line is that no part of the submitted work may come from anyone else. Not a paragraph, not a graph built for the student, not a conclusion handed over, not a rewritten section returned for pasting in. The working test given to every student in the first session is whether they could explain and defend each sentence to their school supervisor with no help. If the answer is no for any sentence, that sentence should not be in the report.

Saying this out loud is also commercially useful rather than merely principled. Parents in this market are routinely offered coursework assistance whose boundaries are never described, and a provider that states the limit in advance is easier to trust than one that leaves it vague. The student benefits more directly: a report they fully understand is a report they can discuss confidently with a supervisor, and the supervisor's confidence is part of what the final moderated mark rests on.

faqs.question: Is IB Chemistry HL mostly organic chemistry at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Organic work is the largest single block of Higher Level-only content, but it is not the whole of it. Reactivity 3 holds the mechanisms, pH curves and buffers, and electrochemical cells, which makes it the biggest Higher Level allocation in the course. The extensions in Reactivity 1 and Reactivity 2, covering Born-Haber cycles, Gibbs free energy, rate equations and quantitative equilibrium, together account for a comparable amount of teaching time. Students who think of Higher Level Chemistry as organic chemistry tend to be surprised by how much of the paper is quantitative.

faqs.question: Why does my child understand Chemistry in class but lose marks on paper?
faqs.answer: This is the signature of the mathematics wall rather than a chemistry problem. Gibbs free energy, Born-Haber cycles, rate equations and equilibrium constants all demand confident rearrangement, logarithms and sign discipline. A student can explain the chemistry perfectly aloud and still freeze at the algebra under examination pressure. It is one of the faster things to fix, usually four to six sessions, because the content is already understood and the work is procedural fluency rather than new learning. A diagnostic question settles it in minutes.

faqs.question: How do students practise mechanisms they have never seen before?
faqs.answer: By learning to reason from electron density rather than recognising reactions. A Higher Level question is often built around an unfamiliar molecule precisely to test whether the student can identify the functional group, work out where electron density is concentrated, and predict the attack. Memorised reaction lists fail that test. The route through it is secure functional group recognition from Structure 3 first, then curly-arrow reasoning built from scratch, then past-paper mechanisms attempted cold and marked line by line rather than discussed in general terms.

faqs.question: What is in the Chemistry data booklet and should my child memorise it?
faqs.answer: No. The booklet supplies constants, the periodic table, average bond enthalpies, standard electrode potentials, characteristic infrared absorption ranges and proton nuclear magnetic resonance chemical shift ranges, among other reference material. Memorising printed values is wasted revision. What is worth practising is finding a value in seconds under time pressure, and the reasoning the booklet cannot supply: definitions, sign conventions, which half-cell oxidises, and what a broad absorption actually indicates. That division is the single most useful thing to get straight before mock season.

faqs.question: How do we pick a Chemistry investigation topic that will score well?
faqs.answer: Start from data sufficiency rather than from interest. Three filters settle most questions: can the reagents be obtained and will the school approve them, can the independent variable be varied across at least five values with repeats inside the laboratory time available, and is the dependent variable measurable to a precision that makes the differences real. A question about a fascinating reaction that produces four usable points cannot carry the Data analysis criterion. Asking those questions in week one, while the question can change, is worth more than any amount of later editing.

faqs.question: Can online lessons help with Chemistry practical work?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the boundary is worth stating. Hands-on bench work belongs to the school, which holds the equipment, the reagents, the risk assessments and the supervision, and nothing delivered over video replaces standing at a bench. What online one-to-one work does well is the part the investigation criteria actually reward: method design, variable control, uncertainty handling, graph choice, processing raw data, and evaluating a method against its own specific weaknesses. Those are screen-and-paper skills, and a shared data set with a tutor asking why a point was discarded is an efficient use of an hour.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram provide in-home Chemistry tutoring in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Al Ain families are taught online, one-to-one, over live video at Gulf Standard Time slots. The reason is Higher Level supply: a Chemistry specialist who has taught the current Structure and Reactivity guide and marked investigations against the current criteria is scarce within driving distance of any one Al Ain district, and online delivery takes distance out of the matching decision completely.

faqs.question: How much do Chemistry tutors charge per hour in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Market figures rather than our own: qualified subject tutors online sit at roughly AED 150-300 per hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. IB specialists online run AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 survey quoting AED 200-450 plus. In-home work in the emirate runs AED 180-500, which includes the tutor's travel hour. Those are the sources named. Our own rate is quoted after the free trial against level, component and weeks remaining.

faqs.question: Which body inspects private schools in the Garden City?
faqs.answer: ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools across the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, Al Ain included. Dubai sits under KHDA, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the Ministry of Education. The practical consequence for an Al Ain parent is that inspection reports, policy circulars and staff conduct rules come from ADEK, so guidance written about Dubai's framework describes a different authority.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Abu Dhabi emirate need a licence?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued by MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so a specific amount quoted anywhere should be treated with caution.

faqs.question: Should we switch from Standard Level to Higher Level Chemistry?
faqs.answer: If a university route requires it, the decision needs taking in the first term of DP1 and no later. The Higher Level extensions are threaded through all six units rather than sitting in one block, so a late switch means catching up on material in Structure 2, Structure 3, Reactivity 1, Reactivity 2 and Reactivity 3 simultaneously while the current teaching continues. Where a school can still accommodate it early, eight to twelve hours of one-to-one work usually covers the gap. Where the switch has become unrealistic, we will say so rather than sell against it.

faqs.question: Our child has ten weeks left. What is the best use of them?
faqs.answer: Triage, then technique. Mark two full past papers and sort the units into secure, shaky and not recoverable in the time available, then spend the hours on the two things that move fastest: Paper 1B data analysis as a separate skill, and command-term precision on Paper 2 questions that cross units. Data booklet navigation under time pressure is the third. Re-teaching Reactivity 3 from the beginning in ten weeks while revision is also needed elsewhere is not realistic, and we will say that plainly rather than sell the hours.

faqs.question: Can lessons move during Ramadan and examination weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most Al Ain families need both. School hours shorten during Ramadan and useful study time shifts into the evening, so the weekly slot typically moves rather than pausing. School examination weeks, family travel and the days around eid are handled the same way. Keeping the same tutor through the changes matters more than keeping the same hour, because a tutor who has been marking a student's scripts for a term does not have to spend a session re-diagnosing anything.

faqs.question: Is Chemistry HL required for medicine applications from the UAE?
faqs.answer: It is a stated requirement for a large share of medicine, pharmacy and dentistry routes, but the requirement belongs to each university and should be read from the programme's own page rather than from a tutoring site. Ministry of Education equivalency is a separate process that no tutoring provider performs or guarantees, and for the IB specifically no points threshold should be taken from any tutoring page. Check the programme requirement, then check equivalency on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority, then plan the grade target around both.

faqs.question: What if no Higher Level Chemistry specialist is available at our slot?
faqs.answer: We say so instead of substituting a general science tutor. The early-evening Gulf Standard Time window is the most contested part of the week for Higher Level sciences. Where the slot you need is full, the honest options are a different weekday, a weekend session, or starting with the component least dependent on specialism, such as data booklet navigation or Paper 1B technique, while the specialist slot opens. We will tell you which of those applies rather than fill the hour with whoever is free.

intro.heading: Start from where your child is, not from the syllabus front page
paragraphs: A parent searching for an IB DP computer science tutor in Al Ain is almost never starting from nothing. There is usually a DP1 report with a 3 or a 4 in Computer Science, a half-finished Internal Assessment folder, and a student who can read code but freezes when asked to write it under time pressure. The useful question is not what the syllabus contains. It is how many weeks sit between the grade on that report and the grade your child needs, and what has to happen inside each of those weeks.

That timeline is the shape of this page. Computer Science is a subject where the gap between understanding and performance is unusually wide. A student can explain what a while loop does and still lose six marks on Paper 2 because the answer describes the loop rather than tracing it. A student can build a working program and still score poorly on the Internal Assessment because the documentation does not evidence the design decisions. Both failures are fixable, but they are fixed by different work, in different weeks, and knowing which one you are looking at is the whole diagnosis.

Al Ain adds a practical constraint that Dubai and Abu Dhabi island do not. The city's private-school set is small, and Diploma Computer Science is a minority option inside it. Some Al Ain campuses run it at Standard Level only. Some run a single mixed SL and HL class. That means a student at Higher Level may be the only person in the room doing the Paper 3 case study, and the local pool of people who have taught the HL extension topics recently is correspondingly thin. Driving to the capital for a weekly session costs three hours of a school night before anyone opens a laptop.

Which is why lessons here are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared screen. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a programming subject this is not a compromise. Code is read on a screen, not on paper, and a tutor who can take control of the editor, set a breakpoint and step through your child's own failing program is doing something a tutor sitting at your dining table with a printout cannot do as well.

What follows is the honest version of the next few months. The four components and what each actually rewards. The specific places Al Ain students lose marks. The Internal Assessment counted backwards from the school's submission date rather than forwards from today. What the Al Ain market charges, in AED, with the source named. And the point at which a timeline is genuinely too short to recover, because telling you that in October is worth more than taking your money in April.

These are the programme stages Al Ain families ask about most, with what each one means for a student heading towards Diploma Computer Science.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Design and MYP Mathematics are the two feeders into Diploma Computer Science, and neither of them teaches the thing the Diploma assesses. MYP Design rewards the cycle: inquiry, development of ideas, creating the solution, evaluation. It does not require a student to write a syntactically correct program under a time limit. A student can finish MYP with a 7 in Design and no fluency in a text-based language at all.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Ain this matters more than it does in a large Dubai school, because the MYP cohort and the DP cohort are often the same thirty children moving up together. If the MYP Design teacher used block-based tools, the whole year group arrives in DP1 without having typed a semicolon. Ask the school which language MYP Design used in Years 9 and 10 before you assume your child is behind individually.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, first year
programmes.description: DP1 covers the core system fundamentals, computer organisation, networks and the introduction to programming. The Internal Assessment is usually proposed late in DP1 and built across the DP1 summer. A student who reaches the end of DP1 without a confirmed IA client, a scoped problem and some working code has lost the part of the year that was easiest to use.
programmes.countryNote: The Al Ain academic year runs roughly September to late June, with the long break across July and August. That break is the single largest block of uninterrupted IA time an Al Ain student will ever have, and families who travel for six weeks of it tend to return to a DP2 September that is already compressed. Planning the IA build around travel dates in May is the cheapest intervention available.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, second year
programmes.description: DP2 adds the remaining content, the HL extension topics for Higher Level students, and the Paper 3 case study where applicable. The IA is finished and submitted, mocks are sat, and the final weeks are pure technique: tracing algorithms by hand, converting a description into an explanation, and managing the time split across papers.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain students sit the May session alongside the rest of the northern-hemisphere IB world. Registration and internal coursework deadlines are set by the school's Diploma coordinator and fall months before the papers. Confirm every date with the coordinator directly rather than with the student, because the student's version of a deadline is reliably two weeks later than the school's.

programmes.name: Higher Level Computer Science
programmes.description: Higher Level adds abstract data structures, resource management and control, plus the Paper 3 case study. The extension content is conceptually harder than anything at Standard Level: recursive tree traversal, linked-list manipulation and the trade-offs an operating system makes between competing processes. It is also where a student who has been coasting on intuition finally runs out of intuition.
programmes.countryNote: If your child is the only Higher Level Computer Science student in an Al Ain cohort, assume the extension topics will be taught in fewer contact hours than a larger school would give them. That is the specific gap one-to-one online tuition is best at closing, because the material is self-contained and does not need a class to work.

al-ain/ib-dp-computer-science-tutor.subjectsIntro: Computer Science is the subject on this page, but most Al Ain families who book one tutor end up asking about a second. These are the Diploma subjects our tutors cover for Al Ain students, with what each one actually assesses and where the marks tend to go.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Java-based programming, system fundamentals, computer organisation, networks and, at Higher Level, abstract data structures and resource management. Marks are lost on dry-run tracing, on explaining rather than describing, and on Internal Assessment documentation that does not evidence the design choices the student actually made.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The usual partner subject for a Computer Science student heading to an engineering or computing degree. Proof, sequences, calculus and the non-calculator Paper 1 are the pressure points. Students who are strong at code are often weak at algebraic manipulation, because the compiler never asked them to simplify anything by hand.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and the graphical calculator carry more weight here than in Analysis and Approaches. It pairs well with Computer Science for data-oriented degrees, and the statistics content overlaps usefully with any Internal Assessment that processes a real dataset.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The electronics and circuits content gives a Computer Science student useful grounding in how the hardware under the abstraction actually behaves. The assessment punishes vague use of terms, and the data-analysis questions reward the same careful unit discipline that a well-documented program does.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Often chosen alongside Computer Science by students who came through MYP Design. The design cycle is familiar; the assessed written papers are not. Students underestimate how much terminology the papers demand and how precisely the command terms are applied.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A common third subject for students whose Internal Assessment client is a family business. The subject's own assessment rewards application to a named organisation rather than textbook recall, which is the same discipline the Computer Science IA documentation needs.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and real-world examples carry the marks. Students who write confidently about code often write loosely about markets, and the fix is the same: say which thing changed, by how much, and why, rather than gesturing at a direction.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The subject that most often drags a technically strong student's total down. Paper 1 is an unseen text under time pressure, and the Individual Oral needs a global issue chosen months in advance. Both reward planning rather than talent.

subjects.name: Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The core components a Computer Science student can turn into an advantage, because a well-scoped computing Extended Essay reuses the research discipline the Internal Assessment already demanded. Support here is teaching, feedback and process coaching on the student's own work only.

al-ain/ib-dp-computer-science-tutor.regionsIntro: Al Ain spreads across a wide, low-density grid, and the practical difference between districts is how long the evening drive takes and which campus the children in that district attend. For an online session the only thing that matters is when the household is actually home.

regions.note: Central, dense by Al Ain standards, and close to several of the older private campuses. Families here can often get a child home by 15:45, which makes a 16:00 start realistic for a student who needs a session before fatigue sets in.

regions.name: Asharej
regions.note: The university side of the city, with a high proportion of academic households. Computer Science requests from Asharej skew towards Higher Level and towards students who already code recreationally but have never been assessed on it formally.

regions.name: Al Mutaredh
regions.note: Older villa district near the centre with short runs to the central schools. The common pattern here is two children in the same household on different programmes, which makes back-to-back evening slots easier to schedule than a single awkward one.

regions.name: Al Towayya
regions.note: Residential and well served by the ring roads, so the school run is predictable rather than long. Predictability matters more than distance for a weekly recurring slot, because a fixed time that never slips is what builds the habit.

regions.name: Falaj Hazzaa
regions.note: Established central district with a mix of campuses within a short drive. Families here frequently ask about a second subject alongside Computer Science, usually Mathematics, which is easier to staff as one tutor with two slots than two tutors with one each.

al-ain/ib-dp-computer-science-tutor.modesIntro: Three delivery patterns cover almost every Al Ain Computer Science request. All three are one-to-one and live over video with a shared screen; the difference is cadence and what the time is spent on.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through the term
modes.description: A fixed slot that tracks the school's own scheme of work, usually 60 or 90 minutes. The tutor sees the current topic, the last assessment and the next one, and the session alternates between content that was missed and technique that was never taught. This is the pattern that moves a 4 towards a 6 over two terms rather than two weeks.

modes.description: A concentrated run of sessions timed around the school's internal deadlines, usually across the DP1 summer and early DP2. The work is scoping, success criteria, design documentation and debugging. The tutor reviews, questions and teaches technique; the student writes the code and the documentation, because the IA is assessed as the student's own work.

sections.heading: What an Al Ain parent is actually asking when they search for this
paragraphs: The search means one of three things. Either a DP1 report came back with a 3 or a 4 in Computer Science and nobody at home can tell whether that is a crisis or a normal start; or the Internal Assessment has stalled and the school's deadline is visible on the calendar; or DP2 mocks have happened and the predicted grade is now a university problem. Each of those needs a different first session, and a tutor who opens with the same introductory lesson in all three cases has wasted the one hour you were most willing to pay for.

The practical answer for most Al Ain families is a weekly one-to-one slot over live video, 60 or 90 minutes, starting after 16:30 so the school run from Zakher or Hili is finished. Market rates in the UAE for a qualified subject tutor working online run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, and for an IB or A-Level specialist roughly AED 200 to 450 and upwards, according to provider rate cards and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table read in October 2026. Those are market bands, not our price list; the first session with us is free and no figure is quoted until you have heard the tutor teach.

What makes Computer Science different from the other Diploma sciences is that two thirds of the grade is written and one third is a build. A student can be good at one half and hopeless at the other, and the two halves fail in opposite directions. The strong coder loses marks because the Paper 2 answer assumes the examiner can see what the student means. The strong writer loses marks because the Internal Assessment program does not actually run. Before anyone books twenty sessions, it is worth knowing which child you have.

The rest of this page is the diagnosis and the plan: what each component rewards, where Al Ain students specifically lose marks, the Internal Assessment counted backwards from its deadline, what the market charges, and the point at which the remaining weeks are genuinely not enough. Nothing here requires a tutor to be read usefully.

sections.heading: Reading a DP1 Computer Science report without panicking
paragraphs: A 4 at the end of DP1 is not the same thing as a 4 in DP2, and schools know this even when the report does not say so. DP1 reports are generally awarded against the final standard, not against where a DP1 student ought to be, which means a mid-year 4 in a two-year course is closer to on-track than most parents assume. The number that actually matters is the direction of travel between the first and second reporting cycles, and whether the Internal Assessment appears in the comments at all.

Read the comment rather than the grade. A comment about effort, homework or missed deadlines describes a work-habit problem, and tuition fixes those slowly and expensively. A comment about not being able to apply knowledge to unfamiliar problems describes a technique problem, and that is what one-to-one time is unusually good at. A comment about specific content — networks, computer organisation, recursion — describes a gap, which is the cheapest of the three to close because it has a finite edge.

Then ask the school two questions the report will not answer. Which components has your child been assessed on so far, and has the Internal Assessment problem been approved? A student in the second term of DP1 with no approved IA problem is behind in a way the grade column does not show, because the IA is a fixed proportion of the final mark and the time available to build it only ever shrinks. In a small Al Ain cohort an unapproved IA can sit unnoticed for a whole term.

Finally, get the school's own internal deadline dates in writing from the Diploma coordinator. Not the IB's deadlines — the school's, which sit earlier because teachers need time to mark, moderate and upload. Every plan below counts backwards from that date, and families who plan from the student's recollection of it routinely lose three to four weeks.

sections.heading: The assessed components and what each one actually demands
paragraphs: Diploma Computer Science is assessed through written papers and one internally assessed piece of coursework. Standard Level students sit two papers plus the Internal Assessment. Higher Level students sit three papers plus the Internal Assessment, with the third paper based on a case study the IB releases in advance. The component weightings and durations differ by level and are published in the subject guide your child's cohort is following, so confirm the exact figures with the school's Diploma coordinator before building a revision plan around them.

Paper 1 is the long structured paper and carries the most content. It rewards precision in the use of terminology and the ability to trace an algorithm by hand on paper, which is a skill almost no student practises voluntarily because the computer has always done it for them. Paper 2 is the options or applied paper and rewards applying the same ideas to a described scenario; this is where the gap between describing and explaining is most expensive. Higher Level Paper 3 is the case study paper and rewards preparation done months earlier.

The Internal Assessment is a working solution to a real problem for a real client, submitted with documentation covering the planning, the design, the development and the evaluation. Marks are allocated against published criteria, and the single commonest failure is a program that works well and documentation that does not evidence why it was built that way. The examiner cannot award marks for a design decision the student made silently.

The table below is the planning view: what each component tests, roughly how long it runs, and the specific failure mode a tutor should be looking for. Treat the durations and weightings as the shape of the assessment rather than as verified numbers for your child's cohort, and check both against the current subject guide.

sections.heading: Java is where most Al Ain students stall, and why
paragraphs: Diploma Computer Science is taught through a text-based language, and in practice that means Java for most cohorts. Students arriving from MYP Design having used block-based or visual tools hit three specific walls in the first term, and all three are recognisable from the outside. The first is syntax anxiety: the student can describe the algorithm correctly in English and cannot get it to compile, so every piece of homework takes four times as long as the teacher budgeted and confidence drains out of the subject.

The second wall is the inability to read an error message. A compiler error names a line, a type and a reason, and a student who has never been taught to read that triple treats every red message as an undifferentiated failure. Teaching a student to read errors is perhaps two sessions of work and it changes the economics of every hour they spend coding afterwards, because they stop needing a teacher present to make progress.

The third wall is tracing. Examination papers ask what a fragment of code outputs, or ask the student to complete a trace table showing each variable at each iteration. Students who have only ever run code to find out what it does have no manual method for this, and they lose marks in clusters because the same weakness appears in several questions on the same paper. Tracing is mechanical, teachable and almost entirely absent from most students' practice.

In Al Ain there is a fourth factor, which is isolation. In a cohort of eight Computer Science students, a child who is stuck has nobody at the next desk at the same level to compare with, and a teacher covering both levels has limited time to sit beside one student and step through their program. A shared-screen online session is the closest available substitute for that missing shoulder-to-shoulder time, and it is why the subject responds to one-to-one work better than its reputation suggests.

sections.heading: The Internal Assessment counted backwards from the school deadline
paragraphs: The Internal Assessment is the part of the course a family can actually control, and it is also the part most often lost to drift. The work splits into four unequal phases: finding and scoping a problem with a real client, writing success criteria that can be tested, building and documenting the solution, and evaluating it honestly against those criteria. The building is the part students want to start with and the part that should start third.

Count backwards rather than forwards. Take the school's internal submission date from the Diploma coordinator, subtract two weeks for the student's own final checking, and you have the real date the build must be finished. Subtract the development window, the design window and the scoping window from there and you arrive at the date the client conversation needed to happen. For most Al Ain cohorts that date falls inside DP1, which is why a summer spent travelling without a scoped problem is so expensive.

A tutor's role across this is narrow and should be stated plainly. The tutor can help a student understand the published criteria, question whether a success criterion is testable, teach a debugging method, and review a draft and say where it does not evidence what the student did. The tutor cannot and will not produce the solution or the documentation; the Internal Assessment is assessed as the student's own work and any other arrangement puts the student's whole diploma at risk under IB academic-honesty rules.

sections.heading: The Higher Level case study, and why late is fatal here
paragraphs: Higher Level students sit an additional paper built on a case study that the IB publishes in advance of the session. The case study introduces a scenario and a body of specialist terminology, and the paper expects the student to apply course concepts to that scenario in extended written answers. Because the material is released early, the paper is not a test of recall under surprise. It is a test of how many months the student spent reading around it.

This is the component where Al Ain's small cohorts show up most clearly. In a large school the case study becomes a running thread through DP2: a reading list, a glossary built collectively, guest discussion, practice essays marked and returned. In a cohort of six with one teacher covering two levels, it frequently becomes three lessons in March. A student who meets the specialist vocabulary for the first time a fortnight before the paper will write generally where the examiner wanted specifics.

The work itself is unglamorous and perfectly suited to weekly one-to-one time. Build a glossary of every term in the released material and be able to define each one without notes. Map each concept in the case study back to the part of the syllabus it comes from. Write and mark practice responses that use the scenario's own vocabulary rather than generic examples. Read the secondary material the case study points at, a little each week, from the term it is released.

If your child is Higher Level, ask the school in the first term of DP2 what the plan for the case study is and when the released material will be handed out. If the answer is vague, that is the gap worth buying tuition for, because it is finite, it is known in advance, and it is worth a fifth of the Higher Level grade in a component nobody can revise in a weekend.

sections.heading: What Computer Science tuition costs at Al Ain market rates
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes figures, which is why parents ring four providers and get four non-answers. The bands below come from UAE provider rate cards and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, read in October 2026. They describe what the market charges, not what IB Gram charges. Al Ain sits inside the Abu Dhabi emirate's pricing rather than Dubai's, and in-home rates here carry more travel loading than the capital because the city is spread out and tutors are fewer.

Read the table as a budget tool. A single weekly 60-minute session with a qualified online subject tutor at the middle of the band is a predictable monthly figure, and families generally find that easier to commit to than an intensive block bought in panic three weeks before a paper. Monthly packages advertised in the UAE have included roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and roughly AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, which is the cleanest illustration of what travel time costs when someone has to drive.

Two cost traps are specific to a subject like this one. The first is paying specialist rates for general help: a mathematics tutor can support the algorithmic thinking but cannot mark Internal Assessment documentation against Computer Science criteria, and families often discover this in month three. The second is buying hours instead of buying a plan, which produces a pleasant tutor, a satisfied student and an unchanged grade.

Whatever you pay, the figure should be attached to a named plan with dates in it. Ask what the next six sessions will cover, what will be different at the end of them, and how you will know. A provider that cannot answer that is selling hours.

sections.heading: Online, in-home, or the drive to Abu Dhabi: the honest comparison
paragraphs: Al Ain families weighing a Computer Science tutor have three real options and a fourth that is usually a fantasy. The three are an online one-to-one specialist, a local in-home tutor who can travel to the district, and a weekly drive to the capital for a face-to-face specialist. The fantasy is a local in-home tutor who is also a Higher Level Computer Science specialist with recent case-study experience, because in a city this size that person usually does not exist and waiting for them costs a term.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen; home visits are a service we run only in India. We say that before the comparison rather than after it, because a parent who wants someone at the door should know immediately. What we would argue is that for this particular subject the online format is not the second-best version. A tutor who can take the keyboard, set a breakpoint and step through the student's own failing program is doing something that cannot be done over a printout.

The arithmetic on the capital drive is worth doing once. Al Ain to Abu Dhabi island is around 130 kilometres each way; a weekly session there costs roughly three hours of travel on top of the lesson, on a school night, for a student who still has homework. Over a two-year Diploma that is a large number of hours spent in a car, and the sessions get cancelled first whenever anything else goes wrong.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and the line this subject makes tempting
paragraphs: Computer Science is the Diploma subject where the boundary between help and malpractice is easiest to cross by accident, because code can be copied invisibly and because a parent who writes software professionally is sitting right there. The IB's position is that assessed work must be the student's own. Support may teach, explain, question and give feedback. It may not produce the artefact.

In practice that means a tutor may explain how a hash map works, may ask why a particular data structure was chosen, may teach a method for isolating a bug, and may read documentation and say that a design decision has not been evidenced. A tutor may not supply working code for the solution, restructure the program on the student's behalf, or rewrite the documentation into something the student could not have produced. We say no to those requests, and we would rather lose the booking than put a diploma at risk.

The same line applies to anything found online. Code taken from a forum or generated by a tool and submitted without acknowledgement is a malpractice issue, and the student is the one who faces the consequence. The defensible habit is to record the source of every fragment that did not originate with the student and to be able to explain line by line what each one does. A student who can do that is also a student who will survive the written papers.

This is also why we never offer to supply past papers, mark schemes, subject guides or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those documents belong to the IB and to the examination boards. We reference them, point at the official source, and expect the school's coordinator to be the route to anything your child's cohort is entitled to see.

process.title: Tell us the level and the deadline
process.description: Two facts decide the match: Standard or Higher Level, and the date of the next thing that matters — an internal Internal Assessment deadline, a mock, or the May papers. Everything else can be worked out in the first session, but those two determine which tutor is the right one to start with.

process.title: A free first session with the actual tutor
process.description: Not a sales call and not a generic diagnostic. The tutor works on your child's current topic, with your child's own code or last assessment open on the shared screen, so you can hear how they explain something your child has already failed to understand once.

process.title: A written plan with dates
process.description: After the trial you get a short plan naming what the next six sessions cover and what should be different at the end of them. If the plan does not say anything specific, that is a reason to say no, and we would rather you asked for it than paid without it.

process.title: A fixed weekly slot on Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Scheduled around the Al Ain school run and kept the same every week, because a recurring time that never moves is what keeps a weekly booking alive through a full term. Ramadan and travel weeks are planned around rather than cancelled into.

process.title: Review against the plan, not against a feeling
process.description: Every few weeks we check the plan against what has actually happened: marks on timed questions, Internal Assessment milestones hit or missed, topics closed. If the plan is not working we change the plan or the tutor, and that conversation starts with us rather than with you.

whyPoints.title: Matched on level, not on postcode
whyPoints.description: A Higher Level student with a case study to prepare needs someone who has taught that paper, and in Al Ain that person is unlikely to live within driving distance. Online delivery means the filter is subject and level rather than geography, which is the whole argument for the format in a city this size.

whyPoints.title: Shared-screen work on the student's own code
whyPoints.description: The tutor takes the editor, sets a breakpoint and steps through the program your child wrote, with your child watching the variables change. That is the single most useful hour available in this subject and it is easier to do over a shared screen than across a table.

whyPoints.title: The Internal Assessment treated as the student's work
whyPoints.description: We coach the process, question the scope and review drafts against the published criteria. We do not produce solutions or documentation. Saying this plainly costs us some enquiries and it is the only position compatible with your child keeping their diploma.

whyPoints.title: Al Ain's calendar, not a generic UAE one
whyPoints.description: Sessions are planned around the September-to-June Al Ain year, the long summer that is the real Internal Assessment window, Ramadan timings and the school's own internal deadlines rather than the IB's published ones.

whyPoints.title: Figures with their source attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page names where it came from and when it was read. We do not publish an invented price list, a satisfaction percentage or a star rating, because a number without its method behind it is worth nothing to a parent making a decision.

whyPoints.title: An honest no when the timeline is too short
whyPoints.description: There is a point in the final term where a subject that has been neglected for two years cannot be rebuilt, and the right advice is to protect the components still in reach. We will say so rather than sell twenty sessions into a wall.

faqs.question: My child has a 4 in DP1 Computer Science. Is a 6 realistic by the May papers?
faqs.answer: Often yes, if the 4 is a technique problem rather than a content void. Ask the teacher which components the 4 came from. If it is written-paper marks lost on describing instead of explaining, and on tracing done mentally rather than on paper, that is perhaps two terms of weekly one-to-one work and it moves reliably. If the 4 reflects a student who cannot yet get a program to compile and has no approved Internal Assessment problem, the realistic target is a 5 and the priority is the coursework, because that mark is still fully recoverable while paper technique is not.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my child's problem is coding or exam writing?
faqs.answer: Set two tasks at the kitchen table. First, ask them to complete a trace table for a short loop on paper, with every variable written at every iteration. Second, ask them to write a five-line answer to a past-paper question that begins with the command term explain. A student who manages the trace but writes a description has an examination-writing problem. A student who writes well but cannot trace has a programming-fluency problem. Most struggling students fail both tasks, and the order of repair is tracing first, because it is mechanical and it unblocks marks across several questions on the same paper.

faqs.question: Does my child need to know Java before starting the Diploma Computer Science course?
faqs.answer: No, the course teaches it, but arriving with no text-based programming experience makes the first term harder than it needs to be. Students coming out of MYP Design having used block-based tools typically spend their first weeks fighting syntax rather than learning concepts, and that is where confidence in the subject is usually lost. A few hours of structured work on syntax, compiler errors and basic control flow before DP1 begins is the cheapest intervention available in this subject, and the August before DP1 is the natural window for it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Computer Science Internal Assessment without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor may explain the published assessment criteria, challenge whether a success criterion is testable, teach a method for isolating bugs, and read a draft and say where a design decision has not been evidenced. A tutor may not supply the solution code, restructure the program on the student's behalf or rewrite the documentation. The Internal Assessment is assessed as the student's own work and anything else is a malpractice risk that falls on the student, not the tutor. We state that limit at the first session rather than after a booking.

faqs.question: When should an Al Ain student start the Computer Science Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: The client conversation and the problem scope should happen inside DP1, with the build running across the DP1 summer. Count backwards from the school's internal submission date rather than forwards from today: subtract two weeks for the student's own final checking, then the development, design and scoping windows, and you usually land somewhere in the middle of DP1. Families who spend July and August travelling without a scoped problem lose the single largest uninterrupted block of coursework time the two years contain, and DP2 has no spare space to give it back.

faqs.question: Which schools in Al Ain actually offer Diploma Computer Science?
faqs.answer: Provision is patchy and changes year to year, so the only reliable answer is the one you get from the school. Several Al Ain campuses offer the subject at Standard Level only, some run a combined Standard and Higher Level class, and a few do not offer it at all. Ask the Diploma coordinator three questions: is the subject running for your child's cohort, at which levels, and how many contact hours a week the Higher Level extension topics receive. The answer to the third question is the one that predicts whether outside support will be needed.

faqs.question: What happens in the Higher Level case study paper and when should preparation start?
faqs.answer: The IB releases a case study ahead of the session, introducing a scenario and a body of specialist terminology, and the paper asks the student to apply course concepts to it in extended answers. Because the material is published early, the paper rewards months of reading rather than last-minute revision. Preparation should start in the term the material is handed out: build a glossary of every term, map each concept back to the syllabus, and write practice responses using the scenario's own vocabulary. Three lessons in March is the commonest version of this going wrong.

faqs.question: Is it worth driving from Al Ain to Abu Dhabi for a face-to-face Computer Science specialist?
faqs.answer: Rarely, once the arithmetic is done. Al Ain to Abu Dhabi island is around 130 kilometres each way, so a weekly session costs roughly three hours of travel on a school night on top of the lesson itself. Over a two-year Diploma that is a very large number of hours, and the sessions get cancelled first whenever anything else in the week goes wrong. For a subject where the work happens on a screen anyway, a live video session with a shared editor gets you a wider pool of Higher Level specialists and no travel at all.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our villa in Zakher or Hili?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs only in India. Tutoring for Al Ain families is delivered one-to-one over live video with a shared screen, on Gulf Standard Time. For Computer Science specifically this is a genuine advantage rather than a compromise, because the tutor can take control of the editor and step through your child's own failing program line by line. We say this before quoting anything, so a family who wants someone physically present knows immediately.

faqs.question: What does weekly Computer Science tuition cost for an Al Ain family?
faqs.answer: Market rates in the UAE for a qualified subject tutor working online run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, and for an IB specialist roughly AED 200 to 450 and upwards, according to provider rate cards and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table read in October 2026. In-home rates sit higher, around AED 180 to 500, because travel is priced in, and in a spread-out city that loading is heavier than in the capital. Those are market bands rather than our price list. The first session with us is free and you hear the tutor teach before any figure is discussed.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Diploma Computer Science student usually need?
faqs.answer: One weekly session of 60 or 90 minutes covers most term-time cases, with short additional blocks around the Internal Assessment and in the final twelve weeks. Two sessions a week makes sense only when there is a specific backlog with a deadline attached, such as an unbuilt Internal Assessment with three months left. More than two is generally a sign that the problem is work habits rather than subject knowledge, and that is slow and expensive to fix with paid hours rather than with a different routine at home.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor cover Computer Science and Mathematics for one student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking because two subjects with one tutor is easier to schedule than two tutors with one slot each. The overlap is real at the algorithmic end: sequences, logic and the discipline of working a problem by hand. The overlap stops at coursework. A mathematics specialist cannot mark Computer Science Internal Assessment documentation against its published criteria, and a Computer Science specialist should not be your only support for the non-calculator Analysis and Approaches Paper 1. Where both are needed properly, two matched tutors is the honest answer.

faqs.question: My child is the only Higher Level Computer Science student in their Al Ain class. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It matters for two specific things. The extension topics — abstract data structures, resource management and control — tend to get fewer contact hours when one teacher is covering both levels, and the case study often becomes a short unit rather than a running thread. Neither is a reflection on the school; it is arithmetic. Both are also well suited to one-to-one work, because the material is self-contained and does not need a class to function. Ask the coordinator how many weekly hours the extension content gets, and plan outside support around the gap that answer reveals.

faqs.question: Will sessions still run during Ramadan and the long Al Ain summer?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the timing changed rather than the frequency. During Ramadan most families move the weekly slot later, after Iftar, and shorten it; a 60-minute session at 21:00 works better than a 90-minute one at 17:00. The summer is different in kind: July and August are the largest uninterrupted Internal Assessment window the Diploma offers, and a short block of sessions across it is usually worth more than the same hours bought in a panic in February. Travel weeks are planned around in advance rather than cancelled at short notice.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Al Ain need a permit, and how can I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, free of charge, for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask any tutor directly whether they hold one, and check the current rules on mohre.gov.ae rather than taking a provider's word for it.

faqs.question: It is six weeks before the papers and nothing has been done. What is actually recoverable?
faqs.answer: Paper technique, and not much else. In six weeks a student can be drilled on trace tables, on the command terms and on timed past-paper answers, and that alone is often worth a grade because the losses are systematic rather than scattered. Content taught from scratch across a two-year course is not recoverable in six weeks, and an unbuilt Internal Assessment at that point is a conversation with the school rather than with a tutor. We will say that plainly, and we would rather protect the marks still in reach than sell hours into a deadline that has already passed.

al-ain/ib-dp-computer-science-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the free session, then decide
al-ain/ib-dp-computer-science-tutor.closingBody: The useful next step is small. Tell us whether your child is at Standard or Higher Level and what the next real deadline is — an internal Internal Assessment date, a mock, or the May papers. We match a Diploma Computer Science tutor on level rather than on location, and the first session is free: your child's own code or last assessment open on a shared screen, with the tutor working on the thing that is actually stuck. Afterwards you get a short written plan with dates in it, and you decide whether the plan is worth paying for. If six weeks is too few, we will tell you that instead.

al-ain/ib-dp-english-a-language-and-lite.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Diploma Programme English A: Language and Literature at both levels: unseen non-literary analysis, the comparative essay on literary works, the Individual Oral and the Higher Level essay. Al Ain students are matched on level and on the component with the nearest deadline.

intro.heading: Four components, four different clocks
paragraphs: English A: Language and Literature is the Diploma subject where the gap between a 4 and a 6 is almost never about reading more. It is about four separate assessments, each with its own clock, and a student who is behind on all four needs a different plan from one who is behind on three but has a strong Individual Oral already recorded. The first useful question is not what your child has read. It is which components are already fixed, which are in progress, and how many weeks remain on each.

That is the shape of this page, because it is the shape of the actual problem. Paper 1 and Paper 2 are sat at the end and can be improved up to the final fortnight. The Individual Oral is assessed internally, usually in DP2, and once it is recorded the mark is effectively fixed. The Higher Level essay has a submission date months before the papers. A parent who understands that ordering can direct money and attention at the component where it still changes something, instead of spreading it thinly across all four.

Al Ain adds a specific wrinkle that Dubai pages never mention. Many students here come from households where English is the language of school but not the language of home, and Language and Literature assumes a reader who can handle an unseen advertisement, political cartoon or opinion column written for an audience somewhere else entirely. A student with excellent English and no cultural footholds in the text loses marks on inference rather than on language. That is a teachable gap, but it has to be named before it can be taught, and most schools do not name it.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For this subject the format is genuinely well suited: the work is annotating the same text and the same marked script at the same time, which a shared screen does cleanly, and which also leaves a record of every annotated paragraph that both the student and the parent can go back to.

What follows is the honest sequence. How to read the grade you already have. The four components and which one is still movable. Paper 1 and the first twelve minutes that decide it. The Individual Oral, counted backwards from the recording date. The Higher Level essay. The learner portfolio, which is the cheapest insurance in the course. Which Language A route suits a bilingual Al Ain student. And what the Al Ain market charges, in AED, with the date and the source named. Where a UAE university place is the destination rather than a UK or US one, we also cover how the Ministry of Education equivalency route reads a Language A grade, because that is the one detail Al Ain families are most often told wrongly.

Paper 1 is unseen non-literary analysis under a hard time limit
Paper 2 is a comparative essay on literary works studied in class
The Individual Oral uses one literary and one non-literary extract, 40 lines maximum

al-ain/ib-dp-english-a-language-and-lite.programmesIntro: The English grade a student leaves the Diploma with is partly decided before DP1 begins, and the route into Language and Literature matters as much as the course itself. These are the stages that shape an Al Ain student's outcome in this subject.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Language and Literature is the direct feeder, and it rewards a slightly different thing from the Diploma. MYP marking credits personal response and creative engagement generously; Diploma marking credits analysis of how a text produces its effect. A student can leave MYP with a 7 for writing beautifully about how a poem made them feel and arrive in DP1 with no habit of naming a technique and explaining its function.
programmes.countryNote: Because Al Ain cohorts are small and often continuous from MYP into DP, a year group's writing habits tend to be uniform. If the MYP department prized personal response, the whole DP1 class will be writing personal responses in October and losing the same marks in the same place. That is worth knowing, because it means your child's weakness may be a house style rather than an individual gap.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, first year
programmes.description: DP1 covers the first areas of exploration, the first literary works and the start of the learner portfolio. The global issue for the Individual Oral is often chosen late in DP1, and the extracts selected soon after. A student who reaches the end of DP1 with an empty portfolio and no idea what a global issue is has lost the year's cheapest work.
programmes.countryNote: The Al Ain school year runs roughly September to late June, with a long July and August gap. For this subject the summer is reading time rather than coursework time: the Paper 2 literary works are best read once in the summer and reread in DP2, and a student who has never read the works outside class is starting the comparative essay from nothing.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, second year
programmes.description: DP2 completes the areas of exploration, records the Individual Oral, submits the Higher Level essay where applicable, and ends in timed practice on the two papers. The order matters: the Oral is the component that stops being movable once it is recorded, so it deserves attention before the papers do.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain students sit the May session. The Individual Oral recording window and the Higher Level essay submission date are set by the school rather than published nationally, so get both from the Diploma coordinator in writing in the first term of DP2. Families planning from the student's recollection of those dates reliably lose two to three weeks.

programmes.name: Higher Level Language and Literature
programmes.description: Higher Level sits two unseen texts in Paper 1 rather than one, which changes the paper from a careful piece of close reading into an exercise in time management. It also adds an essay of 1,200 to 1,500 words on a text or body of work studied in the course, developed from the learner portfolio and externally assessed.
programmes.countryNote: In a small Al Ain cohort the Higher Level essay is frequently the component with the least class time attached to it, because the teacher is covering shared content for both levels. It is also the component most easily rescued with one-to-one work, since it is a single piece of writing with a known deadline and a published set of criteria.

al-ain/ib-dp-english-a-language-and-lite.subjectsIntro: Language and Literature is the subject on this page. These are the Diploma subjects our tutors cover for Al Ain students, described by what the marks actually reward.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen non-literary analysis, the comparative essay on literary works, the Individual Oral and, at Higher Level, the essay. Marks are lost on feature-spotting without function, on comparative essays that run two separate essays side by side, and on Orals where the global issue is too broad to anchor an argument.

subjects.name: English A: Literature
subjects.description: The alternative Language A route, built entirely on literary works with no non-literary texts in the papers. It suits a confident reader who finds advertising and journalism harder to analyse than poetry, and it removes Paper 1's unseen non-literary text in favour of an unseen literary one.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: A language acquisition course rather than a Language A course, assessed on reading, writing, listening and speaking rather than on literary analysis. The right route for some students, and choosing between English B and English A Language and Literature is a conversation to have in Year 11, not in DP1.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Al Ain students frequently take an Arabic course alongside English A, and the two can support each other: analytical vocabulary transfers, and a student who understands how rhetoric works in one language sees it faster in the other. Timetabling two language subjects does compress revision time, though.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The closest analytical cousin to this subject. Source analysis in History rewards exactly the skill Paper 1 rewards: identifying what a text is trying to do to its reader and saying how. Students strong in one usually transfer quickly to the other once the command terms are mapped.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Shares the evaluative essay structure and the need to use evidence rather than recite it. Students who learn to connect a limitation to a claim in Psychology tend to stop feature-spotting in English, because the underlying habit is the same.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Often the subject a strong English student is weakest in, and the one that drags the total. Proof, sequences and the non-calculator paper are the pressure points, and the fix is practice volume rather than insight.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: A common pairing for students heading towards digital humanities or media degrees. The Internal Assessment demands the same documentation discipline that a learner portfolio demands, which is to record decisions as they are made rather than reconstruct them later.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Language and Literature students are well placed in both, because the subject already asks how meaning is made and who decides. Support is teaching, feedback and process coaching on the student's own work only, never production of it.

sections.heading: What an Al Ain parent is usually asking by the time they search this
paragraphs: In practice the search comes at one of three moments. A DP1 report has come back with a 4 and the comment says the writing is descriptive rather than analytical. A DP2 mock Paper 1 has come back poorly and the student says they ran out of time. Or the Individual Oral recording window has been announced and nobody at home knows what a global issue is. Each of those wants a different first session, and the answer to all three is not more reading.

The practical shape of the help is a weekly one-to-one slot of 60 or 90 minutes over live video, starting after 16:30 so the school run is finished, with the hour pointed at whichever component still has time on it. Market rates in the UAE for a qualified subject tutor working online run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, and for an IB specialist roughly AED 200 to 450 and upwards, according to provider rate cards and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table read in October 2026. Those are market bands rather than our price list, and the first session with us is free.

The reason sequencing matters so much in this subject is that the components stop being movable at different times. Once the Individual Oral is recorded, that mark is fixed. Once the Higher Level essay is submitted, so is that one. The two papers remain improvable until the final fortnight. A family that spends February on Paper 2 while the Oral recording window passes unprepared has spent money on the component that needed it least.

The rest of this page sets out each component, what it rewards, where Al Ain students specifically lose marks, and the point at which a remaining timeline is honestly too short. All of it is readable without buying anything.

sections.heading: Reading the English grade you already have
paragraphs: A 4 in English A at the end of DP1 is a far less alarming number than it looks, because reports in a two-year course are generally marked against the final standard rather than against where a DP1 student should be. What matters is the comment, and English comments are unusually informative if you know how to read them. There are really only four things a teacher can be saying, and each one has a different price attached.

A comment about writing being descriptive rather than analytical means the student names features and does not explain their function. This is the commonest comment in the subject and it is the cheapest to fix, because it is a sentence-level habit: identify the technique, then say what it does to the reader, then say why that serves the text's purpose. Students can be taught that three-part move in a handful of sessions and then practise it for months.

A comment about organisation or focus means the essays are not planned. That is a timing and planning problem rather than a reading problem, and it is fixed with a six-minute planning routine practised until it is automatic rather than with more content. A comment about expression and language means accuracy and register, which moves slowly and steadily and responds to volume of marked writing more than to explanation.

The fourth comment is the one to take seriously: not understanding the texts. If a student genuinely cannot follow what an unseen opinion column is doing, the problem is inference and cultural context rather than technique, and in a bilingual Al Ain household that is a very common and entirely fixable situation. It is also the one that needs the most lead time, so the comment is worth asking about explicitly rather than waiting for it to appear in writing.

sections.heading: The four components and which one is still movable
paragraphs: Language and Literature is assessed through two written papers, an internally assessed oral and, at Higher Level, an essay. Paper 1 is guided textual analysis of unseen non-literary material: Standard Level students work on one text, Higher Level students on two, with a guiding question attached to each. Paper 2 is a comparative essay answering one general question using two of the literary works studied in class, with no texts available in the examination room. The Individual Oral is a prepared ten-minute presentation followed by five minutes of questions. The Higher Level essay runs to 1,200 to 1,500 words.

Component weightings differ by level and are published in the subject guide your child's cohort follows, so confirm the exact percentages and durations with the school's Diploma coordinator rather than taking them from any website. What does not change is the marking architecture: the components are assessed against criteria covering knowledge, understanding and interpretation; analysis and evaluation; focus and organisation; and language. Knowing which criterion a student loses marks on is more useful than knowing the total, and most students have never been told.

The table below is the planning view. Read the final column first, because it is the one that determines where this term's money should go. A component that is already recorded or submitted cannot be improved, however much tuition is bought, and a component sat in May can be improved up to the last fortnight.

One further point parents rarely hear: Paper 2 is sat without the texts. Everything the student quotes has to come from memory, which means the revision task is partly a memory task and needs to start earlier than a student's instinct suggests. Building a small bank of quotations that can serve several possible questions is a DP2 autumn job, not an April one.
