whyPoints.description: Al Ain is under ADEK, not KHDA, and the MoHRE private tuition permit is a federal requirement with a published legal basis. We state what each authority does, link the official route, and claim no accreditation from any of them.

whyPoints.title: A stated boundary on coursework
whyPoints.description: The investigation and the Extended Essay must be the student's own work. Our tutors teach, question, mark and give criterion-referenced feedback, and they produce no part of a submission. The boundary is explained to the student in the first session.

whyPoints.title: Plans that are allowed to end
whyPoints.description: A single-theme repair block runs three to five sessions and then stops. An investigation clinic is four to six hours. Saying so in advance is how a family can tell the difference between support and a subscription.

faqs.question: How many weeks of Physics HL tutoring does an Al Ain student usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends on which of three problems you have. A single Higher Level topic that went past too fast, such as induction or thermodynamics, is typically three to five sessions. The scientific investigation is a four-to-six-hour block spread across planning, analysis and drafting. A predicted grade that has slipped across the whole course is a term of weekly sessions, because the repair work sits earlier in the syllabus than the symptom. We say which of the three it is after the trial lesson, and block bookings for the first two carry an agreed finish point rather than rolling on.

faqs.question: Which parts of IB Physics are Higher Level only?
faqs.answer: Under the current guide the Higher Level additions sit in named sub-topics rather than being spread evenly: rigid body mechanics and Galilean and special relativity in Theme A, thermodynamics in Theme B, electromagnetic induction in Theme D, and quantum physics in Theme E, along with extended treatment of interference and the Doppler effect in Theme C. Theme C and Theme D depend heavily on the vector and energy work from Theme A, so a student who joins Higher Level late loses more than a proportional share. Confirm the exact sub-topic list against your school's own scheme of work.

faqs.question: Is Paper 1B worth training separately from the rest of the course?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the clearest return on tutoring hours in the final months. Paper 1B asks students to handle unfamiliar experimental data: plot it, linearise it, read a gradient as a physical quantity, propagate uncertainty, and judge whether the data support a relationship. The skill set is small and repeatable, which is why four or five focused sessions move marks. General content revision in the same hours usually moves fewer, because by the spring of DP2 content knowledge is rarely the binding constraint on a Higher Level script.

faqs.question: Why does my child suddenly find Theme D fields impossible?
faqs.answer: Almost always because Theme A was never fully secured. Fields work assumes fluent vector resolution, comfort with inverse-square relationships and the ability to track energy through a system, all taught in the first term of DP1 and all easy to get through with approximations. Theme D does not tolerate approximation. The visible wall is in fields; the actual gap is a year earlier. A diagnostic session that asks the student to attempt a Theme A question aloud usually finds it inside twenty minutes, and fixing it there is faster than re-teaching Theme D repeatedly.

faqs.question: What does the scientific investigation get marked out of?
faqs.answer: Twenty-four marks, across four criteria carrying six marks each: Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation. The report is capped at 3,000 words, it is marked by the school and moderated by the IB, and it carries 20% of the final grade at both Higher and Standard Level. Research design is decided before any data exists, which makes it the criterion where early help is worth most. Evaluation is the one UAE students most often lose marks on, because it needs weaknesses specific to this method rather than general statements about human error.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Physics investigation without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clear. A tutor can question whether the research question is answerable with school equipment, teach uncertainty propagation on separate practice data, mark the student's own draft against each criterion, and say which paragraph is failing and why. A tutor cannot supply text, build graphs that go into the report, rewrite paragraphs, or suggest a conclusion the student has not reached from their own data. The test we use with students is whether they could defend every sentence to their school supervisor unaided. If not, it should not be submitted.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Physics tutor to our home in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Lessons for Al Ain families are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. The reason is supply rather than cost: a Higher Level Physics specialist who has taught the current guide and marked investigations against the current criteria is hard to find within driving distance of any single Al Ain district, and online delivery removes distance from the matching problem entirely.

faqs.question: What do in-home Physics tutors in Al Ain charge compared with online?
faqs.answer: Market sources put in-home one-to-one tutoring in the UAE at roughly AED 180-500 an hour depending on level and tutor, with Bestimate's 2026 survey quoting AED 180-350 for general in-home work and specialist IB rates at AED 200-450 and above. Online bands sit lower for comparable qualifications, largely because no travel hour is being paid for. Those are market figures from the providers named, not an IB Gram price list; our own rate is quoted after the free trial against the level and the weeks remaining.

faqs.question: Is Al Ain under KHDA or a different school regulator?
faqs.answer: ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, Al Ain included. Dubai schools sit under KHDA, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the Ministry of Education. The distinction matters because inspection reports, policy circulars and staff conduct rules for an Al Ain campus come from ADEK. Any page that explains Dubai's KHDA framework to an Al Ain parent is describing the wrong regulator.

faqs.question: Does a Physics tutor in Al Ain need a government permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any quoted amount with scepticism. Ask any tutor to show the permit.

faqs.question: Can my child's own school Physics teacher tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: In Abu Dhabi emirate this is reported to be prohibited. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported to bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct has been reported to carry the same restriction. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it. The practical position for an Al Ain parent is that an offer of your child's classroom teacher for paid lessons is a question to raise with the school, not a convenience to accept quietly.

faqs.question: My child has eight weeks until the papers. Is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks is enough to change a paper grade and not enough to re-teach two years. The plan in that window is built from the student's own marked scripts rather than from a revision sequence: triage the themes into secure, shaky and abandoned, drill Paper 1B data analysis as a separate skill, and work command terms on Paper 2 questions that cross themes. We will tell you honestly if the realistic gain is half a grade rather than two, because buying twenty sessions on a false expectation is worse for the student than buying eight on a true one.

faqs.question: Will the weekly Physics slot still work through Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most Al Ain families ask for it. School hours shorten during Ramadan and the useful study window moves later in the evening, so the weekly slot usually shifts rather than pausing. Keeping the same tutor across the move matters more than keeping the same hour, because a tutor who has seen a student's scripts for a term does not need to re-diagnose anything. Slots also move for school examination weeks, family travel and the days either side of the eid holidays without losing your place with that tutor.

faqs.question: Does Physics HL affect the Ministry of Education equivalency process?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is run by the Ministry of Education and no tutoring provider performs or guarantees it. For British-track students the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. No IB points threshold should be taken from a tutoring page, this one included. Confirm the IB position on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority before planning around it.

faqs.question: What happens if no Physics HL specialist is free at the slot we need?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substituting a general science tutor. The Gulf Standard Time early-evening window is the most contested part of the week for Higher Level sciences, and a Physics HL match sometimes means waiting a week or taking a slightly earlier slot. Where the wait is not workable, the honest options are a different weekday, a weekend session, or starting with the component that is least tutor-specific, such as Paper 1B data technique, while the specialist slot opens up. We will tell you which applies.

al-ain/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the deadline that is closest
al-ain/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.closingBody: If you are reading this in DP1, the thing that pays for itself is the investigation: get the research question pressure-tested before any data is collected, and the Research design marks follow. If you are reading it in the spring of DP2, bring your child's last two marked Physics scripts to the trial lesson instead of a list of topics. Tell us the school, the level, the theme that is not working and the next internal deadline, and we will match an IB DP Physics HL tutor against that rather than against a general subject request. Lessons run live online, one-to-one, timed to Gulf Standard Time, and the first one is free with no card details taken.

al-ain/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Diploma Programme Psychology at Standard and Higher Level: the biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches, the option topics, research methodology and the internally assessed experimental study. Al Ain students are matched on level and option choice first, then on a workable evening slot.

intro.heading: Psychology taught against the rules your school actually works under
paragraphs: Almost every page about IB Psychology tuition in the UAE is written as though the UAE were one place with one regulator. It is not. Al Ain sits inside the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, which means your child's school is licensed and accredited by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, and not by Dubai's KHDA. That distinction changes which inspection report you should be reading, which authority sets the rules on teachers tutoring privately, and which published guidance applies to the Arabic and Islamic Education lessons sitting in your child's timetable next to Psychology.

It also changes the local supply picture. Al Ain is 130 kilometres inland from the capital and its private-school set is small, so Psychology is often a single class covering both Standard and Higher Level, with option topics chosen by the teacher rather than by the student. A Higher Level student needs two option topics, research methodology for the third paper and the Higher Level extensions inside each core approach. In a combined class, some of that gets fewer hours than it needs — not through neglect, but through arithmetic.

Psychology is also the Diploma subject most often chosen by students who expect it to be easier than it is. It reads approachably, it has no mathematics at Standard Level beyond descriptive statistics, and the content is genuinely interesting. Then the first assessed essay comes back with a 3, because the student wrote everything they knew about a study instead of answering the command term in the question. That failure is specific, diagnosable and entirely fixable, and it is what most of the sessions on this page are spent on.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For Al Ain that is the format that works rather than a compromise: it puts a Psychology specialist who has marked these essays in front of your child without anyone driving to the capital, and it keeps a weekly slot alive through a term instead of collapsing the first time the school run runs late.

What follows is the version of this subject anchored to this emirate rather than to a generic UAE. Who regulates your school and what their published report actually means for a tuition decision. Which Al Ain campuses run the subject, at which levels, and how a combined Standard and Higher Level class changes what gets taught thoroughly. The assessed components and the command terms that decide the grade more often than content does. The experimental study from design approval to submission, counted backwards from the school's own internal deadline. The mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies lessons that sit alongside the Diploma and quietly eat the evenings a revision plan assumed were free. The Ministry of Education equivalency route for a student heading to a UAE university, with the figures we can source and a plain statement of the one figure we will not publish. And the market rate in AED, with the date it was read and the source named, because a price without a method behind it helps nobody choose.

al-ain/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.programmesIntro: Psychology exists only at Diploma level in the IB, but the route into it starts earlier and the exit route runs through equivalency and university admission. These are the stages that matter for an Al Ain family, with what each one means in this emirate specifically.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: There is no MYP Psychology, so the feeders are Individuals and Societies and the MYP sciences. What transfers is the ability to use evidence to support a claim and the habit of writing to a criterion rather than to a word count. What does not transfer is essay discipline under a command term, because MYP marking is far more forgiving of a student who writes everything they know.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Ain the MYP and DP cohorts are often substantially the same group of students moving up through one small campus, so a year group that was never pushed on evidence-based writing in Individuals and Societies arrives in DP1 Psychology with the same habit intact. Ask the school which MYP subject your child's Psychology teacher also teaches; the answer frequently explains the house style of the marking.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, first year
programmes.description: DP1 covers the three approaches to behaviour — biological, cognitive and sociocultural — plus research methodology and ethical considerations. The experimental study is usually designed and run late in DP1 or across the summer. A student who finishes DP1 able to recite studies but unable to evaluate them has done the easier half of the year.
programmes.countryNote: The Al Ain academic year runs roughly September to late June with a long July and August break. For Psychology that break is the natural window for the experimental study, because running a replication needs participants and time that term weeks do not give. Families travelling for most of the summer should have the design approved before they leave rather than after they return.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, second year
programmes.description: DP2 adds the option topics, the Higher Level extensions and, for Higher Level students, the research methodology paper built on an unseen abridged study. The experimental study report is finished and submitted, mocks are sat, and the final term is essay technique against the published criteria rather than new content.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain students sit the May session. Internal coursework deadlines are set by the school's Diploma coordinator and sit months before the papers because teachers need time to mark, moderate and upload. Get those dates in writing from the coordinator rather than from the student, and treat them as the real deadlines in any plan.

programmes.name: Higher Level Psychology
programmes.description: Higher Level adds a second option topic, the Higher Level extension content inside each core approach, and a paper on research methodology that presents an unseen abridged study and asks about its design, ethics and conclusions. That paper rewards a student who has read real studies critically all year, and punishes one who has only memorised the prescribed ones.
programmes.countryNote: If your child is one of very few Higher Level Psychology students in an Al Ain cohort, ask the coordinator how many weekly hours the second option topic and the research methodology paper receive. Combined-level classes in small schools tend to teach the shared core thoroughly and compress the Higher Level additions, and that compression is exactly where one-to-one time pays.

al-ain/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.subjectsIntro: Psychology is the subject on this page. These are the Diploma subjects our tutors cover for Al Ain students, described by what the assessment actually rewards rather than by what the syllabus contains.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: The biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches, one or two option topics, research methodology and the experimental study. Marks are lost on command terms ignored, on studies described rather than used as evidence, and on evaluation that lists strengths and weaknesses without connecting them to the claim being argued.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The usual partner for a Psychology student heading towards medicine or neuroscience. The overlap with the biological approach is real — localisation, neurotransmission, hormones — but Biology's assessment demands far more precision in terminology and far more care with data analysis.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Shares Psychology's essay structure and its need for real-world application, and the behavioural economics content overlaps directly with cognitive biases. Students who evaluate well in one subject usually transfer the skill, which makes a shared tutor efficient where the timetable allows.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Motivation theory, organisational culture and leadership overlap with the sociocultural approach. The assessment rewards application to a named organisation rather than theory recall, which trains the same discipline the Psychology essays need.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Another group 3 subject Al Ain schools commonly pair with Psychology. The written papers reward precise use of case studies and data, and students who can structure a Psychology essay generally structure a Geography one well once the command terms are mapped across.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The subject that most often limits a Psychology student's total, because Paper 1 is an unseen text under time pressure and the Individual Oral needs a global issue chosen months ahead. Both reward planning rather than flair.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The statistics content is directly useful to the experimental study: sampling, measures of central tendency, dispersion and the logic of inferential testing. Students doing Psychology and this course together tend to write stronger analysis sections.

subjects.name: Arabic and UAE mandatory subjects
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies run alongside any international curriculum in UAE private schools under federal rules. These are separate from the Diploma and marked by the school, but they occupy timetable space and homework time that a Psychology revision plan has to work around.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Psychology is a popular Extended Essay subject and a natural source of Theory of Knowledge examples, because the subject's own debates about evidence and method are knowledge questions already. Support is teaching, feedback and process coaching on the student's own work only.

al-ain/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.regionsIntro: Al Ain is low-density and spread out, and for a weekly online session the only variable that matters is when the household is genuinely home and settled. These are the districts Psychology enquiries most often come from, and what each one does to the evening.

regions.name: Al Jimi
regions.note: Central and close to several of the older campuses, so a 16:00 start is realistic. Psychology enquiries here often come mid-DP1, after the first assessed essay comes back lower than the student expected.

regions.name: Asharej
regions.note: The university district, where households are frequently academic and the student has often read well beyond the syllabus. The work needed is usually structure and command-term discipline rather than content, which is a fast kind of improvement.

regions.name: Al Mutaredh
regions.note: Older villa area near the centre with short school runs. Families here commonly book Psychology alongside a second group 3 subject, which is easier to timetable as one tutor across two evenings than two tutors competing for the same slot.

regions.name: Al Towayya
regions.note: Well connected by the ring roads, so arrival times are predictable. Predictability is what keeps a weekly Psychology slot intact across a whole term, and it matters more than raw distance from the school.

regions.name: Falaj Hazzaa
regions.note: Established central district within reach of several campuses. Requests from here often involve a student who chose Psychology expecting a lighter workload and met the evaluation requirement in term two.

regions.note: Towards the southern edge, where a 15:00 pick-up can mean arriving home after 16:15. A 17:00 or later start is the version that survives; earlier bookings from Zakher are the ones that quietly stop happening.

regions.name: Hili and Al Foah
regions.note: The northern districts near the Oman side of the city. Long runs in both directions make an online slot the only realistic weekly format, and they are also why the drive to a capital-based tutor rarely lasts beyond a few weeks.

sections.heading: ADEK, not KHDA: what your regulator actually changes
paragraphs: Al Ain is part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so your child's private school is regulated by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Dubai's KHDA has no authority here. This matters practically rather than academically: the inspection report you should be reading is ADEK's, the fee approval route is ADEK's, and the professional-conduct rules that apply to your child's own Psychology teacher are Abu Dhabi's.

That last point is worth knowing before you ask the school for private help. Press reporting of ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff indicates that teachers are prohibited from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Treat that as press-reported rather than as ADEK's exact current wording, and verify it against the current ADEK policy document before relying on it. The practical consequence is simple: the obvious solution of paying your child's own teacher is the one route that is likely closed.

The regulator map across the UAE is five bodies, not one, and no competitor page in this market sets it out. Dubai has KHDA, responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi, and therefore Al Ain, has ADEK. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority. Ras Al Khaimah has the Department of Knowledge. The Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so in those emirates curriculum approval sits with the regulator and not only inspection.

None of this is bureaucratic trivia for a parent choosing tuition. It tells you whose published report to read when judging a school, whose rules constrain who may legally teach your child privately, and which authority to contact when something goes wrong. All of it comes from the federal portal at u.ae, which is the source to check rather than any tutoring company's summary of it.

sections.heading: Which Al Ain schools run Psychology, and how it is usually staffed
paragraphs: Psychology is a group 3 option, and in a city with a small private-school set that makes it a departmental decision rather than a guaranteed offering. Some Al Ain campuses run it at both levels. Some run a single combined class. Some do not offer it at all and steer students into Geography or Business Management. Before you look for a tutor, establish from the Diploma coordinator which levels are actually running for your child's cohort, which option topics the department has chosen, and how many weekly contact hours the Higher Level additions receive.

The combined-level class is the pattern worth understanding, because it produces a predictable gap. The three core approaches are shared between Standard and Higher Level, so a combined class teaches them to everybody and teaches them well. What gets compressed is the Higher Level-only material: the second option topic, the extension content inside each approach, and the research methodology paper. In a class of fifteen with four Higher Level students, that compression is a timetabling fact rather than a failure of teaching.

The option topics are the second thing to pin down. A Standard Level student studies one option; a Higher Level student studies two. Which options your child's school has chosen determines what revision material is relevant, and a tutor working from the wrong option wastes the term. Abnormal psychology, developmental psychology, health psychology and human relationships each carry their own studies, their own debates and their own typical essay questions, and they are not interchangeable.

Finally, ask how the experimental study is organised. Some departments assign a narrow menu of replicable studies to keep the process manageable; others let students propose their own and then spend weeks rescuing undeliverable designs. Knowing which model your school uses tells you whether the support you need is design help in DP1 or analysis and write-up help later.

sections.heading: The assessed components and what each one rewards
paragraphs: Diploma Psychology is assessed through written papers plus one internally assessed experimental study. Standard Level students sit papers on the core and on one option, alongside the experimental study. Higher Level students sit the core paper, a paper covering two options and an additional paper on research methodology, alongside the same experimental study. Exact durations and component weightings are published in the subject guide your child's cohort follows, so confirm them with the Diploma coordinator before a revision plan is built on them.

The core paper is the one most students underestimate. It mixes short answers requiring tight, controlled responses with an extended response demanding a sustained argument. Short answers fail when a student writes an essay; extended responses fail when a student writes a list. Both failures come from the same root, which is not reading the command term and not planning the shape of the answer before writing.

The options paper rewards depth over breadth. A student who knows four studies well in a single option outperforms one who knows twelve superficially, because the marks sit in how the evidence is used rather than in how much is cited. The Higher Level research methodology paper is different in kind: it presents an unseen abridged study and asks about its design, ethics and conclusions, which rewards a student who has spent the year reading studies critically rather than memorising them.

The experimental study is the only component entirely within the student's control. It is a report on a replication of a simple published experiment, assessed against published criteria, and the commonest failures are a design too ambitious to deliver, ethical considerations treated as a paragraph of boilerplate, and an evaluation that lists limitations without explaining what each one does to the conclusion.

sections.heading: The command terms that decide a Psychology grade
paragraphs: More Psychology marks are lost to command terms than to missing content. The question tells the student exactly what kind of answer is wanted, and a student who writes a good answer to a different question gets credit for almost none of it. Outline wants a brief account. Describe wants a detailed account without judgement. Explain wants reasons and causes. Discuss wants a balanced review of the arguments. Evaluate wants a judgement supported by evidence on both sides. Contrast wants differences made explicit rather than two separate descriptions placed side by side.

The diagnostic is quick and you can run it at home. Take your child's last marked essay and ask them, without looking, what the command term in the question was. A student who cannot say is a student whose essays will keep scoring in the middle regardless of how much they revise, because the revision adds content to an answer whose shape was wrong. This is the single highest-return thing tuition fixes in this subject, and it usually takes weeks rather than terms.

Evaluation is where it bites hardest. Students are taught to produce strengths and weaknesses, so they produce a list: the sample was small, the setting was artificial, the study was ethically questionable. None of that scores well on its own. What scores is connecting the limitation to the claim: if the sample was twenty undergraduates in one country, say what that does to the generalisation the student has just made. The difference between those two answers is often two grades.

The second recurring failure is the study used as decoration. A named study dropped into a paragraph without being tied to the argument reads as recall. The habit worth building is one sentence of claim, one of evidence from a named study, one of what that evidence does to the claim. Practising that three-sentence unit on unfamiliar questions is more useful than rereading notes, and it is what timed practice in the final term should mostly consist of.

sections.heading: The experimental study, from design to submission
paragraphs: The experimental study is a report on a replication of a simple published experiment, and almost every problem with it is created at the design stage. A student who picks a study requiring specialist equipment, a large sample or a sensitive population has chosen a project that cannot be delivered inside an Al Ain school term, and the weeks spent discovering that are weeks taken from the write-up. The useful discipline is to test the design against four questions before any data is collected: can the participants be recruited, can the procedure be standardised, can the data be analysed with the statistics the student knows, and is it ethically defensible.

Ethics is not a paragraph to be added at the end. Informed consent, the right to withdraw, debriefing, protection from harm and the handling of data about minors all have to be thought through before the study runs, and in a school setting the participants are frequently other students. A report where the ethical considerations clearly came after the data is visible to a marker in a sentence, and it loses marks it never needed to lose.

A tutor's role here has a hard boundary and we state it at the first session. A tutor may explain the published criteria, challenge whether a design is deliverable, teach the statistics, question whether an evaluation actually connects to the conclusion, and read a draft and say where evidence is missing. A tutor may not design the study, analyse the data on the student's behalf or rewrite the report. The experimental study is assessed as the student's own research, and anything else puts the diploma at risk under IB academic-honesty rules rather than merely being against our policy.

Count the plan backwards from the school's internal deadline rather than forwards from today. Subtract a fortnight that belongs to the student for final checking, then the write-up, the analysis, the data collection and the design approval. For most Al Ain cohorts the design needs approving inside DP1, which is why the long summer matters: it is the only block of time in two years when a student can run a replication without a timetable in the way.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: A Psychology revision plan for a UAE student has to work around subjects that do not appear in the Diploma at all. Under federal rules, private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Those subjects sit in the timetable alongside the Diploma, carry their own homework, and are assessed by the school rather than by the IB. Parents planning tuition around a Diploma timetable alone routinely underestimate how much of the week they occupy.

The most detailed published guidance on how these subjects run is KHDA's mandatory-subjects document, which applies to Dubai rather than to Al Ain but is worth reading as the clearest statement of the model. It requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and social studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. It sets Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies.

The same guidance calculates instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. It also states that for these subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, and that schools must ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate approval from KHDA to teach them. That last constraint is why no tutoring provider should offer bespoke material for these subjects: the content is not ours to vary.

For an Al Ain family the practical takeaway is scheduling. Find out how many timetabled periods a week the mandatory subjects take and what homework they carry, and build the Psychology slot into the evening that is genuinely free rather than the one that looks free on a Diploma-only timetable.

sections.heading: Equivalency: what a Psychology student needs for a UAE university
paragraphs: Families in Al Ain frequently ask whether a Diploma with Psychology will be accepted for a UAE university, and the answer runs through the Ministry of Education's equivalency process rather than through the subject choice. Equivalency is the recognition of a foreign secondary certificate against UAE requirements, and it is a process the family and the school complete with the authority. No tutoring provider performs it, guarantees it or speeds it up, and anyone implying otherwise is misdescribing a regulatory process.

The requirements that are properly sourced are the British-track ones. Students on that route must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five required subjects. That five-subject rule is worth knowing precisely, because at least one provider ranking for these searches publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong.

The American-track requirements are also published: English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics through at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB specifically there is no points threshold we are prepared to publish, because we have not read one on the Ministry's own site. Anyone quoting an IB equivalency score without a moe.gov.ae source is guessing, and a guess about a regulatory threshold is the worst kind of error to inherit.

The practical advice for a Psychology student is unchanged by any of this: take the subject combination the intended degree asks for, keep the certificates and transcripts the authority will want, and ask the school's university counsellor to confirm the equivalency route early rather than in the final term. Tutoring does not enter into equivalency at all, and no page should imply that it does.

sections.heading: What Psychology tuition costs in Al Ain, and how to read the figures
paragraphs: Most providers in this market publish no rate at all, which is why parents ring four companies and get four deflections. The bands below come from UAE provider rate cards and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, read in October 2026. They describe what the market charges, not what IB Gram charges. Al Ain prices sit inside the Abu Dhabi emirate rather than Dubai, and in-home rates here carry heavier travel loading than the capital because the city is spread out and tutors are fewer.

Use the table as a budget tool rather than as a quote. A single weekly 60-minute session with a qualified online subject tutor at the middle of the band gives a predictable monthly commitment, which most families manage better than a panic block bought three weeks before a paper. Monthly packages advertised in the UAE have included roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and roughly AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, which is the clearest illustration available of what travel time adds to a rate.

Two traps are specific to this subject. The first is paying a specialist rate for general essay help: a generic humanities tutor can improve a paragraph but cannot mark an extended response against Psychology's own criteria or tell you why an evaluation scored poorly. The second is buying a block of hours rather than a plan, which produces a pleasant tutor, a satisfied student and a grade that has not moved. Ask what the next six sessions cover, what should be different by the end of them, and how you will know.

On the figures we do not publish: there is no IB Gram price list on this page, no satisfaction percentage, no star rating and no claimed grade improvement. A number without its sample, date and method attached tells a parent nothing, and we would rather show the market bands with their source than an invented statistic about ourselves.

sections.heading: How lessons are delivered, and the home-tutor question answered straight
paragraphs: Parents in Al Ain searching for Psychology help are usually weighing three options: a local tutor who can travel to the district, a weekly drive to a specialist in the capital, or an online one-to-one specialist. It is worth knowing what each actually costs. A local in-home tutor is priced with travel included, which in a spread-out city pushes the rate towards the upper end of the market band. The capital drive is around 130 kilometres each way, which is roughly three hours of travel on a school night on top of the lesson.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video; home visits are a service we run only in India. We put that before the argument rather than after it, because a family who wants someone physically present should not have to read four paragraphs to find out. What we would say for the format is narrower and more honest than the usual pitch: it is not that screens are better than rooms, it is that in Al Ain the online pool contains Psychology specialists who have marked these essays and the local pool frequently does not.

There is a second reason the format suits this subject. Psychology tuition is largely essay work, and essay work is done well when the tutor and the student are looking at the same marked script, annotating the same paragraph, at the same time. A shared screen does that cleanly. It also means the record of what was taught survives: the annotated scripts accumulate somewhere both the student and the parent can see, rather than in a notebook that gets lost in March.

Scheduling is the last piece. Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time, usually between 16:30 and 21:00 on school nights, built around the Al Ain school run and around the mandatory-subject homework load. During Ramadan most families move the slot later and shorten it; a 60-minute session after Iftar beats a 90-minute one that nobody has the energy for. The summer is treated as the experimental study window rather than as a gap.

A tutor working from the wrong option topic wastes a term, and this is the one piece of information schools often have not put in writing anywhere a parent can see.

process.title: A free first session with the actual tutor
process.description: Not a sales call. The tutor works from your child's last marked essay, open on a shared screen, and shows what the command term in that question was asking for. You hear how they explain something your child has already lost marks on once.

process.title: A short written plan with dates
process.description: After the trial you get a plan naming what the next six sessions cover and what should be different afterwards: command-term control, a usable bank of studies, an experimental study design approved. If the plan has nothing specific in it, that is a reason to decline.

process.description: Scheduled around the Al Ain school run and the mandatory-subject homework load, and kept the same every week. Ramadan timings move later rather than being cancelled, and the summer is planned as the experimental study window well before July.

process.title: Review against evidence, not impressions
process.description: Every few weeks we compare the plan with what has happened: marks on timed essays, experimental study milestones met or missed, command terms now controlled. If it is not working we change the plan or the tutor, and we raise that conversation rather than waiting for you to.

faqs.question: Which authority regulates my child's school in Al Ain, and why does it matter for tutoring?
faqs.answer: ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools across the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, which includes Al Ain. Dubai's KHDA has no authority here. It matters for three practical reasons: the inspection report you should read when judging a school is ADEK's, the fee approval route is ADEK's, and the professional-conduct rules that govern whether your child's own teacher may tutor them privately are Abu Dhabi's. Any tuition advice written as though the UAE had a single regulator is advice about somebody else's school.

faqs.question: Can I pay my child's own Psychology teacher for private lessons in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Probably not, and this is the question most Al Ain parents ask first. Press reporting of ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates that private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi are prohibited from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Treat that as press-reported rather than exact current wording and check the current ADEK policy document. In practice, plan on needing someone outside the school.

faqs.question: Does every Al Ain school offer IB Psychology at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: No. Psychology is a group 3 option and in a city with a small private-school set its availability is a departmental decision that changes year to year. Some Al Ain campuses run both levels, some run a single combined class, and some do not offer the subject at all. Ask the Diploma coordinator which levels are running for your child's cohort specifically, which option topics the department has chosen, and how many weekly contact hours the Higher Level additions receive. The third answer is the one that predicts whether outside support will be needed.

faqs.question: Why do my child's Psychology essays keep scoring in the middle despite good revision?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the answers are the wrong shape rather than because content is missing. Take the last marked essay and ask your child, without looking, what the command term in the question was. Outline wants a brief account; describe wants detail without judgement; discuss wants a balanced review; evaluate wants a judgement supported on both sides; contrast wants differences made explicit. A student who cannot name the command term will keep scoring mid-band however much they revise, because revision adds content to an answer whose structure was already wrong.

faqs.question: How do I know which Psychology option topics my child is actually studying?
faqs.answer: Ask the department in writing, because this is the single piece of information most often missing from reports and most often guessed at. A Standard Level student studies one option topic and a Higher Level student studies two, chosen from abnormal psychology, developmental psychology, health psychology and human relationships. Each carries its own studies, debates and typical questions, and they are not interchangeable. A tutor working from the wrong option will teach competently for a term and move nothing, so confirm this before the first paid session rather than after.

faqs.question: What does a strong evaluation paragraph in IB Psychology actually look like?
faqs.answer: It connects a limitation to the claim rather than listing it. A weak paragraph says the sample was small, the setting was artificial and the ethics were questionable. A strong one says the sample was twenty undergraduates in one country, so the generalisation just made about adult behaviour cannot be supported beyond that population, and then says what evidence would be needed instead. The usable habit is a three-sentence unit: one sentence of claim, one of evidence from a named study, one of what that evidence does to the claim.

faqs.question: How should my child choose a replicable study for the Psychology experimental study?
faqs.answer: Test any candidate design against four questions before collecting data. Can the participants actually be recruited in a school setting; can the procedure be standardised so every participant experiences the same thing; can the results be analysed with the statistics your child already knows; and is it ethically defensible with minors. A design that fails any of the four should be abandoned in the planning weeks rather than rescued in the write-up weeks. Ambitious designs are the single commonest reason this component underperforms.

faqs.question: What can a tutor legitimately do on the Psychology experimental study?
faqs.answer: A tutor may explain the published assessment criteria, challenge whether a design is deliverable, teach the descriptive and inferential statistics, question whether an evaluation connects to the conclusion, and read the student's own draft and say where evidence is missing. A tutor may not design the study, run the analysis on the student's behalf or rewrite the report. The experimental study is assessed as the student's own research, and crossing that line is a malpractice risk that falls on the student. We state the boundary at the first session rather than after a booking.

faqs.question: Do the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons affect a Diploma revision plan?
faqs.answer: Yes, more than most families expect. Under federal rules UAE private schools must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed curriculum, and those subjects carry their own timetable periods, homework and assessments. KHDA's mandatory-subjects guidance, which is Dubai-specific but the clearest published version of the model, calculates instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. Before fixing a weekly Psychology slot, find out how many periods and how much homework these subjects take, and build around the evening that is genuinely free.

faqs.question: Is the IB Diploma with Psychology accepted for equivalency in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is a Ministry of Education process that recognises a foreign secondary certificate, and it is completed by the family and school with the authority rather than by any tutoring provider. The British-track requirements are published: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education, plus one Advanced Level at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at E. For the IB specifically we will not publish a points threshold, because we have not read one on the Ministry's own site. Verify on moe.gov.ae and ask the school's counsellor early.

faqs.question: What does weekly IB Psychology tuition cost for a family in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Market rates in the UAE for a qualified subject tutor working online run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, and for an IB specialist roughly AED 200 to 450 and upwards, according to provider rate cards and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table read in October 2026. In-home rates sit higher, around AED 180 to 500, because travel is priced in, and in a spread-out city that loading is heavier than in the capital. Those are market bands and not our price list. The first session with us is free, before any figure is discussed.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Psychology tutor to our home in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs only in India. Tutoring for Al Ain families is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We say so before any pricing conversation, because a family who wants someone physically present should know immediately. For an essay-based subject the format carries a real advantage: the tutor and student annotate the same marked script at the same time on a shared screen, and the annotated scripts accumulate somewhere both the student and the parent can see.

faqs.question: Is it worth driving to Abu Dhabi weekly for a face-to-face Psychology specialist?
faqs.answer: Rarely, once the time is counted. Al Ain to Abu Dhabi island is around 130 kilometres each way, so a weekly session costs roughly three hours of travel on a school night on top of the lesson. Over two Diploma years that is a very large number of hours, and those sessions are the first thing cancelled whenever anything else in the week goes wrong. Since Psychology tuition is largely work on marked scripts, a live video session with a shared screen gets a wider pool of specialists and no travel at all.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does an Al Ain Psychology student usually need?
faqs.answer: One weekly session of 60 or 90 minutes covers most term-time cases, with a short block around the experimental study and a denser run in the final twelve weeks. Two sessions a week makes sense when there is a specific backlog with a deadline attached, such as an unwritten report with two months left. Beyond two, the problem is usually work habits rather than subject knowledge, and paid hours are a slow and expensive way to fix a routine that needs changing at home instead.

faqs.question: Can sessions move later during Ramadan and still be useful?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most Al Ain families do exactly that. The usual pattern is a shorter session later in the evening, after Iftar, rather than the normal slot at a time when nobody has the energy to argue about methodology. A focused 60 minutes at 21:00 is worth more than 90 distracted minutes at 17:00. Essay marking and feedback work particularly well in that format because the thinking is short and concentrated. The frequency stays the same; only the timing and length change, and the slot is agreed before Ramadan starts rather than week by week.

faqs.question: My child chose Psychology thinking it would be lighter than a science. Was that a mistake?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, but the expectation needs correcting early. Psychology has no heavy mathematics at Standard Level and the content reads approachably, which is why it is often chosen as the easier group 3 option. The assessment is not easier: it demands sustained evaluative writing under command terms, a bank of studies deployed as evidence rather than recited, and an experimental study with real design and ethics decisions. Students who adjust in the first term do well. Students who discover it in DP2 lose a year of essay practice they cannot get back.

al-ain/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the option topics and the last marked essay
al-ain/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.closingBody: Two things make a first session useful: the option topics your child's department actually chose, and the most recent marked Psychology essay. Send us the level and those two items and we will match a Diploma Psychology tutor who has taught that option, at a time that fits an Al Ain evening. The first session is free and runs on the real script rather than on a generic diagnostic, so you can hear how a command term gets explained before you commit to anything. Afterwards you get a short written plan with dates, and the decision is yours.

al-ain/ib-dp-theory-of-knowledge-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach the Diploma core rather than a single subject: the prescribed title essay, the exhibition, and the reading habits that hold both together. Each works online with Al Ain families and starts with a free trial lesson used as a diagnosis.

intro.heading: Start from the date, not from the subject
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge is the one Diploma course with no textbook, no past papers to work through and no content a student can revise the night before. That is why it behaves so differently from Chemistry or Maths in a family's planning. A parent can watch a maths grade for a term and act in week ten. With TOK, the course produces exactly two pieces of assessed work in two years, and both of them have a date attached. Miss the window around either one and there is nothing left to fix.

So this page is organised as a timeline rather than a syllabus tour. The first question any useful session asks is not what your child thinks about knowledge. It is where they are standing. A DP1 student in February who has seen one lesson on areas of knowledge is in a different position from a DP2 student in October holding a marked exhibition commentary and a prescribed title they do not understand. Those two students need different work, in a different order, and the number of weeks available decides which.

Al Ain adds its own constraints to that timeline. The city sits roughly 130 kilometres inland from Abu Dhabi island, under ADEK rather than KHDA, and its private school set is much smaller than the capital's. For the Diploma core that matters in a practical way: a school with two or three DP cohorts often has one TOK teacher carrying every student, and the internal deadline that teacher sets is the only one your child will see until the school uploads. There is rarely a second specialist down the corridor to ask.

What a Theory of Knowledge tutor in Al Ain can usefully add is not more content. It is structure, a second reader, and a schedule that survives contact with the real school year. An outside reader who has marked against the TOK assessment instrument can tell you in one session whether a draft is descriptive or evaluative, whether the knowledge arguments are arguments at all, and whether the three objects in an exhibition are doing different jobs or the same job three times. That diagnosis is cheap. Rewriting a 1,600-word essay in the last fortnight is not.

Everything here is delivered as online one-to-one TOK sessions over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Al Ain or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. For this course that limitation costs a family nothing and gains them something real. The work is reading, questioning and redrafting on a shared screen, and the pool of people who have actually assessed TOK work is national rather than whatever lives within a twenty-minute drive of Al Jimi.

al-ain/ib-dp-theory-of-knowledge-tutor.programmesIntro: Theory of Knowledge belongs to the Diploma Programme, but the thinking it assesses is built earlier. Al Ain schools running the full IB continuum hand their DP1 cohort students who have already been asked to justify a claim; schools that begin at DP1 do not. The three programmes below are where that difference is made.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The two-year Diploma carries three core elements alongside six subjects: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. TOK is assessed through an internal exhibition and an externally marked essay on one of six prescribed titles released by the IB for each session. The grade is a letter, and the letter combines with the Extended Essay grade to award core points toward the final total.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Ain the DP cohort in any one school is usually small, so a student's TOK experience depends heavily on one teacher's timetable. ADEK licenses and inspects these schools, and its published inspection reports are the only outside read a parent gets on how well a school delivers the core. Ask the coordinator for the school's internal exhibition and essay deadlines in writing at the start of DP1.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP asks students to evaluate sources, state a perspective and reflect on their own process through interdisciplinary units and the Personal Project. Those are the same moves TOK assesses two years later, under different names. A student who has written a Personal Project report with a genuine reflection section arrives in DP1 already able to do the thing TOK criterion language asks for.
programmes.countryNote: Only part of Al Ain's private school set runs the MYP, so a typical DP1 class here mixes MYP graduates with students arriving from Cambridge IGCSE, CBSE and American diplomas. That mix is the single biggest reason TOK marks spread so widely in one Al Ain cohort, and it is the first thing a trial lesson should establish about your child.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs DP courses with a career-related study and its own core, including a reflective project rather than TOK. Families comparing routes in the final IGCSE year sometimes discover the CP exists only after choices close. The reflective project rewards the same evaluative writing TOK does, so support for one transfers usefully to the other.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision across the Emirate of Abu Dhabi is thin and concentrated on the island rather than in Al Ain, so inland families weighing it should confirm directly with ADEK's school listing and the school itself before assuming a place exists. Where a student does sit the reflective project, the same online one-to-one supervision model applies.

al-ain/ib-dp-theory-of-knowledge-tutor.subjectsIntro: A TOK essay is stronger when it draws on courses the student is actually sitting, because the detail is already in their head. The subjects below are the ones Al Ain Diploma students most often bring into a prescribed title, with the kind of example each one reliably supplies.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Supplies the cleanest material on proof, axioms and whether mathematical knowledge is discovered or invented. Students who have sat a proof by contradiction can discuss certainty with real authority, which is exactly what an essay on evidence or justification needs. The risk is drifting into exposition of the maths rather than a claim about it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Gives modelling and statistics examples: regression that fits but predicts badly, correlation presented as cause, a model whose assumptions are invisible in the output. These are strong for prescribed titles on reliability and on the limits of method, and they are far less used than the proof examples, which helps an essay stand out.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Useful for paradigm change and for the gap between a measurement and a claim. Uncertainty work in the internal investigation gives a student a lived example of how much a result can be trusted. Essays using physics go wrong by narrating an experiment instead of asking what the experiment licenses anyone to believe.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Offers models that are known to be wrong and still used: the octet rule, idealised gas behaviour, simple bonding pictures that break at the edges. That is productive ground for a title on the usefulness of a model against its truth, and it is rarely the example an examiner has already read five times that session.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Strong on classification and on the ethics of knowledge production. Where a species boundary sits, what counts as a control, and what a study on a small sample can claim are all accessible to a DP student and map onto titles about shared knowledge and about method.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The default area of knowledge for most essays, which is both its strength and its trap. Source evaluation taught for Paper 1 transfers directly to TOK, but a history example only works if the student states whose account it is and why that matters, rather than summarising events.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Gives interpretation, authorial intention and the question of whether a text can be read wrongly. Students who have done the individual oral already know how to build a reading from a specific passage, which is the discipline a TOK knowledge argument needs.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Productive on assumptions a discipline agrees to make, on prediction as a test of knowledge, and on data that is measured rather than observed. Al Ain students often have local examples to hand, which makes an essay specific instead of generic.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Supplies replication problems, ethical limits on method, and the difficulty of measuring something defined by the measurement. Used carefully this is some of the best TOK material available to a DP student; used carelessly it becomes a list of studies with no argument attached.

sections.heading: Where a Theory of Knowledge student usually is when a parent starts searching
paragraphs: Most families who search for an IB DP Theory of Knowledge tutor in Al Ain are at one of four points. Either a DP1 student has been handed the exhibition and does not know what an object is for; or a DP2 student has chosen a prescribed title and produced a draft that reads as description; or a marked commentary has come back at the bottom of a band; or the school has emailed an internal deadline that is closer than the family expected. Each of those has a different first session.

The reason this matters more in TOK than elsewhere is that the course has no recoverable middle. A student behind in Chemistry can be behind in energetics and caught up in four weeks, because the content is finite and divisible. TOK produces two artefacts, both with a submission date, and neither of them can be improved after the school uploads. The calendar is the syllabus.

So the first thing a useful tutor asks for is not an essay. It is three dates: the school's internal exhibition deadline, its internal essay deadline, and the date the coordinator intends to upload. Those three dates, counted backwards, tell a parent exactly how many sessions are available and therefore what is honestly achievable. If the answer is two sessions before an upload, the right advice may be to spend them on the commentary structure and leave the essay alone.

A second reader matters here for a structural reason, not a flattering one. The TOK teacher who sets the title conversation is also the person marking the exhibition, and in a small Al Ain cohort that is often one teacher for the whole year group. An outside reader who has no stake in the mark can say plainly that a knowledge argument is a restatement, which is harder to hear from the person who taught it.
bullets: Bring the school's two internal deadlines and the intended upload date
Bring the most recent marked work, even if the mark was poor
Bring the six prescribed titles for the session, if they have been released
Bring the student's six subjects, because the examples come from there

sections.heading: The two assessed tasks, and what each one actually demands
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge is assessed twice. The exhibition is internal: the student selects three objects, links each to one of the internal assessment prompts, and writes a commentary explaining how the object shows TOK working in the world. The prescribed title essay is external: the student writes on one of six titles issued by the IB for that session, within 1,600 words, and the school uploads it for marking outside the school.

Families consistently underestimate the exhibition and overestimate the essay. The exhibition looks like a soft task because it involves objects, and students treat the objects as illustrations of a theme. The marks go to the link between a specific object and a specific prompt, which is a narrow and testable thing. A commentary that describes an object beautifully and never answers the prompt scores badly however well written it is.

The essay fails for the opposite reason. Students who can write fluently produce 1,600 words of general reflection with no claim being tested. The assessment rewards a sustained argument about knowledge, developed through real examples, with the counter-position taken seriously rather than mentioned. A tutor's job on an essay draft is mostly to point at the paragraphs that assert and ask what would have to be true for the opposite to hold.

Both tasks sit alongside three documented interactions with the TOK teacher, which the school records as part of the essay process. Those conversations are not a formality and they are not something an outside tutor replaces. A good online session prepares the student to use them well: arriving with a specific question about the argument rather than a request to be told whether the draft is good.

sections.heading: The Theory of Knowledge year, counted backwards from the upload
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market publishes a calendar, which is odd, because the calendar is the thing parents are actually asking about. The table below counts backwards from the point a school uploads the essay. The dates themselves are set by the school and the IB, and they move between schools and between sessions, so the column that matters is the one describing what should already be finished.

IB session dates are not restated here on purpose. The IB publishes the examination and submission calendar for each session, and schools translate it into internal deadlines that sit weeks earlier. Any date a tutor gives you should be confirmed against your child's IB coordinator and against ibo.org, because a tutoring page is not an authority on an IB submission deadline and should not pretend to be one.

The planning principle is simpler than the calendar. Work backwards from the internal deadline, allow two weeks of dead time for illness, travel and the week your child has three other deadlines, and then divide what is left. If the division produces fewer than four sessions for an essay that does not yet exist, the plan needs to change scope rather than intensity: fix the argument and the structure, and accept that the prose will be adequate rather than polished.

One Al Ain-specific point belongs in the calendar as well. A smaller cohort means the internal deadlines are frequently set by one teacher managing every student's drafts at once, so the marked feedback a student waits for can take longer to come back than in a larger capital school. A plan that assumes a draft returns within a week may idle for a fortnight. Build the reading time in, and use the waiting weeks for the exhibition or for subject work rather than leaving them empty.

sections.heading: Where TOK marks go missing, in the order they cost most
paragraphs: The most expensive failure is a grade E, because it is a failing condition for the Diploma rather than a few points off a total. A student can pass every subject and still not receive the certificate. Families in Al Ain frequently discover this in DP2, which is late. Anyone planning tutoring spend across two years should know that the core carries this risk and that subject hours do not protect against it.

Below that, the losses are predictable. Description instead of evaluation is the first. A paragraph that explains what historians do, or how a scientific method works, is not yet an argument about knowledge. The test is whether the paragraph could be contradicted by a reasonable person; if not, it is exposition. This is the single most common comment on a weak draft and the easiest to fix once a student can see it.

Second is the unused example. Students collect examples and then narrate them. An example earns marks when it does work the argument needs: showing that a claim holds in one case and not another, or that two disciplines settle a dispute differently. Third is the counter-position that is named and then dismissed in one sentence, which reads as a box ticked rather than a position considered.

Fourth, and specific to the exhibition, is three objects that make the same point. A student picks a newspaper front page, a photograph and a social media post, and all three say that media shapes belief. Three objects need three different jobs. Fifth is the word limit: at 1,600 words an essay that spends 400 on preamble has lost a quarter of its argument before it starts.

sections.heading: What Theory of Knowledge support costs at Al Ain market rates
paragraphs: Three of the six competitor pages researched for this market publish no price at all, and two of those that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family transacts in. The table below collects what providers in this market have published in AED, read in October 2026. These are market rates from other providers, not an IB Gram price list; IB Gram's own arrangement starts with a free trial lesson and a quoted plan after it.

Core support behaves differently from subject tutoring in how it is priced. A Chemistry student buys a term of weekly hours. A TOK family usually buys a block attached to one piece of work, and the block is short. That makes the hourly rate less important than the number of hours actually needed, which is why the honest answer to the cost question starts with a diagnosis rather than a figure.

Two further cost realities are worth naming. A visiting tutor's rate includes travel, and in a city as spread out as Al Ain travel is a real share of the hour. And rates quoted for the Diploma core sometimes assume the tutor will read and comment on drafts between sessions; if that reading is not in the rate, the published figure is not the figure you will pay. Ask what the hour includes before comparing two numbers.

It is also worth setting tutoring against the fees already being paid. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package; fee decisions for Al Ain sit with ADEK rather than KHDA, so that specific freeze does not apply here. Either way, a short core block of four to eight hours is a small addition to a year's school fees, and a two-year weekly habit is not. Deciding which of those you are buying is the real budgeting question.

sections.heading: Online sessions against a visiting tutor for an Al Ain address
paragraphs: Parents searching for TOK help in Al Ain are often really asking whether someone can come to the house. The honest answer has two halves. In-home tutoring exists in this market, it costs more because travel is inside the rate, and for a conversation-and-redrafting course it buys very little that video does not. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Al Ain or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service offered only in India, and every UAE lesson runs online.

The case for online here is not convenience, it is supply. Al Ain's private school set is small, and the number of people in the city who have marked TOK against the assessment instrument is smaller still. A family restricted to tutors who will drive to Zakher on a Tuesday is choosing from a short list. A family working online is choosing a TOK specialist and scheduling around Gulf Standard Time instead.

The second argument is mechanical. TOK work is a shared screen: a draft open, comments going in live, the student reading their own sentence back and hearing why it asserts rather than argues. That is the same experience in a video call as at a kitchen table, and it produces a written artefact the parent can read afterwards. A visiting tutor's hour leaves the house with the tutor unless they write something down.

There is a third point that only applies to the Diploma core. Subject tutoring benefits from continuity with one person; core work benefits from a second opinion. A student who has heard one teacher explain what a knowledge argument is for a year may simply need it framed differently, and an outside reader is the cheapest way to get that. Online delivery makes a second reader practical in a city where the number of people who have assessed TOK work is small enough to count.
