sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch: the academic honesty line
paragraphs: This is the part of the market that needs saying plainly, because one provider researched for this project sells completed Internal Assessments outright. Under IB rules the prescribed title essay and the exhibition commentaries must be the student's own work. A tutor who writes a paragraph, restructures an argument in the document or edits prose to a finished state has put the student at risk of a malpractice finding, which is an outcome no grade improvement is worth.

What a tutor may do is substantial. They may teach the course content, explain what a knowledge argument is, work through unseen examples, question the student's claims until the weak ones collapse, and read a draft and write comments about it. They may say that paragraph three asserts without evidence. They may not say, here is the sentence to use instead.

The practical test we apply in sessions is whether the words that reach the submitted document came out of the student's keyboard. Comments live outside the draft. Where a student wants a model, we build one on a different title, so the thinking transfers and the text does not. Families should expect any tutor to describe this boundary before taking money, and should treat an offer to produce coursework as a reason to walk away.

The same rule governs artificial intelligence. A student who generates text and submits it has committed the same breach as one who pays for it. Used well, a language model can be a source to interrogate, which is actually good TOK material. Used as a drafting tool for assessed work it is a malpractice route, and schools in Al Ain are increasingly explicit about that in their own policies.
bullets: Teaching, questioning and written comments: permitted and useful
Writing, rewriting or editing assessed text to completion: not permitted
Modelling on a different title rather than the student's own: the safe route
Generated text submitted as the student's own work: a malpractice breach

sections.heading: Al Ain, ADEK and the school year a plan has to survive
paragraphs: Al Ain is part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so its private schools sit under ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which u.ae describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Dubai schools answer to KHDA, Sharjah to SPEA, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. Competitor pages in this market name ADEK almost never, which leaves inland families reading advice written for Dubai.

What a regulator does and does not do matters for a tutoring decision. ADEK licenses and inspects schools and publishes inspection outcomes. It does not vet private tutors for you, and it grants no form of approval to tutoring providers, this one included. The permit question sits elsewhere: individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need a MoHRE private tutor work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Ask any tutor whether they hold one.

Alongside the Diploma, your child is also taking the UAE's mandatory subjects. The federal position is that private schools must cover Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies regardless of the international curriculum they are licensed for. Those lessons occupy timetable space, and in DP2 that space competes directly with essay weeks. A realistic plan accounts for them rather than pretending the Diploma is the whole load.

Then there is the calendar itself. Ramadan shortens school days and shifts family routines, and the long inland summer empties the city. Sessions can move to after iftar, and holiday blocks are often the most productive weeks available for core work precisely because nothing else is due. The plan that fails is the one that assumes forty uninterrupted weeks.

process.title: Send the three dates
process.description: Before any lesson, send the school's internal exhibition deadline, its internal essay deadline and the intended upload date, plus the most recent marked work. Those four items decide what is achievable. A plan built without them is guesswork, and guesswork in a course with two assessments is expensive.

process.title: Free trial lesson, used as a diagnosis
process.description: The first session is free and is spent finding out what the student can already do: read a short passage, state a claim, and defend it under pressure. The output is a written diagnosis naming the specific weakness, not a general impression, and a recommendation on how many sessions the remaining weeks support.

process.title: Agree a dated plan
process.description: The plan names the number of sessions, what each block is for, and which deadline it is counted back from. Where the weeks are too few for the full scope, that is said in writing before any money changes hands, with the reduced scope spelled out. Families should expect to be told when tutoring will not fix something.

process.title: Teach, question, comment, repeat
process.description: Weekly sessions run on the student's own work and on unseen examples. Drafts come back with written comments rather than edits. After each session a short note goes to the parent naming what was covered and what the student owes before the next one, which keeps a two-month block visible rather than opaque.

process.title: Review against the real deadline
process.description: At four weeks, or halfway through a short block, the plan is checked against the school's dates and the evidence. If the student is on track the plan continues; if not, the scope changes. The review is based on marked drafts, not on how the sessions felt.

whyPoints.title: The timeline comes first
whyPoints.description: Every plan starts from the school's dates counted backwards, because in a course with two assessed artefacts the calendar decides what is possible. Families get told how many sessions the remaining weeks actually support, including when the answer is fewer than they hoped.

whyPoints.title: Core specialists, not general subject tutors
whyPoints.description: Theory of Knowledge is not a subject with content to revise, and a strong Chemistry tutor is not automatically useful on a prescribed title. The tutors matched here work on the Diploma core and have marked against the TOK assessment instrument.

whyPoints.title: Evidence a parent can read
whyPoints.description: Sessions produce written comments on drafts and a short note after each lesson. That means a parent who does not know the course can still see what changed between week one and week six, rather than relying on a report that everything is going well.

whyPoints.title: A stated academic honesty boundary
whyPoints.description: The line is described before any session: teaching, questioning and comments on the student's own work, never writing or editing assessed text to completion. Modelling happens on a different title. This is a genuine difference from providers in this market that sell finished coursework.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built for an inland city
whyPoints.description: Sessions are set on Gulf Standard Time around the Al Ain school run, with later starts for outlying districts and after-iftar slots during Ramadan. Holiday blocks are used deliberately for core work, because they are the weeks with no competing deadlines.

whyPoints.title: Sourced facts, and silence where sources are missing
whyPoints.description: Regulatory and permit statements on this page cite u.ae and MoHRE. IB submission dates are deliberately not published here, because they are set per session and per school and belong to your coordinator and ibo.org rather than to a tutoring page.

faqs.question: Our son is in DP1 at an Al Ain school and has not started Theory of Knowledge work. Where should he be by now?
faqs.answer: In most DP1 timetables the first year is for the exhibition and for building the habit of evaluating claims. If he has had TOK lessons but produced nothing, the honest position is that he is normal rather than behind. What should exist by the end of DP1 is a sense of what an internal assessment prompt is asking and at least a shortlist of possible objects. Ask the coordinator for the school's internal exhibition deadline in writing. That one date tells you whether there is room for a weekly session or whether this needs to be a short block.

faqs.question: How many weeks does a Theory of Knowledge essay take from prescribed title to final upload?
faqs.answer: Most students who do it properly spend eight to twelve weeks on the essay, and that is not eight to twelve weeks of writing. The first two weeks go on unpicking the title and testing whether a candidate argument can actually be defended. The middle weeks build knowledge arguments with examples from the student's own subjects. The last weeks are redrafting against the 1,600-word limit. Schools set an internal deadline well before their upload, so count backwards from that internal date, not from the IB window, and add a fortnight of slack for illness and competing deadlines.

faqs.question: What should a plan look like for a student eleven weeks from the school's internal TOK deadline?
faqs.answer: Eleven weeks is comfortable if the student starts now and uncomfortable if they start in week four. A workable shape is two sessions on the title and the argument, three on building and testing knowledge arguments with examples from their six subjects, two on a full draft read and commented on in writing, and two near the end on structure and the word limit. That leaves two weeks unassigned, which is the point: something will go wrong, and a plan with no slack becomes a plan that gets abandoned.

faqs.question: My daughter's exhibition commentary came back at the bottom of the band. Can that be rebuilt in time?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether the school has submitted it. Before submission there is usually room to fix the most common cause, which is three objects that make the same point or commentaries that describe an object without answering the chosen prompt. That is two or three sessions of work. After the school has uploaded, the exhibition mark is what it is, and the sensible move is to put the remaining hours into the essay, where the marks are still live. Ask the coordinator which side of submission you are on before buying anything.

faqs.question: Does a Theory of Knowledge tutor need the MoHRE private tuition work permit to read a draft over video?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need a private tutor work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through MoHRE. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a short processing time. The regulation is about who is providing paid private tuition rather than about the format of the lesson, so a parent should ask any tutor they pay whether they hold one. Tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no amount is published.

faqs.question: Which weeks of the Al Ain school year are the worst to put Theory of Knowledge sessions in?
faqs.answer: The weeks when three other things are due. In practice that means the fortnight around subject internal assessment deadlines, mock examination weeks, and the days immediately after a long break when nothing has been read. Ramadan shortens school days and shifts energy to the evening, so sessions usually move to after iftar rather than disappearing. The useful move is to look at the school calendar in September, mark the weeks that are already full, and place the core work in the gaps rather than discovering the collision in February.

faqs.question: What may a tutor actually do to a Theory of Knowledge draft without putting the diploma at risk?
faqs.answer: A tutor may read it, mark it against the assessment instrument, and write comments explaining why a paragraph asserts rather than argues. They may ask questions until a weak claim falls over. They may teach the course content and work through examples that are not the student's. They may not write a sentence that ends up in the submitted essay, restructure the argument inside the document, or edit the prose to a finished state. Comments stay outside the draft, and every word submitted comes from the student. Any provider offering to produce the work should be avoided.

faqs.question: How do we tell whether our child's problem in Theory of Knowledge is writing or thinking?
faqs.answer: Ask them to explain their argument out loud without notes, in two minutes. A student with a thinking problem cannot say what claim they are testing, or they restate the title back at you. A student with a writing problem gives you a clear, defensible argument verbally and then produces a draft that buries it. The two need opposite work. The thinking problem is solved by questioning and by reading better examples; the writing problem is solved by structure, paragraph discipline and a word budget. One free trial session is usually enough to tell them apart.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting Theory of Knowledge support in the final term of DP2?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, with a narrow scope. If the essay is still unsubmitted there is real work available: tightening the argument, cutting preamble to recover words, and making sure the counter-position is genuinely considered. Three or four sessions can move a draft meaningfully. If both the exhibition and the essay have been uploaded, the honest answer is that TOK is finished and the money is better spent on subjects with examinations still ahead. A tutor who takes a booking in that situation without saying so is not acting in your interest.

faqs.question: What should the first Theory of Knowledge session produce that a parent can read?
faqs.answer: A written diagnosis, not a feeling. It should name the specific weakness, say which of the two assessed tasks is at risk, state how many sessions the remaining weeks support, and list what the student needs to bring next time. If the honest finding is that the school's teaching is sufficient and no tutoring is needed, that belongs in the note too. A first session that ends with a general reassurance and an invoice has told you nothing you can act on, and you should treat the diagnosis as the product you paid for.

faqs.question: How does ADEK's role in Al Ain change the way a school runs Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: Al Ain sits in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so its private schools are licensed and inspected by ADEK rather than by Dubai's KHDA. ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation and publishes inspection outcomes, which is the main outside signal a parent gets about a school. It does not set the TOK syllabus, which is the IB's, and it does not vet private tutors. What it does affect is school-level practice: inspection pressure tends to make internal deadlines earlier and better documented, which is useful to a family planning backwards.

faqs.question: What does Theory of Knowledge support cost per hour at Al Ain market rates?
faqs.answer: Published rates in this market, read in October 2026, run from AED 45-65 at the budget online end up to AED 650 for a premium named tutor, with IB and IGCSE specialists commonly quoting AED 200-450 and visiting in-home tutors AED 180-500 because travel sits inside the rate. Core support is usually bought as a short block attached to one piece of work rather than as a term of weekly hours, so the number of sessions matters more than the hourly figure. IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson rather than from a list.

faqs.question: Can Theory of Knowledge sessions run after iftar during Ramadan for an Al Ain family?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for many households that is the better slot. School days shorten during Ramadan and afternoons are low-energy, so a session placed after iftar often gets more from a student than the same hour at 4pm. Because lessons are delivered online there is no travel to arrange around the timing. The practical advice is to agree the Ramadan slot in advance rather than rescheduling week by week, and to treat the following break as a block for sustained core work when no other deadlines compete.

faqs.question: If we start this month, what do week one, week four and week eight look like?
faqs.answer: Week one is diagnosis and the title: what is actually being asked, what key terms mean, and whether the student's first instinct can be defended. Week four should have two knowledge arguments standing up, each with an example from one of their own six subjects doing real work rather than being narrated. Week eight should have a full draft read and returned with written comments, with the counter-position in place and the word count visible. If week four looks like week one, the plan changes rather than continuing.

faqs.question: Does the Theory of Knowledge grade appear in a UAE Ministry of Education equivalency file?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is assessed by the Ministry of Education against published requirements per curriculum, and the British-track rules are specific: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels. For IB candidates no points threshold should be quoted from a tutoring page; the figure must be read on the Ministry's own site or confirmed with the attestation authority. Treat equivalency as a process to verify directly, and never as something a tutor performs for you.

faqs.question: What happens if no Theory of Knowledge specialist is free in the slot an Al Ain family needs?
faqs.answer: You are told, before any payment. Core specialists are a smaller pool than subject tutors, and a narrow slot in an exam term sometimes cannot be filled immediately. The options then are a different weekday, a weekend session, a short wait with a named date, or a shift of scope to what a different tutor can genuinely cover. Being offered an unnamed tutor who will work it out is the wrong answer. No competitor page researched for this market discloses a coverage limit at all, which is precisely why it is stated here.

al-ain/ib-dp-theory-of-knowledge-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the dates, then decide what to buy
al-ain/ib-dp-theory-of-knowledge-tutor.closingBody: If your child is sitting Theory of Knowledge at an Al Ain school, the most valuable thing you can do this week costs nothing: ask the IB coordinator for the internal exhibition deadline, the internal essay deadline and the intended upload date, in writing. Bring those three dates and the most recent marked work to a free trial lesson, and you will leave with a written diagnosis and a realistic number of sessions rather than a general impression. Lessons run online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time, and if the finding is that no tutoring is needed, that is what the note will say.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor.heroSubtitle: A search for an IB home tutor in Al Ain is usually a search for four different things at once, and most parents are quietly weighing three alternatives against each other without ever writing them down. This page writes them down: the visiting tutor, the tuition centre group class, a teacher from the school itself, and live one-to-one over video. IB Gram delivers the fourth of those. Home visits are a service we provide only in India, and this page explains what that choice costs and what it buys an Al Ain family.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach Diploma and Middle Years subjects over live video to families across Al Ain. Each profile names the subjects and the levels that person teaches, so you can compare a specific match against the local alternatives described on this page rather than against an unnamed pool of availability.

intro.heading: The three alternatives you are already weighing
paragraphs: Parents in Al Ain rarely begin with a format. They begin with a problem in a subject and then discover, usually from other parents at the school gate, that there are several quite different ways of buying help. A neighbour recommends someone who drives over on Tuesdays. A cousin's child goes to a centre near Al Jimi Mall twice a week. Somebody suggests asking the subject teacher directly. And a platform offers live one-to-one over video. Those four options differ on price, on who is permitted to teach, on how large the pool of possible tutors is, and on what happens when the arrangement stops working.

The phrase people type is home tutor, and that phrase is doing a lot of work. For some families it means literally a person in the house. For others it means tuition that happens at home rather than at a centre, which video satisfies perfectly well. For most it means something looser: one-to-one, in our own time, without another car journey at the end of a long day. Separating those three meanings is the most useful thing a parent can do in the first ten minutes, because the second and third are satisfied by a format that costs less and draws on a far larger pool.

Al Ain sharpens the comparison more than most UAE cities. The city is spread across districts that are twenty to thirty minutes apart in evening traffic, from Zakher in the south to Hili in the north. Its private-school set is smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, which means the number of people living in the city who can teach Higher Level Physics or Higher Level Chemistry at Diploma depth is genuinely small. A visiting tutor must be drawn from that small set and must be able to reach your district at the hour your child is home. Those two constraints multiply, and what they multiply down to is a very short list.

The permit position matters too, and it is the part most comparisons leave out. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, the eligible categories are published, and individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. The published route is the Ministry's own private tutor licensing service, which lists a two-working-day completion time and no fee. A parent is entitled to ask any tutor, from any of the four options, whether they hold it.

What follows compares the four options on the things that actually differ: the hourly figure and what sits inside it, the size of the pool you are choosing from, travel and timing, the permit question, continuity when something changes, and how each one handles coursework boundaries. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE; the service we provide to Al Ain families is live one-to-one tuition over video, and the case for it is made here by comparison rather than by assertion. Where another option fits a family better, the comparison will show that too.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Which option suits a family depends partly on which programme the student is in, because the three IB programmes make different demands on continuity and on subject specialism. A Primary Years child and a Diploma Higher Level candidate are not shopping in the same market even when the parent types the same phrase into Google.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: At primary level the subject specialism required is modest and the supervision requirement is high, which is the one case where a visiting adult has a genuine advantage: a seven-year-old needs someone physically turning pages. What primary children actually need is reading fluency, number facts held in memory and the habit of recording a method, none of which requires a Diploma specialist. A university student at the lower market band, properly permitted, is often the sensible match here.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Ain this is the one segment where the local pool is adequate, because the requirement is general rather than specialist and the city has a large student population around the United Arab Emirates University. Families in Asharej in particular find visiting primary tutors easily. The comparison on this page matters much less at this level, and we say so rather than arguing for video where it adds nothing.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Middle Years marks four criteria per subject from one to eight, and the help a student needs is usually in one criterion rather than across a subject. That is specialist work in a narrow band: knowing what criterion C rewards in a science investigation is not general teaching knowledge. The pool of people who know a given subject's criteria properly is smaller than the pool who know the subject, which starts to favour choosing on expertise rather than on proximity.
programmes.countryNote: Several Al Ain schools run Middle Years and a British Year 10 and 11 stream in the same building, so a visiting tutor who covers one may be assumed to cover the other. They are different assessment systems with different mark schemes. Asking directly which of the two a candidate has taught, and for how many cohorts, separates the two groups quickly and is a question worth putting to any of the four options.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is where the comparison tilts hardest. Six subjects, three at Higher Level, externally marked papers in May and internally assessed work spread across two years: this is the point at which a generalist stops being useful and a subject specialist at the right level becomes the whole value of the hour. Continuity over two years matters as much as specialism, because a tutor who has held the record since the first year knows what was repaired and what is next.
programmes.countryNote: The number of adults resident in Al Ain who can teach Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Chemistry or Economics at Diploma depth is small, and those few are sought by every family in the city at the same hour of the same weekday. That is the structural reason a visiting arrangement at this level is hard to secure and harder to keep. Removing the travel radius changes the pool from a city to a timezone.

programmes.name: The Diploma core
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity and service sit outside the six subjects and together carry up to three bonus points, with failing conditions that can cost the whole Diploma. Core support is episodic rather than weekly: a block of sessions around a research question, then another around a draft. That shape suits booked blocks far better than a standing weekly visit, whichever option a family chooses.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain's smaller supervisor pool means an Extended Essay in a specialised field may be supervised by a teacher outside it, which is where independent subject review earns its place. The boundary must be explicit under any option: review, challenge and criterion explanation are legitimate, and supplying any part of a text that will be assessed is not. We put that in writing before a core block starts.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: The subject list below is ordered by how hard each one is to staff with someone resident in Al Ain, because that is the variable the four-way comparison actually turns on. Where the local pool is adequate the options are genuinely close. Where it is thin, proximity stops being a feature and becomes the thing limiting your choice.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The hardest Diploma subject to staff locally in Al Ain, and the one families most often settle for a generalist in. Higher Level carries additional content and an extra paper, and the data-analysis questions need practice with uncertainty and gradients. A tutor who teaches Middle Years science well is not automatically able to teach Higher Level fields and circuits.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics drive the requests; stoichiometry and multi-step calculation reading is where marks are most reliably recovered. The internal assessment needs a measurable, controllable variable chosen early. Local availability at Higher Level is thin, and a chemistry teacher comfortable at IGCSE depth is a different proposition from one comfortable at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency carry the course, and Higher Level rewards moving between algebraic and graphical arguments at speed. Marks are lost in unjustified steps rather than wrong answers. This is the subject where parents most often compare a nearby maths tutor against a distant specialist, and where the two are least interchangeable at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and assumed calculator fluency define this route. Students who crossed from a Middle Years course are often procedurally sound but unused to interpreting output in context. Higher Level adds statistical inference that cannot be absorbed late. Confirm which of the two maths routes a candidate has actually taught; many have taught only one.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy, with recall structure rather than understanding as the usual limiting factor. Extended responses need command-term discipline, since explain, outline and evaluate reward different things. Local availability is better than for physics and chemistry, so for biology the four options sit closer together than this page's general argument suggests.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the internal assessment commentaries decide most grades. Marks go on diagrams that do not match the article and on evaluation that lists both sides without judging. Higher Level adds quantitative content. Economics specialists are scarce in Al Ain specifically, which is why this subject appears so often in requests that begin as a search for a visiting tutor.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Upper-band answers apply a named framework to a given organisation rather than describing it. The Higher Level research project needs its scope agreed early and real data available. Business is more widely taught than economics, so the local pool is deeper, though at Higher Level the research project still rewards someone who has supervised one before.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two assessed orals and a paper on unseen non-literary texts make this a skills course with a reading list attached. The individual oral rewards preparation because the student chooses the extract and the global issue. Availability in Al Ain is reasonable, but experience with the current assessment model rather than an older one is the question to ask.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Al Ain asks for Arabic more often than most UAE cities, and the route matters: Arabic A is language and literature for first-language speakers, Arabic B an acquisition course with a different structure. Matching the wrong route wastes a term. Local first-language teaching capacity is good; capacity for the Diploma assessment model specifically is narrower.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The programming solution dominates the internal assessment and documents badly when nobody has supervised one before. Paper questions on data structures and system fundamentals need taught content rather than coding practice. Among the thinnest subjects locally, and one where a nearby enthusiast and an experienced Diploma teacher are not close substitutes.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies have to be recalled precisely and deployed as evidence rather than retold, and the internal assessment is a replication with strict reporting conventions. Requested steadily in Al Ain and almost never available locally at Diploma level, which makes it a clear case where the radius is the constraint rather than the budget.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Because three of the four options involve somebody driving, the district a family lives in changes the comparison directly. The notes below describe each area in terms of what a visiting arrangement would actually require there, which is the detail a general tutoring page tends to skip.

regions.name: Al Jimi
regions.note: Central, dense and close to several long-established campuses, so a visiting tutor can plausibly fit two households in one evening. This is the district where in-home arrangements work best in Al Ain, and where the price gap between options is therefore the smallest.

regions.name: Al Mutaredh
regions.note: Villa district by the oasis and the main hospital, with many medical and university households on shift patterns. A visiting tutor needs a time that survives a changing rota, which is exactly the kind of arrangement that breaks after a month of rescheduling.

regions.name: Asharej
regions.note: Beside the United Arab Emirates University campus, so the local pool of available adults is unusually large at primary and lower-secondary level. For Diploma Higher Level that pool is no deeper here than anywhere else in the city.

regions.name: Al Towayya
regions.note: Established area where British and Indian curriculum timetables often run in one household. Two siblings on different boards usually need two specialists, and expecting one visiting tutor to cover both is the most common way these arrangements disappoint.

regions.name: Falaj Hazzaa
regions.note: Large villa neighbourhood with a strong Emirati household share, where Arabic as a first language and Islamic Education sit alongside Diploma subjects. Scheduling has to avoid the school's own Arabic support sessions, which tightens the window a visiting tutor could use.

sections.heading: What an Al Ain parent actually means by a home tutor
paragraphs: Three different requests hide behind the same phrase. The first is literal: an adult in the house, sitting next to the student. The second is locational: tuition that happens at home rather than requiring a trip to a centre. The third is practical: one-to-one attention at a time the family chooses, with no second car journey after a long school day. Only the first requires anybody to drive anywhere, and it is the least common of the three once parents are asked directly.

That distinction decides the whole comparison. If the requirement is the second or third meaning, live video satisfies it and the hourly figure drops by the travel component, while the pool of possible tutors expands from people living in Al Ain to people available at that hour anywhere. If the requirement is genuinely the first, then the comparison on this page should push you towards a local visiting arrangement, and we would rather say that than sell you something else.

IB Gram provides the online version to UAE families. We do not sell home visits in the UAE; that is a service we offer only in India, where the operating model is different. So the honest framing of this page is not that one option is better, but that for a Diploma student in Al Ain needing a Higher Level specialist, the local supply is small enough that proximity and specialism are usually in direct conflict, and most families, once they see the trade clearly, choose the specialist.
bullets: Literal meaning: an adult physically present, which only a local visit provides
Locational meaning: tuition at home rather than at a centre, which video satisfies
Practical meaning: one-to-one at our chosen time with no second journey
Ask yourself which of the three you actually need before comparing prices

sections.heading: Option one: the visiting tutor who lives nearby
paragraphs: The visiting tutor is the default mental model and it has real advantages. A person in the room can see a student's working as it happens, can take a phone away, and can read the body language that tells an experienced teacher when someone has stopped following. For younger children and for students who genuinely will not engage without physical supervision, that is worth paying for and worth the logistics.

The costs are equally real and tend to be understated at the point of agreement. Published in-home rates in this market run from around AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table giving AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. Travel time sits inside that figure. In a city where districts are twenty to thirty minutes apart in evening traffic, a tutor giving a sixty-minute lesson in Zakher has committed two hours of their evening, and the rate reflects that whether or not it is itemised.

The structural limit is the pool. Only someone living in or near Al Ain can take the booking, and they must be free at the hour your child is home. For Diploma Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Chemistry, Economics, Computer Science or Psychology, the number of Al Ain residents who meet both conditions is very small, and the usual outcome is not a long wait but a quiet substitution: the family accepts a capable generalist instead, and nobody describes the compromise out loud.

sections.heading: Option two: the tuition centre and its group class
paragraphs: Centres occupy a different part of the market and they are frequently the cheapest option per hour, because the cost is divided across a group. For some students that works well: a motivated child who needs structure, pace and the company of others revising the same paper can do better in a group of four than one-to-one, and the social accountability is genuinely useful during an exam term.

What a group cannot do is run at one student's speed. If the gap is two absent syllabus topics in Higher Level Chemistry, a class covering the scheme of work will not stop for them, and the student spends the hour watching content they already have. Group size is the variable that decides this, and it is worth asking for the actual number rather than the advertised maximum, along with how the group is split by level, since Standard and Higher Level students in one room get a compromise aimed at neither.

A centre is also a different legal animal from an individual tutor. An operation with premises and staff is a business, and in Dubai that means a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and an annual renewal requested ahead of expiry. Al Ain centres answer to ADEK as the Emirate of Abu Dhabi's regulator for private education, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. The point for a parent is simply that a centre should be able to answer a direct question about its own permissions, and an individual arriving at a villa should be able to answer the equivalent question about theirs.

sections.heading: Option three: a teacher from your child's own school
paragraphs: This is the option families raise most often and the one most quickly closed. The appeal is obvious: the teacher knows the scheme of work, sets the assessments and knows the student. The difficulty is that the same facts create a conflict of interest, and Abu Dhabi has addressed it directly.

Reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff states that teachers are prohibited from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that staff tutoring outside school hours must hold the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document itself, so a family relying on it should verify the current wording with the school or with ADEK directly. The direction of the rule, though, is not in doubt.

What this means practically is that a parent should not ask, and a school should not facilitate, paid tutoring by a child's own subject teacher in Abu Dhabi emirate, which includes Al Ain. A teacher from a different school is a different matter and may be entirely proper, provided they hold the permit. We never market access to a student's own teacher, and a provider who offers that in this emirate is offering something a parent should question rather than buy. The second reason to avoid it is less often discussed: a teacher paid privately by one family in a class they also mark is in an impossible position when that class is assessed, and the student carries the consequences of any suspicion raised later.

sections.heading: Option four: live one-to-one over video, and what it changes
paragraphs: The fourth option keeps the one-to-one attention and the at-home convenience and removes the travel. What that buys is not primarily money, although the hourly band is lower. It buys the pool. A student in Al Maqam can work with a Higher Level Physics specialist without anyone calculating whether a round trip from the city centre at six in the evening is worth the fee, which means the match is made on subject and level rather than on geography.

It also buys the honest hour. A visiting tutor who must reach a second household has a hard stop; a video session can sit at six-thirty or seven, which in Zakher, Hili and Al Muwaiji is when a student is actually home and able to concentrate. Sessions move rather than cancel during Ramadan, usually to after Iftar, and they survive a family's travel because only the clock changes. Those three things together are why online arrangements in this city last longer than visiting ones, in our experience of the ones that replace them.

What it does not do should be stated plainly too. A tutor on a screen cannot confiscate a phone, cannot make a reluctant nine-year-old sit still, and cannot run a chemistry practical. For practical work the honest position is that an online tutor teaches the technique, the data analysis and the alternative-to-practical question types, while the practical itself happens at school. Where a family needs physical presence, option one is the right answer and we will say so.

sections.heading: Is the person teaching your child permitted to do it?
paragraphs: This is the question almost no comparison asks, and it applies equally to all four options. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and the published eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students.

The application route is the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own service for issuing a new private tutor work permit, which lists a two-working-day completion time and no fee, applied for through the Ministry's smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, and a figure circulating online could not be verified, so no amount appears on this page.

For a parent the practical step is one sentence in a first message: do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and may I see it? A permitted tutor answers without hesitation. The question is free to ask, it costs a permitted tutor nothing to answer, and asking it of every option, including a platform, is a reasonable standard rather than an accusation. IB Gram holds no permit or accreditation from ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and does not claim one.

sections.heading: The travel arithmetic in a city this spread out
paragraphs: Al Ain is not a dense city, and that single fact drives most of the price difference between the options. From Zakher in the south to Hili and Al Foah in the north is a substantial drive, and the central schools pull children from every direction at the same time of day. A tutor crossing the city for one sixty-minute lesson spends most of an evening on it, and prices accordingly.

Run the numbers for a two-subject household. Two visiting lessons a week in different subjects means two tutors making two round trips, and the realistic slots will be whatever suits their routes rather than whatever suits your evening. The same two subjects over video can be booked back to back from six o'clock, with two specialists who never meet, in one quiet room. The practical saving is not just the fee; it is that both sessions actually happen in the same week, every week, which is what produces a result.

There is a second-order effect worth naming. Because a visiting arrangement is expensive per hour, families buy fewer hours and buy them later, usually once a mock result has already arrived. Because the online band is lower, the same budget buys a weekly slot through the first Diploma year, which is the stage where an hour does the most good. The format therefore changes not only the price of an hour but the stage at which a family can afford to start, and starting earlier is the single largest cost saving available in this market.

sections.heading: A six-question test that separates the four options
paragraphs: Rather than ranking the options, work through six questions about your own household. First: does your child need physical supervision to work at all? If yes, option one, and the rest of this page is interesting rather than useful. Second: is the subject a Higher Level science, mathematics at Higher Level, economics, computer science or psychology? If yes, the resident pool in Al Ain is thin and proximity will cost you specialism.

Third: what time is your child genuinely home, able to eat and then concentrate? If the honest answer is after six, a visiting arrangement in an outer district is hard to sustain. Fourth: how long do you expect to need this, one term or two years? Continuity favours whichever option you can keep, and a cheaper arrangement that collapses in February is not cheaper. Fifth: can every candidate, under any option, answer the permit question?

Sixth, and most often skipped: what is the coursework boundary, written down? Internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay must be the student's own work, and a tutor's role is to teach, question and explain criteria. Any provider or individual who offers more than that on assessed work is offering the student a malpractice risk, and that risk sits with the student rather than with the tutor. Ask the question in writing and keep the answer, whichever of the four options you choose. Taken together the six answers usually point at one option rather than two, and they point there for reasons a parent can explain to a sceptical spouse, which is more than can be said for choosing on a recommendation at the school gate.

process.title: Decide which of the three meanings you need
process.description: Tell us whether you need a person physically present, tuition that happens at home, or one-to-one at a time you choose. The first points to a local visiting arrangement and we will say so. The second and third are what we deliver, and knowing which it is saves a conversation that otherwise takes a week.

process.title: Name the subject and the level precisely
process.description: Higher Level or Standard, which maths route, which board for a sibling on a different system. Precision here decides whether the match is a specialist or a generalist, and in Al Ain that distinction matters more than in Abu Dhabi or Dubai because the resident pool is smaller.

process.title: Ask us the permit question
process.description: Ask whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and ask the same of every other option you are considering. It is free to obtain, valid for two years, and a permitted tutor will answer at once. Treat hesitation from anyone, including us, as information.

process.title: Trial the match against the alternative
process.description: One lesson at no charge, one per family, with no card details taken beforehand. Run it in the same week you trial a local option if you can, because comparing two real sessions tells you more than comparing two descriptions. Then choose on evidence rather than on format.

process.title: Set the slot and write the boundaries down
process.description: Fix the weekly time against your child's real arrival home, and agree in writing what the tutor may do with coursework. Those two documents, a time and a boundary, are what make an arrangement last past February. They take ten minutes and they prevent the two failures we see most.

whyPoints.title: The comparison is written down, not implied
whyPoints.description: Most provider pages compare themselves against an unnamed alternative. This one names four models, gives the published rate bands with their sources, and states where another option fits a family better. For a primary-age child needing physical supervision, that option is not us.

whyPoints.title: No radius on the match
whyPoints.description: Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Chemistry, Economics, Computer Science and Psychology are the subjects Al Ain is thinnest in. Matching over video removes the travel constraint entirely, so the choice is made on subject and level rather than on who happens to live within a twenty-minute drive.

whyPoints.title: Slots set to this city's evenings
whyPoints.description: A six or six-thirty start in Zakher, Hili or Al Muwaiji is normal for us and impossible for a tutor with a second household to reach. Sessions move to after Iftar during Ramadan rather than pausing, and they follow a family through travel because only the clock changes.

whyPoints.title: The permit question asked in both directions
whyPoints.description: We ask tutors for the MoHRE private tuition work permit and we tell parents to ask us, and every other provider, the same thing. We also state what we do not hold: no accreditation or approval from ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board.

whyPoints.title: Coursework boundaries in writing
whyPoints.description: Before any block on an internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay, the boundary is agreed in writing. Review, challenge and criterion explanation are in scope. Supplying text that will be assessed is not, under any deadline. The malpractice risk sits with the student, which is why this is non-negotiable.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what video cannot do
whyPoints.description: A tutor on a screen cannot take a phone away, cannot settle a reluctant young child, and cannot run a practical. We teach practical technique, data analysis and the alternative-to-practical question types; the practical itself happens at school. Where presence is the requirement, a local arrangement is the better answer.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB home tutor who comes to our villa in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Not from us. IB Gram does not sell in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we provide only in India, where the operating model is different. What we offer Al Ain families is live one-to-one tuition over video, which satisfies the two meanings most parents actually have in mind: tuition at home rather than at a centre, and one-to-one at a time you choose with no second journey. If what you need is genuinely an adult physically present in the room, a local visiting arrangement is the right answer, and this page sets out what that market charges so you can judge it fairly.

faqs.question: What does a visiting IB tutor in Al Ain charge once travel is included?
faqs.answer: Published in-home rates in this market run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour. Bestimate's 2026 rate table gives AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors quote AED 200 to 500. Travel sits inside that figure rather than beside it, which matters in Al Ain because the districts are far apart: a tutor giving one hour in Zakher has committed most of an evening. Ask whether the quoted rate assumes a particular district, because a figure set for a central Al Jimi household often rises for the outer areas. These are other providers' published bands, not IB Gram's prices.

faqs.question: How big is the pool of IB Higher Level tutors living in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Smaller than most families expect, and that is the single most important fact in this comparison. Al Ain has far fewer IB World Schools than Abu Dhabi island, so the number of adults resident here who teach Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Chemistry, Economics, Computer Science or Psychology at Diploma depth is genuinely small. Those same few people are sought by every family in the city at roughly the same hour of the same weekday. The usual outcome is not a long wait but a quiet substitution to a capable generalist, which nobody describes out loud at the time and which shows up in the second year.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre group class a reasonable substitute for one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is often the cheapest option per hour. A motivated student who needs pace, structure and the company of others working the same paper can do better in a small group than alone, and the accountability helps through an exam term. What a group cannot do is stop for one student's two missing topics. Ask for the actual group size rather than the advertised maximum, and ask how groups are split by level, because Standard and Higher Level students in one room receive a compromise aimed at neither. For narrow content repair, one-to-one is the format that works.

faqs.question: Can my child be tutored privately by a teacher from their own school?
faqs.answer: In Abu Dhabi emirate, which includes Al Ain, you should not pursue this. Reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff states that teachers are barred from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation permit's code of conduct carries the same restriction. That reporting should be checked against the current policy document, but the direction of the rule is clear. A teacher from a different school is a separate matter and may be entirely proper, provided they hold the permit. We never market access to a child's own teacher.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Abu Dhabi emirate need a permit, and who issues it?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories published by the authorities include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. The application route is the Ministry's own private tutor licensing service, which states a two-working-day completion time and no fee. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor arriving at my door is permitted to teach?
faqs.answer: Ask one direct question in your first message: do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and may I see it? Because the permit is free and takes two working days to issue, a working tutor has no good reason not to hold one, and a permitted tutor will answer immediately. Ask the same question of a centre about its own business permissions, and of any platform, including this one. The question costs nothing, and hesitation in response to it is useful information. Do not accept a general claim of being licensed as a substitute for the document itself.

faqs.question: What is the difference between an agency, a marketplace and a freelance tutor?
faqs.answer: An agency selects the tutor for you, holds the relationship and usually handles replacement, at a higher price. A marketplace lists many tutors and leaves selection, vetting and continuity to you, at a lower price and with more variance. A freelance tutor found by word of mouth is the cheapest per hour and carries the whole risk in one person: if they relocate, the arrangement ends that week. The relevant question is not which model is best but who carries the risk of a wrong match, and whether anything happens when the match is wrong.

faqs.question: Why does IB Gram not send tutors to homes in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Because the model would make the service worse for the families we serve here. Sending someone to a villa means the tutor must live within reach of that villa and be free at that hour, which in Al Ain reduces the pool for scarce Higher Level subjects to a handful of people. Online matching removes that constraint and lets a student in Al Maqam work with a Higher Level Physics specialist on a weekday evening. In-home tuition is a service we run in India, where the density and the operating model are different, and we do not claim it in the UAE.

faqs.question: Does an online lesson lose the things a home visit gives you?
faqs.answer: It loses three things honestly. A tutor on a screen cannot take a phone away, cannot settle a reluctant younger child, and cannot run a practical experiment. For practical work the position is that the tutor teaches technique, data handling and the alternative-to-practical question types, while the practical itself happens at school. What is not lost is seeing a student's working: a shared screen, a document camera or a photographed page shows a method as clearly as sitting beside someone. For a motivated secondary student the difference is small; for a distractible eight-year-old it is not.

faqs.question: What happens to a home-tutor arrangement when the tutor moves away?
faqs.answer: It ends, usually with little notice, and that is a real cost of a single-person arrangement in a city with a mobile expatriate population. The replacement search starts from nothing, the new tutor repeats a diagnosis the family has already paid for, and a term's continuity is lost at whatever point in the year it happens. Continuity is worth money in a two-year Diploma: a tutor who has held the record since the first year knows what was repaired and what deadline is next. Ask any provider, under any option, what actually happens if the person stops being available.

faqs.question: Which of the four options is cheapest over a full Diploma year?
faqs.answer: On published bands, a centre group class is cheapest per hour, live one-to-one over video sits next at the AED 150 to 300 qualified-tutor band, and a visiting tutor is most expensive at AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the figure. Over a year, though, the bigger variable is when a family starts. A lower hourly rate that allows a weekly slot from the first Diploma term usually costs less in total than a higher rate bought late, because the late purchase buys specialist hours under deadline pressure. The expensive decision is rarely the tier; it is the delay.

faqs.question: Can two siblings share a session to bring the cost down?
faqs.answer: Not in the same hour, in our view, unless they are in the same subject at the same level and roughly the same position, which is rare. What works is consecutive slots on one evening: each child gets their own tutor and their own hour, and one quiet room covers both. That halves the household's logistical load without giving either child a lesson aimed at the other. In villa districts where study space is contested, the shared-room arrangement is often the real constraint, and sequencing solves it better than combining.

faqs.question: How do we trial each option before committing to one?
faqs.answer: Run them in the same fortnight if you can. Ask a local visiting tutor for a first session, ask a centre for a trial class, and take a trial lesson with us, which is at no charge, one per family, with no card details taken beforehand. Then compare what each produced rather than what each promised: did the tutor identify something specific, did they name the syllabus topics at issue, and did they say what the next six weeks would contain? Two real sessions tell you more than ten descriptions. Nobody should expect a family to choose a format blind.

faqs.question: Does a home tutor need to be told my child's school deadlines?
faqs.answer: Any tutor does, under any option, and surprisingly often nobody passes them on. Internal assessment dates, mock windows and Extended Essay checkpoints are set by the school's own departments, and a tutor working without them plans against a generic calendar rather than your child's. Write every internal deadline on one page at the start of the year and give a copy to whoever teaches your child privately. A tutor who does not ask for that list within the first two sessions is working from a template, which is worth noticing early rather than in February.

faqs.question: What should be written down before any tutoring arrangement starts?
faqs.answer: Three things, and they take ten minutes. The weekly time, set against when your child is genuinely home rather than when school ends. What happens if a session is missed by either side. And the coursework boundary: that internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay are the student's own work, that the tutor teaches, questions and explains criteria, and that no text which will be assessed comes from the tutor. That last point protects the student, because an academic-honesty breach is a malpractice matter for the candidate rather than for the person who caused it.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor.closingHeading: Choose the option, then choose the tutor

Decide first whether you need physical presence, tuition at home, or one-to-one at your chosen hour, because that answer eliminates two of the four options immediately. Then ask every remaining candidate the permit question and get the coursework boundary in writing. If the answer leads you to a local visiting tutor, this page has given you the market bands to judge the quote against. If it leads to live one-to-one over video, take the trial lesson, which runs at no charge, one per family, with no card details taken first, and judge the match on what the session actually produced.

intro.heading: The two situations behind this search, and why both need a plan before a tutor
paragraphs: Almost everyone searching for help across both boards in Al Ain is in one of two positions. The first is a single student in transition: a Year 11 finishing IGCSE and starting the Diploma Programme in September, usually with a sense that the step up is real but no concrete idea where it will bite. The second is a household with siblings on different tracks, one sitting Cambridge IGCSE papers and another two years into the Diploma, with one family budget, one evening and one set of school runs to fit both into.

Those two problems have one thing in common: the hard part is not finding someone who knows the subject. It is sequencing. A transition student does not need Diploma content in June of Year 11; they need to know which habits built for an IGCSE mark scheme will cost them marks in a Diploma paper, and which three or four topics the Diploma assumes they already own. A two-board household does not need two full tutoring programmes; it needs a decision about which child's problem is costing more grades this term, because almost no family can fund and sustain both at full intensity.

The step between the systems is real and specific rather than general. IGCSE rewards accurate recall and clean method under time pressure, and its mark schemes are relatively mechanical: the mark is there or it is not. Diploma papers want the same accuracy plus sustained reasoning, evaluation and, in several subjects, a command of unfamiliar data. Internal assessment moves from being a small component or absent entirely at IGCSE to being a substantial, individually produced piece of work marked against lettered criteria in most Diploma subjects. A student who was efficient at IGCSE and is now sinking is usually meeting those two changes rather than running out of ability.

Al Ain adds a supply dimension to all of this. The city is part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi and its private schools are licensed by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Its private-school set is considerably smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, so Higher Level Diploma sciences and the less common languages are the recurring gaps, and a household needing one tutor for Cambridge 0580 and another for Higher Level Chemistry is drawing on two pools, one comfortable and one thin.

On delivery, the position is stated rather than implied. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE and holds no office, centre or branch in the country, because in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Al Ain families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For a two-board household that is a practical advantage before it is anything else: back-to-back slots for two children in different systems, with no tutor's journey between them and no requirement that one person happen to know both boards.

al-ain/ib-igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: A household crossing both systems is dealing with up to four stages at once. These are the stages, what each actually assesses, and what an Al Ain family should be watching for in each.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced from the start, which is the single biggest difference from a Key Stage 3 course. Students are assessed against published criteria with descriptors rather than against a mark total, and the habit of reading a descriptor and writing to it is the most transferable skill the programme builds. Personal Project sits at the end of MYP 5.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Ain, MYP students sometimes move into an IGCSE track rather than straight into the Diploma, because of which schools offer what. That crossing is underestimated: MYP students arrive at IGCSE strong on extended reasoning and short on the mechanical accuracy and timed recall that an IGCSE paper rewards.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years ending in externally marked papers. Cambridge Extended sciences use a multiple-choice paper worth 30%, an extended theory paper worth 50% and Paper 6 Alternative to Practical worth 20%. Pearson's 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 use two written papers with practical skills assessed inside them. Mathematics splits into Core and Extended for 0580, Foundation and Higher for 4MA1.
programmes.countryNote: The grade matters more in Al Ain than in a larger city, because it decides whether a Higher Level combination is available locally at all. A student who wants Higher Level Chemistry and Physics in a city with fewer Diploma places needs the IGCSE grades that make that case, and sometimes a conversation about commuting.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme, subjects at SL and HL
programmes.description: Six subjects, three or four at Higher Level, each with external papers and, in most subjects, an internally assessed component produced by the student and marked against lettered criteria set out in the current subject guide. The step from IGCSE is in sustained reasoning, evaluation and handling unfamiliar material rather than in volume of content alone.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. This page publishes no specific IB exam or results date, because no IB session date in this project has been confirmed against the IB itself; confirm every date with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org before planning around it.

programmes.name: The Diploma core: Extended Essay, TOK and CAS
programmes.description: The Extended Essay is an independent research piece with a word limit set in the current IB guidance; Theory of Knowledge is assessed through an essay and an exhibition; CAS is not academically assessed but is a completion requirement. The core is where most Diploma time management fails, because none of it has a weekly deadline from a teacher.
programmes.countryNote: This is also where the integrity line matters most. A tutor may teach research skills, question a research question, and give written feedback on a student's own draft. No tutor may write, complete or produce an Extended Essay, TOK essay or Internal Assessment, and a provider offering to is putting the student's diploma at risk, not their own business.

al-ain/ib-igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: For the Diploma side of a two-board household, these are the subjects Al Ain families most often need, with what each actually assesses and where the step up from IGCSE is felt.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route that assumes algebraic fluency from the first week. An IGCSE Extended student arrives with the technique but not the habit of proof and sustained multi-part reasoning. The internally assessed exploration is where most SL students lose ground, because it needs a question narrow enough to answer properly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, data and technology-led work rather than proof. Students who chose it to avoid algebra discover that the reasoning demand is comparable and the statistics content is heavier. University prerequisites differ between the two routes, which is a decision to check before DP1 rather than after.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The largest jump from IGCSE of any science. Questions build across several parts, graphs must be interpreted rather than read, and uncertainty treatment becomes an assessed skill. HL adds substantial content on top. Students who scored well at IGCSE on recall meet reasoning here for the first time.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry most of the difficulty, and the internally assessed investigation demands a genuinely testable question. Al Ain's thinner Higher Level pool makes this one of the subjects where local tutor supply runs out soonest.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume is the obvious challenge and command terms are the real one: distinguish, outline, evaluate and discuss each demand a different structure, and marks go missing when a knowledgeable student writes the wrong shape of answer. Data-based questions reward practice more than rereading notes.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, definition precision and evaluation decide the grade. Students arriving from IGCSE Business or Economics carry useful vocabulary and underestimate how much of the mark sits in the evaluative final paragraph of a long answer.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with tools that must be applied to the stimulus rather than described. The internally assessed work requires real organisational material, which is a research and access problem as much as an analytical one and benefits from early planning.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen text analysis and comparative work, assessed partly through oral components. The step from IGCSE English is from writing about a text to constructing an argument about how a text works, which is a different skill and the main reason strong IGCSE candidates stumble.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: For students working in English as an additional language. Receptive, productive and interactive skills are all assessed, including oral components, so practice has to include speaking rather than only writing. Progress is visible quickly with structured weekly work.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Algorithmic thinking, data structures and a substantial internally assessed solution developed for a real client. Suits students who enjoyed Cambridge 0478, and it is one of the thinnest Higher Level pools in a smaller city like Al Ain.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Study-based argument: students must deploy named research accurately and evaluate it. The failure mode is describing studies rather than using them, which is a structural habit a tutor can correct quickly once it is identified from a marked paper.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Separate routes for first-language and additional-language candidates, and the mismatch between them is a common tutoring error. Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic alongside their licensed curriculum, so most Al Ain students carry Arabic in some form regardless of their Diploma choices.

al-ain/ib-igcse-home-tutor.igcseSubjectsIntro: On the IGCSE side of the same household, these are the subjects and codes to give any tutor before a first session, with the loss pattern each typically produces.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Edexcel 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher tier
igcseSubjects.description: Route and tier are set at entry, months before revision. Marks go on algebraic fractions, non-calculator work and questions where method must be shown. The most comfortable tutor pool in Al Ain, so choose on route experience rather than availability.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Edexcel 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: Electricity, moments and formula rearrangement. Cambridge candidates also carry Paper 6 Alternative to Practical at 20% of the grade, which is written reasoning about experiments and unusually coachable because question types repeat.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Edexcel 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: Three distinct problems inside one subject: moles and reacting masses need drilling, qualitative analysis needs a memorised table, organic chemistry needs pattern recognition. A general Chemistry booking usually addresses whichever the tutor prefers.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Edexcel 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: Command terms do most of the damage. Describe, explain and suggest want different answer shapes, and a knowledgeable student scoring half marks is almost always meeting that rather than a content gap.

igcseSubjects.name: Coordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654)
igcseSubjects.description: Widely used in Al Ain because triple science blocks are small. The paper structure differs from the single sciences, so timed practice must use 0654 papers. Preparation with 0625 or 0620 material builds misplaced confidence.

igcseSubjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500, Edexcel 4EA1)
igcseSubjects.description: Directed writing and composition carry the grade, and the work is writing to a mark scheme rather than writing well. Useful groundwork for English A at Diploma level, though the analytical demand there is a genuine step up.

igcseSubjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606), Further Pure (Edexcel 4PM1)
igcseSubjects.description: The best preparation available for Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and the thinnest tutor pool in Al Ain. Calculus notation, binomial expansion and trigonometric identities carry the lost marks.

igcseSubjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (Cambridge 0450, 0455)
igcseSubjects.description: Case-study technique and the evaluation mark at the end of long questions. Students continuing into Diploma Economics or Business Management carry the vocabulary forward and have to rebuild the answer structure.

igcseSubjects.name: Computer Science and ICT (Cambridge 0478, 0417)
igcseSubjects.description: Pseudocode and trace tables for 0478; timed practical technique for 0417. Both work well over live video because the whole subject lives on a shared screen, and 0478 is the natural feeder into Diploma Computer Science.

regions.name: Al Jimi
regions.note: Central and dense by Al Ain standards, with short school runs. Households here can usually run two consecutive sessions from 5pm, which is the only part of the city where a double evening starts that early and holds.

regions.name: Al Mutaredh and Al Khabisi
regions.note: The districts where two-board households are most common, because the mixed curriculum catchments nearby mean siblings often attend different schools. Back-to-back slots are the standard arrangement rather than the exception.

regions.name: Falaj Hazza and Al Muwaiji
regions.note: Established villa districts with the study space for two students working separately. The constraint is arrival time rather than room, which is why a 5.30pm first slot and a 7pm second slot is the pattern that survives a term.

regions.name: Hili and Al Qattara
regions.note: Longer northern bus routes, so the first session rarely starts before 5.30pm and the second lands after 7pm. Shorter sessions work better here than longer ones nobody has the energy for.

regions.name: Al Towayya and Asharej
regions.note: Near the university quarter and heavy on academic households, which shows in the requests: Higher Level sciences and Extended Mathematics rather than general homework support, and planned blocks rather than open bookings.

regions.name: Zakher
regions.note: Spread-out southern district where local supply thins fastest for Higher Level subjects. For a household needing both an IGCSE tutor and a Diploma specialist, the Diploma side is the one that will not be found nearby.

regions.name: Al Maqam and Al Yahar
regions.note: Outlying districts where a tutor's round trip can exceed a lesson, let alone two. A no-journey arrangement from 4.30pm is what makes two sessions in one evening practical at all here.

regions.name: Al Foah and Al Sarooj
regions.note: Fewer private-school catchments nearby, so families routinely look beyond their own area for subject help. For Diploma subjects that is the normal position rather than a compromise.

schoolClusters.note: Al Ain has fewer Diploma places than Abu Dhabi island, which has two consequences for a household. Higher Level combinations can be limited, and a student wanting a specific pairing sometimes commutes or changes school. It also means Diploma cohorts are small, so a subject may be taught by one teacher with no departmental second opinion available.

For a sibling pair split across IGCSE and the Diploma, these are usually the schools on the IGCSE side of the household.
