sections.heading: What an IB IGCSE home tutor in Al Ain means in practice
paragraphs: The phrase bundles three different requests. Some families want one person who can teach both systems, which exists but is rarer than the search implies, because the boards reward different things and genuine fluency in both is a specialist position rather than a default. Some want a tutor for a student moving between the systems, which is a transition job with a defined shape. And some want two tutors in one arrangement for two children, which is a scheduling and budget problem more than a teaching one.

On home tutoring specifically, the market position in Al Ain deserves a straight answer. In-home one-to-one tutoring exists here and families use it. Published UAE rates run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor working online, with monthly packages seen around AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions and around AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are market observations read in October 2026 and attributed to the providers who published them, not an IB Gram price list.

For a two-board household the arithmetic turns sharply. Two children at an in-home rate, each weekly, is a monthly figure most families will not sustain for two years, and it requires either one tutor who covers both boards or two separate journeys into the same evening. In a city where Higher Level Diploma sciences are a thin local pool, the chance that the person who can drive to Zakher on Tuesdays also happens to teach both Cambridge 0580 Extended and Higher Level Chemistry is small.

IB Gram's arrangement removes that constraint and the page should say how. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE and no premises in the country; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Al Ain families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which makes two consecutive sessions with two different specialists an ordinary Tuesday rather than a logistical feat. sections.heading: The IGCSE-to-Diploma gap, subject by subject
paragraphs: This is the section Al Ain families actually need and almost nobody writes. The step from IGCSE into the Diploma Programme is not uniform. In some subjects it is mostly content, in others mostly reasoning, and in a few it is a new kind of assessment the student has never met. Knowing which of those applies to your child's chosen Higher Levels tells you where the summer before DP1 should go.

Mathematics is the clearest case. A student arriving in Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level from Cambridge 0580 Extended has the algebraic technique but not the habit of proof, and will meet multi-part questions where each part depends on the last. A student arriving from Additional Mathematics 0606 is in a much stronger position, which is why 0606 is worth taking if the school offers it and worth building externally if it does not. Applications and Interpretation looks gentler and demands comparable reasoning with heavier statistics.

The sciences split differently. Physics is the largest jump, because IGCSE rewards recall and clean substitution while Diploma Physics asks for interpretation, uncertainty handling and reasoning across several parts of a question. Chemistry's jump sits in energetics, equilibrium and mechanisms. Biology's is volume plus command terms. In all three, the internally assessed investigation is a research-design task that no IGCSE course prepares a student for, and it is the single most common source of DP1 panic.

The table maps the main routes. Treat the weeks column as a planning estimate for a focused transition block rather than a promise, and read it alongside the subject's own current guide, which your school's IB coordinator holds. The point of the table is to let a family spend the summer on the two subjects where the gap is widest rather than on all six equally.

sections.heading: What changes between an IGCSE paper and a Diploma paper
paragraphs: Underneath every subject-specific gap sits the same structural shift, and naming it helps a student more than another topic list. IGCSE assessment is mostly externally examined, relatively mechanical in its marking, and built around accurate recall and clean method under time pressure. Marks are discrete: a unit is present or absent, a step is shown or missing. That rewards a particular kind of efficiency, and students who are good at it become good at it quickly.

Diploma assessment keeps all of that and adds two things. The first is sustained reasoning: longer questions where later parts depend on earlier ones, unfamiliar data to interpret, and evaluation marks that require a judgement rather than a fact. The second is internal assessment. In most Diploma subjects the student produces an individually assessed piece of work marked against lettered criteria, each with its own mark allocation published in the current subject guide. A student who has only ever sat papers has never managed a project with no weekly deadline before.

Command terms change too, and this is where good IGCSE candidates lose marks first. At IGCSE the working set is dominated by describe, explain, calculate and suggest. At Diploma level the same words appear with greater expectations alongside outline, distinguish, discuss, evaluate, justify and to what extent. A student who answers a discuss question with a well-organised description has written something accurate that scores poorly, and will usually insist the marking was harsh. The fix is reading the command-term list in the subject guide and practising each shape deliberately.

The practical lesson for a transition block is to spend the first two or three sessions on assessment literacy rather than on content. Read the criteria. Read the command terms. Mark a past answer together against the published descriptors. That work is boring and it pays immediately, because it changes every answer the student writes for the next two years rather than one topic.

sections.heading: Internal assessment: what a tutor may do, and the line that protects the diploma
paragraphs: Internal assessment is the part of the Diploma where families are most often sold something they should refuse. One provider competing in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright. That is an academic-integrity breach under IB rules, and the consequence lands on the student, who can lose the qualification, rather than on the seller. IB Gram does not write, complete or produce an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay, Personal Project or any assessed coursework, and does not edit a draft until it stops being the student's own work.

What a tutor may legitimately do covers most of what actually helps. Teach the skills the task assesses. Explain the criteria and their descriptors in the student's own words, using the current subject guide the school holds. Interrogate a research question before three weeks are spent on an unanswerable one, which is the commonest cause of a weak internal assessment. Model an analysis on different data so the method is understood rather than copied. Read the student's own draft and say where a claim is unsupported. Hold a schedule of internal deadlines the student actually meets.

The distinction a parent can hold onto is that a tutor works on the student's thinking and never on the student's text. If a session produces sentences the student did not write, the line has been crossed. If it produces a student who can explain why their own paragraph was weak, it has not. Ask any prospective tutor to state their position on this before the first session, and treat vagueness as an answer.

There is a copyright dimension as well. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides are referenced and linked from their official sources, never reproduced or supplied as downloads. A provider offering to send you a folder of board material is telling you how else they cut corners. For current IB subject guides and command-term lists, the school's IB coordinator is the correct and legitimate source.

sections.heading: The other transitions an Al Ain household meets
paragraphs: IGCSE to Diploma is the headline crossing, and it is not the only one. Al Ain's smaller school set means students move between curricula more often than in a city with more options, usually because a family relocates within the UAE, because a school changes its offer, or because the subject combination a student wants exists somewhere else. Each crossing has a predictable gap, and naming it converts a vague worry into a few weeks of targeted work.

MYP into IGCSE is the crossing families underestimate most. MYP students arrive strong on extended reasoning and criterion-referenced writing and short on mechanical accuracy and timed recall, which is exactly what an IGCSE paper rewards. The work is not remedial; it is a change of register. Three or four weeks of timed short-answer drilling usually closes it, and a student who was told they were weak often turns out to have been well prepared for a different test.

CBSE or another national curriculum into IGCSE runs the opposite way. Those students typically arrive with strong computational fluency and meet a question style that asks them to explain, justify and apply rather than to reproduce. The first weeks of any tutoring arrangement should go on question style and command terms before any new content is touched, because the gap is in how answers are rewarded rather than in what is known.

American curriculum into the Diploma, and British Year 11 into DP1, are their own cases, and in every one the useful first step is the same: an assumed-knowledge audit for the specific subjects chosen, not a general catch-up. sections.heading: Two children, one evening, one budget
paragraphs: This is the practical problem a two-board household actually has, and it is arithmetic before it is pedagogy. Start with the evening. One child arrives home from an Al Ain school run between 4pm and 5pm depending on the district and the route; the other may arrive later. Two 90-minute sessions plus food and the rest of life does not fit before a reasonable bedtime for a Year 10, so something gives. Usually what gives is the younger child's session, quietly, over about six weeks.

Then the money. At the published market band for a qualified subject tutor, roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, two children at 90 minutes a week each runs to a monthly figure most families will reconsider by the second term, and the in-home band of AED 180 to AED 500 an hour makes it considerably steeper. The honest planning answer is usually not two full programmes. It is one child at a time, chosen on evidence, with a stated plan to reassess.

Choosing between your own children feels uncomfortable and is the right call. The deciding question is which subject is costing the most grades relative to what it will take to fix, and that comes from marked papers rather than from who seems more upset. A command-term problem in Diploma Biology may be a six-session fix with a large payoff. A content gap across two years of Chemistry is a term's work. A Year 10 who is coping can usually wait a term; a DP2 student four months from the May session cannot.

The table runs the arithmetic for the common household shapes at published market bands, so a family can see the real monthly commitment before agreeing to anything. These are market figures, not IB Gram prices; our rate is agreed after a free trial lesson and a tutor match, and the structure that works for most two-board households is sequential rather than simultaneous.

sections.heading: Two calendars in one house: IGCSE series and the Diploma year
paragraphs: A household running both boards is running two timetables that do not align, and planning them together is the most useful thing a parent can do in September. On the IGCSE side the dates are published and sourced. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year.

Entry deadlines are the pressure point. Cambridge's published March 2027 series had final entries due 27 November 2026 for an exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results to centres on 13 May and certificates in late June. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables in advance, and because they can be revised, work from the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

On the Diploma side this page is deliberately thin, and that is a factual position rather than an omission. UAE schools sit the May session. No IB session, upload or results date in this project has been confirmed against the IB itself, so no specific IB date appears here; confirm every one with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org, and plan the DP2 year from the school's own internal deadline calendar, which is the document that actually governs an internally assessed component.

One operational detail affects the IGCSE child directly. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the centre's zone, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Your school's exams officer knows the zone. And Ramadan, whose dates move each year, reshapes the study day for both children at once: shorter school hours, post-Iftar sessions, consolidation rather than full timed papers, with the heavy practice moved to the weeks either side.

sections.heading: Permits, ADEK and what to verify before you pay anyone
paragraphs: The checks are the same for both boards and they take one message. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The official route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a published two-working-day completion time.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published by the ministry, so any specific amount quoted to you is unsourced and none appears on this page. A tutor who says the permit costs money or takes months has not applied for one, since it is free and the published completion time is two working days.

For Al Ain, the ADEK layer matters. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, and its professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school; the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. This is press-reported rather than quoted from the current ADEK policy document, so verify the exact wording with ADEK. In a two-board household the temptation is larger, because one parent often knows one child's teacher well. Do not pursue it.

Finally, status. A tutoring operation with premises and staff needs an educational services permit from the relevant education authority, which is a different instrument from an individual's tutor permit. IB Gram is an independent online tutor-matching platform with no premises, centre or branch in the UAE, and holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. On Ministry of Education equivalency, the published British-track rule asks for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. No IB points threshold is published in the sources used here, so none is stated; verify on moe.gov.ae, and note that equivalency is a process the Ministry runs rather than anything a tutoring provider performs or guarantees.

process.title: Say which situation you are in
process.description: One student crossing from IGCSE into the Diploma, or two children on different boards. The two need different plans, and telling us which saves a conversation. For a transition, send the chosen Higher Level subjects; for a household, send both children's subjects, boards and year groups.

process.title: Send the codes and one marked paper per child
process.description: For the IGCSE side, the board, syllabus code, tier and series. For the Diploma side, the subjects and levels and the school's internal deadline calendar. One recently marked paper per child turns a description of the problem into a diagnosis a specialist can act on.

process.title: Agree which child gets the hours first
process.description: Most households cannot sustain two full programmes, and pretending otherwise produces two half-programmes that move nothing. We will say which loss pattern looks cheapest to fix and which deadline is closest, and recommend an order, including the option to start with one child and reassess next term.

process.title: Take the free trial before any rate is agreed
process.description: One trial per child, with the relevant specialist rather than one person stretched across both boards. Use it to test whether the tutor can read the marked paper and name the loss. If a match is wrong, say so and a different specialist is proposed; nothing is paid before a match is agreed.

process.title: Fix consecutive slots the school run survives
process.description: Work backwards from each child's normal arrival time, not the best case, and add thirty minutes. Central Al Ain households usually run 5pm and 6.30pm; Hili, Zakher, Al Maqam and Al Yahar households are better served from 5.30pm and 7pm. No journey sits between the two sessions.

process.title: Review each child separately on marked work
process.description: Every four to six weeks, compare marked papers side by side per child rather than comparing siblings. If a loss pattern has closed, that child's hours can move to the other. Reduction and stopping are legitimate outcomes and should be stated out loud at each review.

whyPoints.title: Two boards, two specialists, one schedule
whyPoints.description: Each child is matched to a tutor who has taught their own specification rather than one person stretched across both systems. Cambridge Extended sciences, Pearson's two-paper structure and Diploma internal assessment reward different work, and fluency in one does not imply fluency in another.

whyPoints.title: The transition treated as its own job
whyPoints.description: A defined block across the end of Year 11 and the first term of DP1, aimed at assumed knowledge, command terms and the first internally assessed task. It is the cheapest intervention in the whole Diploma, because preventing a DP1 spring crisis costs a fraction of repairing one.

whyPoints.title: Honest budget arithmetic
whyPoints.description: This page runs the monthly numbers at published market bands for one child and for two, because a household needs the real figure before agreeing to anything. The arrangement most families sustain is sequential, and we will say so rather than selling two programmes.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Teaching, criteria explanation, research-question interrogation and written feedback on the student's own draft. No writing, completing or producing an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, TOK essay or Personal Project. A provider in this market sells completed IAs; the student carries that risk, not the seller.

whyPoints.title: Dates only where they are sourced
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson milestones on this page come from the boards' own published material. No IB exam or results date appears, because none has been confirmed against the IB itself. A page that invents a date for an assessment calendar is worse than a page that admits the gap.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and coverage both disclosed
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; there are no home visits in the UAE and no premises in the country, since in-home tutoring runs only in India. Where a Higher Level subject has no specialist free, we give a realistic match time instead of placing a generalist.

faqs.question: Will one tutor cover both my children if one sits IGCSE and the other the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, but it is rarely the best arrangement. The boards reward different work: IGCSE marking is largely mechanical and externally examined, while Diploma subjects add sustained reasoning and an individually produced internally assessed component marked against lettered criteria. Genuine fluency in both is a specialist position rather than a default. The arrangement that works better is two specialists in consecutive slots in the same evening, each with their own plan for their own child, which over live video involves no journey between the two and no compromise on specification match.

faqs.question: What actually gets harder between IGCSE and the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Two things, and neither is simply volume. The first is sustained reasoning: Diploma questions build across parts, present unfamiliar data to interpret, and carry evaluation marks that need a judgement rather than a fact. The second is internal assessment, where the student produces an individually marked piece of work against lettered criteria in the current subject guide, with no weekly deadline from a teacher. Command terms widen too, from describe, explain and calculate to include discuss, evaluate, justify and to what extent, and a well-organised description of a discuss question scores poorly.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subject is the biggest jump from IGCSE for an Al Ain student?
faqs.answer: Physics, in most cases. IGCSE Physics rewards recall and clean substitution into a formula, while Diploma Physics asks for graph interpretation, uncertainty handling and reasoning across several parts of one question, with Higher Level adding substantial content on top. Chemistry's jump sits in energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is a large step unless the student has taken Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 or Pearson Further Pure 4PM1, which is the best available preparation and worth building externally if the school does not offer it.

faqs.question: When should a transition block between Year 11 and DP1 happen?
faqs.answer: Across the summer after the IGCSE papers and into the first term of DP1, which is when the gap is visible and still cheap to close. Eight to twelve sessions aimed at assumed knowledge for the chosen Higher Levels, the command terms that change, and the first internally assessed task planned rather than rushed. The alternative is the DP1 spring, when a student is carrying six subjects, the core, and a first internal assessment deadline at once, and repair work costs several times what prevention would have.

faqs.question: Where exactly is the line on Internal Assessment help for a DP1 student?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear line. A tutor may teach the skills the task assesses, explain the criteria and descriptors from the current subject guide, interrogate a research question before weeks are wasted on an unanswerable one, model an analysis on different data, read the student's own draft and say where a claim is unsupported, and hold a deadline schedule. A tutor may not write it, complete it, or edit it until the voice is no longer the student's. A provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments, and the student who submits bought work carries the malpractice consequence.

faqs.question: How do we choose which child gets the tutoring budget?
faqs.answer: On evidence and on deadlines rather than on who seems more distressed. Look at marked papers for both and ask which loss pattern is costing the most grades relative to what it will take to fix: a command-term problem in Diploma Biology may be a six-session fix with a large payoff, while a two-year content gap in Chemistry is a term's work. Then weigh proximity to a deadline. A DP2 student months from the May session cannot wait; a Year 10 who is coping usually can, and should be revisited next term.

faqs.question: Is my child moving from MYP into IGCSE at a disadvantage?
faqs.answer: Differently prepared rather than behind. MYP students arrive strong on extended reasoning and on writing to criteria, and short on the mechanical accuracy and timed short-answer recall an IGCSE paper rewards. That is a change of register rather than a knowledge deficit, and three to five weeks of timed drilling usually closes it. The misdiagnosis to avoid is treating it as weakness: a student told they are struggling often turns out to have been well prepared for a different kind of test, and responds very quickly once the format is practised.

faqs.question: Does Al Ain have enough Diploma Programme places for a Higher Level science combination?
faqs.answer: Fewer than Abu Dhabi island, which has a real effect on choice. Al Ain's private-school set is smaller, so Diploma cohorts are small and Higher Level combinations can be limited, with a subject sometimes taught by one teacher and no departmental second opinion available. Some students commute or change school for a particular pairing. The planning advice is to establish in Year 10, not Year 11, whether the combination your child wants is available locally, because the IGCSE grades needed to make that case are earned before the question becomes urgent.

faqs.question: What does an IB Diploma tutor cost compared with an IGCSE tutor in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Higher at the specialist end, because the pool is thinner. Published market bands put a qualified subject tutor online at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists quoted at roughly AED 200 to AED 450 and premium named tutors as high as AED 650. In-home one-to-one runs roughly AED 180 to AED 500 with travel included. Those are market observations from October 2026 attributed to the providers who published them, not IB Gram prices; our rate follows a free trial lesson and a tutor match.

faqs.question: How do we schedule two tutoring sessions in one Al Ain evening?
faqs.answer: Work backwards from each child's actual arrival time and add thirty minutes for food. Central districts such as Al Jimi and Al Mutaredh usually sustain a 5pm and a 6.30pm slot. Hili, Zakher, Al Maqam and Al Yahar households, with longer bus routes, are generally better at 5.30pm and 7pm. The reason two consecutive sessions work at all over live video is that nobody travels between them, so the second starts when the first ends rather than when a tutor arrives.

faqs.question: Do the IGCSE and IB exam calendars clash for a household running both?
faqs.answer: They overlap in the spring, which is exactly why a household plan matters. Cambridge and Pearson both run a May/June series and a November series, and UAE schools sit the May IB session, so April and May are the pressure months for both children at once. This page publishes no specific IB date because none has been confirmed against the IB itself, so build the Diploma child's plan from the school's own internal deadline calendar and the coordinator's dates, and diarise the IGCSE child's entry deadlines in November.

faqs.question: Should my child take Additional Mathematics 0606 before the Diploma?
faqs.answer: If the school offers it and the student is aiming at Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, yes. It is the single best preparation available, because it introduces calculus notation, binomial expansion and trigonometric identities in a form the Diploma course assumes. The complication in Al Ain is supply: 0606 has the thinnest tutor pool of any IGCSE subject here, cohorts are very small, and school clinics for it are rare. If it is not offered, a focused block on the same content before DP1 achieves much of the same effect.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education relevant to a household on both boards?
faqs.answer: Yes, in two ways. Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed curriculum, so both children carry them regardless of board, and that workload is real when planning tutoring hours. Second, on Ministry of Education British-track equivalency, Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects required at no less than E or grade 3, so they cannot be counted towards that total. Verify the current wording on moe.gov.ae before relying on it.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our home in Al Ain for either board?
faqs.answer: No. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE and no office, centre or branch in the country, because in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Both children are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For a two-board household this is the practical advantage: two specialists, two consecutive slots, no journey between them, and a shortlist for each child drawn from everyone who has taught that specification rather than from whoever can reach your district by six.

faqs.question: What should we verify about any tutor before the first paid session?
faqs.answer: The MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is granted free of charge for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and applied for through MoHRE's own service with a published two-working-day completion time. Then the specification: which board, which code, which level, and how recently. Then the commercial terms in writing: per hour or per session, what happens to a missed session, and whether the figure includes any tax the provider must charge, which should be confirmed with the provider and against the Federal Tax Authority rather than assumed.

faqs.question: How do we know the Diploma side is working when the next exam is a year away?
faqs.answer: Use the school's own assessment points and the internally assessed timeline as the evidence, not a feeling about engagement. In DP1 that means school tests, the first internal assessment proposal and draft, and marked past-paper questions against the published criteria. Ask for the annotated work from each session to be saved and sent, plus a short written note of what was covered and set. At the four-to-six-week review, compare two pieces of marked work directly. If the loss pattern has not changed, the plan should, not the student.

intro.heading: The search that usually comes from a household running two curricula
paragraphs: A single parent search for IB IGCSE tuition near me in Al Ain almost never comes from a household with one child on one syllabus. It comes from a family where an older sibling is eighteen months from Diploma examinations and a younger one is sitting Cambridge papers in the summer, and where both need help in the same four-week window. The question behind the search is not really about distance. It is about whether one arrangement can carry two different assessment systems without the week collapsing.

Al Ain makes that question sharper than Dubai does. The city is part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so its private schools answer to the Department of Education and Knowledge rather than to KHDA, and its private-school set is far smaller than the capital's. A family on Khalifa Street may find that the nearest school offering Higher Level Chemistry and the nearest school offering Edexcel International GCSE Further Maths are twenty minutes apart in different directions. The pool of local specialist tutors is thinner again, because it tracks the number of schools rather than the number of students.

The practical result is that proximity stops being the useful filter. A tutor eight minutes away who last taught Core IGCSE Maths four years ago is not a better match for a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches student than a specialist who appears on screen at seven in the evening Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram works on that basis: lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service offered only in India, not anywhere in the UAE. That is stated plainly here because the alternative is to let a parent assume otherwise.

There is a second Al Ain-specific wrinkle. Because the city sits 130 kilometres inland from the capital, families here sometimes treat Abu Dhabi island as the overflow option for anything the local schools cannot timetable, and a weekly drive to a tutor in the capital is genuinely proposed in some households. Counted honestly, that is three hours of road for one taught hour, repeated weekly through an examination year. The same hour on screen costs nothing in travel and widens the pool from one city to the whole market, which is the trade most families accept once it is set out as arithmetic rather than as a sales line.

What follows is the detail a two-curriculum household actually needs. How ADEK frames an Al Ain school and what its published reports do and do not tell you. Where the IGCSE route and the Diploma route diverge, subject by subject, so a Year 11 decision is made on evidence. The two exam calendars laid over one family year, counted backwards from the papers rather than forwards from today. What the Ministry of Education requires from each track at the end. And what the Al Ain market charges in AED per hour, with the source of every band named, so you can judge any quote you receive against something checkable.

al-ain/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.programmesIntro: Three programmes cover almost every Al Ain household that searches this phrase: the Middle Years Programme in the years before the Diploma, the international GCSE taken under Cambridge or Pearson, and the Diploma itself. The notes below are specific to what Al Ain schools can and cannot timetable.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessment is criterion-referenced. Each subject group is marked against four criteria, A to D, each on a nought-to-eight scale, and the four are converted to a single grade of one to seven by published boundaries. A student can produce stronger work than last term and still drop a grade band if the criteria weighted that term were different ones. Understanding which criterion a piece of work was marked against is the whole of the diagnosis.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Ain the MYP is run by a small number of IB World Schools, which means a student who needs support in a specific subject group often cannot find a classmate at another local school on the same unit. Families frequently pair MYP support with Cambridge preparation, because several Al Ain schools move students onto IGCSE papers in Year 10 rather than continuing MYP to Year 11.

programmes.name: International GCSE
programmes.description: Two boards dominate the UAE: Cambridge International, with syllabus codes such as 0580 Mathematics and 0620 Chemistry, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, with codes such as 4MA1 and 4CH1. The two award the same qualification in a university's eyes but set different papers, tier differently, and assess practical science by different routes. A tutor who has only taught one of them will misread the other board's mark scheme.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain's British-curriculum schools split between the two boards, and some run one board for sciences and another for mathematics. Before booking any tuition, check the syllabus code on your child's own specification sheet rather than the board name on the school website, because option blocks are set per subject and the website is often a year behind.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject is graded one to seven, giving forty-two subject points, with up to three further points from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix. The maximum total is forty-five. Internal assessment carries twenty to thirty per cent of most subject grades, so a meaningful share of the total is settled before any written paper.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain's Diploma cohorts are small, which has two consequences. Option blocks are tight, so a student wanting Higher Level Physics alongside Higher Level Economics may find the timetable will not allow it. And where a subject attracts five candidates, the school may run it with a teacher covering three subjects. Both are reasons Al Ain families look outside the city for subject-specialist support.

programmes.name: International A Level
programmes.description: The main alternative to the Diploma after IGCSE, taken as three or four subjects with no compulsory core. It suits a student with a settled subject direction and a weak spot in one of the six Diploma groups, typically a second language. Papers are longer and narrower than Diploma papers, and the step up from Extended IGCSE in the same subject is steeper than most Year 11 students expect.
programmes.countryNote: Several Al Ain British-curriculum schools run A Levels rather than the Diploma, so the Year 11 decision in this city is often a decision between two schools as well as two qualifications. The Ministry of Education's British-track equivalency route is written around A Levels and AS Levels, which is one reason families weigh it seriously here.

al-ain/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones Al Ain households most often need on both sides of the house at once: an IGCSE version for the younger child and a Diploma version for the older one. Each note says what the assessment actually rewards.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: IGCSE Core and Extended · DP Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation HL/SL
subjects.description: The commonest double booking in an Al Ain household. Extended IGCSE ends roughly where Standard Level Applications begins, but Analysis and Approaches assumes algebraic fluency that Extended papers never test under time pressure. Marks go on method lines left unwritten and on calculator work shown without the setup.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IGCSE Core and Extended · DP HL and SL
subjects.description: Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 both reward a clear statement of which quantity is constant before any substitution. At Diploma level the loss shifts to uncertainty treatment and to graph gradients quoted without units. Students who were comfortable at IGCSE often stall on the first mechanics paper for exactly this reason.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IGCSE Core and Extended · DP HL and SL
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and moles arithmetic account for most of the gap in both systems. The Diploma adds energetics and equilibrium, where the common error is a sign convention rather than a calculation. Practical skills are assessed by written paper rather than by observed laboratory work in both boards' IGCSE routes.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IGCSE Core and Extended · DP HL and SL
subjects.description: The content volume is the problem rather than the difficulty of any one topic. Command terms decide marks here more than anywhere else: outline, explain and discuss carry different mark tariffs, and a student writing a discussion for an outline question loses time without gaining credit.

subjects.name: English
subjects.levels: IGCSE First Language and Second Language · DP Language A Language and Literature HL/SL
subjects.description: The IGCSE rewards accurate directed writing against a given audience and purpose. The Diploma replaces that with unseen textual analysis and an individual oral built on a global issue. Students who scored well at IGCSE frequently underperform in the first Diploma paper because the task has changed, not because the writing has.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides more marks than prose quality in both. At Diploma level the internal assessment requires three commentaries on published news articles, each with a strict word limit, and the commonest fault is an article too old or too broad to carry the required analysis.

subjects.name: Business
subjects.levels: IGCSE 0450 · DP Business Management HL and SL
subjects.description: Case-study papers in both systems reward applying a named tool to the stimulus rather than describing the tool. The Diploma's pre-released case study for Higher Level rewards preparation done months early, which is the single best use of tuition hours in that subject.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions differ between boards and between the IGCSE and the Diploma, and students lose marks writing valid Python where the mark scheme expects the board's own pseudocode. The Diploma adds a solution-development internal assessment with its own documentation requirements.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.levels: IGCSE First and Foreign Language · DP Language B and ab initio
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the international curriculum for the groups the regulator specifies, and separately examinable. Al Ain households often need two different Arabic streams at once, because a child who took Arabic as a first language at IGCSE may be placed in Language B at Diploma level or the reverse.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for Higher Level mathematics or A Level Maths. It covers calculus and trigonometric identities that Extended 0580 does not, and it is the clearest bridge available in Al Ain for a student who will otherwise meet differentiation for the first time in Diploma year one.

al-ain/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.regionsIntro: Al Ain is spread out, and where a household sits changes which schools are realistic and what time a weekday lesson can start. The notes below are about scheduling and school access rather than scenery.

regions.name: Al Jimi
regions.note: Central and dense, close to Al Jimi Mall and several long-established private schools. Short school runs mean a lesson can usually start by half past four, which is the earliest practical slot for a Diploma student with coursework.

regions.name: Al Muwaiji
regions.note: Western Al Ain, heavily Emirati, with high demand for Arabic as a first language and Islamic Education support running alongside the international curriculum. Two different Arabic streams in one household is common here.

regions.name: Al Mutaredh
regions.note: Older central district near the Al Ain Oasis, within reach of the city's British-curriculum schools. Families here often have one child on IGCSE and an older one who moved to a different campus for sixth form.

regions.name: Asharej
regions.note: East of the centre and close to United Arab Emirates University, so households include academic staff with a clear view of what a UAE university entry profile needs. Evening lessons compete with campus commitments.

regions.name: Falaj Hazza
regions.note: South-west, residential, with several school catchments overlapping. The decision between a Diploma school and an A Level school is live in a lot of these households because both options sit within a fifteen-minute drive.

regions.name: Zakher
regions.note: Southern villa belt, spread thin, with longer runs to the central schools. The late return home is the main constraint on weekday lesson timing, which is why a seven o'clock video slot works better here than a visitor.

regions.name: Al Towayya
regions.note: Near the hospital campus, so shift rotas shape the week. Households here often need a fixed weekly slot that survives a changed rota, and sometimes a weekend slot instead of a weekday one.

regions.name: Hili
regions.note: Northern Al Ain, close to the Omani border crossing at Buraimi. Some households cross the border daily, which affects both the school choice and the reliability of a weekday evening start.

schoolClusters.city: Central and western Al Ain
schoolClusters.note: The city's longest-established private schools sit in this arc. Between them they run British-curriculum IGCSE under both boards, Indian-curriculum streams and an IB pathway, which is why a single household can end up with two children on genuinely different assessment systems.

schoolClusters.city: Southern and eastern Al Ain
schoolClusters.note: Newer campuses on the southern and eastern approaches, including the schools most likely to offer the Diploma rather than A Levels. Families in Zakher, Falaj Hazza and Asharej usually choose between this cluster and the central one on drive time rather than on curriculum.

al-ain/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.modesIntro: Three formats cover what an Al Ain two-curriculum household realistically needs. All three are delivered over live video, one-to-one unless stated, and timed to Gulf Standard Time so a lesson fits between the school run and dinner.

modes.title: Two fixed weekly slots, one per child
modes.description: The arrangement most of these households settle on. Each child has a named tutor for a named syllabus and a slot that does not move week to week, usually back to back on the same evening so the household only loses one evening rather than two. The older child's slot is placed later, because Diploma coursework work benefits from a longer block than an IGCSE revision session does.

modes.title: Exam-term intensive before a series
modes.description: A short block in the eight to ten weeks before a Cambridge, Pearson or Diploma session, built around timed past-paper work rather than new content. Sessions typically double in length and the focus moves to mark-scheme reading: what a four-mark question expects, where a command term changes the answer, and how long each question should actually take.

modes.title: Coursework and internal assessment supervision
modes.description: For the Diploma child, a scheduled sequence of feedback points on the internal assessments, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, timed around the school's own internal deadlines. The tutor reads the student's own drafts, questions the method, and points at the criterion the work is being marked against. The writing stays entirely the student's.

sections.heading: Two curricula under one roof, and what that does to a week
paragraphs: A household with an IGCSE child and a Diploma child is running two different machines. The IGCSE year is content-heavy and assessment-light: almost everything is decided by terminal papers in a single window, with little or no coursework carrying marks. The Diploma is the reverse. Between twenty and thirty per cent of most subject grades is settled by internal assessment completed months before the examinations, and the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge sit outside subject teaching entirely while still contributing to the total.

That difference changes what tuition is for in each case. For the IGCSE child, the most valuable hours are the ones closest to the papers, spent on timed questions and mark-scheme reading. For the Diploma child, the most valuable hours are the ones nobody is asking for yet: the weeks when an internal assessment method is being chosen, long before a deadline appears on the school calendar. A household that treats both children the same way tends to over-tutor the younger one in October and under-support the older one at exactly the point where the marks are being quietly decided.

The second collision is the calendar. Cambridge and Pearson both run a November series alongside the summer one, and internal school mock windows are usually set three to four months before each. Diploma internal deadlines cluster in the same months. In practice this means a family can face an IGCSE mock fortnight, a Diploma internal assessment deadline and an Extended Essay checkpoint inside the same three weeks. Knowing that in September rather than discovering it in February is most of the benefit of planning at household level rather than child by child.
The table below sets out the shape of each child's year side by side. It is deliberately about assessment load rather than content, because that is what competes for the same evenings.

sections.heading: One regulator, two curricula: how ADEK frames an Al Ain school
paragraphs: Al Ain is part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so every private school in the city answers to the Department of Education and Knowledge. The u.ae government portal states that ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. That is a different authority from the one most online tutoring content assumes, because almost all of it is written about Dubai and KHDA. A page that tells an Al Ain parent to check a KHDA inspection report is pointing them at the wrong database.

What matters practically is that ADEK's framework applies to the school, not to the curriculum. An IB World School and a Cambridge school in Al Ain are assessed by the same authority against the same inspection framework, which is why their published reports are comparable in a way their examination results are not. A report can tell you about teaching quality, leadership and the progress of groups of students. It cannot tell you whether that school's Higher Level Chemistry teaching is strong this year, because inspection samples across a school rather than auditing a single subject cohort of nine students.

The regulator map across the UAE is worth knowing if you move, or if you compare schools across emirates when choosing. It is also the part of UAE education nearly every competing tutoring page leaves out: Abu Dhabi's own regulator is not named at all on most of them. The federal baseline sits underneath all of it. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations, which is where the mandatory-subject requirement in every emirate originates.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE stops and the Diploma starts, subject by subject
paragraphs: The Year 11 decision in Al Ain is usually a decision about two schools as well as two qualifications, because the city's campuses split between the Diploma and A Levels. The useful way to make it is subject by subject, against the actual gap between an Extended IGCSE grade and the entry point of the Diploma course in the same subject. The gap is not uniform. In some subjects an Extended grade 7 is genuinely adequate preparation for Higher Level. In others it is not close.

Mathematics is the clearest case and the one that causes the most trouble locally. Extended 0580 or 4MA1 contains no calculus. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level starts using differentiation within the first term and assumes algebraic manipulation at a speed Extended papers never demand. A student arriving from Extended Maths with no exposure to 0606 Additional Mathematics meets that content cold. Applications and Interpretation is a far gentler step from Extended, and it is accepted by many university courses that do not require calculus, so the honest answer in a lot of Al Ain households is that Applications is the better route and nobody has told them so.

Sciences differ from mathematics. The content step from Extended to Standard Level is manageable; the step that catches students is the assessment of experimental work. IGCSE routes in both boards assess practical skills through a written paper. The Diploma requires a designed and reported investigation, marked against criteria that reward the quality of the method and the treatment of uncertainty rather than the neatness of the result. A student can know all the content and still score poorly on that component because nobody taught them what the criteria actually ask for.

Languages and humanities move the other way. Many Al Ain students find the Diploma's humanities subjects more accessible than the IGCSE versions, because the Diploma rewards sustained argument where the IGCSE rewarded coverage. English is the exception: a strong IGCSE First Language grade predicts Diploma Language A performance less well than parents expect, because directed writing and unseen literary analysis are different skills.

sections.heading: Two exam calendars laid over one family year
paragraphs: Entry deadlines are the part of the examination system that surprises parents, because they sit months before the papers and are handled by the school without a letter home. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Cambridge also publishes key dates for a March series, and that series is the clearest illustration of how far ahead the administrative work sits.

For the Cambridge March 2027 series, the examination period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries are due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades are due on 27 February 2027 and results reach centres on Cambridge Direct on 13 May, with certificates in late June. Read that sequence backwards and the implication is plain: the decision about which papers your child sits, and at which tier, is effectively locked more than two months before the first examination. A tier change argued in January is usually too late.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. That is not a detail for schools alone. A parent planning travel around an examination window needs the zone timetable the school actually sits, not a timetable found online.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable is always the document to work from rather than a date restated on a tutoring page. For the Diploma child, the UAE sits the May session, and the registration is handled by the school's IB coordinator; we do not publish specific IB session or results dates here, because the IB's own site is the only reliable source for them and it should be checked directly.

sections.heading: What the Ministry of Education counts from each track
paragraphs: At the end of both routes sits the same question: what does a UAE school leaver need on file to have their certificate recognised here. The equivalency rules are published by the Ministry of Education and they differ by curriculum track, which is precisely why a two-curriculum household should know them early rather than in the summer after the final examinations.

On the British track, as reported when the UAE clarified its equivalency requirements, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That last point matters in Al Ain, where many students take both as mandatory subjects and reasonably assume they count. One competing tutoring site tells UAE families they need six IGCSE subjects; the sourced figure is five.

On the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL internet-based test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test. For the International Baccalaureate, no points threshold is published in that source, so we do not state one. Anyone who tells you the number without pointing at a Ministry page is guessing. Check it on the Ministry's own site or with the emirate attestation authority.

None of this is something a tutoring platform performs or guarantees. Equivalency is a process run by the Ministry and the attestation authorities, and tuition is not a requirement for it. What tuition can do is make sure the grades a student is aiming at clear the thresholds that apply to their track, which is a different and more honest claim.

sections.heading: What tuition for two children actually costs in this market
paragraphs: Published rates for the UAE tutoring market vary by a factor of ten, and almost no competing page in this search prints a single AED figure. The bands below are market rates collected from providers' own published pricing and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. They are not IB Gram's price list. They are there so that a quote you receive in Al Ain can be judged against something, which is the part of the market that is currently opaque.

At the bottom of the market, budget online tutoring from university students runs from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits in the AED 150 to 300 band, where Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An in-home one-to-one visit, travel included, runs roughly AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate quoting 180 to 350 and independent home tutors 200 to 500. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutors sit at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named or examiner-track tutoring reaches AED 650, as BartyED publishes.

The arithmetic that matters to a two-curriculum household is the monthly one. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year support. Monthly packages in the market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Two children at specialist examination-year level is therefore a materially different commitment from one, and the honest planning move is to stagger intensity rather than run both at full rate all year.

Context helps as well. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package. That is a Dubai measure rather than an Abu Dhabi one, so it does not apply to Al Ain fees, but it is a reminder that school fees are the dominant household education cost and tuition is the smaller variable line. IB Gram does not publish a rate card on this page. The sensible next step is a free trial lesson, which is a single introductory session at no charge once a tutor has been matched, and then a quote against the actual subject and level.

sections.heading: Proximity, coverage and what happens when nobody local covers a subject
paragraphs: The phrase in this search contains the word near, so it deserves a direct answer. For lessons delivered over live video, the tutor's distance from your villa has no effect on the lesson. What distance does affect is availability: the number of qualified specialists inside a twenty-minute drive of Al Jimi or Zakher is small, and for a subject like Higher Level Computer Science or Arabic as a first language at Diploma level it may be nought. A household that insists on a local tutor for those subjects is often choosing between a non-specialist nearby and nobody.

IB Gram's position on this is stated rather than concealed. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. Where a UAE-based tutor covers the subject, that is the first match offered, because the overlap of school context and time zone is genuinely useful. Where no UAE-based specialist is available for a subject at the level needed, the match comes from the wider tutor pool, teaching at Gulf Standard Time, and that is disclosed before any lesson is booked rather than after.

This is the disclosure that competing pages in this search do not make. Several route UAE parents to a non-UAE telephone number while implying local delivery; one shows a Dubai address on an Abu Dhabi page. Saying plainly which subjects are thinly covered in Al Ain, and what happens when they are, is more useful to a parent than a claim of complete coverage that falls apart at the first booking. sections.heading: The lines this page does not cross
paragraphs: A search for tuition in the UAE returns a number of providers offering things they should not. The most serious is completed coursework. Internal assessments, Extended Essays and Theory of Knowledge essays are assessed work that must be the student's own, and a provider that supplies finished pieces is exposing the student to a malpractice finding that can cost the Diploma entirely. A tutor's role is to teach, to question a method, to read a student's own draft and point at the criterion it is being marked against, and to stop there. No part of an assessed piece is ever authored by an IB Gram tutor.

The second is claimed status. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International or Pearson. Those bodies are named on this page because explaining what they do is useful to a parent, not because any of them endorses this platform. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE.

The third is the permit question, which affects any tutor you hire in Al Ain, from us or from anyone else. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. The Ministry's service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, listing no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the Ministry's smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount is quoted here.

The fourth is a point specific to Abu Dhabi, and therefore to Al Ain. Press reporting of ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates that private and charter school staff are barred from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it. Either way, asking your child's own subject teacher to tutor them privately is not a route this page will suggest.

process.title: Tell us what both children are sitting
process.description: Name the boards and the syllabus codes from each child's own specification sheets, the levels or tiers, and the next assessment date each one faces. Two children on two curricula need two different conversations, and the codes are what prevent a mismatch between a Cambridge student and a tutor who has only taught Pearson papers.

process.title: Send the last report and one marked paper each
process.description: A report gives the school's view; a marked script shows where the marks actually went. For the Diploma child, the most useful document is a marked internal assessment draft with the criterion feedback attached, because that identifies which criterion is costing marks rather than which topic looks weak.

process.title: Meet a matched tutor for a trial lesson at no charge
process.description: One introductory session per child, once a tutor has been matched to the named syllabus. There is no charge for it and no card is required to book it. Watch for whether the tutor asks diagnostic questions in the first ten minutes or starts teaching immediately; the first is the better sign.

process.title: Fix the two slots and the feedback rhythm
process.description: Agree a fixed weekly time for each child, usually back to back on one evening so the household loses one evening rather than two, and agree what arrives after each lesson in writing. Changing the slot every week is the commonest reason a tuition arrangement quietly stops working by November.

process.title: Review against the calendar, not the clock
process.description: Check progress at the points the boards and the school have set: before entries close, after the mock window, before each internal assessment deadline. Reviewing on a fixed monthly cycle instead means the review lands at a moment when nothing has been assessed and there is nothing to judge.

whyPoints.title: Two curricula planned as one household
whyPoints.description: The IGCSE child's heaviest weeks and the Diploma child's heaviest weeks rarely coincide, which is usable if someone maps them in September. Planning child by child instead produces the February collision that most two-curriculum families describe after the fact.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus codes, not year groups
whyPoints.description: A tutor is matched to 0580 or 4MA1 or Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, not to a year. Boards set different papers, tier differently and write different mark schemes, and a tutor who knows one board's scheme will misread the other's.

whyPoints.title: Al Ain's regulator, not Dubai's
whyPoints.description: Al Ain schools answer to ADEK. Most online tutoring content is written about KHDA and Dubai, and a parent following it checks the wrong database and reads the wrong inspection framework. This page follows the authority that actually applies.

whyPoints.title: Rates with sources attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, with the market framing kept separate from anything IB Gram charges. Three of the six competing pages in this search publish no price at all, and two quote in a currency UAE families do not transact in.

whyPoints.title: Coverage stated before you book
whyPoints.description: Where Al Ain has no specialist for a subject at the level needed, that is said before a lesson is booked and the match comes from the wider pool at Gulf Standard Time. No competing page in this cluster discloses a coverage limit at all.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question and give feedback on the student's own drafts. No internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay is authored, finished or edited to completion by a tutor, because that route costs the student the qualification.

faqs.question: Our two children are on different curricula - can one tuition plan cover both?
faqs.answer: One plan, two tutors. The plan is the household calendar: which weeks carry the IGCSE mocks, which carry the Diploma internal assessment deadlines, and which evening holds both slots. The teaching has to be separate, because Extended IGCSE Chemistry and Higher Level Diploma Chemistry are different courses with different mark schemes, and a tutor strong in one is not automatically useful in the other. In practice most Al Ain families we work with run back-to-back slots on a single evening, with the older child's session placed second and longer.

faqs.question: What does a search for IB IGCSE tuition near me actually return in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Three things, mixed together: tuition centres advertising group classes, individual tutors listing a district, and platforms that will match you with someone online. Google's local results rank partly on proximity, which means a listing can appear first because it is close rather than because it covers your child's syllabus. The city's specialist pool is small, so for Higher Level sciences or Arabic at Diploma level the nearest qualified person may be some distance away or not in Al Ain at all. Checking the syllabus a tutor has actually taught is more informative than checking the district.

faqs.question: Does ADEK inspect an IB school and an IGCSE school against the same framework?
faqs.answer: Yes. The u.ae government portal states that ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, which includes Al Ain, and its inspection framework applies to the school rather than to the curriculum it licenses. That makes two Al Ain schools on different curricula comparable on teaching quality and leadership. What it cannot tell you is whether a particular Higher Level subject is taught strongly this year, because inspection samples across a school rather than auditing a cohort of nine candidates in one subject.

faqs.question: Which Al Ain schools run the Diploma and which run Cambridge IGCSE?
faqs.answer: The split changes, so check each school's current listing rather than a tutoring page. Broadly, Al Ain's longer-established British-curriculum schools run IGCSE followed by A Levels, while a smaller number of IB World Schools in the city run the Middle Years Programme and the Diploma. Some schools run IGCSE and then offer the Diploma afterwards. Because the sixth-form offer differs between campuses, the Year 11 decision in Al Ain is often a decision between two schools as well as two qualifications, and it is worth asking each one how many candidates sat each Higher Level subject last year.

faqs.question: How do the IGCSE and IB exam windows overlap in one household calendar?
faqs.answer: The examination windows themselves usually do not collide badly. The collisions happen earlier. Cambridge final entries for a March series fall in the preceding November; Pearson publishes its November timetable with entries well ahead of the late-October start. School mock windows sit three to four months before each series, and Diploma internal deadlines cluster in the same months. A family can therefore face an IGCSE mock fortnight, a Diploma internal assessment deadline and an Extended Essay checkpoint inside three weeks. Mapping that in September is the point of planning at household level.

faqs.question: Is my Year 11 child better off moving to the Diploma or staying on A Levels in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject spread and on how the student handles a compulsory second language. The Diploma requires six subjects across groups plus Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, which suits a broad student and penalises one with a single weak area that cannot be dropped. A Levels allow three or four subjects and no core. The Ministry's British-track equivalency route is written around A Levels and AS Levels. In Al Ain the choice also involves changing campus for several families, so drive time is a real factor alongside the academic one.

faqs.question: How much does tuition for two children on two curricula cost in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Judge it against published market bands rather than a single number. A qualified subject tutor working online is advertised in the UAE market at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, while specialist IB and IGCSE tutoring runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year work. Two children at examination-year intensity is a materially larger commitment, so staggering intensity usually makes more sense than running both at full rate.

faqs.question: Do we need separate tutors for IGCSE Maths and Diploma Maths?
faqs.answer: Almost always, yes. Extended IGCSE Mathematics contains no calculus, while Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level uses differentiation inside the first term and assumes fast algebraic manipulation. The mark schemes reward different things: unshown method lines at IGCSE, and unjustified steps or missing units at Diploma level. A tutor who teaches both well exists, but matching on the specific syllabus is more reliable than hoping for the overlap. If one tutor does cover both, ask which Diploma mathematics course and which board's IGCSE they last taught, and when.

faqs.question: What does the Ministry of Education require from an IGCSE leaver and from a Diploma leaver?
faqs.answer: For the British track, as reported when the UAE clarified its equivalency requirements, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. No International Baccalaureate points threshold appears in that source, so none is published here. Confirm the current rules on the Ministry's own site or with the emirate attestation authority before relying on them.

faqs.question: How close does a tutor need to be if the lessons happen on screen?
faqs.answer: Distance makes no difference to a lesson delivered over live video, which is how IB Gram teaches UAE families. What distance affects is availability. The number of qualified specialists within a short drive of Al Jimi or Zakher is small, and for Higher Level Computer Science or Diploma Arabic as a first language it may be none. Insisting on a local tutor for those subjects often means choosing a non-specialist nearby over a specialist on screen. For common IGCSE subjects the local pool is deeper and the question matters less.

faqs.question: Can lessons for both children run back to back on the same evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most two-curriculum households in Al Ain prefer it. Two consecutive slots mean the family loses one evening a week rather than two, and the household routine only has to accommodate a single fixed commitment. The usual arrangement puts the IGCSE child first in a shorter session and the Diploma child second in a longer one, because coursework feedback benefits from an unbroken block. Where the school run from Zakher or Al Yahar lands late, the pair of slots moves later rather than being split across two nights.

faqs.question: What happens to our tuition schedule during Ramadan in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten and the usable part of the evening moves, so the weekly slot moves with it. Families typically choose one of three patterns: an early-afternoon session straight after the shortened school day, a post-Iftar session, or a pause for the month with the hours made up afterwards. Because lessons are delivered over live video there is no travel to work around, which makes the post-Iftar option far easier to run than a visiting arrangement would be. Agree the pattern before the month starts rather than rescheduling week by week.

faqs.question: Which subjects do Al Ain families most often ask for at both levels?
faqs.answer: Mathematics first, by a wide margin, usually Extended IGCSE for the younger child and Analysis and Approaches for the older one. Chemistry and Physics follow, then Economics and Business at Diploma level. Arabic as a first language is heavily requested here specifically, because Al Ain's Emirati and Arabic-speaking population is proportionally larger than in some coastal cities and the mandatory subject stream sits alongside the international curriculum. English First Language to Language A is a common pairing that families underestimate, because the task type changes completely.

faqs.question: If no Al Ain tutor covers a subject, what do you do?
faqs.answer: We say so before a lesson is booked, and offer a match from the wider tutor pool teaching at Gulf Standard Time. For some Diploma Higher Level subjects the number of candidates in the whole city is small enough that no local specialist exists, which is a fact about Al Ain rather than about any platform. The alternative, which several providers in this market take, is to imply local coverage and then substitute someone remote after payment. Disclosure before booking is the better arrangement, even when the answer is less convenient.

faqs.question: Is the first lesson really at no charge, and what are the conditions?
faqs.answer: The trial is one introductory session, booked after a tutor has been matched to your child's named syllabus and level, and nothing is charged for it. No card is required to book it and there is no obligation afterwards. It exists so that the match can be judged on a real lesson rather than a profile, so use it to watch how the tutor diagnoses: a tutor who spends the first ten minutes asking what the student can already do is reading the problem, while one who starts teaching immediately is guessing.

al-ain/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.closingHeading: Start with the two calendars, then the two tutors
al-ain/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.closingBody: If you take one thing from this page, make it the September mapping exercise. Put both children's assessment years on one sheet: entry deadlines, mock windows, internal assessment dates, examination windows. The collisions become obvious, and they are nearly always earlier than families expect. Then match each child to a tutor by syllabus code rather than by year group or postcode, run the two trial lessons at no charge, and fix a single evening that carries both slots. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time; home visits are an India-only service and are not offered anywhere in the UAE. Tell us the boards, the levels and the next date each child faces, and we will start from there.
