intro.heading: Why an MYP report is harder to read than any other school report
paragraphs: A parent in Al Ain who receives a Middle Years Programme report sees eight subject groups, a grade from one to seven in each, and four letters with numbers beside them. Nothing on the page explains what the letters mean, why a child scored six on one criterion and three on another in the same subject, or what to do about it. The report is accurate and detailed, and it is almost unusable without a translation. That translation is the first thing an IB MYP tutor in Al Ain should be providing, before any teaching happens at all.

The system is criterion-referenced rather than norm-referenced. Each subject group has four criteria, A to D, with their own published strand descriptors, and each is marked out of eight. The four marks add to a raw total out of thirty-two, which the school converts to a grade from one to seven using the published boundary table. Nothing is averaged against the rest of the class. A student is measured against a written description of what the work has to show, which is the fairest system in secondary education and the least intuitive to read from outside.

Two consequences follow, and both surprise parents. The first is that a child can produce visibly better work than last term and still see the grade fall, because the units assessed that term weighted different criteria. A Sciences unit assessed on Criterion A, knowing and understanding, measures something quite different from one assessed on Criterion B, inquiring and designing. Marks move when the thing being measured moves. The second is that revision, in the sense a parent remembers it, is close to useless here. There is nothing to revise for a Criterion C task; there is a skill to build.

Al Ain adds its own texture. The city is part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so every private school here is inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge rather than KHDA, and the number of IB World Schools running the MYP locally is small. Several Al Ain schools run the MYP to Year 9 and then move students onto Cambridge or Pearson international GCSE papers for Years 10 and 11, rather than continuing to MYP Year 5. That fork changes what MYP support should be aiming at, and it is the single most important thing to establish before booking anything.

This page sets out the criteria group by group, the boundary arithmetic, why a band drops without the work worsening, what the Personal Project is and where a tutor must stop, the honest size of the gap from MYP into the Diploma, and what support costs in this market with every AED figure attributed. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service offered only in India.

The total converts to a one-to-seven grade using the published boundary table

al-ain/ib-myp-tutor.programmesIntro: Three programmes bracket an Al Ain MYP student: the Primary Years Programme behind them, the MYP itself, and whichever of the Diploma or international GCSE the school moves them onto. The notes below are about the joins between them.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups studied each year, each assessed against four criteria marked out of eight, with at least one interdisciplinary unit and a culminating project. Approaches to learning skills are taught across subjects in five categories: thinking, communication, social, self-management and research. Service as action runs alongside. Nothing in the programme is assessed by a single terminal examination unless the school opts into the IB's on-screen assessments.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Ain the MYP is offered by a small number of IB World Schools, which has a practical effect families notice quickly: there is rarely a classmate at another local school working on the same unit, so comparing notes across schools is not available in the way it is for IGCSE cohorts. It also means local MYP-specialist tutors are genuinely scarce, more so than for IGCSE subjects.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led and transdisciplinary, with no criterion marks of the MYP kind and no numerical grades in most schools. The move into MYP Year 1 is therefore the first time a student meets a four-criterion mark scheme, and the first time a parent sees a grade from one to seven. The content step is mild; the assessment step is not.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain families moving a child from a PYP school into MYP Year 1 most often ask for help in the first term of the new year, when the grades arrive and look lower than the primary reports suggested. In almost every case the work has not deteriorated; the measurement has changed. One or two sessions explaining the criteria to the student directly often does more than a term of subject tuition.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher and Standard Level with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Assessment returns to examination papers with internal assessment attached, graded one to seven per subject, out of a maximum total of forty-five. The criteria habits built in the MYP transfer directly to Diploma internal assessment, which is the strongest argument for taking MYP criteria seriously in Year 9.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain's Diploma cohorts are small and option blocks are tight, so a student who wants a particular Higher Level combination may find the local timetable will not permit it. An MYP student aiming at Higher Level sciences is worth steering early, because subject choices made in MYP Year 4 narrow the Diploma options available two years later.

programmes.name: International GCSE
programmes.description: The route several Al Ain schools take after MYP Year 3, under Cambridge or Pearson. Assessment flips from criterion-referenced coursework to terminal papers with mark schemes and tiered entry, Core or Extended. A student who has spent three years being assessed against descriptors meets, for the first time, a scheme that awards marks for specific stated points in a specific order.
programmes.countryNote: This is the fork that defines MYP tutoring in Al Ain. Ask your school directly whether your child continues to MYP Year 5 and the Personal Project, or transfers to IGCSE papers in Year 10. The answer changes what the next two years of support should be building, and the two destinations reward almost opposite habits.

al-ain/ib-myp-tutor.subjectsIntro: Each MYP subject group has its own four criteria with its own wording. The notes below name them and say where Al Ain students most often lose marks, which is rarely where the parent expects.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria are A knowing and understanding, B investigating patterns, C communicating, D applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Most marks are lost on B and D, not A. A student who can solve the equations can still score three on B because the general rule was never stated and justified, which is what the descriptor asks for.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: A knowing and understanding, B inquiring and designing, C processing and evaluating, D reflecting on the impacts of science. B and C are where the drop happens: a hypothesis without a scientific reason behind it, and a conclusion that restates the data instead of evaluating method and reliability.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: A analysing, B organizing, C producing text, D using language. Strong writers often score lowest on A, because analysis means explaining the effect of a writer's choices rather than describing what happens. Al Ain students arriving from systems that reward summary feel this most sharply.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: A listening, B reading, C speaking, D writing, assessed by phase rather than by year group. A student can be in Phase 4 for reading and Phase 2 for speaking, and the single reported grade hides that. Asking the school which phase applies per criterion is the useful question.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: A knowing and understanding, B investigating, C communicating, D thinking critically. D is the criterion that separates grades here. Source evaluation that names the origin and purpose of a source, rather than calling it biased, is the specific skill the descriptor rewards.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: A inquiring and analysing, B developing ideas, C creating the solution, D evaluating. The design cycle is the mark scheme, and students who build an excellent product while skipping the research and specification stages score poorly. The documentation is not paperwork; it is where most of the marks live.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: A investigating, B developing, C creating or performing, D evaluating. The process journal carries marks in its own right. A finished piece with no recorded development behind it cannot reach the upper strands of B, however accomplished the outcome is.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: A knowing and understanding, B planning for performance, C applying and performing, D reflecting and improving performance. Written work counts here, which surprises parents whose children are physically capable and score mid-band because the planning and reflection components were treated as optional.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the international curriculum for the groups the regulator specifies, and in Al Ain a heavily requested stream. A student may sit Arabic as a first language under Language and Literature criteria or in Language Acquisition phases, and the two are marked against entirely different descriptors.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Marked against their own four criteria rather than the contributing subjects' criteria, which is why a separate grade appears on the report. Students lose marks by writing two subject essays side by side instead of producing one piece that genuinely integrates both disciplines.

sections.heading: What a five out of eight actually means
paragraphs: Each MYP criterion is marked out of eight, and the eight marks are grouped into four bands, usually 1-2, 3-4, 5-6 and 7-8, each with a written descriptor. A five is therefore not sixty-two per cent of anything. It is the lower half of the third band, and the descriptor for that band says something specific about what the work demonstrated. Reading the band descriptor tells you precisely what the next band requires, which is information no percentage can carry.

The four criterion marks add to a raw total out of thirty-two, and the school converts that total to a grade from one to seven using the IB's published boundary table. The published boundaries are narrow at the bottom and wide in the middle, which produces an effect parents find counter-intuitive: a single mark on one criterion can move a reported grade, while a three-mark improvement spread across two criteria sometimes moves nothing at all. Confirm the boundary table your child's school applies with the MYP coordinator, because schools report against the IB table and the arithmetic is worth seeing once.

The practical consequence is that the useful question to a teacher is never how my child can improve generally. It is which criterion was assessed in this task, which band did the work land in, and what does the next band descriptor require that this work did not show. Teachers answer that question readily. Almost no parent asks it, because nothing in the reporting format suggests that it is the question.

sections.heading: The four criteria, subject group by subject group
paragraphs: The criteria are not generic. Each subject group has its own four, with its own wording, and they are published in the IB's subject guides. Knowing them by name changes what a parent can ask for and what a tutor can target. It also explains why a student can be a strong mathematician and a weak MYP Mathematics candidate: the subject rewards investigating patterns and applying mathematics in real-life contexts as two separate quarters of the mark, and neither is tested by solving equations accurately.

The most commonly misread criteria are the second and third in each group, because those are the ones that assess process rather than knowledge. Sciences Criterion B asks for a designed investigation with a scientific hypothesis and controlled variables. Sciences Criterion C asks for data processing and an evaluation of method and reliability. A student who knows the content perfectly and writes a conclusion that restates the results will score in the lower bands on C every time, and no amount of content revision will move it.

Design is the clearest illustration of the pattern. Its four criteria follow the design cycle, and three of the four are documentation: inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, and evaluating. Only one is creating the solution. A student who builds something impressive in a weekend and writes the research up afterwards has inverted the mark scheme. The documentation is not administrative overhead attached to the real work; it is three quarters of the real work.

sections.heading: Why a band drops when the work did not get worse
paragraphs: This is the single most common reason an Al Ain family contacts a tutor about the MYP, and the answer is usually structural rather than academic. Not every unit assesses every criterion. A school plans its units so that across the year all four criteria in each subject group are assessed at least twice, but any one term may weight two of them heavily and leave the others untouched. If the term that just ended assessed Criteria B and C in Sciences, and your child's strength is Criterion A, the reported grade falls while the child's understanding has not changed at all.

A second cause is the task-specific clarification. Teachers are required to write task-specific wording for each criterion, drawn from the general descriptors, and the standard rises through the MYP years. A performance that reached the third band in MYP Year 2 may sit in the second band against MYP Year 4 wording for the same criterion. The student has improved; the bar moved further. Nothing on the report says so.

A third cause, and the most fixable, is that the student has never read the descriptor. Students who read the band descriptor for the criterion they are about to be assessed on, before starting the task, typically gain marks without gaining knowledge, because they stop omitting the one thing the descriptor explicitly requires. In Mathematics Criterion B that is stating and justifying a general rule. In Sciences Criterion C it is commenting on the reliability of the method. These are not insights; they are instructions, printed in the guide, that nobody read.

Before booking subject tuition, it is worth asking the school three questions: which criteria were assessed this term, what the task-specific wording was, and which band the work landed in. Often that conversation removes the need for tuition entirely, and when it does not, it tells a tutor exactly where to start.
bullets: Ask which criteria the term's units actually assessed
Ask for the task-specific clarification, not just the general descriptor
Have the student read the band descriptor before starting the task
Compare marks criterion by criterion across terms, never grade to grade

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: In MYP Year 5 students undertake the Personal Project: a self-directed piece of work with a goal they set themselves, a process journal kept throughout, a product or outcome, and a written report. It is marked against its own criteria and externally moderated by the IB, and it is the first piece of genuinely independent work most MYP students have produced. For students who continue to the Diploma it is also the clearest rehearsal available for the Extended Essay, which is why the habits built here matter beyond the grade.

Students fail to reach the upper bands for predictable reasons, and almost none of them are about ability. The goal is set too broadly to be assessed against. The process journal is written retrospectively in the final fortnight, so there is no evidence of the decisions the criteria ask about. The product is finished and the report treated as paperwork. Or the student chooses a goal that cannot generate evidence of research, because it was chosen for enthusiasm rather than for assessability.

What a tutor may legitimately do here is narrow and useful. Ask what the goal is and whether it can be assessed. Ask what is in the journal this week. Read the student's own draft and point at the criterion it is being marked against. Question a method. Help plan a schedule backwards from the school's checkpoints. What a tutor may not do is supply content, text, structure written for the student, or a finished product. The Personal Project must be the student's own work, and a tutor who crosses that line exposes the student to an academic honesty investigation. No part of a submitted project is ever authored by an IB Gram tutor, and we say so here rather than leaving it to be assumed.
bullets: The process journal carries marks and must be kept as the work happens
A goal that cannot be assessed cannot reach the upper bands, however ambitious
Coaching means questions about the student's work, not content for it
External moderation means the school's internal view is not the final word

sections.heading: MYP Year 5 into the Diploma: the honest size of the gap
paragraphs: The MYP is often described as preparation for the Diploma, which is true in habits and misleading in content. The habit transfer is real and substantial: criterion-referenced marking, independent investigation, a process journal, a long self-directed project. A student who has taken the Personal Project seriously arrives at the Extended Essay already knowing how a long piece of independent work is actually built, which most students entering the Diploma from a terminal-examination system do not.

The content transfer is weaker, and mathematics is where it shows. MYP Mathematics, even on the extended route, does not cover calculus. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level uses differentiation inside the first term and assumes algebraic manipulation at a speed MYP tasks never require under time pressure. A student moving from extended MYP Mathematics into Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level without a bridging block typically meets the first real difficulty around the end of the first term, by which point the class has moved on.

The sciences present the opposite shape. Content continuity is reasonable, and the MYP's Criterion B and C work maps almost directly onto Diploma internal assessment, which also rewards a designed investigation and an evaluation of method. A student who scored in the upper bands on Sciences Criteria B and C in MYP Year 5 is genuinely well placed for the Diploma internal assessment. The gap is content volume and examination technique, both of which are learnable in a term.

In Al Ain there is a further practical constraint. Diploma cohorts here are small, option blocks are tight, and a student wanting a particular Higher Level combination may find the local timetable will not allow it. Subject choices made in MYP Year 4 can close Diploma options two years later, so the conversation about Diploma subjects is worth having before the MYP options are picked rather than after.

sections.heading: What MYP support costs here, and what the hour should contain
paragraphs: Published UAE tutoring rates range widely and almost no competing page in this search prints an AED figure at all. The bands below are market rates taken from providers' own published pricing and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. They are the market, not IB Gram's price list, and they are here so that any Al Ain quote you receive can be measured against something.

Budget online tutoring from university students is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits in the AED 150 to 300 band, where Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits including travel run roughly AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate quoting 180 to 350 and independent home tutors 200 to 500. IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named tutoring reaches AED 650, as BartyED publishes. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year support.

MYP support usually sits lower in that range than Diploma support, for a reason worth understanding. The MYP is not an examination year, so the work is habit-building rather than examination preparation, and a criterion clinic of three or four sessions often resolves what looked like a term-long problem. Paying examination-year rates for MYP Year 2 support is a common and avoidable overspend. The exceptions are MYP Year 5 with the Personal Project running, and any MYP student being bridged into Higher Level mathematics.

What the hour should contain is a fair test of any quote. For MYP work, a session that does not reference a criterion letter or a band descriptor at any point is not MYP tutoring; it is general subject tutoring with an IB label. Ask, before booking, which criteria the tutor will be working from and how they will know the strand has moved.

sections.heading: Online delivery, coverage in a small city, and the limits
paragraphs: Lessons for UAE families are delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service available only in India. For MYP work the online format has a specific advantage beyond convenience: the student's own marked task, the criterion wording and the band descriptors can all be on a shared screen at once, annotated live, which is exactly the material an MYP session should be working from. A tutor at a kitchen table with no sight of the school's task-specific clarification is working blind.

Coverage in Al Ain deserves an honest statement. MYP specialists are scarcer locally than IGCSE subject tutors, because the number of local MYP cohorts is small. For Mathematics, Sciences and English the UAE-based pool is usually adequate. For Design, Arts and the less common Language Acquisition phases, there may be no UAE-based specialist free, and the match then comes from the wider pool teaching at Gulf Standard Time. That is disclosed before any lesson is booked, not after. No competing page in this market discloses a coverage limit at all, which does not mean they do not have one.

The limits on what is claimed here are worth stating in plain terms. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation or the International Baccalaureate, and there is no IB Gram office anywhere in the UAE. No grade is promised, no statistic appears here without a named source, and no IB subject guide, past paper or mark scheme is supplied as a download; the IB's own site is the place for those. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the Ministry's own service, and tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

process.title: Send the last report and one marked task
process.description: The report gives the grades; the marked task shows which criterion was assessed and which band the work reached. Those two documents together make a first session diagnostic rather than exploratory, and they are usually enough to say whether a short criterion clinic or weekly support is the right shape.

process.title: Tell us whether the school continues to MYP Year 5
process.description: Several Al Ain schools move students onto Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE papers in Year 10 instead of completing MYP Year 5 and the Personal Project. The two destinations reward different habits, so the answer changes what the next two years of support should build towards.

process.title: Agree which criteria the work will target
process.description: Support is set against named criteria, not against a subject in general: Sciences Criterion C, or Mathematics Criterion B. That makes progress checkable, because the next marked task either shows movement in that strand or it does not, and nobody has to rely on an impression.

process.title: Meet the matched tutor for a trial session at no charge
process.description: One introductory session once a tutor is matched to the subject group, with nothing charged and no card required to book. Judge it on whether the tutor opens the student's marked work and names a criterion, or starts teaching topics without looking at what was assessed.

process.title: Review after the next marked task
process.description: Not monthly, and not by feel. The review point is the next piece of criterion-assessed work, because that is the first moment there is real evidence. If the targeted strand has moved, the approach is working; if it has not, the diagnosis was wrong and should change rather than continue.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis by criterion, not by topic
whyPoints.description: An MYP problem is almost always a strand problem, and topic revision does not touch it. Sessions start from the marked task and the band descriptor, so the thing being worked on is the thing the school is actually marking.

whyPoints.title: The Year 9 fork taken seriously
whyPoints.description: Whether an Al Ain school continues to MYP Year 5 or moves to IGCSE papers changes everything about what Year 9 support should build. Establishing that before booking prevents two years of work aimed at the wrong destination.

whyPoints.title: Al Ain's regulator, not Dubai's
whyPoints.description: Al Ain private schools are inspected by ADEK. Most online tutoring content is written about KHDA and Dubai, which sends a local parent to the wrong database and the wrong inspection framework.

whyPoints.title: Rates with their sources attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, and kept separate from anything IB Gram charges. Most pages competing for this search publish no price at all.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on the Personal Project
whyPoints.description: Coaching means questions about the student's own work and feedback against the criteria. Content, text and finished products are not supplied, because external moderation and academic honesty rules make that route a risk to the student's own result.

whyPoints.title: Coverage said out loud
whyPoints.description: Where Al Ain has no available specialist for a subject group or language phase, that is stated before booking and the match comes from the wider pool at Gulf Standard Time. Scarcity in a small city is a fact, not something to conceal.

faqs.question: What is the MYP actually assessing when my child gets a 5 out of 8?
faqs.answer: A criterion mark out of eight sits in one of four bands, each with a written descriptor, so a five is the lower half of the third band rather than a percentage. The descriptor for that band states what the work demonstrated, and the descriptor above it states what the next band requires. That is the actionable information. Ask the teacher which criterion the task assessed and what the band above asks for, because the answer is a specific instruction, not a general comment about effort or attainment.

faqs.question: How do the four MYP criteria translate into a subject grade?
faqs.answer: The four criterion marks, each out of eight, add to a raw total out of thirty-two, and the school converts that total into a grade from one to seven using the IB's published boundary table. The boundaries are not evenly spaced, so one mark on a single criterion can move a reported grade while three marks spread thinly can move nothing. Ask your child's MYP coordinator to show you the boundary table the school applies, then look at the four criterion marks rather than the single grade.

faqs.question: Why did my child's MYP report drop a band without the work getting worse?
faqs.answer: Usually because the units assessed that term weighted different criteria. Schools plan so that all four criteria are assessed across a year, not within every term, so a term heavy on Sciences Criteria B and C will report lower for a student whose strength is Criterion A. The second common cause is task-specific wording rising with the MYP year, so the same performance sits a band lower against Year 4 wording than against Year 2 wording. Neither is a decline in the child's understanding.

faqs.question: When does the MYP Personal Project start and how is it marked?
faqs.answer: It runs through MYP Year 5, is marked against its own criteria and is externally moderated by the IB. The components are a self-set goal, a process journal kept as the work happens, a product or outcome, and a written report. The journal is where most lost marks sit, because students write it retrospectively in the final fortnight and the criteria ask about decisions that are no longer evidenced. Starting the journal in the first week, badly, beats starting it perfectly in the last month.

faqs.question: Can a tutor support the Personal Project without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor may ask whether the goal can be assessed against the criteria, ask what is in the journal this week, read the student's own draft and point at the criterion it is being marked against, question a method, and help plan backwards from the school's checkpoints. A tutor may not supply content, text, structure written for the student, or a finished product. The project is externally moderated and must be the student's own work; crossing that line puts the student's result at risk, so it does not happen here.

faqs.question: Does my child sit MYP eAssessment in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Only if the school has opted into it. The IB offers on-screen examinations and ePortfolio routes leading to an MYP certificate at the end of MYP Year 5, and schools choose whether to enter candidates. Many do not, and report internally assessed criterion grades instead. This is a question for your school's MYP coordinator rather than for a tutoring page, and the answer matters: a cohort sitting on-screen examinations needs examination technique in the final year, while one that is not needs continued criterion work.

faqs.question: How much MYP tutoring does a Year 9 student in Al Ain usually need?
faqs.answer: Less than families expect, if the diagnosis is right. A criterion clinic of three or four sessions on a single weak strand often resolves what looked like a term-long subject problem, because the student was omitting something the descriptor explicitly required. Weekly year-round support makes sense in two situations: a genuine content gap that has been accumulating for more than a year, and a student being bridged towards Higher Level mathematics. Paying examination-year rates and intensity for a Year 9 MYP student is a common overspend.

faqs.question: Which MYP subject groups do Al Ain families ask about most?
faqs.answer: Mathematics first, then Sciences, then Language and Literature. Arabic as a first language is requested more heavily in Al Ain than in some coastal cities, because the local Arabic-speaking population is proportionally larger and the mandatory subject stream runs alongside the international curriculum. Design appears less often than it should: it is the subject group where the mark scheme is most commonly inverted by students, since three of its four criteria assess documentation rather than the product everyone focuses on.

faqs.question: Why does my child get a separate grade for an interdisciplinary unit in MYP?
faqs.answer: Because it is assessed against its own four criteria rather than the criteria of the contributing subjects, so it reports separately. The skill being measured is genuine integration of two disciplines, which is why the commonest failure is a submission that reads as two subject essays placed side by side. Students who score well usually state explicitly what each discipline contributes to the single question being answered. It is also the grade parents most often ignore, which is a missed signal, because it reveals how well a student transfers thinking between subjects.

faqs.question: How does MYP Mathematics prepare a student for Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: Partially. The investigation habits from Criterion B transfer directly, and the real-life context work from Criterion D is useful preparation for modelling questions. The content does not: MYP Mathematics, including the extended route, does not cover calculus, while Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level uses differentiation within the first term and assumes rapid algebraic manipulation. A bridging block in the gap between MYP Year 5 and Diploma year one is the usual fix, and it is far cheaper than catching up mid-term once the class has moved on.

faqs.question: My child is moving from MYP 5 into the Diploma - what is the real gap?
faqs.answer: The habits transfer well and the content transfer is uneven. Criterion-referenced marking, independent investigation and a long self-directed project all map onto Diploma internal assessment and the Extended Essay, which puts an MYP student ahead of one arriving from a purely examination-based system. What is missing is examination technique, content volume and, in mathematics specifically, calculus. In Al Ain there is also a timetable constraint: Diploma cohorts are small, so a particular Higher Level combination may simply not be available locally.

faqs.question: Are approaches to learning skills something a tutor can actually teach?
faqs.answer: Some of them, directly. The five categories are thinking, communication, social, self-management and research. Research and self-management respond well to one-to-one work, because they are concrete: how to record a source properly, how to plan backwards from a deadline, how to keep a journal as the work happens. Social skills are not a tutoring target in any honest sense. The useful approach is to attach a named skill to a real task the student already has, rather than teaching the skill in the abstract and hoping it transfers.

faqs.question: What does MYP tutoring cost in Al Ain and what should the hour contain?
faqs.answer: Judge any quote against published market bands. A qualified subject tutor working online is advertised in the UAE market at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200, while specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Bestimate's monthly estimate for weekly one-hour sessions is AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market. As for content, a session that never mentions a criterion letter or a band descriptor is general subject tutoring with an IB label attached, whatever the rate.

faqs.question: Does an MYP certificate count for anything with the UAE Ministry of Education?
faqs.answer: The MYP is a middle-school framework, not a school-leaving qualification, so it is not what the Ministry assesses for equivalency. The Ministry's published requirements address school-leaving certificates, and for the British track they specify five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects. Verify the current rules on the Ministry's own site. What the MYP affects is readiness for whichever leaving qualification follows it.

faqs.question: How does a tutor on video handle an MYP science investigation?
faqs.answer: By working on the parts that carry the marks, which are mostly not the practical itself. Criterion B is the design: a hypothesis with a scientific reason behind it, named independent, dependent and controlled variables, a method someone else could repeat. Criterion C is the processing and the evaluation of method and reliability. Both are written work, and both annotate well on a shared screen. The hands-on measurement happens in the school laboratory, which is where the school's own safety and supervision arrangements apply.

al-ain/ib-myp-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the criterion, not the topic
al-ain/ib-myp-tutor.closingBody: If an MYP grade has moved and nobody can say why, the answer is almost always in the criterion marks rather than in the content. Find the marked task, find which criterion it assessed, read the band descriptor above the one the work reached, and you will usually have a specific instruction rather than a vague worry. Send us that task and the last report, tell us whether the school continues to MYP Year 5 or moves to IGCSE papers in Year 10, and we will match a tutor to the subject group and the strand. Lessons are one-to-one over live video at Gulf Standard Time; home visits are an India-only service and are not offered in the UAE.

Everything on this page is anchored to that system rather than to a national average.

al-ain/ib-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work with Al Ain households over live video in Diploma and Middle Years subjects. Each profile states the subjects and levels that person teaches rather than a general availability claim, and all sessions are scheduled against the Al Ain school week and Gulf Standard Time rather than a tutor's own working day.

intro.heading: Al Ain is governed by ADEK, and that changes the detail
paragraphs: Most tutoring pages aimed at this country are written once for the UAE and then stamped with a city name. The result reads plausibly and is wrong in the details that matter. Al Ain is part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, which means its private schools come under the Department of Education and Knowledge, not under Dubai's Knowledge and Human Development Authority. A page that explains Dubai inspection bands to an Al Ain parent is describing another emirate's system, and a parent who acts on it will be asking their school the wrong questions.

The regulator map across the country has five separate bodies. In Dubai, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In Abu Dhabi, which includes Al Ain, the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah's Private Education Authority regulates private education in that emirate, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Those five bodies are the whole picture, and the competitor pages ranking for these searches name almost none of them.

Some rules sit above all five. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That federal baseline is why an IB World School in Al Ain running the Diploma still timetables Arabic and Islamic Education alongside six Diploma subjects, and why a family planning tuition has less free time in the week than the Diploma subject list alone suggests.

The calendar is the third local variable. Al Ain schools sit the May Diploma session, the UAE academic year runs from late summer to summer with a long winter break, Ramadan shifts the shape of the school day and the useful hours of the evening, and the entry deadlines for externally examined qualifications fall months before the papers themselves. A tutoring plan that ignores any of those four produces a slot the family cannot keep. One honest caution belongs here: IB session and results dates in this project have not been verified against the IB's own publications, so every specific date should be confirmed with your school's IB coordinator.

What follows is an Al Ain page rather than a UAE page. It covers who regulates the school and what that authority's remit actually is, how the local school year lines up against Diploma assessment, what Ramadan and Gulf Standard Time do to the available hours, how the federally required subjects fit alongside the Diploma, what equipment a video lesson genuinely needs here, and how entry deadlines work for a candidate sitting externally examined papers. Lessons are one-to-one and delivered live online; IB Gram does not provide home visits in the UAE.

al-ain/ib-online-tutor.programmesIntro: The three IB programmes are each timetabled differently in Al Ain schools because the federally required subjects have to fit alongside them. The notes below describe each programme and then what it looks like inside this emirate's school week specifically, which is where the generic version of this page usually goes wrong.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units replace separate subject syllabuses, and reporting is against learner attributes and approaches to learning rather than numbered grades. There is no external assessment, so the measurable things a family can act on are narrow: reading fluency, number facts held in memory, and whether a method gets recorded. Those three transfer directly into Middle Years and are the only primary targets worth paying for.
programmes.countryNote: In an Al Ain primary classroom, Arabic and Islamic Education are already timetabled alongside the transdisciplinary units, so the week is fuller than a parent comparing against a British primary school expects. Adding a weekly tuition hour at this age works best at the weekend or immediately after a short school day, and in the outer districts the drive home has already consumed the obvious slot.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked one to eight, and those criterion marks are the only numeric evidence available before the Diploma. The information is in the spread rather than the total: a strong criterion A beside a weak criterion D points at reflection or communication rather than knowledge. Year five adds the personal project, which is the first real test of a student's own scheduling.
programmes.countryNote: Several Al Ain schools run Middle Years and a British Year 10 and 11 stream under one roof, so the same building marks criteria and prepares IGCSE papers in the same term. For a parent that means asking which system your child's report is written in before comparing it with a neighbour's. Both sit under ADEK, and both still carry the federally required subjects.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, graded one to seven, with externally marked papers in the May session and internally assessed work across two years. Higher Level adds syllabus content, usually an extra paper in the sciences, and a different expectation of independence in the internal assessment. The three Higher Level choices determine the shape of the next two years more than any other decision.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain's IB World School count is much lower than Abu Dhabi island's, so fewer Higher Level options actually run and a student may be steered by the timetable rather than by their university plans. The Diploma subject block also has to coexist with the federally required subjects, which is why Al Ain Diploma students often have less discretionary time in the week than their equivalents abroad.

programmes.name: The Diploma core
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity and service sit outside the six subjects and carry up to three bonus points, with failing conditions capable of costing the whole Diploma. None of the three has weekly homework, which is exactly why their deadlines collide with everything else in the second year. Support is episodic: a block at the question stage, another at the draft stage.
programmes.countryNote: Core deadlines in Al Ain schools are set by each school's own coordinator rather than centrally, so two students at different Al Ain campuses can face quite different internal dates for the same component. Ask your coordinator for the school's published checkpoint dates, write them on one page, and plan tuition against that rather than against any generic calendar, including the one on this page.

al-ain/ib-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones Al Ain households request most, with notes on what each assesses and where this emirate's school picture affects it. Where a subject is genuinely hard to staff within the city, that is stated rather than implied, because availability is a fact a parent is entitled to before booking rather than after.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields, circuits and the quantitative treatment of waves cause more difficulty here than mechanics does. Higher Level adds content and an extra paper, and the data-analysis questions reward practice with uncertainty and gradients. The subject Al Ain is thinnest in locally, which is why it is the most frequent reason a family here moves to a video arrangement.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics generate the requests; stoichiometry and careful reading of multi-step calculations are where marks come back. The internal assessment needs a measurable, controllable variable fixed early. Practical work stays at school; a tutor covers technique, uncertainty and the data-handling question types around it.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Recall structure limits more students than understanding does. Building topic summaries from the syllabus statements rather than from class notes is the single habit that moves grades. Command-term discipline matters in extended responses, because explain, outline and evaluate reward different things and are commonly answered identically.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency carry the course, and marks go on unjustified steps rather than wrong answers. Over video this subject works particularly well, because a shared screen or photographed working shows a method line by line, which is exactly what the grading rewards.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and assumed calculator fluency define the route, and Higher Level adds statistical inference that cannot be absorbed late. Students arriving from Middle Years are often procedurally sound but unused to interpreting output in context. The route choice should be checked against the admissions requirements of the universities on the student's list.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the internal assessment commentaries decide most grades. Marks are lost on diagrams that do not match the article and on evaluation that lists both sides without judging. Higher Level adds quantitative content, and economics specialists are notably scarce among Al Ain residents.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two assessed orals and a paper on unseen non-literary texts make this a skills course with a reading list attached. The individual oral rewards preparation because the student selects both the extract and the global issue. Higher Level adds an essay on a studied work that needs an argument rather than a summary.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Requested more often in Al Ain than in most UAE cities, and the route matters: Arabic A is language and literature for first-language speakers, Arabic B an acquisition course with a different assessment structure. This is also the subject most likely to overlap with the school's federally required Arabic provision, so timing needs coordinating.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Upper-band answers apply a named framework to a given organisation rather than describing it. The Higher Level research project needs its scope agreed early and genuine data available. Al Ain students often choose a family business, which works where the figures can actually be obtained and shown.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The programming solution dominates the internal assessment and documents badly without supervision. Paper questions on data structures, resource management and system fundamentals need taught content rather than coding practice. Among the thinnest subjects locally at Diploma level, and one where video matching makes the largest difference.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies must be recalled precisely and used as evidence rather than retold, and the internal assessment is a replication with strict reporting conventions. Requested steadily in Al Ain and rarely available locally at Diploma level, so almost every match in this subject is made beyond the city.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Up to three bonus points and a failing condition that can cost the Diploma, with no weekly homework to keep either visible. The highest-value intervention is at the question stage, before weeks are invested in a question that cannot be answered in the word limit. Review and challenge only; the drafting stays with the student.

al-ain/ib-online-tutor.regionsIntro: Al Ain's districts differ in how the school run, the local campus mix and the household pattern shape the week. The notes below are written around scheduling against the local school day rather than around neighbourhood character, because the time a lesson can actually occupy is what determines whether a plan survives the year.

regions.name: Al Jimi
regions.note: Central and close to several established campuses, so the gap between the bell and a student being ready to work is short. Sessions here can sit at five without strain, which makes Al Jimi the district where a second subject on the same evening is easiest to schedule.

regions.name: Al Mutaredh
regions.note: Villa area near the oasis and the main hospital with many medical and university households. Shift patterns mean a fixed slot the student keeps without needing a lift is worth more than a flexible one, and the sciences dominate requests from these streets.

regions.name: Asharej
regions.note: Adjacent to the United Arab Emirates University campus. Households frequently contain somebody on the UAEU timetable, so the quiet hour at home arrives later than the school day suggests and a seven o'clock start is often the first genuinely workable slot.

regions.name: Al Towayya
regions.note: Established district where British and Indian curriculum timetables often run in the same household, which means two different term calendars and two sets of internal deadlines. Writing both on one page before booking anything prevents the February collision that otherwise arrives.

regions.name: Falaj Hazzaa
regions.note: Large villa neighbourhood with a strong Emirati household share, so the school's Arabic as a first language and Islamic Education provision sits alongside Diploma subjects. Tuition has to be timed around that provision rather than on top of it.

regions.name: Al Muwaiji
regions.note: West of the centre, with a longer run back from the city-edge campuses. Five-thirty is a safer first slot than four-thirty, and the sensible approach is to start later for a fortnight and move earlier once the real arrival time is known.

regions.name: Zakher

sections.heading: Which authority governs your child's school, and why it matters
paragraphs: Al Ain's private schools come under the Department of Education and Knowledge, the Emirate of Abu Dhabi's authority, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. That is a different body from Dubai's Knowledge and Human Development Authority, and the two publish different frameworks, different inspection arrangements and different guidance documents. A parent reading a Dubai-written tutoring page is being told about a system their child is not in.

The practical consequences are small but real. Questions about a school's inspection outcome, its fee approvals or its curriculum permissions go to the emirate's own authority, and the documents a parent can read are that authority's rather than another emirate's. Where a figure or a rule is quoted on this page from a Dubai source, it is labelled as Dubai's, because importing it silently is exactly the error the competing pages make.

The wider map is worth knowing because families move within the country. Sharjah's Private Education Authority regulates private education in that emirate, and both Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval rather than inspection alone sits with the emirate. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. A family relocating from Al Ain to any of those changes regulator, and often changes the published guidance that applies to them. A move within the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, from Al Ain out to the island or back, does not change the authority at all, which is worth knowing before anyone starts rereading guidance they have already read.

sections.heading: What sits above all five regulators
paragraphs: Two things apply nationwide and both affect a tutoring plan. The first is curriculum: private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That is the federal rule underneath every emirate's version of the requirement, and it is why an Al Ain Diploma student's timetable is fuller than the six Diploma subjects imply.

The second is the tutoring permit itself. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Published eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without the permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts has been published, so none appears here.

A third point belongs in this section because it is the one families most often get wrong in this emirate. Reporting on Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff states that teachers may not provide paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that staff tutoring outside school hours must hold the Ministry's private tuition permit, whose code of conduct carries the same restriction. That is press-reported rather than taken from the policy text, so verify the current wording with your school. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or permit from ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and claims none.

sections.heading: The Al Ain school year against Diploma assessment
paragraphs: The UAE academic year runs from late summer through to the following summer, with a substantial winter break and a shorter spring one, and the Diploma session Al Ain schools sit is May. Those two calendars interlock badly if nobody maps them. The winter break falls in the middle of the second Diploma year, exactly when coursework from several subjects is converging, and the spring break falls close enough to the papers that families either use it well or lose a fortnight.

Build the map from your own school's documents rather than from a general calendar. Ask the IB coordinator for the school's internal checkpoint dates for every component, ask each department for its internal assessment deadline, and write the mock window beside them. The pattern that emerges is usually a cluster, and a cluster is manageable if you can see it in September and unmanageable if you discover it in January.

A caution belongs here rather than buried. No IB exam session or results date in this project has been confirmed against the IB's own publications, because the organisation's site blocks automated access. Secondary sources agree on a late-April to mid-May window for the May session, but we do not publish a specific date on that basis. Confirm your child's actual dates with the school's IB coordinator, and treat any provider quoting precise IB dates without naming their source with care. Cambridge and Pearson dates, by contrast, are published by those boards and can be used directly.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Gulf Standard Time and the hours a lesson can occupy
paragraphs: Scheduling is the part of online tutoring that fails most often, and it fails for reasons specific to this country rather than to the format. During Ramadan the school day shortens, late-afternoon energy drops sharply, and most households prefer academic work after Iftar. The wrong response is to pause for a month, which in the coursework middle of the second Diploma year is expensive. The right response is to move the slot, which costs nothing because no one is driving anywhere.

Gulf Standard Time is the second factor, and it only matters because the tutor may not be in it. Every session we schedule is expressed in Gulf Standard Time, which removes the single most common cause of a missed first lesson. Families who travel during the summer or the winter break keep the slot and change only the clock reference, which is a genuine advantage of the format in a city with a highly mobile population.

The third factor is the Al Ain school run itself. School finishing time is not the time a student is able to work: between the bus, a sibling pick-up and the drive from a central campus to Zakher or Hili, the honest gap is often ninety minutes. Setting the first slot later than seems necessary, holding it for a fortnight and only then moving it earlier is what makes a weekly arrangement survive to February. A visiting tutor with a second household to reach cannot offer a six-thirty start; a video session can.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: Every family new to the UAE system is surprised by this, and almost no competing tutoring page mentions it. Private schools here must provide Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies regardless of the international curriculum they are licensed to teach. For a Diploma student that means subjects outside the six, taught in school hours, assessed by the school, and occupying time a parent planning tuition has already mentally allocated.

The most detailed public guidance on how this works is Dubai's rather than Abu Dhabi's, and it is worth reading even though it governs another emirate, provided nobody pretends it applies here directly. Dubai's authority requires separate classes by group for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for Arabs and non-Arabs are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. It also sets the language of instruction for each stream, requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold its own approval to teach those subjects, calculates instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit, and prohibits any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry.

That last rule shapes how any tutoring in these subjects must be described. Material cannot be substituted or supplemented at will, so support in Arabic or Islamic Education means working on the student's own school material and on the language and study skills around it, not importing an alternative course. In Al Ain, where a high proportion of households in districts such as Falaj Hazzaa take Arabic as a first language, the scheduling question also matters: tuition should sit around the school's own provision rather than clashing with it.

sections.heading: What an online lesson in Al Ain actually needs
paragraphs: Less than most families assume, and the things that matter are not the obvious ones. A laptop or tablet with a working camera, a reliable connection and headphones cover the technical side. The variable that decides whether the hour works is physical: a table in a room where the door closes, with the household aware that the hour is not interruptible. In villa districts where several children share study space, that is the genuine constraint rather than bandwidth.

For mathematics and the sciences, the single most useful addition is a way of showing written working. A cheap document camera, a phone on a stand, or a tablet with a stylus all do the job. A tutor who can watch a derivation appear line by line can see where the method breaks, which is the thing families worry is lost over video and which is in fact entirely available. Photographing a completed page and sending it before the session works nearly as well and costs nothing.

On connection quality, the sensible test is a short call at the hour the lesson would run rather than at midday, because household demand in the early evening is when a connection shows its limits. If video is unstable, audio plus a shared screen is a reliable fallback and loses very little. We would rather a family test this during the trial lesson than discover it in week three, which is one more reason the trial exists.

sections.heading: Why an entry deadline sits months before the paper
paragraphs: Families consistently discover entry deadlines late, and the gap between an entry closing and the paper being sat is larger than almost anyone expects. Because no IB date in this project is verified, the clearest worked example comes from a board that publishes its own: Cambridge International. For its March 2027 series, the exam period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries are due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades are due on 27 February 2027, results reach centres through Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. Entries therefore close more than two months before the first paper.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. That is a real risk for a family tracking a timetable they found online rather than the one their centre supplies. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE series in May and June and in November, publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, and its November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026.

The lesson for an Al Ain IB family is procedural rather than specific. Find out from the school who holds the entry responsibility, when that school's internal entry deadline falls, and whether your child is entered through the school or as a private candidate at an approved centre. Then confirm every IB date with the school's coordinator rather than from a secondary source. A tutoring plan is built backwards from a real date, and a wrong date produces a plan that peaks a fortnight late.

sections.heading: What an online tutor in Al Ain cannot do
paragraphs: A page anchored to this emirate's system should also be honest about the format's limits, because the competing pages are not. A tutor over video cannot confiscate a phone, cannot make a reluctant young child sit at a table, and cannot run a laboratory practical. Where physical presence is the actual requirement, a local arrangement is the right answer and we say so rather than arguing the point.

Nor can a tutor do anything about the parts of the system that belong to the school and the authorities. Predicted grades are the school's. Entry decisions are the school's. Equivalency from the Ministry of Education is a process a family completes through the Ministry's own channel; the published British-track requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade three, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. No IB points threshold has been read on the Ministry's own pages, so we publish none, and nothing about equivalency requires tutoring.

The coursework boundary is the last limit and the firmest. Internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay must be the student's own work. A tutor may teach the underlying content, question a research question, name the criterion a paragraph fails to address and explain what that criterion rewards. A tutor may not supply any part of a text that will be assessed, at any point and under any deadline, because an academic-honesty breach is a malpractice matter for the candidate rather than for the person who caused it.

process.title: Tell us which school and which programme
process.description: The campus and the programme tell us which regulator applies, which federally required subjects are in the timetable, and roughly when the school's internal deadlines fall. In this emirate that is ADEK, and knowing the school means the first conversation is about your child's actual week rather than a national average.

process.title: Send the coordinator's checkpoint dates
process.description: Ask the IB coordinator for the school's published internal dates and send them with your first message. Those dates, not a generic calendar, are what a plan is built backwards from. If you have a recent marked paper as well, two minutes of reading it tells a tutor more than twenty minutes of description.

process.title: Pick the hour against the real school run
process.description: We set the slot in Gulf Standard Time against when your child is genuinely home and able to concentrate, which in Zakher, Hili or Al Muwaiji is later than the school day suggests. Hold the first choice for a fortnight before adjusting it, because a slot that survives February is worth more than one that looked tidy in September.

process.title: Test the room and the connection in the trial
process.description: The trial lesson runs at no charge, one per family, with no card details taken first, and it is the right moment to test the practical side: the room, the connection at that hour, and how your child shows written working. Better to find a problem then than in week three of a paid arrangement.

process.title: Agree the coursework boundary in writing
process.description: Before any work touches an internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay, we put the boundary in writing. Teaching, questioning and criterion explanation are in scope. Supplying assessable text is not, under any deadline, because the malpractice consequence falls on the student rather than on the tutor.

whyPoints.title: Written for this emirate, not for the country
whyPoints.description: Al Ain comes under ADEK, and every regulatory point on this page is attributed to the body that actually issues it. Where a rule is Dubai's, it says so rather than being quietly imported. That distinction is missing from almost every page competing for these searches.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled in Gulf Standard Time
whyPoints.description: Every slot is expressed in Gulf Standard Time, moved to post-Iftar hours through Ramadan rather than suspended, and kept through family travel by changing only the clock reference. The single most common cause of a missed first lesson is a timezone assumption nobody stated.

whyPoints.title: The federally required subjects accounted for
whyPoints.description: Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies sit in every UAE private school timetable, which is why an Al Ain Diploma student has less discretionary time than the six-subject list implies. We plan around that provision instead of pretending the week is empty after three o'clock.

whyPoints.title: Dates only where a board publishes them
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson dates on this page come from those boards' own published material and are attributed. No specific IB session or results date appears anywhere, because none has been verified against the IB's own publications. Confirm yours with the school's coordinator.
