sections.heading: Drive times and the earliest slot each district supports
paragraphs: The reason a nearby tutor fails in Al Ain is rarely the teaching. It is that the arrangement was scheduled against the school bell rather than against the moment a student walks through the door. School finishes in the early afternoon; a child living in Zakher who attends a central campus, waits for a bus, collects a sibling and then drives south is not working at four-thirty whatever the timetable says.

Set the slot late and bring it forward, rather than the reverse. Hold the first choice for a fortnight, watch the real arrival time, and only then move earlier if the evidence supports it. Two missed sessions in September reliably push a slot to a weekend, where it competes with everything else a family does, and a weekend slot that competes usually loses by December. That sequence is the single most common way a tutoring plan dies in this city, and it has nothing to do with the tutor.

A video session can sit at six-thirty or seven because nobody has to be anywhere afterwards. That is the practical advantage, and it is larger in a spread-out city than in a dense one. During Ramadan the same flexibility moves the whole arrangement after Iftar rather than pausing it for a month, and when a family travels, only the clock reference changes. None of that is available to a visiting tutor with a second household to reach at seven. Setting the slot honestly in September is the cheapest decision in the whole plan, and it is almost always the one made carelessly.

sections.heading: The permit question, which no listing answers
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a work permit, and a proximity listing never mentions it. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Published eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen.

The route is the Ministry's own service for issuing a new private tutor work permit, which states a two-working-day completion time and no fee, applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount is quoted here, and a figure circulating online could not be verified.

In Abu Dhabi emirate there is a second rule worth knowing before you follow a recommendation from the school gate. Reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff states that teachers may not provide paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that the permit's code of conduct carries the same restriction. Verify the current wording with the school, but do not pursue that arrangement. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or permit from ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and claims none.

sections.heading: Five questions worth asking anyone, local or not
paragraphs: First: which level and which assessment model have you taught, and how recently? A tutor who taught Higher Level Chemistry four syllabus revisions ago is a different proposition from one teaching it now, and the answer takes a sentence. Second: which weekday evenings after six are genuinely open? This eliminates more candidates than anything else and does it before anyone has spent money.

Third: what would the first two sessions consist of? The answer you want describes a diagnosis against syllabus content, not a general statement about building confidence. Fourth: what may you do with my child's internal assessment or Extended Essay? The correct answer names teaching, questioning and criterion explanation and rules out supplying any assessable text. Anything looser than that is a malpractice risk carried by the student rather than by the tutor.

Fifth: do you hold the private tuition work permit? Ask it of a local listing, of a centre about its own permissions and of a platform, including this one. Taken together, those five questions sort a shortlist far better than distance does, they cost nothing, and they can be asked by message before a single hour is booked. If a candidate from your local search answers all five well, take them. The argument on this page is about the radius as a filter, not about the people inside it. Keep the answers. A family who has five written replies from two candidates can compare them side by side a fortnight later, which is more than most parents have when they choose.

faqs.question: Why do near me searches for IB tutors in Al Ain return so few real options?
faqs.answer: Because two constraints multiply. Al Ain is a low-density city where districts sit twenty to thirty minutes apart at school-run time, so a twenty-minute radius is a genuine boundary rather than a formality. And Al Ain has far fewer IB World Schools than Abu Dhabi island, so the number of resident adults who teach Higher Level sciences, mathematics, economics, computer science or psychology at Diploma depth is small to begin with. Filter that small pool by who is free at six on a Tuesday and who is taking new students, and the result is often nothing. The map looks full because listings are not filtered by level.

faqs.question: How far apart are Al Ain's districts in driving time?
faqs.answer: Far enough to change what a tutoring arrangement can look like. At school-run time, crossing between districts typically takes twenty to thirty minutes, and the extremes are longer: Zakher on the southern edge towards Jebel Hafeet and Hili and Al Foah to the north are a substantial drive from the central school cluster. For a visiting tutor that means a sixty-minute lesson consumes most of an evening, which is why in-home rates in this city sit at the upper end of the published bands. For a family it means the obvious after-school slot does not exist.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether my child's tutor lives in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: For the teaching itself, no. What matters is whether the tutor has taught that subject at that level to the current assessment model, and whether they are free when your child can work. Local knowledge has a narrow real value: knowing how a particular campus sequences its internal deadlines, or that a school uses one exam board rather than another. Both of those can be supplied by you in two sentences. Where residence does matter is if you need somebody physically present, in which case it is the whole requirement rather than a preference.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are hardest to staff locally in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Physics and Computer Science are the thinnest, with Psychology close behind and frequently unavailable locally at Diploma level at all. Higher Level Chemistry and Higher Level Economics are thin rather than absent. Mathematics is moderate, with better coverage at Standard Level than Higher and with the two routes, Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, often conflated in listings. Biology and English A: Language and Literature are reasonably covered, so for those two a nearby tutor is a genuine option rather than a compromise. We publish this list because nobody else in this market does.

faqs.question: How long does a match take for an uncommon Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: For the thinner subjects, a week or more in term time, and sometimes longer if the family needs a specific evening. For mathematics, biology and English the usual wait is a few days, and the trial lesson is normally the slower step because it has to fit a real evening in your district. What we do not do is fill a Higher Level slot with a generalist to avoid quoting a wait. If the honest answer is ten days, you get ten days in writing, with the option to start in a different subject meanwhile.

faqs.question: What is the earliest a weekday session can start in each part of Al Ain?
faqs.answer: In Al Jimi and Al Khabisi, five o'clock holds. In Al Mutaredh and Al Sarooj, half past five, with the caveat that shift-pattern households need a slot the student can keep without a lift. In Asharej, seven is often the first genuinely quiet hour because of contested study space. In Al Towayya and Al Muwaiji, half past five. In Zakher, six. In Hili and Al Foah, half past six. Those are honest figures rather than optimistic ones, and booking against them is why a slot survives to February instead of drifting to a weekend.

faqs.question: Is a nearby generalist better than a distant specialist?
faqs.answer: It depends on what is limiting the student. If they understand the content and will not do the work, a present adult helps and subject depth matters less, so a nearby generalist can be the right choice. If they work willingly and still cannot answer the question, the problem is expertise and distance is irrelevant. Most Diploma referrals we see from Al Ain are the second kind, and most primary referrals are the first. Diagnose which one you have before choosing, because the two answers point in opposite directions and both are sometimes right.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor I found through a local listing?
faqs.answer: Five things, all free to ask by message. Which level and which version of the syllabus have you taught, and how recently? Which weekday evenings after six are genuinely open? What would the first two sessions consist of? What may you do with an internal assessment or Extended Essay? And do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit? The first two eliminate most candidates before anyone spends money. The fourth is the one that protects your child, because a loose answer there is a malpractice risk the candidate carries, not the tutor.

faqs.question: How do I verify a tutor's subject experience rather than taking their word?
faqs.answer: Ask for specifics that are hard to fake. How many Diploma cohorts have you taken through this subject? Which paper do your students find hardest and why? What changed in the most recent syllabus revision? A teacher who has done the work answers those in detail and often unprompted. Then ask for a contactable family from the previous year. Star ratings on listings rarely carry a count, a date or a source, and self-published ratings are not evidence. One good reference and three specific answers outweigh any number of stars.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor covers the subject my child needs?
faqs.answer: You are told, before you pay, and given a realistic timeframe. The alternative that this market practises instead is quiet substitution: a capable generalist takes the slot, the sessions feel productive, and the specific gap is still there in March. We would rather hold the slot, state the wait, and offer to start in a different subject in the meantime. If the subject is one we genuinely cannot cover at the level required, we say that too, which is a short conversation and considerably cheaper for the family than a term of the wrong lessons.

faqs.question: Do you charge more when the tutor is outside the UAE?
faqs.answer: No. Where a tutor sits is not part of what a family buys, so it does not change the figure. What a family buys is an hour with somebody who teaches that subject at that level, and pricing it by the tutor's address would make the service worse by pushing matches towards the nearest available person. For market context, other providers publish online rates of roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor and AED 200 to 450 and above for specialists; those are their published bands rather than ours, and our own figure is set at consultation.

faqs.question: Can we meet the tutor before the first paid lesson?
faqs.answer: Yes, that is what the trial lesson is for. It runs at no charge, one per family, and no card details are taken beforehand. It is deliberately run as a working session rather than an introduction: the tutor diagnoses something specific, teaches a piece of content, and then sets out what the following six weeks would contain. If the match is wrong, say so and we change the tutor rather than asking the student to adjust. The trial is also the right moment to test the room, the device and the connection at the hour the real session would run.

faqs.question: How many tutors should I trial before choosing?
faqs.answer: Two is usually enough and three is rarely worth the disruption. What matters more than the number is comparing them on the same basis: ask each to work on the same topic, then look at which session produced something specific. A tutor who names two syllabus topics, explains where marks went on a particular paper and describes the next six weeks has told you more than one who was warm and encouraging. Trialling more than three tends to delay the start by a month, and in the first Diploma year that month is worth more than the marginal improvement in choice.

faqs.question: What does continuity cost when a local tutor leaves Al Ain?
faqs.answer: A term, usually, and more in a two-year Diploma. The search starts again from nothing, the new tutor repeats a diagnosis the family has already paid for, and the written record of what was covered rarely survives the handover. In a city with a mobile expatriate population this is a real risk rather than a theoretical one. Ask any provider, under any format, what actually happens if the person stops being available: whether a replacement is found, whether the record transfers, and whether anything is refunded. A single-person arrangement carries that risk entirely.

faqs.question: Are evening slots in Al Ain harder to get than afternoon ones?
faqs.answer: With local tutors, yes, and that is the heart of the scheduling problem. The hours that actually work in this city, six to eight on a weekday, are the hours a visiting tutor can serve fewest households in, because each one consumes travel at both ends. So the slots offered tend to be the earlier ones that families cannot keep. Over video the constraint disappears: nobody has to be anywhere afterwards, so half past six in Zakher is as easy to staff as five in Al Jimi, and the slot is set to the student rather than to a route.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need to know Al Ain schools to be useful?
faqs.answer: Less than you would think, and the part that matters is easily supplied. What is genuinely useful is knowing which exam board a school uses, how it sequences internal deadlines, and when its mock window falls. All three come from you or from the school's coordinator in a couple of sentences, and a good tutor asks for them in the first two sessions. What cannot be supplied that way is experience of the subject at the right level, which is why the match should be made on that and the local detail handled by asking.

al-ain/ib-tutor-near-me.closingHeading: Use the five questions, then ignore the map
al-ain/ib-tutor-near-me.closingBody: A proximity search is a reasonable place to start and a poor place to decide. Take whatever your local search returned, put the five questions on this page to each name, and see how many survive. Then compare the survivors with a match made on subject and level rather than distance. The trial lesson is at no charge, one per family, with no card details taken first, and it is the only fair way to judge: run it in the same week as a local session and look at which one identified something specific about your child's work. If the nearby option wins that comparison, take it. We would rather you chose on evidence than on a radius.

intro.heading: Why an Al Ain IGCSE plan is not an Abu Dhabi plan with the place name changed
paragraphs: Al Ain is part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, which means its private schools are licensed by the Department of Education and Knowledge rather than by Dubai's authority. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, so when a parent in Al Jimi or Zakher reads general UAE tutoring advice built around KHDA inspection bands and KHDA mandatory-subject circulars, half of it does not apply to their child's school. Getting the regulator right is not pedantry: it decides which inspection report is the one to read and which rules govern who may legally tutor your child.

The second fact that shapes everything is scale. Al Ain's private-school set is considerably smaller than the one on Abu Dhabi island, and smaller still than Dubai's, where 387,441 students attended 227 private schools across 17 curricula in 2024-25. A smaller school set means smaller cohorts, and small cohorts are where tutoring demand concentrates: Higher Level Diploma sciences, Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606, Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 and the less common languages are the subjects Al Ain families struggle to find local help for, because the number of teachers in the city who have taught them is genuinely small.

The third is geography. Al Ain is a low-density, widely spread city, and the districts families actually live in, Al Jimi, Al Mutaredh, Al Muwaiji, Falaj Hazza, Hili, Al Towayya, Zakher, Al Khabisi, Al Maqam and Al Yahar, sit minutes apart on a map and a long way apart in practice once the school run and a tutor's round trip are added up. A home tutor who takes 35 minutes to reach Al Yahar from the centre is being paid for 35 minutes of driving, whether or not it appears on the invoice.

So the honest answer to the search is this. Private in-home tutoring exists in Al Ain and parents use it; published UAE in-home one-to-one rates run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. Those bands are market observations from October 2026, not an IB Gram price list. What you buy with the premium is a person in the room. What you give up is the size of the pool you are choosing from, which in a city this size is the thing that actually determines whether your child gets a specialist in their exact syllabus.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Al Ain or anywhere else in the UAE, and has no office, centre or branch in the country; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. IGCSE support for Al Ain families is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The reason to prefer that here is not convenience, it is supply: a family in Al Maqam gets a tutor who has taught Cambridge Physics 0625 Extended through several series, rather than whichever tutor is willing to drive out at 6pm on a Tuesday.

al-ain/igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Al Ain schools run IGCSE inside different sequences depending on the curriculum they are licensed for, and the tutoring that helps differs at each stage. These are the stages an Al Ain family passes through, with what each one actually demands.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 and Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The years before IGCSE option blocks are set. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October and are diagnostic rather than certificated. The useful work here is foundational: index laws, fractions, rearranging formulae, writing a paragraph with evidence, and reading an unfamiliar diagram without freezing.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Ain this stage decides more than families expect, because the city's smaller school set means a subject your child wants at IGCSE may not be offered at the school they are in. Finding that out in Year 9 leaves room to change course or to build the subject outside school; finding out in Year 10 does not.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Core and Extended routes
programmes.description: Two years, two routes, one grade ceiling decision. Extended science candidates sit a multiple-choice paper worth 30%, an extended theory paper worth 50% and Paper 6 Alternative to Practical worth 20%. Mathematics 0580 splits into Core and Extended paper pairs and requires a paper sat without a calculator under the current syllabus.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain's Cambridge cohorts are small enough that the school may teach Core and Extended in the same room, with differentiation left to worksheets. That is where private support earns its money: an Extended candidate taught at Core pace loses the top band quietly, and it does not show up until a mock paper comes back.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Tiered into Foundation and Higher rather than Core and Extended. Mathematics A 4MA1 is examined through two papers of equal weight. The sciences, 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1, use two written papers with practical skills assessed inside them rather than through a separate practical component.
programmes.countryNote: Several Al Ain schools enter candidates for a mix of boards across subjects, which catches parents out when they hire a tutor by subject name alone. Ask the school for the code on each entry; a single message to the exams officer prevents a term of preparation aimed at the wrong paper structure.

programmes.name: What IGCSE feeds: IB Diploma or AS and A Level
programmes.description: Al Ain students move on to either the IB Diploma Programme or AS and A Level depending on the school. The IGCSE grade is the entry ticket: a Higher Level DP science or an A Level in maths normally expects an Extended or Higher tier grade, which is why the gap between a 6 and a 7 is a sixth-form decision, not a bragging point.
programmes.countryNote: Because Al Ain offers fewer Diploma Programme places than Abu Dhabi island, a student who wants a specific Higher Level combination sometimes has to change school or commute. Planning that in Year 10, with the IGCSE grades it requires, is considerably cheaper than discovering it in Year 11.

al-ain/igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Availability in Al Ain is subject-specific rather than general. These are the IGCSE subjects Al Ain families ask for, with the syllabus codes to give any tutor before a first lesson.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher tier
subjects.description: The highest-volume request in the city. Marks go missing on algebraic fractions, non-calculator arithmetic, bearings and any question requiring working to be shown. Route and tier are set at entry, so the decision is made months before revision starts.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606), Further Pure (Edexcel 4PM1)
subjects.description: The thinnest cohort of any IGCSE subject in Al Ain, which makes it the hardest to staff locally. Calculus notation, binomial expansion and trigonometric identities carry the lost marks, and school clinics for it are rare because there are few candidates.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Electricity, moments and anything requiring a formula to be rearranged under time pressure. Cambridge candidates must handle Paper 6 Alternative to Practical, which rewards method criticism; Edexcel candidates meet practical skills inside the written papers instead.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Moles, reacting masses and qualitative analysis tables account for most dropped marks, with organic mechanisms close behind. The Alternative to Practical paper is learnable technique rather than talent, and it is 20% of the Cambridge grade.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The subject where command terms do the most damage. Students who know the content still lose marks because describe, explain and suggest each demand a different answer shape. Genetics and transport in plants are the usual pressure points.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Sciences (Cambridge 0654, 0653)
subjects.description: Common in Al Ain where triple science option blocks are small. Content overlaps the single sciences but the paper structure differs, so preparing a 0654 candidate with 0625 past papers wastes paid hours and produces false confidence.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500, Edexcel 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and composition decide the grade. A student who writes fluently still has to write to a mark scheme, which means register, audience and the specific split between structure marks and expression marks.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510, 0511)
subjects.description: A large cohort across Al Ain's bilingual households. The exercise types are predictable and unforgiving about following instructions, so timed practice with immediate correction beats vocabulary lists.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (Cambridge 0450, 0455; Edexcel 4BS1, 4EC1)
subjects.description: Case-study papers punish general-knowledge answers. The evaluation mark at the end of a long question is where most candidates stop short, and it is the most coachable part of either specification.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT (Cambridge 0478, 0417)
subjects.description: Pseudocode and trace tables for Computer Science; timed practical technique for ICT. Few tutors are strong at both, and in a city with small cohorts the honest answer is sometimes that a specialist has to be found outside Al Ain.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First and as an Additional Language (Cambridge 0508, 0544)
subjects.levels: First language and foreign language routes
subjects.description: Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies beyond their licensed curriculum. The first-language and foreign-language routes are separate specifications and need separately matched tutors.

subjects.name: Geography and History (Cambridge 0460, 0470; Edexcel 4GE1, 4HI1)
subjects.description: Source-handling and case-study recall decide these papers. The marks lost are usually structural: a student who knows the content answers the question they expected rather than the one printed, and that is a technique fix.

al-ain/igcse-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Al Ain's districts are minutes apart on a map and a long way apart in a tutor's evening. These are the areas families ask from, with what each one changes about scheduling.

regions.name: Al Jimi
regions.note: Central, dense by Al Ain standards, and close to several of the city's longest-established private campuses. Short school runs mean a 5pm start is realistic here, which is the earliest reliable slot anywhere in the city.

regions.name: Al Mutaredh and Al Khabisi
regions.note: Central-west residential districts with a mix of British and Indian curriculum catchments. Families here are the most likely to have two children at different schools, so consecutive one-to-one slots usually beat a single shared session.

regions.name: Al Muwaiji and Falaj Hazza
regions.note: Established villa districts west of the centre. Drive times from the central school belt are modest but add up for a tutor making a round trip, which is where the in-home travel premium becomes visible in a quote.

regions.name: Hili and Al Qattara
regions.note: Northern districts where school buses run longer routes, so children often arrive home after 4.30pm. A 5.30pm or 6pm online start holds week after week; an earlier one usually does not.

regions.name: Zakher
regions.note: A spread-out southern district popular with larger families. The distance from central Al Ain makes it one of the areas where in-home tutoring supply thins noticeably for specialist subjects.

regions.name: Al Towayya and Asharej
regions.note: Close to the university quarter, with a correspondingly high share of academic households. Demand here skews towards Extended Maths and triple science rather than general homework support.

regions.name: Al Maqam and Al Yahar
regions.note: Outlying southern and western districts where a tutor's round trip can exceed the lesson itself. For Cambridge 0606 or Computer Science 0478, an online specialist is realistically the only way to get one at all.

regions.name: Al Foah and Al Sarooj
regions.note: Northern and central districts with smaller private-school catchments nearby. Families here frequently look outside their immediate area for subject help, which online delivery makes a non-issue.

schoolClusters.city: The British-curriculum set serving central and southern Al Ain
schoolClusters.note: These campuses run Key Stage 3 into IGCSE and then into either AS and A Level or the Diploma Programme. Option blocks are narrower than on Abu Dhabi island, so a student wanting an unusual combination may find the subject taught in a very small group or not offered at all. That is the single most common reason Al Ain parents look for outside support.

schoolClusters.city: The Indian and bilingual curriculum set across the city
schoolClusters.note: Large cohorts, strong maths and science performance, and a steady flow of families moving a child onto an IGCSE or Diploma track mid-school. sections.heading: What an IGCSE home tutor in Al Ain actually involves
paragraphs: Start with the literal question. A home tutor in Al Ain is an individual who travels to a family's address and teaches there, usually for 60 or 90 minutes, usually in the early evening. Published UAE in-home one-to-one rates run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor working online. Monthly packages seen in the market sit around AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, and around AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are market figures read in October 2026, attributed to the providers who published them, not prices quoted by IB Gram.

What the premium pays for is travel and scarcity, in that order. A tutor driving from central Al Ain to Al Yahar or Al Maqam spends a meaningful part of the evening in the car, and that time is billed whether or not it is itemised. Scarcity compounds it: the number of people in Al Ain who have taught Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 through a full series is small, and the subset of those willing to drive to an outlying district at 6pm is smaller again. That is the real constraint on in-home tutoring in this city, and it is a supply problem rather than a price problem.

Parents choose in-home for reasons that deserve respect rather than a sales rebuttal. A younger student who will not sit still at a screen, a household where supervision matters, a child who reads a tutor's face better than a tutor's voice. Those are legitimate, and in a city where most households have the space for a study room, in-home arrangements work for plenty of Al Ain families. The question worth asking is narrower than online against in-home: does the person who can drive to you have the specification your child is examined on?

IB Gram's answer is to remove travel from the equation entirely. There are no home visits in the UAE and no premises in the country; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. For Al Ain families, lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The practical gain is that the shortlist is drawn from everyone who has taught the syllabus code rather than everyone who lives within a 25-minute drive, which in Al Ain are very different lists. The practical cost is that you need a quiet room and a stable connection, which is a fair thing to know before booking.

sections.heading: ADEK, not KHDA: what changes because Al Ain sits in the Abu Dhabi emirate
paragraphs: The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, and Al Ain sits inside that emirate. Dubai's authority has no role here, which matters because most general UAE tutoring content is written about Dubai. If you are reading about KHDA inspection bands, KHDA mandatory-subject circulars or KHDA fee decisions, you are reading about a different regulator than the one that licenses your child's school.

ADEK's remit is licensing and accreditation, which is a stronger word than inspection. A school operating in Al Ain holds its licence from ADEK, and its curriculum and accreditation sit within that framework. The federal baseline underneath it is the same across the country: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. So your child's school chose Cambridge or Pearson or the IB freely, and then layered the mandatory UAE subjects on top.

There is one ADEK rule that changes a decision parents actually make. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. This is press-reported rather than quoted from the current ADEK policy document, so verify it against ADEK before relying on the exact wording. The direction of travel is unambiguous: the arrangement some families hope for, paying their child's own classroom teacher for evening lessons, is the one to avoid.

What ADEK does not do is set private tutoring rates or vet individual tutors for you. No UAE regulator approves what a tutor charges. That gap is why market bands published with their sources are more useful to an Al Ain parent than any provider's claim about quality, and it is why this page publishes the bands instead of a ranking.

sections.heading: Drive times, school buses and when an Al Ain session can realistically start
paragraphs: The single most common reason a tutoring arrangement collapses in Al Ain is not the tutor. It is a start time nobody could hold. School buses in a low-density city run long routes, and a child in Hili or Al Yahar can arrive home close to an hour after a child in Al Jimi left the same campus. Agreeing a 4.30pm session for a household whose child walks in at 4.25pm produces three good weeks and then a pattern of rushed, resentful lessons.

Work backwards instead. Establish the realistic arrival time on a normal day, not the best day. Add thirty minutes for food and decompression, because a session that starts on an empty stomach is a session spent on behaviour rather than physics. That gives the earliest slot the family can hold every week for a term. For most central districts that lands between 5pm and 5.30pm; for the outlying districts and for families with a long bus route it is closer to 6pm.

For an in-home arrangement, add the tutor's journey to the same calculation and then add the risk. A tutor coming from central Al Ain to Al Maqam has to leave before they know whether the previous session ran over. That is why in-home sessions in outlying districts drift later across a term and why cancellation rates climb. Removing the journey does not make a tutor better, but it removes the one variable neither party controls.

sections.heading: The Al Ain school year, counted around Ramadan and the series
paragraphs: Nobody competing for this search names a term, a session or a deadline, which makes the calendar the easiest advantage to take. Two boards matter to Al Ain IGCSE families. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year.

Entry deadlines, not exam dates, are what catch families out. Cambridge's March series is the clearest published illustration: the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries were due 27 November 2026, forecast grades are due 27 February 2027, results reach centres on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. Entries closed more than two months before the first paper. The tier and route decision, Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher, is therefore made before any revision happens, and a tutor engaged afterwards is working inside a choice already locked in.

Pearson's published record gives similar anchors. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables in advance, including International GCSE November 2027, and because provisional dates can be revised the only safe practice is to work from the live official timetable rather than a date restated on any website.

Ramadan sits inside this calendar and moves each year, which is the detail general tutoring advice ignores. School hours shorten, energy patterns change, and the evening becomes the productive part of the day for many Al Ain households. Planning around it is straightforward if it is planned: shift sessions to a post-Iftar slot, shorten them, and move the heaviest paper practice out of that window into the weeks on either side. A plan that pretends the month is a normal month produces four weeks of poor sessions and a demoralised student. For IB families reading this because of a sibling, note that UAE schools sit the May session, but no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed against the IB itself, so check every IB date with the school's IB coordinator.

sections.heading: The thin-cohort problem: subjects a smaller school set cannot always staff
paragraphs: This is the part of Al Ain tutoring nobody advertises, because it is a limitation rather than a selling point. A city with a smaller private-school set has smaller subject cohorts, and smaller cohorts mean three things at once: the school may not offer the subject, the teacher covering it may be covering two others, and the number of local tutors who have taught it through a full series may be very small. Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606, Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1, Computer Science 0478 and several language specifications all sit in this category here.

The consequence for a parent is a choice that is rarely spelled out. You can take a generalist who will learn the specification alongside your child, which sometimes works and always costs more hours than it looks like. You can take a group class covering a different but adjacent syllabus, which produces confident answers to the wrong paper. Or you can accept that the specialist is not in Al Ain and take them over live video, which is the honest version of the same decision and the one that keeps the subject matched to the code.

What a provider should do here is disclose, not conceal. No competitor page found in research discloses a coverage limit at all, and several route UAE parents to overseas phone numbers without saying where the tutor is. Our position is the reverse: if no specialist is available for your subject and slot, we say so, give a realistic match time, and tell you where the tutor would be teaching from. A disclosed wait is a decision you can make; an undisclosed substitution is one made for you.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies running alongside IGCSE
paragraphs: Almost no competitor page in this market mentions the mandatory UAE subjects, and Al Ain families meet them every week. The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. So whichever international curriculum an Al Ain school is licensed for, these subjects sit alongside it, and they appear on reports and in timetables that parents planning IGCSE revision often treat as background noise.

They are not background noise, for two reasons. The first is workload: a Year 11 student carrying nine IGCSE subjects plus mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies is carrying a heavier week than the IGCSE count suggests, and a tutoring plan that ignores it will be the thing that gets dropped. The second is equivalency. On the Ministry of Education's British track, the requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. A family counting Arabic towards the five would be short, which is a real and avoidable error.

Dubai publishes the most detailed public guidance on how these subjects are organised, and while it is issued by the Dubai authority rather than ADEK, it indicates the shape of the requirement nationally. Its mandatory-subject guidance states that for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited due to the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. It also sets instructional time based on a 40-minute lesson unit, advising that any mandatory-subject lesson be at least 25 minutes. Al Ain parents should confirm the equivalent arrangements with ADEK and their own school rather than assuming Dubai's wording applies.

One constraint matters for anyone buying Arabic or Islamic Education tutoring. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. A tutor supporting these subjects therefore works on the student's own prescribed material and on skills, not on an alternative syllabus they prefer. Ask any prospective Arabic tutor which route your child sits, first language or foreign language, because they are separate specifications with separate demands.

sections.heading: Permits, ethics and the question of who may legally teach your child
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work, not unregulated work. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The official route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time.

Two practical tests follow from that. If a tutor tells you the permit is expensive, they have not applied for it, because it is free. If they tell you it takes months, they have not applied either, because the published completion time is two working days. And individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published by the ministry, and a figure circulating online could not be verified, so treat any specific amount quoted at you as unsourced, including the absence of one here.

For Al Ain specifically, the ADEK layer matters. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported and verify it against the current ADEK policy document. Either way, do not go looking for your child's own subject teacher as an evening tutor: it places the teacher at professional risk and it removes the independent second opinion that is half the value of tutoring.

A final clarification about status, because this market is full of borrowed authority. A tutoring operation with premises and staff needs an educational services permit from the relevant education authority, which is a different instrument from an individual's tutor permit. IB Gram is an independent online tutor-matching platform with no premises, centre or branch in the UAE, and it holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Any provider implying otherwise is making a claim worth checking before you pay them.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with coursework, and the line that protects the qualification
paragraphs: One of the pages competing in this market sells completed Internal Assessments. That is not a cheaper route; it is an academic-integrity breach where the student carries the consequence and the seller does not. IB Gram does not write, complete or produce an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay, Personal Project or any assessed coursework, and does not edit a draft to the point where the work ceases to be the student's own.

What a tutor may legitimately do is most of what actually helps. Teach the skills the task assesses. Explain the criteria in the student's own words. Ask the questions that expose a weak research question before three weeks are spent on it. Point at a paragraph and say the claim is unsupported. Model an analysis on different data so the method is understood rather than copied. Hold a deadline schedule. The line is easy to state: the tutor works on the student's thinking, never on the student's text.

For IGCSE candidates in Al Ain the practical consequence is where the money should go. Most current specifications put the marks in written papers and components such as Cambridge Paper 6 Alternative to Practical, which is 20% of an Extended science grade. Apparatus interpretation, method criticism and the ability to identify a controlled variable are coachable and worth paying for. Polishing prose that no examiner will ever read is not. On English specifications the assessed writing is produced under controlled conditions, so timed practice with mark-scheme feedback is the work.

Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables are referenced and linked from their official sources, never reproduced or supplied as downloads. That is a copyright position as much as an integrity one. A provider offering to send you a folder of board material is telling you something about how else they cut corners.

sections.heading: Equivalency and what happens after IGCSE for an Al Ain student
paragraphs: Families in Al Ain ask about Ministry of Education equivalency more often than Dubai families do, because a larger share plan on UAE universities. The published British-track requirement is specific: proof of five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at the Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at the Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That detail is worth dwelling on, because a competitor page ranking in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. The published rule is five accredited subjects, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from the count. Getting this wrong in either direction costs a family either money or a university place, so verify the current wording on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority before planning around it, and do not rely on a tutoring website, this one included, as your source of record.

For the American track, the published requirements are different again: English proficiency via a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics via at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB, no points threshold is published in the sources available here, so this page states none; confirm it on moe.gov.ae.

Two cautions to close on. Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs, not a service any tutoring provider performs or guarantees, and nobody should imply otherwise. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression; it is a way of closing a specific gap in a specific subject. Any page suggesting your child's progression depends on buying hours is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process.

process.title: Attach one recently marked paper
process.description: A marked paper tells a specialist more than any description of the problem. We use it to separate a knowledge gap from a command-term failure, a timing problem or arithmetic slips under pressure, because those four need four different interventions and guessing between them wastes a term.

process.title: Agree a slot that survives the Al Ain school run
process.description: Work backwards from a normal arrival time, not a good one, and add thirty minutes. Central districts usually land on a 5pm or 5.30pm start; Zakher, Al Maqam and Al Yahar households are generally better served from 6pm. Pick the slot you can hold every week for a term.

process.description: Put marked past papers side by side rather than comparing impressions. If the loss pattern has not moved, the intervention is wrong and should change. whyPoints.description: Al Ain sits under ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the Abu Dhabi emirate. Advice written about KHDA does not govern your child's school. Getting that straight changes which inspection record you read and which ethics rules apply to who may tutor your child.

whyPoints.description: A tutor is matched to the specification the school enters for. Cambridge Extended sciences use a multiple-choice paper at 30%, a theory paper at 50% and Paper 6 at 20%; Pearson 4PH1 uses two written papers with practicals assessed inside them. Preparing for the wrong structure wastes paid hours.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE home tutor to our address in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE and holds no office, centre or branch in the country; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. For Al Ain families, IGCSE lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The practical gain in this city is supply: the shortlist is drawn from every tutor who has taught your child's syllabus code rather than those living within a drivable radius of Zakher or Al Maqam. The practical requirement is a quiet room and a stable connection at the agreed time.

faqs.question: What does a private home tutor charge per hour in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Published UAE in-home one-to-one rates run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, with travel included in the figure, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor working online. Monthly packages seen in the market sit around AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are market observations read in October 2026 and attributed to the providers who published them, not IB Gram prices. In outlying Al Ain districts expect the upper end, because the drive is longer and fewer specialists will make it.

faqs.question: Which authority regulates my child's private school in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: The Department of Education and Knowledge, ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi. Al Ain sits inside that emirate, so Dubai's authority has no role. This matters when you read general UAE guidance: material about KHDA inspection bands or KHDA circulars describes a different regulator from the one that licenses your school. The federal baseline applies on top: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

faqs.question: Can my child's own teacher at an Al Ain school tutor them privately in the evening?
faqs.answer: Avoid it. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. This is press-reported rather than quoted from the current ADEK policy document, so verify the exact wording with ADEK. Beyond the rules, an independent tutor gives you a second opinion on your child's work, which is half the point of hiring one at all.

faqs.question: Why is it hard to find an Additional Mathematics 0606 tutor in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Because the cohort is small and so is the teaching pool. Al Ain's private-school set is considerably smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, so a subject with a handful of candidates per school is taught by a teacher covering two or three other courses, and the number of people in the city who have taken 0606 through a full series is genuinely small. Live video widens the pool to everyone who has taught the specification. Where no specialist is free we say so and give a match time rather than placing a generalist, and we tell you where the tutor teaches from.

faqs.question: What is the earliest a weekly tutoring session can realistically start in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Work backwards from a normal arrival time rather than a good one, then add thirty minutes for food. Central districts such as Al Jimi, Al Mutaredh and Al Khabisi usually land on a 5pm or 5.30pm start. Hili, Al Qattara and Zakher households, with longer bus routes, are generally better served from 5.30pm or 6pm. For Al Maqam and Al Yahar, an online slot from 4.30pm is practical precisely because nobody has to drive. The slot that matters is the one the family can hold every week for a whole term.

faqs.question: How should tutoring work around Ramadan in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Plan for it rather than pretending the month is normal. School hours shorten, sleep patterns shift, and the evening becomes the productive part of the day for many households. The arrangement that works is a post-Iftar slot, shorter sessions than usual, and lighter content: consolidation, flashcard work and short question sets rather than full timed papers. Move whole past papers into the weeks on either side. Because the dates move each year, agree the revised schedule a few weeks ahead rather than in the first week, and confirm the school's adjusted timetable before setting a slot.

faqs.question: Does a tutor in Al Ain need a permit, and how do I check?
faqs.answer: Yes, and you check by asking to see it. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a published two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so distrust specific amounts.

faqs.question: My child sits Cambridge but their cousin in Al Ain sits Edexcel, so are the tutors interchangeable?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. Cambridge Extended sciences use a multiple-choice paper worth 30%, an extended theory paper worth 50% and Paper 6 Alternative to Practical worth 20%. Pearson Edexcel 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 use two written papers with practical skills assessed inside them. Mathematics differs too: 0580 splits into Core and Extended routes and requires a non-calculator paper, while 4MA1 tiers into Foundation and Higher with two equally weighted papers. A tutor fluent in one board may well be fluent in the other, but ask rather than assume, and give them the code.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education count towards UAE equivalency for an IGCSE student?
faqs.answer: No. The published Ministry of Education British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. A ranking competitor page states a higher subject count, which does not match the published rule. Those subjects are still compulsory at school, since private schools must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed curriculum, but they do not fill the equivalency count. Verify the current wording on moe.gov.ae before planning around it.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects should an Al Ain student take tutoring in at once?
faqs.answer: Rarely more than two, and often one. A Year 11 student in Al Ain is usually carrying eight or nine IGCSE subjects plus mandatory Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies, which is a heavier week than the subject count suggests. Adding three tutored subjects produces a timetable the student quietly abandons. The better approach is to diagnose from marked papers which one or two subjects are costing the most grades, work on those until the loss pattern changes, then reassess. Spreading hours thinly across five subjects is the most common way a tutoring budget produces nothing.

faqs.question: Is a group class at an Al Ain centre as useful as one-to-one lessons?
faqs.answer: It depends whether your child's problem is shared. Group classes are priced well below one-to-one and work when a whole cohort needs the same syllabus coverage in the same order, which suits breadth revision. They work poorly for a diagnosed individual weakness, because the pace cannot stop on your child's particular error. A reasonable combination is group revision for coverage plus a few one-to-one sessions on the specific components dragging the grade. Note that a centre with premises and staff needs an educational services permit, which is a different instrument from an individual tutor's permit.

faqs.question: What does Paper 6 Alternative to Practical actually test, and can a tutor help online?
faqs.answer: It tests practical reasoning on paper: reading apparatus diagrams, identifying controlled variables, criticising a described method, reading scales correctly, plotting and interpreting data, and suggesting improvements. It is worth 20% of a Cambridge Extended science grade, and it is one of the most coachable components on the specification because the question types repeat across series. All of that works over live video, because the skill being examined is written reasoning about an experiment rather than manipulation of equipment. Pearson candidates do not sit a separate practical paper; practical skills appear inside the written papers instead.

faqs.question: When should an Al Ain family book tutoring for a June series?
faqs.answer: Before the entry decision, which is earlier than most families expect. Cambridge's published March 2027 series had final entries due 27 November 2026 for an exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027, which shows how far ahead entry closes on any series. Tier and route, Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher, are therefore settled before revision starts, and that decision deserves evidence from marked work. Practically: start in September or October for a June series, both because the market is soft then and because scarce-subject specialists still have slots.

faqs.question: Will an online tutor know what my child's Al Ain school is actually teaching this term?
faqs.answer: They will if you give them the information, and a good tutor asks for it. The useful inputs are the school's scheme of work or topic list for the term, the most recent marked assessment, and the syllabus code for each entry. With those, a weekly session can run alongside the class rather than behind it, which is what stops a student arriving at a topic twice unprepared. Without them, any tutor, in the room or on screen, is guessing at sequence. Ask at the first session what documents they want, and treat a tutor who wants none as a warning.

intro.heading: Where your child is, where they need to be, and what the weeks in between contain
paragraphs: Most tutoring in this market is sold as a subscription to hope. A family books an hour a week, the hour happens, everyone is polite, and nine weeks later nobody can say what has changed. The alternative is unglamorous and far more effective: establish the current grade from marked work, name the specific reason marks are being lost, agree the number of weeks available, and write down what each week will contain and how it will be checked. That is what an IGCSE online tutor in Al Ain should be selling, and it is what this page describes.

The starting point is always evidence, never an impression. A parent's sense that their child is struggling in Chemistry is real but imprecise, and imprecision is expensive at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, which is the published market band for a qualified online subject tutor. One recently marked school paper, with the marks and the examiner-style comments still on it, tells a specialist more in ten minutes than a month of weekly sessions will. It separates four very different problems that look identical from the outside: missing knowledge, misread command terms, running out of time, and accuracy failure under pressure.

Those four need four different plans. A student with content gaps across the 0620 syllabus needs coverage, in order, with assessment points. A student who knows the chemistry but writes describe answers when the question says explain needs technique work, which can move a grade in six to eight sessions because nothing new has to be learned. A student who finishes 80% of the paper needs timed drilling and a question-order strategy. A student who loses marks to arithmetic and unit errors needs a checking routine. Buying generic weekly tutoring for any of them is buying the average of four treatments, which is the treatment for nothing.

The second input is the calendar, and here Al Ain families have an advantage if they use it. Cambridge International runs IGCSE exams in a June series and a November series; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November. Entry closes long before the papers: on Cambridge's published March 2027 series, final entries were due 27 November 2026 for an exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027. Count the weeks you actually have, subtract the school's mock fortnight and any Ramadan adjustment, and the real number is almost always smaller than the one in a parent's head.

The third input is honesty about what online delivery does and does not change. IB Gram teaches Al Ain families one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; there are no home visits in the UAE and no premises in the country, since in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. What live video genuinely improves is the match, because the tutor is chosen from everyone who has taught the syllabus code rather than from those who can drive to Al Jimi by six. What it does not do is supply motivation, replace the school laboratory, or make a nine-week problem into a three-week one.

al-ain/igcse-online-tutor.programmesIntro: The plan looks different depending on how far through the course your child is. These are the four positions an Al Ain family is usually in when they first ask about tutoring, and what the sensible timeline is for each.

programmes.name: Year 10, the start of the IGCSE course
programmes.description: Eighteen months of runway and almost no pressure, which makes this the cheapest hour of tutoring a family will ever buy. The work is foundational and preventive: algebraic manipulation, significant figures, the habit of showing method, and learning early what a mark scheme rewards. One session a week through Year 10 usually removes the need for an emergency block in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Ain this is also when a subject-availability problem becomes visible. The city's private-school set is smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, so a student who wants a subject the school runs in a group of four will meet a teacher splitting attention across several courses. Discovering that in Year 10 leaves time to build the subject outside school.

programmes.name: Year 11, autumn term, before mocks
programmes.description: The best time to start if you have not already. There is still time for content coverage and for technique, mocks are close enough to give honest evidence, and the entry decision has not yet closed. A 12 to 14-week block from September, reviewed at mocks, is the most productive shape of support available at IGCSE.
programmes.countryNote: Entry deadlines land in this window. Cambridge's March 2027 series had final entries due 27 November 2026, which illustrates how early tier and route decisions close on any series. Al Ain parents should settle Core against Extended, or Foundation against Higher, on evidence from marked work rather than on optimism.

programmes.name: Year 11, after mocks, before the series
programmes.description: The mock paper is the most valuable document in the house. From here the plan is almost entirely technique: timing, command terms, whole papers under exam conditions, and the three or four question types the student reliably drops. Content coverage is triaged rather than completed, because there is no longer time to teach everything twice.
programmes.countryNote: Specialist availability in Al Ain tightens sharply in this window, and so do rates across the market. A family calling in April for a June series is competing for whatever slots remain, particularly in thin-cohort subjects such as Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 and Computer Science 0478.

programmes.name: Retake and November series preparation
programmes.description: A retake is a technical problem with a known answer, because the result breaks down into components. One paper usually carried the loss. The plan starts from the statement of results and the component marks, targets the weakest paper, and treats the rest as maintenance rather than relearning the whole syllabus.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson's published record is useful here: the November 2026 International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. That gives a real eight-to-ten week preparation window from the August results, which is enough for a targeted single-paper rebuild.

al-ain/igcse-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Timelines differ by subject because the loss patterns differ. These are the IGCSE subjects Al Ain families bring to an online tutor, with what typically needs fixing and roughly how long it takes.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher tier
subjects.description: Technique-heavy, so grade movement can be quick when the issue is method marks rather than content. Non-calculator work, algebraic fractions and multi-step problems are the usual culprits. Six to eight sessions can change a grade boundary outcome if the diagnosis is right.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Electricity, moments and formula rearrangement. Cambridge candidates also carry Paper 6 Alternative to Practical at 20% of the grade, which is unusually coachable: the question types repeat and the reasoning is written rather than physical.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Moles and reacting masses need drilling rather than explaining; qualitative analysis needs a memorised, testable table; organic mechanisms need pattern recognition. Three distinct problems inside one subject, which is why a generic Chemistry booking underperforms.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The subject where command terms do most of the damage. Students who know the material lose marks because describe, explain and suggest want different answer shapes. That is a six-to-eight-session fix, and the fastest available grade movement at IGCSE.

subjects.name: Coordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654)
subjects.description: Common in Al Ain where triple science blocks are small. The paper structure differs from the single sciences, so timed practice must use 0654 papers. Preparing with 0625 material produces confidence that does not transfer to the actual paper.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510, 0511)
subjects.description: Highly predictable exercise types and ruthless about instruction-following. Timed practice with immediate correction moves marks faster than vocabulary work, because most lost marks come from answering a slightly different question than the one asked.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500, Edexcel 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and composition carry the grade. The work is writing to a mark scheme rather than writing well: register, audience, and the split between structure and expression marks. Progress shows in marked pieces, not in reading more.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Additional and Further Pure (Cambridge 0606, Edexcel 4PM1)
subjects.description: The thinnest tutor pool at IGCSE and the longest match time in Al Ain. Calculus notation, binomial expansion and trigonometric identities. Book earlier than you think you need to, because availability collapses close to a series.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (Cambridge 0450, 0455)
subjects.description: Case-study technique decides the grade. Most candidates stop short of the evaluation mark at the end of long questions, which is coachable in a handful of sessions once the habit is identified from a marked paper.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode, trace tables and logic. Works unusually well over live video because the whole subject lives on a shared screen, and a tutor can watch a trace table being filled in real time rather than reading the finished version.

subjects.name: ICT (Cambridge 0417)
subjects.description: Practical task technique under time pressure, which is a different job from Computer Science despite the shelving. Screen sharing makes this teachable remotely, since the examiner is assessing the same software operations the tutor can watch live.

subjects.name: Geography and History (Cambridge 0460, 0470)
subjects.description: Source handling and structured case-study recall. Marks are lost structurally: the student answers the question they prepared rather than the one printed. Essay planning under time is the intervention, and it shows in marked work within a month.

A defined end date, with continuing treated as a decision rather than a default

modes.title: Single-component repair
modes.description: Four to six sessions aimed at one component: Paper 6 Alternative to Practical, the case-study paper, the directed writing task, or non-calculator technique. Used when the rest of the subject is secure and one paper is pulling the grade down. It is also the cheapest honest way to test whether tutoring helps your child at all, because the cost and the finish point are both small.

No ongoing commitment, which is the point of the format

modes.title: Weekly maintenance alongside the school's scheme of work
modes.description: A standing weekly slot that tracks what the class is doing now, used mostly from Year 10 or by students who have already closed a gap and want to keep it closed. Lower intensity, lower cost over a term, and the least likely to produce a crisis in the spring. Progress is measured against school assessments rather than against a tutoring plan.

sections.heading: What the first 30 minutes with an online tutor should produce
paragraphs: A first session that produces warmth and no information has wasted the most valuable hour of the whole arrangement. The first session exists to diagnose, and a diagnosis has a specific output: the two or three places marks are actually being lost, which of them is cheapest to fix, and roughly how many sessions each will take. That output should be written down and sent to the parent. If it is not written down, it will be forgotten by week three and replaced by a feeling about progress.

The raw material is one recently marked paper. Not a description of the difficulty, not a school report, and not last year's grade. A marked paper shows where the marks went, and a specialist reads it the way a mechanic listens to an engine. A student who scores well on the first half of the paper and poorly on the last third has a timing problem. A student who scores evenly but low has content gaps. A student who writes long answers to short questions has a command-term problem. A student whose method is right and whose final answers are wrong has an accuracy problem. These are four different jobs.

The tutor should also establish the constraints honestly in that first half hour. How many weeks are left before the series. What else the student is carrying, which in Al Ain usually means eight or nine IGCSE subjects plus mandatory Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies. What time the student actually gets home, which in Hili or Al Yahar is later than in Al Jimi. Whether Ramadan falls inside the block. A plan built without those four facts is a plan built for a different student.

Finally, the session should end with something checkable. A short set of questions on the diagnosed weakness, to be done before next week, and a stated expectation of what the result will look like if the diagnosis is right. That last part is what separates a plan from a guess: if the prediction fails, the diagnosis was wrong and the plan changes in week two rather than week nine.
bullets: Output of session one: two or three named loss points, ranked by cost to fix
Input required: one recently marked paper, with the marks still visible

A testable prediction, so a wrong diagnosis is caught in week two

sections.heading: Two different journeys: grade 4 to 6, and grade 6 to 8
paragraphs: Parents often ask how long tutoring takes to work, and the honest answer depends on which journey the student is on. Moving from a grade 4 to a grade 6 and moving from a grade 6 to an 8 are not the same distance travelled twice. The first is usually about closing gaps and building reliability; the second is almost entirely about precision, because the student already knows the material and is losing marks in the last 10% of each answer.

The lower journey is more responsive to coverage. A student at grade 4 in Cambridge Chemistry 0620 typically has real holes: moles never properly understood, ionic equations guessed at, qualitative analysis never memorised. Those are teachable in order, and progress is visible within a few weeks because each closed gap converts directly into marks. The risk in this journey is breadth: the temptation is to cover everything, and the correct approach is to cover the topics that appear most heavily in the papers first.

The upper journey is slower per grade and more frustrating, because the work looks like it should already be right. A grade 6 student writes a correct answer that earns two of three marks because the third mark required a comparison, a unit, or a named example. Fixing that means reading mark schemes rather than textbooks, and it means a tutor who can say exactly which word was missing. It is also where a specialist earns the upper end of the market band, because a generalist cannot see the missing mark.

The table below sets out the shape of each journey. Treat the session counts as planning estimates drawn from the common pattern of these loss types, not as a promise: no tutor can promise a specific outcome, and any provider who offers to is making a claim they cannot honour. What can be promised is that the plan will be reviewed against marked papers every four to six weeks and changed if the evidence says it is not working.

sections.heading: A 14-week block, written out week by week
paragraphs: This is the part almost no tutoring provider publishes, which is strange, because it is the only thing a parent is actually buying. A planned block has phases. The first fortnight is diagnosis and the fastest technique wins, because early visible progress is what keeps a sixteen-year-old engaged. The middle stretch is content and consolidation, which is the dull part and the part that produces the grade. The final phase is whole papers under time, where the only new learning is about the student's own behaviour under pressure.

The plan below assumes one 90-minute session a week plus homework, which is the most common arrangement, and it assumes a single subject. Two subjects at once means two plans and roughly double the homework, which is why we usually advise against starting three. In Al Ain, where a Year 11 student also carries mandatory Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside eight or nine IGCSE subjects, the homework load is the constraint that decides whether a plan survives contact with reality.

Two adjustments are built in. The school's mock fortnight is not a tutoring week, it is an evidence week: the mock paper replaces the planned session content and becomes the mid-block review. And if Ramadan falls inside the block, the sessions in that window move to a post-Iftar slot, shorten, and carry consolidation rather than full timed papers, with the heavy paper practice shifted to the weeks either side.

The parent's job in each phase is in the final column, and it is deliberately small. Two or three checks across fourteen weeks is enough: did the predicted early win happen, has the loss pattern on a marked paper changed by the mid-block review, and is the completion rate on timed papers improving in the final phase. A parent checking every week is reading noise. A parent checking nothing is paying for a feeling.
