american-curriculum-to-ib-transition.programmesIntro: Four routes an American-curriculum family in the UAE is actually choosing between at 15 or 16. The Diploma is one, and the comparison that matters most is with Advanced Placement rather than with the standard high-school diploma.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: A single two-year qualification rather than a collection of courses: six subjects across six prescribed groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus an Extended Essay of 4,000 words, Theory of Knowledge with an essay and an exhibition, and CAS. Scored out of 45 points with 24 needed to pass, and three of those points awarded from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge matrix.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE the Diploma is a minority route with a solid institutional base — 7 per cent of Dubai private-school pupils in 2024-25 — and it is growing: three of the seven new schools opening in Dubai for 2026-27 are International Baccalaureate, part of 16,846 new places. For an American-curriculum family that means more Diploma seats, and more competition for experienced Diploma teachers at the same time.

programmes.name: Advanced Placement within a US high-school diploma
programmes.description: Individual college-level courses sat as standalone examinations alongside a standard high-school diploma, each scored 1 to 5. A student chooses how many to take and when, and the diploma itself is awarded on credits and GPA rather than on the AP results. There is no core, no compulsory breadth beyond the school's graduation requirements, and no compulsory second language in most schools.
programmes.countryNote: This is the real alternative, and it is often the better one. A student can take three or four APs in genuine strengths without carrying a forced sixth subject, and can add one in Grade 12 if a university target changes. Per-exam fees are published by the College Board and change, so check the current figure on the College Board's own site rather than on a tutoring page.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The five years before the Diploma in a continuum school, assessed against criteria A to D in every subject group with a Personal Project in the final year. Students arriving into DP1 from MYP have used criterion-based marking and command terms for years, which is precisely the fluency an American-curriculum arrival spends its first term acquiring.
programmes.countryNote: Where a UAE school offers both MYP and a US middle-school programme, moving a child at Grade 8 or 9 rather than at Grade 10 removes most of the cost of this transition. The child reaches DP1 already fluent in criteria, and the family never pays for the first-term adjustment that Grade 10 arrivals almost always need.

programmes.name: IB Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses combined with a career-related study and a separate core including a reflective project and personal and professional skills. Smaller and less widely offered in the UAE than the full Diploma, and genuinely worth asking about where a student is strong in two subjects and would be carrying a third only to satisfy a group requirement.
programmes.countryNote: Availability varies school by school across the emirates, so confirm directly with the sixth form rather than assuming the IB label includes it. For equivalency and admissions purposes, treat it as a different certificate from the full Diploma and check its recognition with the relevant authority before building a plan on it.

american-curriculum-to-ib-transition.subjectsIntro: Subject by subject, where a US Honors or AP background leaves a student relative to a Diploma course, and which gap costs money to close. The pattern is unlike the IGCSE pattern: breadth of coverage is usually fine, depth per topic is the gap.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Honors Algebra II and Precalculus cover much of the Standard Level ground, but the Diploma expects algebraic fluency without technology on one paper and proof as a routine expectation. Students who have always worked with a graphing calculator in reach lose marks on manipulation rather than on concepts, which is a drill problem and cheap to fix early.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Often the better fit for an American-curriculum arrival, because modelling, data handling and technology-permitted assessment match how US courses already work. The HL statistics content is substantial and the exploration still needs supervision, but the adjustment cost is markedly lower than on the Analysis route.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: AP Physics 1 or 2 leaves a student in reasonable shape on mechanics and electricity. What is new is uncertainty treatment, graph linearisation and the individual investigation, which is an open-ended experimental project assessed against criteria rather than a lab report marked for neatness.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: AP Chemistry overlaps heavily with Diploma Higher Level and in places goes further. The adjustment is in assessment style: the data-based question expects use of the provided booklet, and extended-response marks are earned by explanation chains in chemical language rather than by arriving at the right number.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume is the issue. Diploma Biology is wide and examined with precise command terms, and a student used to unit tests on discrete chapters has to hold the whole course at once for a terminal paper. Steady low-intensity support across DP1 costs far less than a concentrated rescue block in DP2.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: American-curriculum students usually write confidently and cite properly. The new apparatus is the analysis of how meaning is constructed in context, plus the individual oral and, at Higher Level, the HL essay. A strong English GPA predicts very little here, which surprises families in the first reporting cycle.

subjects.name: Group 2 languages, including Spanish, French and Arabic
subjects.description: Many US schools require two or three years of a world language, so an American-curriculum arrival is often better placed here than a British-curriculum one. Confirm which languages the Diploma school offers and at which level, because continuity is worth real money and a language restarted at ab initio is two years of work.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: AP US History or World History builds strong source habits and essay structure. The Diploma's historical investigation has a formal structure with its own source-evaluation section, and the Higher Level extension adds a depth study with a separate paper. Reading volume is the cost, which is time rather than tuition.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: AP Microeconomics and Macroeconomics cover much of the content. The Diploma's internal assessment is a set of commentaries on published news articles against specific criteria, which is a research and writing skill rather than a content one and is the component most likely to need structured supervision.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with a substantial internal assessment and, at Higher Level, a pre-released case study the whole cohort prepares. Students from US business or economics electives find the content accessible and the evaluation demands new: recommending and justifying carries the marks.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: A frequently useful choice for an American-curriculum arrival because it can satisfy either the science or the humanities group in some timetables, which relieves pressure on a six-subject grid. Assessment is strongly data and fieldwork based, so a student comfortable with lab work and project assessment tends to settle quickly.

subjects.name: Visual Arts and Film
subjects.description: Portfolio and process subjects assessed over two years against criteria, with documentation requirements that are unlike anything in a US arts elective. Support here is process coaching — journals, sourcing, deadlines — rather than teaching, and families who treat Group 6 as the timetable's easy slot usually revise that view in DP2.

american-curriculum-to-ib-transition.regionsTitle: Where American-curriculum and Diploma schools sit, emirate by emirate
american-curriculum-to-ib-transition.regionsIntro: The geography of this transition is specific: US-curriculum provision and Diploma provision overlap in some communities and not at all in others. These notes are about what that does to school choice and to session timing.

regions.name: Dubai: Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Both systems are well represented along this corridor, and several families change route without changing neighbourhood. Traffic rather than distance sets the session time: a student collected at 3.15pm from this area is rarely settled before 5.30pm, so an online slot at 6.30pm or later holds week after week.

regions.name: Dubai: Dubai Festival City, Garhoud and Mirdif
regions.note: Established American-curriculum provision with Diploma schools reachable but on the other side of a long commute. Families who switch route here often keep the same school bus arrangement, which means a later evening slot and a plan that assumes the student is tired on two weeknights.

regions.name: Dubai: Dubai Hills, Meydan and Nad Al Sheba
regions.note: Newer communities where both curricula have opened recently, so the choice between AP and the Diploma is often available inside one school group. That is the cheapest place to make this decision, because comparing routes does not require comparing admissions processes at the same time.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Al Bateen
regions.note: Strong American-curriculum provision and a thinner Diploma map. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and its professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school — so the cheapest-looking source of help is unavailable by rule.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi: Saadiyat Island and Yas Island
regions.note: Both systems present, with distances that make a weekday in-person arrangement expensive in time for everyone involved. An online slot removes the travel question from a school night entirely, which matters most in DP1 when internal assessment deadlines start to land.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: Regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods rather than only inspecting. American-curriculum schools are present and Diploma places are limited, so a number of families commute into Dubai for Grades 11 and 12.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Under ADEK, with a small school market and real distances between campuses. The practical consequence for this transition is that a subject the local Diploma school does not offer cannot be picked up elsewhere, so confirm the six-group grid before accepting a place rather than after.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah, Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah
regions.note: Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulates private education there; Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit under the federal Ministry of Education. Diploma provision is sparse and Higher Level specialist cover in the local tutoring market is sparser, which makes online matching the realistic route rather than a convenience.

schoolClusters.note: US-curriculum schools across Dubai and Abu Dhabi. Several offer Advanced Placement courses alongside the high-school diploma, and a few offer the Diploma in the same building, which is the simplest place to compare the two routes without also comparing two admissions processes.

sections.heading: GPA to points: the answer in one paragraph, then the detail
paragraphs: An American-curriculum student moving to the Diploma is trading a system that rewards consistent visible effort for one that rewards accumulated understanding and independent project management. A GPA is built continuously from assignments, quizzes, participation and unit tests, and it is recoverable: a weak week is averaged away by a strong one. A Diploma grade in most subjects comes from terminal examinations plus one internal assessment, and nothing done in October appears anywhere except as preparation.

The cost of that trade is concentrated in the first two terms and it falls on a specific kind of student. The diligent, organised, assignment-completing student has mastered the system they are leaving, and their first Diploma reports are frequently worse than their GPA suggested — not because they have become weaker, but because the behaviour that produced the GPA produces middling criterion marks in a system that asks for something else. Meanwhile the student who always tested well and did their homework late sometimes improves.

The second cost is structural and permanent. A US high-school diploma is a credit-based award with elective freedom; the Diploma is a six-group grid. Somewhere in that grid there will be a subject your child would not have chosen. For American-curriculum arrivals the forced subject is usually the second language or the arts and electives group, and it is where the support budget should go — not into the Higher Level the student picked and enjoys.

The third cost is administrative and specific to this track. Ministry of Education equivalency on the American route requires English proficiency shown by IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics shown by at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. Those are published thresholds with fees and preparation time attached. Which track a student eventually sits under depends on the certificate they present, so verify the position for a Diploma certificate on moe.gov.ae — the source we read states no IB points threshold, and this page publishes none.

sections.heading: Advanced Placement against the Diploma, compared on structure and cost
paragraphs: The comparison most American-curriculum families should be making is not Diploma against high-school diploma. It is Diploma against a high-school diploma with three or four Advanced Placement courses in it, because that is the genuinely competitive alternative and it is cheaper to support in almost every case.

AP is modular. A student picks courses one at a time, sits each as a standalone examination scored 1 to 5, and can add one in Grade 12 if a university target changes. There is no compulsory breadth beyond the school's own graduation requirements, no core, and in most schools no compulsory second language in Grades 11 and 12. Support is therefore bought per course and per examination, with a visible end point.

The Diploma is a single integrated award. The six subjects, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS are not separable: a student who abandons the Extended Essay does not get a Diploma with one component missing, they get certificates in individual subjects instead. That integration is exactly why universities value it, and it is also why support costs more — nine places to be weak rather than three or four, and three of them are components no school teaches in a weekly lesson.

On fees, AP examinations carry a published per-exam charge from the College Board that varies by region and changes year to year, so check the current figure on the College Board's own site rather than on any tutoring page including this one. Diploma registration and subject fees are handled through the school and vary by school. In both cases the examination fee is a smaller line than two years of support, which is why this page concentrates on the support arithmetic.

sections.heading: The transcript problem: credits, GPA and a programme that reports neither
paragraphs: A US high-school transcript is a running record. It lists courses, credits earned, letter grades, a weighted and unweighted GPA, sometimes class rank, and it exists from Grade 9 onwards. A Diploma reports seven numbers at the end of two years: six subject grades from 1 to 7 and the core contribution. Between those two reporting cultures sits a practical problem that families discover when they apply to university or to the equivalency authority.

The first part of the problem is interim evidence. A student who moves into DP1 in Grade 11 has a transcript covering Grades 9 and 10 and then a two-year gap in which no external grade exists. Schools fill the gap with predicted grades and internal reports, which are not the same currency. Any application made during DP1 or early DP2 is made on a transcript plus predictions, and families should ask the school early exactly what it will issue and when.

The second part is the credit question. A student moving into a Diploma school mid-stream may have earned credits in courses with no Diploma equivalent, and may be short of credits the Diploma school requires for its own graduation certificate. Some UAE schools award both a Diploma and a high-school diploma; some do not. This is a question for the registrar on the day a place is offered, not for the week before graduation.

The third is the mandatory UAE subjects, which sit outside both reporting systems and inside the timetable. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises at least 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. Those periods occupy the day whichever route a family chooses.

sections.heading: What the move costs a UAE household, with the lines nobody mentions
paragraphs: The fee line is unusually predictable this year. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family moving school to reach a Diploma place, the published fee is the fee for the year ahead, which makes a like-for-like comparison with the current school honest for once.

Capacity is rising at the same time. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools — four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate — creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. A family being told a Diploma seat is scarce should weigh that against the published expansion before paying a non-refundable deposit.

The support line is the one families underestimate, and the figures below are what named providers publish rather than what IB Gram charges. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget end; Unitors publishes IB from AED 200; TutorChase lists AED 270; BartyED lists AED 650 for premium named tutors. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 and specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 or above, with monthly estimates for a weekly hour running AED 240 to 600 at the budget tier, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work.

The lines unique to this track are the tests. SAT or English-proficiency preparation towards the MoE thresholds, and any AP examinations a student has already paid for and may not now sit, are real costs that a comparison between the two routes should include. The published MoE requirements for the American track are IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, plus at least 450 in SAT Math. Those are threshold scores, which means the preparation has a defined end rather than an open-ended one — a useful thing to insist on when buying test support.

sections.heading: Grade 10 to DP1, subject by subject
paragraphs: The subject-level gap in this transition has an unusual shape. American-curriculum students often arrive with wider coverage than a Diploma Standard Level requires and less depth per topic than Higher Level expects, because US courses move through more material at a shallower cut. That means the diagnosis cannot be done by comparing syllabus contents lists; it has to be done by setting Diploma-level questions and marking them.

Three gaps recur. The first is technology dependence in mathematics: a student who has always had a graphing calculator available loses manipulation marks on the paper that restricts it, which is a drill problem solvable in a term. The second is the internal assessment in the sciences, which is an open-ended individual investigation assessed against criteria rather than a lab report, and which needs supervision rather than teaching. The third is command terms, which have fixed meanings across every Diploma subject and which a US-curriculum student has never had to treat as a technical vocabulary.

What transfers well is worth stating too. Citation and academic-integrity practice from US schools is usually strong, which makes the Extended Essay less intimidating than it is for arrivals from systems with no research-writing tradition. Presentation and oral confidence transfer, which helps in the individual oral. And experience of project-based assessment means an internal assessment is a familiar genre, even if the criteria are not.

sections.heading: From assignments to a single examination: changing a study habit on purpose
paragraphs: The habit change is the real work of this transition and it is rarely addressed directly, because it does not look like a subject. A student whose grade has always been built from submitted work studies in response to deadlines: there is a thing due, so there is work to do. A Diploma student has long stretches with nothing due and an examination two terms away, and the study habit that worked for twelve years produces nothing in that gap.

What replaces it is retrieval practice on a schedule the student does not negotiate with. Short, frequent, self-tested recall across everything covered so far, rather than re-reading before a unit test. This is well-established as a study method and it is also deeply unintuitive for a student who has been rewarded for polished submissions. Teaching it explicitly in the first term of DP1 is the single highest-value non-subject intervention available.

The second half of the habit change concerns the internal assessments, which pull in the opposite direction: they are long-horizon independent projects with soft internal deadlines that the student has to self-impose. Students who are excellent at submitting assignments on time can be poor at this, because nobody is setting the intermediate dates. A supervisor's main job in DP1 is to impose those dates and hold them.

Both halves are cheaper to teach early. A student who builds a retrieval routine in September of DP1 and has internal assessment milestones imposed by December needs far less subject tutoring in DP2 than one who arrives in April having done neither. That is the most reliable way to reduce the total cost of this transition, and it is a scheduling intervention rather than an expensive one.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against a tutor in the room for this particular move
paragraphs: American-curriculum families in the UAE often expect in-home tutoring because it is the visible local norm, and the question deserves a straight answer rather than a redirect. In-home tutoring is widely available across Dubai and Abu Dhabi. It costs more per hour because travel sits inside the rate — Bestimate's Dubai 2026 figures put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with independent tutors quoting up to AED 500 — and the available pool is whoever will drive to your community at the hour you want.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. UAE lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video. For this transition the argument is specific: the useful tutor is one who can read a US transcript and a Diploma subject guide in the same conversation, and who knows where Honors Precalculus leaves a student relative to Maths AA. That is a narrow specialism, and searching for it by driving distance is how families end up with a competent tutor of the wrong system.

Scheduling is the second argument. Diploma deadlines cluster, and the weeks when a student needs an extra session are exactly the weeks when nobody has time to receive a visitor. An online slot can move by half an hour, split into two shorter sessions, or shift to a post-Iftar time through Ramadan without renegotiating anyone's route.

The third is that American-curriculum families move often. A relationship built over video survives a transfer from Abu Dhabi to Dubai, or out of the UAE to another posting, which an in-home arrangement does not. For a student mid-Diploma, continuity of supervisor across a relocation is worth more than almost anything else money can buy.

sections.heading: Academic honesty across two traditions, and where they differ
paragraphs: American-curriculum students usually arrive with better citation habits than students from most other systems: plagiarism policies, citation styles and originality checking are standard in US schools. That is a genuine advantage in a Diploma, where the Extended Essay and every internal assessment carry an authenticity requirement. It also creates a blind spot, because the Diploma's academic-honesty rules cover more than citation.

The difference that matters is collaboration and assistance. In many US courses, study groups, peer editing and tutor help with revision are normal and permitted. Under IB rules, the assessed work must be the student's own, and what a supervisor or tutor may contribute is bounded: teaching the skill, explaining the criteria, discussing a proposed question, modelling an approach on a different topic, and giving feedback on a draft the student has written. Rewriting a paragraph, editing a draft to completion or supplying a model essay on the student's own title crosses the line even where the student's ideas are underneath it.

The consequence is asymmetric and worth stating plainly. Malpractice falls on the student, not on whoever helped, and it can cost a Diploma. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; a family comparing providers should read that as information about the seller. Softer versions of the same offer — editing to completion, a written model on your child's own title — carry the same risk in friendlier packaging.

On materials, the same principle holds. We reference and link official subject guides, specimen papers and assessment documents rather than reproducing them, because the official copy is both the lawful one and the current one. And we do not describe tutors as examiners where current examiner status cannot be evidenced, nor use any such status to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, because it provides none.

sections.heading: Making the decision, and what we will tell you not to buy
paragraphs: The decidable version of this question needs three documents on a table: the transcript with its GPA and credits, the six Diploma subjects as the school would actually timetable them, and the list of university destinations with their published prerequisites. Most families find the answer becomes obvious once those three are side by side, and that the thing they were really worried about was the word Diploma rather than any specific consequence.

If the Diploma is the choice, the support budget should go in a specific order. First, one shared adjustment block on criteria, command terms and study habit, worked across subjects rather than bought in each. Second, the forced subject — the Group 2 language or the Group 6 elective. Third, core scoping: one session on the Extended Essay question before research begins and one on Theory of Knowledge structure before the first draft. Only then weekly subject support, and only in the single hardest Higher Level.

There are purchases we will advise against. Three or four weekly subjects bought in response to a first DP1 report, because that report usually measures one shared problem. Open-ended test preparation past a published threshold, when the MoE requirement is a score of 450 or a TOEFL iBT 61 rather than a maximum. Paying for board or College Board documents that are free from the source. And anything priced on an outcome promise, a self-asserted rating or an unevidenced examiner claim.

What happens next is straightforward: a free trial lesson with the specialist who would actually teach the subject, no card details, no commitment, followed by a written view on what the two years need and what they do not. If a scarce combination has no match available — a Group 6 subject with portfolio supervision, or a specific Group 2 language in an early-evening Gulf slot — we say so with an honest timeframe rather than offering an adjacent specialism.

faqs.question: Why did my child's grades drop after moving from a GPA system to the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Because the behaviour that produced the GPA produces middling criterion marks in a system that asks for something else. A GPA is built continuously from assignments, quizzes and participation, and a weak week averages away. A Diploma grade comes from terminal examinations plus one internal assessment per subject, and nothing submitted in October appears in the result. The diligent, assignment-completing student is usually the one whose first reports dip, while the student who always tested well sometimes improves. It is a habit problem, and it is treated once rather than subject by subject.

faqs.question: Is the Diploma or Advanced Placement better value for a UAE family?
faqs.answer: AP is cheaper to support in almost every case, because it is modular: three or four courses chosen in genuine strengths, each a standalone examination, with no core and no forced sixth subject. The Diploma is one integrated award with six subjects plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, which is nine places to need help rather than three. The Diploma's value is the core itself, which is what universities credit it for. A student with an uneven profile and a clear single direction usually belongs on the AP route.

faqs.question: What does the UAE Ministry of Education require from an American-track student?
faqs.answer: English proficiency shown by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics shown by at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. Those are published thresholds rather than targets to exceed, so preparation should be capped once met. Which track applies depends on the certificate your child eventually presents, so verify the position for a Diploma certificate on moe.gov.ae — the source we read publishes no IB points figure, and we will not invent one.

faqs.question: Will my child's US transcript still count after switching to the Diploma?
faqs.answer: The transcript covering Grades 9 and 10 remains what it is, and then there is a two-year stretch with no external grade in it. Schools fill that gap with predicted grades and internal reports, which are a different currency from a GPA. Ask the Diploma school three things when the place is offered: whether it will issue a transcript covering the Diploma years, whether it converts Diploma grades to a GPA for US applications, and whether it also awards a high-school diploma and on what credit basis.

faqs.question: Which mathematics route should an American-curriculum student take in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Applications and Interpretation is frequently the better fit, because modelling, data handling and technology-permitted assessment match how US courses already work. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic and proof-oriented route expected by most engineering, physics and mathematics programmes, and a student used to having a graphing calculator in reach will lose manipulation marks on the restricted paper until that is drilled. Decide against the published prerequisite on each target programme's own admissions page, and have your child attempt marked questions from both courses.

faqs.question: How do I know whether the Diploma is the wrong choice for my child?
faqs.answer: Three signals. An uneven transcript with two clear strengths and one weak area, because the six-group grid will force the weak area back into the timetable. A dislike of extended independent writing, because the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge are unavoidable and carry three of the 45 points. And no world-language study to build on, since a second language is compulsory for both years. Any one of those is manageable; all three together usually means three or four APs in strengths is the better and cheaper route.

faqs.question: What is the single most useful thing to buy in the first term of DP1?
faqs.answer: One shared block on criteria, command terms and study habit, worked across two or three subjects rather than purchased separately in each. The deficit an American-curriculum arrival has is one skill, not several content gaps: criteria read as guidance instead of as a mark scheme, command terms treated as ordinary English, and study driven by deadlines in a programme that has long stretches with nothing due. Treating that once in term one reliably reduces what DP2 costs, which is the opposite of what four weekly subjects does.

faqs.question: How does the science internal assessment differ from a US lab report?
faqs.answer: It is an open-ended individual investigation rather than a prescribed experiment written up. The student chooses the research question, designs the method, handles uncertainty properly, and is assessed against published criteria covering exploration, analysis, evaluation and communication. A US lab report is often marked on accuracy and presentation against a given procedure. The practical consequence is that the help needed is supervision — question scoping, intermediate deadlines, feedback on a draft — rather than subject teaching, and it is cheapest before any data is collected.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's Extended Essay if they have never written a research paper?
faqs.answer: Yes, and American-curriculum students usually start better placed than most because citation and originality practice is standard in US schools. The useful help is at the question: most Extended Essays fail because the question is too broad for 4,000 words or too narrow to sustain one, and no later help rescues a well-written essay answering an unanswerable question. A supervisor may discuss the question, explain the criteria, model an approach on a different topic and give feedback on the student's own draft, and may not author any part of it.

faqs.question: What does Diploma support cost per hour in the UAE market?
faqs.answer: As published in October 2026: Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget end; Unitors publishes IB from AED 200 for a qualified subject tutor online; TutorChase lists AED 270; BartyED lists AED 650 for premium named tutors. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 and specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 or above. Those are other providers' figures. IB Gram quotes per subject and per core component after a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Do we have to change school to change curriculum?
faqs.answer: Not always, and checking is worth real money. Several UAE schools and school groups run both an American-curriculum programme and the Diploma, sometimes on the same campus, which means a family can compare routes without also comparing two admissions processes and two sets of fees. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, within 16,846 new places, so the supply position is better than it was. Ask your current school's registrar before applying elsewhere.

faqs.question: Does a tutor come to our villa in Abu Dhabi or Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. UAE lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time slots. For this move it is the stronger arrangement anyway, because the useful tutor is one who can read a US transcript and a Diploma subject guide in the same conversation, and that is a narrow specialism rather than a local one. Market in-home rates run AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel priced inside them.

faqs.question: How many Higher Levels should a student from a US system take?
faqs.answer: Three is the standard requirement and three chosen by ambition rather than by need is the commonest expensive mistake. Higher Level sits near A Level depth, costs more per taught hour to support — published bands move from AED 150 to 250 for a qualified Standard Level tutor to AED 200 to 450 or above for a Higher Level specialist — and absorbs evenings. Choose the three that the intended programmes actually require, and let the other groups sit at Standard Level even where a student could manage more.

faqs.question: Will the mandatory UAE subjects affect a Diploma timetable?
faqs.answer: They occupy real timetable space whichever curriculum a Dubai school is licensed for. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided weekly totals are met, and KHDA advises at least 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. Factor those periods into the study time a six-subject grid leaves.

faqs.question: Is it too late to switch to the Diploma in Grade 11?
faqs.answer: DP1 is Grade 11, so entering at the start of Grade 11 is the normal point rather than a late one. Entering partway through DP1 is possible at some schools and hard, because internal assessment timelines and the core have already started. Entering in Grade 12 is not realistic for a full Diploma. If the family's position is that the US route is wrong but the timing has passed, the practical alternatives are individual Diploma course certificates, an AP route in the existing school, or deferring the change to university-level choices.

faqs.question: What should I ask before paying anyone for this transition?
faqs.answer: Five questions. Can you read both a US transcript and a Diploma subject guide, and what will you set my child to measure the gap? Is internal assessment supervision inside the quote, and exactly what will you do with a draft? How many sessions does this cover, over what period, towards which deadline? Is any examiner claim evidenced, and what do you say it gives access to — the correct answer is nothing about marking or boundaries. And will you tell me when to stop paying?

intro.heading: What a UAE family is actually choosing when it chooses a tutor
paragraphs: A search for the best IB home tutor in the UAE usually starts with a bad mock paper and a short list of names. The names are the easy part. What decides whether tuition works here is a set of decisions nobody in the family made: which curriculum the school is licensed to teach, which authority inspects it, which board enters the child for examinations, and which compulsory subjects sit on the timetable alongside the Diploma. Hire well and ignore those, and you have bought competent teaching aimed at the wrong target.

The UAE is unusual in how much of this sits above the school. Dubai's private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain answer to the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority. Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the federal Ministry of Education. Five bodies, seven emirates, and a family that moves house can change regulator without changing country.

That matters in a concrete way. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so what a child sits has been signed off locally as well as by the board. In Dubai, Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in every private school whatever curriculum it holds a licence for, and the Ministry controls the content used in them. An IB home tutor in Dubai who treats those lessons as spare revision time is working against the school's own licence rather than with it.

The second choice is format, and the honest answer there is narrow. Rates published by UAE providers put a tutor visiting a home at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the number, against roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject teacher working online. IB Gram delivers lessons one-to-one over live video only. Home visits are a service offered in India, not here. No IB Gram tutor attends a UAE address, and nothing on this page pretends otherwise.

What the online format buys is choice. A Higher Level Chemistry teacher who has taught the current scientific investigation criteria is scarce in any single emirate and scarcer still within a twenty-minute drive of one particular villa. Online IB tutoring in the UAE removes the radius and leaves the variables that actually move a grade: the right specialist, the right level, the right number of hours, and a schedule that survives the school run, prayer times and a shortened Ramadan day. The rest of this page is about what the system has already decided for you, and what it has left open.

best-ib-home-tutor.programmesIntro: The IB runs four programmes, and UAE schools licence them in different combinations. Knowing which one a child is in decides what tuition can usefully do, because the assessment model changes completely between them. Each note below says what the UAE school system adds on top of the IB's own requirements.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations. Learning is organised through transdisciplinary units of inquiry, and reporting is based on teacher judgement against the programme's learning outcomes rather than on marks. Support at this stage is about literacy, number fluency and the habits that make a Middle Years transition survivable: reading stamina, written structure, and comfort with being asked to explain a method rather than produce an answer.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, a PYP child already carries Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies on the timetable, streamed separately for Arab and non-Arab pupils. Families often discover the Arabic stream only when the first report arrives. Getting the stream right early is cheaper than correcting it in Year 7.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP is assessed against criteria lettered A to D in each subject, scored out of 8 per criterion, with grade boundaries applied to the total. Those letters are the grammar of the whole programme, and most lost marks come from writing an answer that never addresses the criterion being tested. Optional eAssessment in Year 11 gives an externally moderated result for schools that choose it.
programmes.countryNote: Several UAE schools run MYP to Year 9 then switch to IGCSE, which means a child can meet two assessment systems in three years. A Middle Years student heading for the Diploma in a UAE school needs the criterion habit intact; a child heading for IGCSE needs the opposite reflex, because mark schemes reward different things.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the core: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject is scored out of 7, with up to three further points from the combination of Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, to a maximum of 45. Twenty-four points is the pass threshold, subject to the IB's conditions on failing grades and core components.
programmes.countryNote: A UAE Diploma student carries the compulsory Ministry subjects on top of six IB courses, so the week is tighter than the IB's own guided-hours figures suggest. Registration for the session is made by the school, not the family, and the Diploma then needs a Ministry of Education equivalency file before it can be used for a UAE university application.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, plus a core of personal and professional skills, service learning, language development and a reflective project. It suits a student who wants Diploma-level subject rigour in two or three areas without the full six-subject load, and it is assessed through a mix of IB examinations and the career-related provider's own assessment.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is licensed by only a small number of UAE schools, so a family that wants it is usually choosing a school as much as a programme. Tuition for a CP student is normally concentrated on the Diploma courses inside it, because those carry the externally examined marks that universities read.

best-ib-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma courses UAE families most often ask about, with what each one actually assesses. The description matters more than the subject name: a tutor who knows Mathematics in general is not the same as one who knows where the Applications and Interpretation papers differ from Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency, calculus and proof, with a no-calculator paper at both levels. Higher Level adds depth across the same five topic areas and a third paper of extended problem-solving. Marks are lost in the move between a correct method and a justified conclusion, and in the exploration where modelling is left unexamined.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-assisted work, with a graphic display calculator permitted throughout. Higher Level adds matrices, graph theory and more demanding statistical inference. Students who chose this route to avoid proof are often surprised by how much interpretation of output the papers ask for in words rather than symbols.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, fields, waves and nuclear physics, with Higher Level extending the same chapters rather than adding separate ones. The scientific investigation and the data-based questions reward uncertainty handling, which is the single most commonly undertaught part of the course in a crowded UAE timetable.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity across organic, physical and inorganic topics, with multi-step calculation under time pressure. Higher Level work on organic mechanisms and energetics separates grades. The internal investigation asks for a research design that can actually be run, and weak designs cap the mark long before the data is analysed.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Unity and diversity, interaction and interdependence, across molecular to ecosystem scales. The volume of content tempts memorisation, but the papers reward applying a named mechanism to an unfamiliar context. Command terms do most of the damage here: outline, explain and justify ask for three different answers of three different lengths.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, assessed through extended response and a portfolio of three commentaries on published articles. Higher Level adds quantitative demands and a policy paper. Diagram accuracy is worth more than most students expect, and an unlabelled axis costs marks no amount of prose recovers.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Organisational structure, marketing, operations and finance, with case-study examinations and a written commentary. Tools are examined as analysis, not recall, so a student who can define a framework but cannot apply it to the case loses the top band. Financial calculation is the fastest place to recover marks before a session.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Non-literary and literary texts, assessed through guided analysis, a comparative essay, an individual oral and, at Higher Level, a separate essay on a studied work. Students who read well but write loosely sit in the middle bands; structure and a controlled line of inquiry move them up.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Receptive, productive and interactive skills across the IB's prescribed themes. For UAE families this course usually runs beside the school's own compulsory Arabic lessons, which follow Ministry content rather than the IB's. Keeping the two separate in a child's head is a real part of the work.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Systems fundamentals, computational thinking and a solution developed for a real client. Higher Level adds abstract data structures and a case study set annually. The solution component fails most often on documentation and testing evidence rather than on code, which is where a review session earns its fee.

best-ib-home-tutor.regionsTitle: Which authority sits above your child's school, emirate by emirate
best-ib-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Tuition plans in the UAE are shaped by the emirate more than by the neighbourhood, because the emirate decides who licenses, inspects and in some cases approves the assessment your child sits. Here is the practical position in each, with what it changes for a family buying private lessons.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The Knowledge and Human Development Authority oversees private education quality here and publishes the mandatory-subject requirements that apply whatever curriculum a school holds. With 227 private schools and 17 curricula in 2024-25, two children on the same street can sit entirely different papers.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and its professional-ethics rules for school staff bar paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. An IB Diploma tutor in Abu Dhabi should never be your child's own class teacher taking cash.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Al Ain sits under the same Abu Dhabi authority as the capital, but with a smaller IB cohort and fewer Higher Level sets per school. That is precisely the situation where a drive-time search returns a tutor for the subject you did not need and nobody for the one you did.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. An IB Higher Level tutor in Sharjah therefore works to a syllabus that has been cleared locally as well as by the board.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Private education here is regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which also approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. Families routinely drive to Dubai or Sharjah for subject help; over live video that drive stops being part of the cost of a Tuesday evening.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Ajman's private schools fall to the federal Ministry of Education, which supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Many Ajman Diploma students commute into Sharjah or Dubai for school, so a session rarely starts before 6pm on a weekday.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised federally by the Ministry of Education. The IB cohort is small enough that a single Higher Level option can run with a handful of students, which makes a specialist outside the emirate the realistic option rather than the fallback.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Supervised by the Ministry of Education, on the opposite coast from the Dubai school cluster. Nobody is driving a Physics Higher Level specialist over the mountains twice a week at a sensible price, which is the clearest case in the country for teaching live over video.

sections.heading: Best IB home tutor in the UAE: what is fixed, and what is actually yours to choose
paragraphs: Treat the search as a shortlist problem and you will compare the wrong things. Most of what determines whether a child's Diploma goes well was decided by an institution: the emirate regulator that licensed the school, the board that administers the papers, the Ministry rule that puts three extra subjects on the timetable, and the option blocks that decided which Higher Levels were even available. None of those move because a better tutor was hired.

What does move is the quality of the match inside those constraints. A family choosing between two tutors is really choosing between two levels of syllabus knowledge, two levels of honesty about availability, and two formats with very different time costs. Those are worth comparing carefully. Whether a tutor lives in Jumeirah or in Mumbai is worth almost nothing once the lesson is delivered live over video.

sections.heading: Four authorities sit above a single IB lesson in the UAE
paragraphs: A Diploma lesson in Dubai looks like a private arrangement between two people. It is not. Five separate bodies have a say in what is taught, when it is examined and who may be paid to teach it, and each of them publishes its position. A provider that cannot name them is telling you something about how closely it has read the market it sells into.

The federal position is the baseline everything else sits on: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That single sentence explains why an IB school in Ajman and a British school in Dubai both run the same three compulsory subjects, and why no international curriculum licence exempts a child from them.

Above the individual lesson sits the private tuition question. Paid private teaching in the UAE runs through the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure is quoted here. A parent may simply ask to see the permit before the first paid lesson.

sections.heading: A school sector adding places faster than it adds Higher Level teachers
paragraphs: The reason a Higher Level specialist is hard to book in a city this size is arithmetic rather than bad luck. Dubai's private sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with the UK curriculum at 37% of the roll, Indian at 26%, US at 14% and the International Baccalaureate at 7%. The Diploma is a minority programme inside a very large market.

The sector is also growing. Six new private schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. The 2026-27 intake adds seven more, four following the UK curriculum and three the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. Three additional IB schools is good news for choice and awkward news for staffing, because experienced Higher Level teachers in the harder sciences and mathematics are the scarcest item in the system and new schools recruit from the same pool everybody else does.

Cost context has moved in the opposite direction. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. A family's tutoring budget is not being compressed by a fee rise this year, which makes the planning question how to spend it well rather than whether to spend at all. The sensible move in a tightening staff market is to book the scarce subject early and treat the easier ones as the flexible part of the plan, rather than the other way round.

sections.heading: The subjects on the timetable that a private tutor may not redesign
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are not optional extras in a Dubai private school. They are mandatory regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. For a Diploma student that means three courses running beside six IB subjects and the core.

What surprises families is how prescriptive the rules are. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies for Arab students runs primarily in Arabic; non-Arabs are taught Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Two further rules constrain what any outside tutor can honestly offer. Schools must ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, and for the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. A tutor who arrives with a worksheet pack of their own for these courses is not adding value; they are working outside the rule the school has to follow. Instructional time, meanwhile, is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with lesson length allowed to vary provided the weekly total is met and at least 25 minutes advised for any mandatory-subject lesson.

paragraphs: Parents type home tutor because that is what the market has sold for twenty years in this region, and the phrase still describes the thing being bought: private, one-to-one teaching organised around the family's week rather than the school's. What has changed is that the delivery no longer requires somebody in the car. IB Gram delivers this as live one-to-one online tuition to families in all seven emirates, and home visits are a service offered in India only.

Said plainly: no IB Gram tutor attends an address in the UAE, in any emirate, at any price. That is a product decision and it has reasons a parent can check. A visiting tutor is selected from whoever teaches the subject within a tolerable drive; an online specialist is selected from everybody who has taught that syllabus at that level. For Higher Level sciences and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, those two pools are not close in size.

The time arithmetic is the other half of it. A visiting tutor usually needs a two-hour minimum because the travel has to be worth the trip, which forces a weekday session that starts late and ends later. A 60 or 90-minute video session fits between the school bus and dinner, survives a traffic day, and can move to a post-Iftar slot during Ramadan without anybody renegotiating a driving route. Below are the AED bands actually published by providers selling into this market, read in October 2026, with the source named in every row. These are market rates, not an IB Gram price list.

Read the bands as descriptions of what is inside the hour rather than as quality tiers. The low band usually buys supervised homework from someone with a good recent grade in the subject. The middle band usually buys a teacher who knows the paper structure and the mark scheme's language. The upper bands buy scarcity: a Higher Level specialist in a thin subject, or short-notice work in an exam term. Travel is the single biggest reason an in-home rate sits above an online one for the same teacher.

Monthly packages are where the arithmetic gets slippery. sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level, and the hours each one actually needs
paragraphs: The level decision does more to a tutoring budget than the choice of tutor does, and it is usually made in a rush during an option-block meeting. The IB publishes guided teaching hours of 150 for a Standard Level course and 240 for a Higher Level one. That ninety-hour gap is roughly a term and a half of classroom time, which is why a student who switches up late cannot be caught up by six weeks of private lessons, however good they are.

Points behave differently from how families expect. Every subject is scored out of 7 whether it is taken at Higher or Standard Level, with up to three further points available from the combination of Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. Moving a struggling Higher Level down to Standard does not cost points directly. What it changes is which university courses will accept the profile afterwards, which is a question for the named university's own entry page rather than for a tutor.

Where tutoring earns its place is after the level is locked. Higher Level work is topic-specific: the extra material in a Higher Level science is depth inside the same chapters rather than separate units, so general revision does very little and targeted teaching does a lot. Standard Level students more often need exam technique, command-term discipline and timing, because the content load is manageable and the marks are lost in how answers are written rather than in what the student knows.

sections.heading: What each piece of internally assessed work is allowed to be
paragraphs: Internally assessed components are where a tutoring relationship either proves itself or becomes a liability for the student. The limits are published in the subject guides and they are limits, not targets: an Extended Essay stops at 4,000 words, a Theory of Knowledge essay at 1,600 on a prescribed title. Markers stop reading at the limit, so a student who writes past it has thrown away the best part of their argument.

Those limits move between syllabus versions, and a page that publishes them as permanent facts will eventually be wrong. Treat the table below as a working reference and confirm each figure against the current subject guide through your child's coordinator, who holds the version the school is actually teaching. The marks matter as much as the word counts. The Mathematics exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria lettered A to E: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. The sciences investigation is marked out of 24 across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Students lose most of their marks in the criteria that reward thinking about the work rather than doing it.

The boundary is simple to state and the thing most essay-selling competitors ignore. A tutor may discuss a research question, teach the criterion a student keeps missing, read one draft and give written feedback the student then acts on, and teach referencing properly. A tutor may not choose the topic, supply paragraphs, process the data or edit a draft to a finished state. Your child's coordinator has to declare what outside help was used, and that declaration must be accurate. IB Gram works only on the teaching side of that line, and the most useful thing a provider can do for a worried parent is say so in writing before any money changes hands.

sections.heading: Who owns each deadline in the exam year
paragraphs: Almost every date that matters in an exam year belongs to somebody other than the parent, and the most expensive mistakes are administrative rather than academic. The pattern is easiest to see in a published Cambridge series. For the March 2027 series, the examination period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, but final entries are due on 27 November 2026 and forecast grades on 27 February 2027. Results reach centres through Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June.

Read that sequence backwards and the planning becomes obvious. The entry deadline sits more than two months before the first paper, which means tier and subject decisions have to be settled in the autumn term, while the mocks that justify a forecast grade have to be sat and marked before late February. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the school which zone it sits in, in writing.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November series, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Because Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, always work from the live official PDF rather than a date copied onto a tutoring page. IGCSE exam entry deadlines in the UAE are set by the board and submitted by the school as examination centre, never by the family. For the IB's own session dates we publish nothing: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so ask your child's coordinator and work from what the school confirms in writing.

sections.heading: Equivalency and attestation: what the Ministry counts, and the number nobody should invent
paragraphs: A Diploma or a set of IGCSEs is not automatically usable for a UAE university application. The Ministry of Education runs an equivalency route that converts a foreign secondary certificate into something UAE institutions recognise, and the requirements differ by curriculum. For the British track, students must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3.

Two details inside that rule are routinely got wrong by pages ranking for these queries. The first is the subject count: the reported requirement is five accredited subjects, and at least one page ranking for UAE tutoring queries tells parents it is six. The second is what counts towards the five: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. On the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying.

For MoE equivalency for IB students there is a deliberate blank on this page. The reporting we have read does not state an IB points threshold, and no figure should be published without reading it on moe.gov.ae or the emirate's own attestation channel. Nor is equivalency something a tutoring company performs or influences. It is a process a family completes with the Ministry, using documents the school issues. What tuition can legitimately do is prepare a child for the standardised tests the American track asks for, and make sure the certificate arriving in June is one worth attesting.

The useful thing a provider can tell a parent is where it runs out, because a wasted trial lesson in an exam term costs more than the lesson. Our position on availability is published rather than implied, and it is the same whether you are in Dubai Marina or Dibba.

Supply is shaped by the same thing that shapes everything else here: cohort size. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, we match a Diploma teacher from our India-based teaching team, delivered over the same live video format, and we say that at the point of matching rather than after the first invoice. The syllabus, the board and the criteria do not change with the teacher's time zone; the session time sometimes does.
