sections.heading: Who presses the entry button, and the months between that click and paper one
paragraphs: Parents consistently assume the exam entry is an administrative formality the school handles. It is handled by the school, but it is a decision with a deadline, and the deadline sits far earlier than most families expect. For the March 2027 series Cambridge published a final entry date of 27 November 2026 against an exam period beginning 3 February 2027. That is roughly ten weeks of gap, and inside those ten weeks the tier, the components and the subject list are fixed.

The table below names the step, the timing, and the person who actually performs it, because the commonest failure in this process is a step that everybody assumed someone else owned. A parent cannot submit an entry. A school cannot request a review of marking without instruction. A student cannot add extra time to their own paper in March. Knowing the owner of each step is what turns a deadline into a task.

One row needs stating twice. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable version for each, and the board states plainly that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. A family that downloads a timetable from a search result rather than from the exams officer has created a real risk for no reason. Ask the centre which zone it sits in and use that version only.

The same logic applies to Pearson Edexcel entries, which run on their own calendar. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, which is precisely why any session table should link the live official timetable rather than restate dates that can be revised.

sections.heading: Sitting Cambridge IGCSE as a private candidate in the UAE
paragraphs: A growing number of UAE families are not on a school roll for every subject. Some are home educating, some have moved mid-year and cannot get a seat, some want one extra subject their school does not teach, and some are repeating a single paper. All of them become a Cambridge IGCSE private candidate, and that status changes what can be entered rather than what can be learned.

The mechanics are straightforward but they are nobody's job but yours. You find a centre in the UAE that accepts private candidates for your syllabus, you register with that centre, and the centre makes the entry on your behalf by the board's final entry deadline. Centres set their own internal cut-offs weeks before the board's, charge their own administration fees, and decide which components they are able to offer. That last point is the one that catches families out.

Practical components are the usual sticking point. A laboratory test needs apparatus, a supervisor and a session slot, so most centres enter private candidates for the alternative-to-practical paper instead, which assesses the same experimental thinking on paper. Coursework options are often unavailable to private candidates altogether, with the centre entering the externally assessed alternative where the syllabus provides one. None of this is a barrier to a strong grade, but all of it has to be confirmed with the centre in writing before the entry goes in, not assumed from a syllabus document.

What online tuition does for a private candidate is supply the structure a school would otherwise impose. There is no scheme of work, no mock timetable and no teacher chasing a deadline, so the weekly session carries all of that as well as the teaching. In practice that means a written plan with dates, work set and marked every week, and a mock run at home under real timing in January because nobody else is going to run one.

sections.heading: Gulf Standard Time is the scheduling asset, not the workaround
paragraphs: Online tutoring is usually sold on tutor choice and priced on convenience. In the UAE the real advantage is narrower and more useful: the clock. Gulf Standard Time sits four hours ahead of UTC, which puts the UAE after-school window squarely inside the working afternoon of tutor pools across South Asia and the early morning of Europe. A family in Fujairah and a family in Jumeirah are choosing from the same pool at 17:00, and neither is choosing from whoever happens to live within twenty minutes.

That matters most in exam term, when slots stop being interchangeable. A 16:30 session and a 20:30 session are different products. One is for teaching new content to a student who can still concentrate; the other is for marking a paper the student sat that afternoon, and it is appropriate for a Year 11 in April and nobody else. Booking the wrong slot and then concluding that online tuition does not work for your child is a common and avoidable mistake.

The table below is what UAE families actually book, with the honest cost of each slot alongside it. Two entries exist for narrow reasons. The exam-morning session is only useful to a student who is already prepared and wants a formula check and a first-question routine; for an unprepared student it does harm. The Ramadan post-Iftar slot works well for Year 11 and badly for Year 9, and it is worth deciding which your child is before committing to a month of late sessions.

The scheduling asset also survives disruption, which is the part families only appreciate once. A session attached to a place dies when the family travels, when the mock timetable moves, or when a road closes. A session attached to a time moves by message and keeps its place in the plan.

sections.heading: What the weekly hour is doing in each of the three UAE terms
paragraphs: The UAE academic year splits into three unequal terms and the weekly hour should not be doing the same job in all three. The first term runs from late August or early September to mid-December and it is the longest clear teaching stretch of the year. This is where content gaps get closed, because there is enough runway for a topic taught properly in October to be consolidated in November and revisited in December. Families who wait until term two to start have given this away.

Term two runs from January to late March and it opens with the mock. The hour's job changes from teaching content to converting a marked paper into a revised plan, then working through components under timing. Coursework deadlines land in this term, and so does the forecast-grade request, which means the teacher's view of your child is being formed and recorded in exactly these weeks. It is also the term Ramadan falls in for the next several years, so the real teaching time inside it is shorter than the calendar suggests.

Term three is short, runs from April to the papers, and should contain no new content at all. The hour becomes a past-paper clinic: sit a component, mark it live against the published mark scheme wording, identify the two or three recurring losses, and drill only those. Students want to revise what they enjoy; the hour exists to make them revise what they are losing marks on. By the final fortnight the sessions get shorter and more frequent, aimed at the next paper on the timetable rather than at the subject as a whole.

Across all three terms the delivery is identical: one-to-one over live video, same slot, same tutor. What changes is the agenda, and a tutor who runs term three the way they ran term one has not been reading the calendar.

sections.heading: Before the clock starts: Checkpoint, the Year 9 option block and the choices that price the next two years
paragraphs: Most tutoring enquiries arrive in Year 11. The decisions that determine how hard Year 11 will be are taken in Year 9, usually between January and March, on a form that goes home with three days' notice. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests sit just before that, in test windows Cambridge offers in March, May and October, and they produce externally marked data in English, mathematics and science that the school uses when it advises on tier and set.

Four choices on that option form have consequences a family can feel two years later. The maths route decides whether your child meets Mathematics 0580 or International Mathematics 0607, which are different courses with different calculator assumptions and different onward fit. The English choice between First Language English 0500 and English as a Second Language 0510 or 0511 changes how the grade is read by universities and by some official processes. The tier indication decides whether the top grades are available at all. And the Arabic stream is set by the school under KHDA rules, which require separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes for both groups strictly prohibited.

What online tuition is for at this stage is not remediation. It is one or two sessions that tell a family what the form actually means, followed, if useful, by a light fortnightly hour in Year 9 to make a borderline Extended entry safe rather than brave. That is a much cheaper intervention than a crash block in Year 11 to rescue a tier the child was never ready for.
The table sets out each stage, when it runs and what it fixes. Treat the last column as the planning column: those are the things that become expensive to change later.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and a revision block that arrives earlier every year
paragraphs: The Hijri year is about eleven days shorter than the Gregorian one, so Ramadan moves earlier each year against the school calendar. For UAE families on a Cambridge timetable that drift has a specific consequence: Ramadan has walked out of the summer holidays and into the revision term, and for the next several years it will sit across February and March, which is exactly where the mock aftermath, the coursework deadlines and the start of serious past-paper work all live.

Schools shorten the day during Ramadan, which sounds like more study time and usually is not. An earlier finish moves the whole afternoon forward while energy levels move the other way, and the hours between late afternoon and Iftar are the least productive of the day for a fasting teenager. Families who try to keep a 17:00 session through Ramadan generally lose three or four weeks of real teaching and conclude that the tutoring stopped working.

The practical answer is to move rather than to pause. Sessions shift to post-Iftar, typically 21:00 to 22:00, where a Year 11 student is genuinely alert and the hour is worth having. Some families prefer a late-morning weekend block instead. Eid then takes a clean week out of the calendar, and the honest planning move is to write it off in advance rather than to schedule sessions that will be cancelled. A plan with Eid removed and post-Iftar slots agreed in January is a plan that survives March.

Because the sessions are delivered over live video, none of this requires renegotiating travel. The slot moves, the tutor is still the same tutor, and the plan keeps its continuity through the month that most disrupts a UAE revision timetable.

sections.heading: What the UAE market charges for Cambridge IGCSE tuition, and what each figure leaves out
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranked pages in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family transacts in. The table below is therefore more useful than it is sophisticated: it is the market, in AED, with every figure attributed to whoever published it and the month it was read. These are market rates, not IB Gram's price list. Our own quote follows the free trial session and the subject, tier and series are what move it.

Read the table with two cautions. The first is that an hourly rate is not a cost per taught minute. A visiting tutor's rate covers travel that the student does not spend learning, and a session that starts twenty-five minutes late because of traffic has a different effective cost from the one advertised. The second is that the cheapest tier in the table is largely university students, which can be exactly right for Year 9 consolidation and exactly wrong for an Extended entry eight weeks from a paper.

Timing moves the number as well. Demand concentrates in the eight weeks before a series and in the fortnight after a January mock, and specialist availability in a narrow subject tightens first. A family that books a Computer Science 0478 specialist in September pays the normal rate and gets the slot they want; the same family in April is choosing from whoever is left. The calendar is a pricing document as much as a planning one.

On context, Dubai school fees are a reasonable anchor. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. A tutoring budget set against a flat fee year is a different conversation from one set against a rising one.

sections.heading: A tutor who drives to a UAE address against a specialist on a screen, tested across one exam term
paragraphs: The fair way to compare the two models is not in the abstract. It is to take one Cambridge exam term, week by week, and ask what each model does when that week happens. Most of the year the two look similar. The differences appear exactly when the stakes are highest, which is the only time they matter.

A visiting tutor is a real service with real advantages, and families choose it for good reasons: a younger child who needs a physical presence, a parent who wants the session happening in the next room, a household where screens are already a battleground. Nobody should pretend those reasons are imaginary. The honest statement is simply this: IB Gram does not provide that service anywhere in the UAE. We deliver one-to-one tuition over live video, and the comparison below is why we think that trade is a good one in an exam year rather than a compromise.

The row that decides it for most families is the syllabus-code row. In the final weeks before a paper, the question is not whether the tutor is present but whether the tutor knows what Paper 4 asks for in that specific code. For Mathematics 0580 or Chemistry 0620 in Dubai there may well be someone excellent nearby. For Computer Science 0478 in Ajman, or Additional Mathematics 0606 in Fujairah, the local pool is often empty, and a screen is the difference between a specialist and nobody.

The second deciding row is disruption. Across one exam term a UAE family will usually hit a moved mock timetable, a shortened Ramadan school day, a half-term abroad and at least one week of genuine traffic chaos. A session attached to a time absorbs all four. A session attached to a place loses several of them.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and who permits the tutor
paragraphs: Five bodies regulate private schools in the UAE and most tutoring pages mention none of them. Dubai sits with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah the Department of Knowledge, both of which regulate private education and approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah fall to the federal Ministry of Education.

That matters to a tutoring plan in a way parents rarely anticipate, because the regulator decides what is already in the week. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but they must follow the ministry's general regulations, and KHDA's mandatory-subject requirements set instructional time calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, with the advice that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least twenty-five minutes. Those lessons are not optional and they are not negotiable, so a Cambridge revision plan has to fit around them rather than over them.

The tutor side is governed separately. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so no figure should be quoted at you by anybody.

Two honesty notes. IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson, and any page that implies otherwise is misleading you. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific instrument issued to training institutes with premises and staff in Dubai, and we do not hold one because we do not operate premises in the UAE. And in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules have been reported as barring private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, so asking your child's own teacher for paid sessions is a question to raise with the school rather than with us.

sections.heading: Results in August, and the five decisions that close before term starts
paragraphs: Results day feels like the end of the process and is actually the start of a short, dense window in which five decisions have to be taken. Boards release to centres before candidates: Pearson's June 2026 International GCSE results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge publishes results for the March series on Cambridge International Direct in mid-May with certificates following in late June. Knowing both dates for your series means nobody in the family is refreshing a page on the wrong day.

The first task is clerical and it takes twenty minutes. Read the statement of results against the statement of entry, subject by subject and component by component. Check that every entry appears, that the tier is the one sat, and that no component is recorded as absent. Errors are uncommon and they are also the only category of problem that is easy to fix, provided somebody looks.

Then come the decisions with deadlines. A review of marking has to be requested through the centre, on the family's written instruction, within a window the board sets for each series and which closes quickly. A resit entry for the next series has to be made before that series' final entry deadline, which for a November series follows results closely. The Ministry of Education equivalency file should be opened as soon as certificates are issued rather than when a university asks, and the British-track requirement is five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among the five, plus one subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary at the same grade. One ranking competitor states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced rule is five.

IB Gram does not perform equivalency or attestation and does not guarantee any outcome in that process, and no tutoring is required for it. We describe the route, name the authority and point you to the official channel. The useful thing a single session can do in that fortnight is read the results properly with the student and decide, calmly, whether a remark, a resit or an AS subject change is the right move.

sections.heading: Coursework, practical write-ups and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: This market contains providers who sell finished assessed work. One of them advertises completed Internal Assessments at a published price. For a Cambridge candidate the equivalent offer is help with a coursework component or a practical write-up, and accepting it puts the student's entry at risk for every subject, not just the one involved. It is worth being explicit about where the line sits, because vagueness here is how families end up on the wrong side of it by accident.

What a tutor may do is substantial. They may teach the skills the component assesses, explain what each published criterion is asking for in plain language, discuss a student's plan and ask the questions that expose a weak argument, read a draft the student has written and say which criterion is not yet met and why, model the technique on a different example, and mark practice work against the mark scheme. All of that is teaching and all of it is what an hour should be used for in the weeks before a submission deadline.

What a tutor may not do is write, rewrite, dictate, restructure or supply any part of the work that is submitted. Not a paragraph, not a conclusion, not a method section, not an improved version to copy from. The student's submitted work has to be the student's own, and a school signs a declaration to that effect. If any tutor or service offers you otherwise, the risk sits entirely with your child, which is reason enough to walk away from it.

For practical components the same boundary applies in a different shape. A tutor can teach experimental design, how to tabulate results, how to plot and read a graph, how to discuss sources of error and how to propose improvements in the language the mark scheme rewards. They cannot produce data, invent results or complete a write-up. On the alternative-to-practical paper none of that is even relevant, which is one practical reason the paper suits an online candidate: everything it tests is teachable over video and none of it is work that must be submitted.

process.title: Send the syllabus code, the tier and the series
process.description: Three facts get the match right on the first attempt. If you do not have them, the school's option sheet or the statement of entry carries all three, and a photograph of either is enough. Without them an enquiry becomes a conversation about subjects in general, which wastes a week neither of us has in exam term.

process.title: A free first session on a question that went wrong
process.description: One session of about forty-five minutes, at no charge, one per student, booked before any payment is taken and with no card required first. It runs on a real past-paper question from your child's own syllabus rather than a general assessment, because watching an attempt tells a tutor what a score cannot.

process.title: A written plan counted backwards from your series date
process.description: After the trial you get the plan in writing: the component weaknesses found, what the weekly hour will do for the next six weeks, and the board date it is aimed at. If the available time is too short for the goal, the plan says so. A plan that only works if nothing goes wrong is not a plan.

process.title: Weekly one-to-one on a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot
process.description: Same tutor, same slot, one-to-one over live video. Work is set between sessions and marked at the start of the next one. The slot can move for Ramadan, travel or a mock timetable change, because nothing in the arrangement depends on anybody being in a particular building.

process.title: A replan at the mock, and an honest answer on availability
process.description: The January mock rewrites the plan rather than confirming it. And if no specialist covers your child's syllabus code and tier at the slot you need, we say so rather than substituting a generalist. Sometimes that means a different slot; sometimes it means we are not the right answer for that subject.

whyPoints.title: The plan starts from a board date
whyPoints.description: Every plan names the series, the final entry deadline and the submission windows it is working towards, taken from Cambridge's or Pearson's own published pages. A tutoring arrangement with no date attached to it cannot tell you whether six weeks is enough, which is the only question a parent in February actually has.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the syllabus code, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: Mathematics 0580 and International Mathematics 0607 are different courses. So are Physics 0625 and the equivalent Pearson code. Because lessons are delivered over live video, the tutor is chosen for the code your child sits rather than for proximity, which is the whole argument for a narrow entry like Computer Science 0478.

whyPoints.title: Every figure attributed, every date sourced
whyPoints.description: The AED ranges on this page name the provider who published them and the month they were read. Board dates are quoted from Cambridge and Pearson key-dates pages. Regulatory statements come from u.ae, KHDA and MoHRE. Nothing here asks you to take a number on trust, and you can check any of it.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach the skills a coursework component assesses, explain the published criteria and give written feedback on a student's own draft. They do not write, rewrite or supply any part of what is submitted. In a market where completed assessed work is openly sold, that boundary is worth stating rather than assuming.

whyPoints.title: No accreditation claimed that we do not hold
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no premises in the UAE. We name those bodies to explain what they govern. Any provider implying endorsement by one of them is telling you something that is not true.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated before you commit
whyPoints.description: Subject and tier coverage is finite, and it tightens in the eight weeks before a series. You are told what is available at your slot before any money changes hands, including when the honest answer is that the specialist you need is not free until a later slot or a later term.

faqs.question: We are starting online lessons in November for a June Cambridge series. How is the year divided up?
faqs.answer: Roughly into three unequal blocks. November to mid-December is the last clear teaching stretch, so it goes on content gaps. January opens with the mock, and the fortnight after it is spent converting the marked papers into a revised plan, then working component by component. From April there should be no new content at all: full papers under real timing, marked live, with drilling only on the recurring losses. Allow for Ramadan and Eid taking real teaching weeks out of February and March, and plan the session slot shift before it arrives rather than after.

faqs.question: Can my son sit Cambridge IGCSE exams in the UAE if he is taught entirely online?
faqs.answer: Yes. Teaching and assessment are separate things. Lessons can be delivered one-to-one over live video from anywhere, but the papers are sat in person at an exam centre, on the timetable for that centre's administrative zone. If your son is on a school roll, the school is the centre and handles the entry. If he is not, you register him with a UAE centre that accepts private candidates for his syllabus, and the centre makes the entry before the board's final entry deadline. Confirm which components that centre can offer before you commit to the entry.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge components can a private candidate in the UAE not enter?
faqs.answer: It depends on the centre rather than on the board alone, which is why this has to be asked in writing before entry. In practice, laboratory practical tests are rarely available to private candidates because they need the centre's apparatus and a supervisor, so centres usually enter the alternative-to-practical paper instead. Coursework options are often unavailable, with the externally assessed alternative entered where the syllabus provides one. Speaking components in language syllabuses vary centre by centre. Written theory and multiple-choice papers are entered exactly as they are for a school candidate.

faqs.question: Does an online tutor work on Gulf Standard Time, or do we fit around another country's clock?
faqs.answer: Sessions are scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, which is four hours ahead of UTC. That is not a courtesy, it is what makes the model work: the UAE after-school window sits inside the working afternoon of large tutor pools and the early morning of Europe, so a 16:30 or 18:30 slot draws on a genuinely wide pool. The slot is yours and it is fixed week to week. It moves when you need it to move, for Ramadan, for travel or for a mock timetable change, and the tutor stays the same tutor through all of it.

faqs.question: What time of day do UAE families usually book a Cambridge IGCSE online lesson?
faqs.answer: The 16:30 to 18:00 window is the most requested across the emirates and it books out first once exam term starts. Dubai families whose school finishes by 14:45 and who are not on a long bus route often take 15:30 instead, which is the better slot for new content. Abu Dhabi and Sharjah families usually need 18:30 or later once the commute is accounted for. Late slots around 20:30 suit Year 11 students in revision term for marking a paper sat earlier that day, and suit nobody else.

faqs.question: Is the Cambridge November series a sensible first entry rather than a resit?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking the school rather than assuming. Cambridge runs June and November series for IGCSE, so a student who is clearly ready in one or two subjects can sit those earlier and reduce the load in the main series. The arithmetic to check is whether the content will genuinely be finished and whether the earlier entry costs revision time for subjects staying in June. The decision belongs to the centre, and it has to be taken before that series' final entry deadline, which arrives earlier than families expect.

faqs.question: How does an online tutor teach a Cambridge practical paper without a laboratory bench?
faqs.answer: Because the paper most online candidates sit is the alternative-to-practical, which assesses experimental thinking on paper rather than manual technique. That means reading apparatus diagrams, designing a fair test, tabulating results with correct units and significant figures, plotting and interpreting graphs, identifying sources of error and proposing improvements in the language the mark scheme rewards. All of it is teachable over video with the paper on screen. Where a student is entered for the laboratory test instead, the practical handling has to be practised at school and the tutor works on the recording and reasoning around it.

faqs.question: Our school runs mocks in January. What should we do with the grade that comes back?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a diagnostic, not a verdict. The useful information is not the grade but the distribution of lost marks: which component, which question type, and whether the loss came from not knowing the content, answering a different question from the one asked, or running out of time. Ask for the marked script rather than the grade, and have it read question by question. The mock is also the last point at which a plan can be rebuilt with enough runway for the rebuild to change the June outcome, so the fortnight after it matters more than the mock itself.

faqs.question: Our daughter is in Year 9. Is it too early to book online Cambridge lessons?
faqs.answer: It is the cheapest point to intervene, which is the opposite of too early. Year 9 is when the option form is signed, and the maths route, the English route and the tier indication all get set there. One or two sessions that explain what the form actually commits her to are worth more than a crash block two years later. If a borderline Extended entry is in question, a light fortnightly hour through Year 9 makes that entry safe rather than brave. That is a much smaller intervention than rescuing a tier she was never ready for.

faqs.question: Do Cambridge Checkpoint results in Year 9 matter once the IGCSE course starts?
faqs.answer: They are not certificated and no university will ask for them, but they are used. Cambridge offers Lower Secondary Checkpoint test windows in March, May and October, and the externally marked results in English, mathematics and science give a department an outside reference point when it advises on set and tier. A family who sees the tier advice without seeing the Checkpoint data behind it is being asked to accept a conclusion without the evidence. Ask for the subject breakdown, not just the overall score, because the per-strand detail is where the teaching decision actually sits.

faqs.question: Ramadan falls across our revision block. How do online sessions move?
faqs.answer: They move rather than pause. The Hijri year is about eleven days shorter than the Gregorian one, so Ramadan has drifted out of the summer holidays and into the revision term, where it now sits across the mock aftermath and the start of past-paper work. Schools shorten the day, and the hours before Iftar are the least productive of the day for a fasting teenager. Most families shift the session to roughly 21:00 to 22:00 post-Iftar, or to a late weekend morning block. Eid is best written off in the plan in advance.

faqs.question: What is the going online rate for one Cambridge IGCSE subject in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Market rates, as published by the providers themselves and read in October 2026: budget online tutoring from around AED 45 to 150 an hour, a qualified subject tutor online roughly AED 150 to 300, and an IGCSE or A Level specialist around AED 200 to 450 and above, with premium examiner-marketed tutors quoted at AED 650. Monthly packages around AED 799 for eight online sessions appear across the market. Those are other providers' figures, not ours. IB Gram quotes after the free trial session, against the subject, tier and series.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Cambridge tutor to an address in Dubai or Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. All UAE tuition is delivered one-to-one over live video, on a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot. The visiting model is something we run in India only, and claiming otherwise on a UAE page would be promising something we do not sell. The search phrase stays honest because the need behind it is real: one-to-one attention on your child's own syllabus. What changes is the delivery, and what you gain is a tutor chosen for the syllabus code rather than for the drive time, plus a session that survives traffic, travel and a moved mock timetable.

faqs.question: How long does matching with a Cambridge specialist take before an entry deadline closes?
faqs.answer: For common codes such as Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625 or Chemistry 0620, a trial session is usually arranged within a few days. Narrow entries take longer: Computer Science 0478, Additional Mathematics 0606 or a less common language can take a week or more, and availability tightens sharply in the eight weeks before a series. The honest planning rule is to start the search when you read the statement of entry rather than after the mock. If nobody suitable is free at your slot, we say so instead of substituting a generalist.

faqs.question: What happens to weekly online lessons when the family travels during February half-term?
faqs.answer: They continue if you want them to, from wherever the family is, on the same slot or a shifted one. This is the practical difference between a session attached to a time and a session attached to a place. February half-term lands in the middle of the most important revision stretch of the Cambridge year, and losing a fortnight there is expensive. Some families keep one session a week while travelling and skip the set work; others keep the full pattern. Both are better than a cancelled block, and the decision is yours.

faqs.question: Where is the line between coaching a Cambridge coursework component and doing it for a student?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the skills the component assesses, explain each published criterion in plain language, question a plan until its weak points show, read a draft the student has written and name the criterion that is not yet met, model the technique on a different example, and mark practice work against the mark scheme. A tutor may not write, rewrite, dictate, restructure or supply any part of what is submitted. The submitted work has to be the student's own and the school signs a declaration saying so. Any provider offering otherwise is putting your child's entry at risk.

faqs.question: When should a UAE family open the Ministry of Education equivalency file?
faqs.answer: As soon as certificates are issued, not when a university asks for the attestation. On the British track the sourced requirement is five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus one subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary at the same grade. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject rule; the sourced figure is five. IB Gram does not perform or guarantee equivalency. Verify current requirements on the ministry's own channel.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education need their own hour beside a Cambridge timetable?
faqs.answer: They already have hours inside the school week, and that is the planning point. Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed curriculum, and KHDA sets mandatory-subject instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit, advising that any such lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. So a Cambridge revision plan has less unallocated time than the timetable appears to show, and the weekly hour has to be placed accordingly.

cambridge-igcse-online-tutor.closingHeading: Start from the date, then decide about the hours
cambridge-igcse-online-tutor.closingBody: Send three things and this becomes a short conversation: the syllabus codes on your child's option sheet or statement of entry, the tier for each one, and the series they are entered for. From those we work backwards to what is genuinely available between now and the papers, and the free first session runs on a real question from that syllabus rather than a general assessment. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on a Gulf Standard Time slot you choose, anywhere from Dubai to Umm Al Quwain. If the time left is too short for the goal, the plan will say so before you pay for anything.

intro.heading: The Cambridge year is already timetabled, so start from the dates
paragraphs: A parent searching for a Cambridge IGCSE tutor in the UAE almost always has a trigger: a mock script that came back two grades down, a report that says working below expectation, or a statement of entry covered in numbers nobody at home recognises. The first useful thing to know is that the year is already timetabled. Cambridge publishes the series, the school submits the entries, the centre is allocated a timetable zone, and a subject teacher will write a forecast grade on a date the school has already chosen. Tuition works inside that frame or it works badly.

So this page is organised by date rather than by promise. It walks a Cambridge series backwards, from the first paper to the week the entries closed, and it names what can still be changed at each point along the way. It uses the board's published key dates for the March 2027 series as the worked example, because those dates are documented and because the fourteen-week gap between the final entry deadline and the first paper is the fact most families in this market discover far too late to use.

The second thing this page does is translate. Syllabus codes such as 0580 and 0625 are not labels; they describe which questions appear and in what form. Component numbers tell you which papers are sat and therefore which technique matters. Core and Extended are different papers with different grade ranges, not two speeds of one course. A parent who can read those three things can judge for themselves whether a tutor knows the course, which is a better filter than any marketing page, this one included.

Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, to families anywhere in the Emirates. IB Gram does not operate a visiting-tutor service in the UAE; that is offered only in India. The reason to prefer the online format here is not cost. It is that a Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 Extended entry needs someone who teaches the supplement content and the alternative to practical paper, and in Al Ain, Ajman or Fujairah that person is unlikely to live twenty minutes from your door.

What follows is specific on purpose. There are AED figures taken from published market sources with the month they were read, a command-word table that explains why a student who knows the content still lands on a grade 5, the KHDA rules covering the three mandatory UAE subjects, the permit a private tutor must hold, and a plain account of what a tutor may and may not touch on an assessed piece. Where a figure could not be sourced from a document anyone can open and check for themselves, it is simply not on the page at all.

Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable

Published UAE rates for secondary tuition run from about AED 45 to AED 650 an hour, depending on the provider model

cambridge-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Cambridge runs a continuous route from Year 7 to Year 13, and the decisions taken at each stage narrow the next one. These are the four stages UAE families ask about, with what each one actually commits a student to and where it bites locally.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, assessed by Checkpoint tests in English, mathematics and science. Checkpoint is diagnostic rather than a certificate, and the scores are the clearest early evidence a school uses when it decides tier placement for Year 10. Work at this stage is about closing arithmetic and writing gaps while they are still cheap to close.
programmes.countryNote: UAE centres run Checkpoint in March, May or October. Families arriving from an Indian or American curriculum often meet it in their first term here, and a weak paper in a subject the student has simply never been taught gets misread as ability rather than coverage.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Core tier
programmes.description: The Core components of a tiered syllabus, taught over two years and examined in a single series. Core content is a subset of the full syllabus and only the lower part of the grade scale is available. It is the right entry for a student who needs accuracy and security rather than reach, and the sensible target is the top of that range.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE a Core entry quietly becomes a sixth-form question, because published entry grades for AS Level courses often sit above the Core ceiling. Raise it with the school in the autumn of Year 11, with marked Extended-style work in hand, not in the spring once the entry has gone.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Extended tier
programmes.description: Core plus supplement content, examined on the Extended components, with the full grade range available including the top grades. The supplement is not harder versions of the same questions; it is additional material, and it is usually the part a student who has been coasting has never met. Hours here go to the supplement and to the long structured questions.
programmes.countryNote: This is the common entry at UK-curriculum schools across Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah. The failure mode is an Extended entry defended against the school's evidence, where marks leak across the whole paper instead of being banked at the top of the lower tier.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The two-year route many Cambridge IGCSE students continue into, examined in the June and November series and also in the March series at allocated centres. Entry grades are set by the school and are normally expressed in IGCSE grades, which is why a tier decision taken in Year 10 reaches further forward than most families expect it to.
programmes.countryNote: Sixth-form places in the UAE are offered on IGCSE results, and the statement of results is accepted before certificates arrive in late June. A student who misses an entry grade in one subject may have a November resit available, but those results do not land until January.

cambridge-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: Cambridge gives every syllabus a four-digit code, and the code rather than the subject name is what a tutor needs. The descriptions below say what each course assesses and where marks are usually lost, so you can tell quickly whether a tutor is talking about your child's course.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Written papers split by tier, with a calculator and a non-calculator paper in each on the current syllabus. Marks leak at the method stage: a correct final answer with no working scores less than a wrong answer with a visible, awardable method. Sessions here are part-mark drills on past questions rather than fresh teaching.

subjects.name: International Mathematics (0607)
subjects.description: A different course from 0580 despite the shared subject name, with a graphics-calculator paper and an investigation-style component at Extended. Students who transfer between UAE schools sometimes change code mid-course, which is the one situation where past papers from the wrong syllabus actively mislead.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 Extended by students heading for A Level Mathematics, and the clearest early indicator of whether that route will be comfortable. Content overlaps the first term of AS, so the hours spent here do double duty for a student who is continuing.

subjects.name: Physics (0625)
subjects.description: Theory papers by tier, plus either a practical test or the written alternative to practical paper. Electricity and the equation-rearranging topics cost most of the lost marks. The alternative to practical is a reading and reasoning paper and is taught well over video; the practical test needs the school laboratory.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: Moles arithmetic, organic reaction pathways and the extended electrolysis questions are where Extended candidates separate from Core ones. The practical and alternative-to-practical components follow the same split as physics, and the same honest limitation applies to the laboratory paper.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: A content-heavy syllabus where marks go to command words rather than knowledge: describing a process when the question asked for an explanation. Sessions work best on marked past-paper sections with the mark scheme open beside the student's own script.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences (0654 and 0653)
subjects.description: The double and single award routes for students not taking three separate sciences. Content is drawn from all three disciplines, so a tutor has to work outside one specialism, and a school's choice between the two routes affects what a sixth form will accept afterwards.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500 and 0990)
subjects.description: Reading and directed writing, assessed against criteria that reward control rather than length. The common fix is not vocabulary but structure: answering the question asked, in the form the task specifies, and keeping a response inside the brief it was given.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510, 0511 and 0991)
subjects.description: The codes differ in how speaking is treated, which is a detail worth confirming on the statement of entry. Progress comes from timed writing tasks marked against the criteria, not from general conversation practice, which is what most informal help defaults to.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450) and Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Both reward applied answers: a point, an explanation, then a judgement tied to the case material in front of the student. Marks are lost to generic answers learned from a revision guide and reproduced whatever the question stem actually says.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode, data representation and a theory paper that trips strong programmers who have never written an algorithm by hand. Sessions are mostly written-answer practice rather than coding, which surprises families who expected the opposite of that.

subjects.name: Arabic (0508 and 0544)
subjects.description: Two separate Cambridge courses, placed by the school according to the student's background. An Arabic grade is a qualification in its own right, but it is not counted among the five accredited subjects the Ministry of Education looks for on the British track.

cambridge-igcse-tutor.regionsTitle: Where your child's school sits, and which authority holds its file
cambridge-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: Delivery is identical in all seven emirates, because the lesson runs over live video. What differs is the authority that licenses the school, which decides what a parent can look up about it, and how thin the local pool of a visiting Cambridge specialist would be. These notes are about those two things.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Schools answer to KHDA, which oversees the quality of private education in the emirate and publishes inspection reports parents can read. Dubai had 227 private schools in 2024-25 serving 387,441 students across 17 curricula, with the UK curriculum the largest single share, so Cambridge entries here are routine.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Press-reported professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, which is why a teacher may decline an evening request from a parent in their own class.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK. The practical difference is distance: the list of visiting specialists willing to drive out for a tiered science entry is short, and the published market rate carries that drive inside it. Online removes the drive and widens the list to whoever teaches the syllabus code.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval and not only inspection sits with the emirate. Useful to know when a school reshuffles an option block.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority. Families moving between Ajman and Dubai mid-course often find option blocks differ, which can change which Cambridge subjects are available and occasionally the syllabus code itself.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. Entries run through the school's own centre, so confirm the timetable zone with the exams officer rather than assuming it matches a Dubai school's.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Supervised by the Ministry of Education. Fujairah appears in almost no UAE tutoring content at all, which is a fair proxy for how many visiting specialists work here. Live online sessions on Gulf Standard Time make the local pool irrelevant to who teaches your child.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under the Ministry of Education, and the smallest of the seven markets. Where a subject and tier combination is uncommon, the realistic options are one-to-one online or a weekly drive to another emirate, and this page is clear about which of the two IB Gram provides.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai
schoolClusters.note: Students supported here sit Cambridge entries alongside KHDA's mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies lessons, which schools timetable on a forty-minute unit. Inspection reports for each school are published by the regulator and are worth reading before any money is spent on tuition.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain
schoolClusters.note: Schools in this cluster are licensed by ADEK. Cambridge and Pearson entries both appear across it, so the first question in any match here is which board and which syllabus code the centre has entered a student for, rather than which of the two boards is preferable.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah and the Northern Emirates
schoolClusters.note: Regulated by SPEA in Sharjah and by the Ministry of Education in Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain. Option blocks are narrower in smaller cohorts, which is where an uncommon subject and tier combination becomes genuinely hard to staff locally.

All four run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and none of them involves anyone travelling to a UAE address.

modes.description: A weekly hour per subject from the start of Year 10. This is the only format that can genuinely influence the tier decision, because it produces marked Extended-style work before the autumn entry conversation happens. It is also the cheapest version of the same outcome, since nothing has to be rebuilt later under time pressure.

Twelve weeks out the plan rebuilds topics; six weeks out it is marked past papers and answer shape; the final fortnight is retrieval and timing only. The whole block is written down at the start so nobody is improvising in April.

sections.heading: What a Cambridge statement of entry fixes, and what is still open
paragraphs: The document that settles most arguments at home is the statement of entry. The exam centre issues it before each series, and it lists, for every subject, the syllabus code, the tier, the component numbers and the candidate number. Parents who have been guessing which course their child is on stop guessing the moment they read it. A tutor should ask for it in the first conversation, because an hour planned against the wrong tier is wasted even when the teaching inside it is good, and that waste is invisible until a mock comes back.

Three things on that sheet are effectively closed once the final entry deadline has passed. The syllabus code is closed: 0580 and 0607 are different courses with different question styles, and a school cannot swap one for the other in April. The exam centre is closed, which is what fixes the timetable version your family should be working to. The tier is closed in practice, because a change needs the centre to submit an amendment supported by the school's own evidence, and most schools will not do that in the final term.

What remains open is everything a tutor can actually reach: the number of past papers your child has marked under time, whether a command word is understood, whether working is written down in a form an examiner is able to award, and the order in which topics get revisited. That is a narrower list than most families expect and a far more useful one. The table separates the two columns, so a first session goes to the open one instead of to a complaint about the closed one.

sections.heading: Counting a series backwards from the day the entries close
paragraphs: The one date most families never see is the final entry deadline. For the Cambridge March 2027 series the board publishes final entries as due on 27 November 2026, with the exam period running from 3 February to 4 March 2027. Fourteen weeks separate the two. A parent who starts looking for help in January is therefore working inside a frame that was locked in late November by a member of staff they have probably never met, on the strength of coursework and mock marks from the autumn term.

Counting backwards changes what you should be asking for. Twelve weeks out, a weekly hour can still rebuild a topic from the ground up. Six weeks out, the gain comes from marked past-paper sections and from writing answers in the shape a mark scheme rewards. Two weeks out, the only safe work is retrieval and timing: no new content, nothing that shakes a student's confidence days before a paper. The same AED per hour buys three genuinely different services depending on where in that count it is spent.

The table lists the published milestones for that series in date order, with the thing a household should have finished by each one. The board's own guidance is the authority on the dates; your centre is the authority on which of them apply to your child. Results for the March series reach centres on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June, which means a family planning a summer move needs the statement of results rather than the certificate for an application.

sections.heading: Three series in a year, and the one most UAE families are never offered
paragraphs: Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series. Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests sit separately, in March, May and October. The Cambridge March series also exists and is used by particular centres; its 2027 exam period runs from 3 February to 4 March. Most UAE schools work to June, because that is where the academic year lands, and a parent generally discovers the alternatives only when something has already gone wrong in one subject.

Series choice belongs to the school, not the family, and it is made at entry. Where it matters most is after a result. A June candidate who misses a grade in one subject has the Cambridge November series available in the same calendar year, but a student who needs that grade for a sixth-form place starting in September does not, because November results reach students in January. Knowing that in advance is the difference between a plan and a scramble in the week results arrive.

The consequence for tuition is simple arithmetic. A June-series student has the whole UAE school year ahead of them and can be taught properly across Years 10 and 11. A November resit candidate has a compressed block running across the summer and the first term, usually with school lessons no longer covering that content at all. Both are workable jobs. They are not the same job, and they should not be quoted, planned or staffed as though they were.

sections.heading: Six administrative zones, and why the timetable you downloaded may not be yours
paragraphs: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, and its guidance for exams officers is unusually blunt about the consequence: it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and the board states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam because the wrong version was used. A Cambridge administrative zone is an administrative fact about the centre rather than about the country, so two UAE schools are not automatically in the same one.

In practice this is the most common planning error a tutor sees. A parent searches for the timetable, finds a PDF, pins it to the fridge and books sessions around it. Two of the subject dates turn out to be an hour out and one is a day out. Sessions end up scheduled on the morning of a paper. The fix costs nothing at all: ask the exams officer which zone the centre sits in and which version of the timetable it is working to, then plan the last fortnight from that document and nothing else.

It also explains something families find suspicious. A cousin in another country sits the same paper at a different local time, and a classmate who transferred in remembers different dates entirely. Neither is evidence of a leak or an administrative error. Zoning exists so that papers are sat inside a controlled window across many time zones at once. For a UAE household the working rule is to treat the centre's own document as the only calendar and anything found through a search engine as a draft.

sections.heading: Reading a component number before you buy an hour
paragraphs: Parents are handed component numbers and given no translation. On a Cambridge science syllabus the numbering follows a pattern which, once learned, tells you most of what a session should cover. Odd and even pairs separate Core from Extended on the written theory papers, and a practical test and a written alternative to practical paper sit at the end of the list. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 and its chemistry and biology equivalents are all numbered on that same shape.

This matters commercially because one subject name hides two different pieces of work. A student entered for the practical test needs laboratory technique and a teacher who can coach method at a bench. A student entered for the written alternative needs something quite different: reading a described experiment, identifying the controlled variable, completing a results table, criticising a method they never performed themselves. One of those is taught over video without compromise. The other needs the school laboratory, and an honest tutor says so in the first conversation.

Cambridge IGCSE Maths 0580 works on the same tier-split logic, with a calculator and a non-calculator paper in each tier on the current syllabus. Confirm the component numbers from the statement of entry rather than from a syllabus PDF found online, because syllabuses are revised and the version your child sits is the one the centre entered them for. The table gives the pattern to expect; your child's own entry gives the fact you should plan against.

sections.heading: The tier conversation to have before the autumn entry goes in
paragraphs: Most Cambridge IGCSE subjects are tiered. The core and extended tier split is not two difficulty settings of one exam; they are different papers with different grade ranges, and the entry decides which range is available to a candidate. A school places a student on the evidence it holds: end-of-Year-10 results, topic tests and how the student copes when a question is unfamiliar. That decision is usually taken in the autumn of Year 11, which is precisely why October is when the conversation is worth having.

Families get into difficulty in two opposite directions. The first is a Core entry made for a student who was quietly improving all summer, which caps a grade below the level a sixth-form course asks for. The second is an Extended entry defended by a parent against the school's evidence, where the student then loses marks steadily across the whole paper instead of securing the top of the lower tier. Neither of those is fixed by buying more hours the following April.

What tuition is genuinely good for here is producing evidence before the entry is submitted. Six to eight weeks of marked work on Extended-style questions, with the marks shown to the subject teacher, is an argument a school can act on. After the deadline the work changes shape: on a Core entry the job is to secure the top of that tier cleanly, which is a real and respectable outcome rather than a consolation prize, and it needs different hours from a reach attempt.

sections.heading: Command words: where Cambridge marks are quietly lost
paragraphs: A student who knows the content and still comes out at grade 5 is usually answering a different question from the one that was asked. Cambridge questions are built on command words, and each one has a mark scheme behind it expecting a particular shape of answer. State wants a fact and no reasoning. Explain wants a mechanism, and will not award the bare fact. Suggest expects a plausible answer applied to a context the student has not seen before and cannot have revised.

This is the single most repairable cause of lost marks, and it stays repairable late in the year because it needs no new content. A session takes four questions the student has already attempted, reads the command word, counts the marks on offer and rewrites the answer to that shape. Two or three weeks of that work moves scripts that have plateaued for a term. It is also why marked past papers matter more than worked solutions: the student has to see where their own sentence failed to earn a mark.

The table pairs common command words with what a mark scheme tends to reward and the failure a tutor sees most often. It is a diagnostic rather than a revision list. Used properly, a parent can read a marked mock script beside it and tell the difference between a child who does not know a topic and a child who knows it and is writing the wrong kind of sentence about it. Those two problems need completely different hours.

sections.heading: What Cambridge IGCSE support costs across this market
paragraphs: Published UAE rates for an hour of secondary tuition run from roughly AED 45 at the budget end to AED 650 at the top of the market, and the spread is not arbitrary. It tracks who is teaching, whether the hour includes marking, and whether anyone has to travel. Budget online hours are generally taught by university students. Specialist IGCSE and IB hours in this market are published between about AED 200 and AED 450, and a visiting tutor's rate carries the travel inside it.

Monthly packages seen in this market include online blocks around AED 799 for eight sessions and visiting-tutor blocks between AED 1,599 and AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. A Dubai cost survey estimates monthly spend for a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are market figures from the sources named, read in October 2026, and not IB Gram's price list.

Two things are worth checking before any of that is paid. First, whether the quoted hour is sixty minutes or a school period of forty, since KHDA itself calculates mandatory-subject time on a forty-minute unit and some providers quote on the same basis. Second, what the rate includes: marking a past paper properly takes a tutor twenty to thirty minutes outside the lesson, and a rate that excludes it is not the cheaper rate it appears to be. Ask for both in writing.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor in this market, set against one-to-one online
paragraphs: The honest version of this comparison starts with what a visiting tutor genuinely offers. Someone in the room can read a hand-written page without a camera angle, can reach for a textbook, and can hold the attention of a young student who drifts on a screen. For a Year 7 or Year 8 Cambridge Lower Secondary student that is a real argument, not a weak one. Published UAE rates for a visiting hour run roughly AED 180 to 500, with the travel priced inside the number.

The cost of that model is the tutor pool. A family in Al Ain or Fujairah choosing from the people willing to drive to them is choosing from a short list, and that list rarely contains a specialist who can teach the Extended supplement and the alternative to practical paper for a tiered science syllabus. Travel also eats the evening: a four o'clock session needing a forty-minute drive each way costs the tutor two hours and the household a fixed slot it cannot move.

IB Gram delivers this as one-to-one online Cambridge IGCSE tuition over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, in every emirate. IB Gram does not operate a visiting-tutor service in the UAE; that is offered only in India. The trade is specific. You give up the person in the room and you gain a specialist matched to the syllabus code and tier, plus a session that can shift by thirty minutes when traffic or a school event intervenes. The table sets the two formats side by side.
