cbse-to-igcse-transition.modesIntro: Three ways a transferring family buys support, each suited to a different point in the calendar. All of them run live online, one student and one tutor, with recorded worked solutions left behind after the session.

modes.title: The transfer term: a diagnostic block
modes.description: Four to six sessions whose purpose is to find out what is missing rather than to teach a syllabus. The tutor works through the receiving school's scheme of work for the year already completed, sets short topic checks against it, and produces a written gap list by syllabus strand. Families use this in the weeks before or just after a move, when nobody yet knows which topics fell through the crack between two different academic years.
bullets: One subject per block, graded against the real syllabus strands
Written gap list a receiving school's head of department can read
Identifies topics the previous board covered in a different year
Informs the Core or Extended tier conversation before entry closes

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through Year 10 and 11
modes.description: A fixed slot in the week, one subject, running across the two IGCSE years. The work is paced against the school's own scheme and the series the school enters for, with past-paper work introduced once a topic is secure rather than from the first session. This is the format most families settle into after a diagnostic block, usually in Maths or one science to begin with.
bullets: Same tutor, same slot, paced to the school's scheme of work
Command-term drilling built in, not bolted on before mocks
Mark-scheme reading taught as a skill in its own right
Progress notes after each session, visible to the parent

modes.title: The final-term push before a series
modes.description: A short, intense block in the eight to twelve weeks before papers, built around the specific components a student is weakest in and the dates in the official timetable for their zone. Sessions are structured around timed sections rather than topics, because by this point the limiting factor is almost always exam execution rather than knowledge.
bullets: Timed question sets under real paper conditions
Component-level targeting: Paper 2, Paper 4 or the practical alternative
Session plan built backwards from the zone's exam dates
Honest advice when a weekly session is no longer the right purchase

sections.heading: What a CBSE family is really asking when they ask about IGCSE
paragraphs: The literal question is whether IGCSE is harder than CBSE. The short answer is that it is differently assessed rather than harder, and that the difference costs marks for about two terms. A CBSE Class 10 student meets more content in Mathematics and the sciences than Cambridge 0580, 0620 or 0625 require. What they have not met is a mark scheme that pays for method, for command terms and for explanation structure, and an examiner who will not award a correct final answer that arrives without visible working.

The second question, usually asked later and more quietly, is whether the move will cost a grade. It can, and the mechanism is almost never content. It is tiering. Most Cambridge IGCSE subjects run Core and Extended papers, and Core caps the available grade at 5. The decision about which tier a child sits is made by the school at entry, months before the exam, and once entries have closed it is not a decision a parent can revisit. A transferring student placed on Core because their first term looked shaky can finish Year 11 with a ceiling they did not know existed.

The third question is about recognition, and here the answer is firm. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One competitor page currently ranking states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the published rule is five.

So the practical shape of the answer is this: the content gap is real but small, the tiering decision is the thing that actually changes outcomes, and the recognition rules are published and checkable. All three are calendar items. None of them is solved by starting a tutor in September and hoping.
bullets: Content gap after CBSE Class 10: roughly one term in Maths, two in Biology and English
Tier decision: made at entry by the school, not revisable at results
Core tier grade ceiling: 5 in most Cambridge subjects
MoE British track: five IGCSE subjects at E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education

sections.heading: The move dated backwards from the series your child will sit
paragraphs: Every decision in an IGCSE year has a deadline in front of it, and almost all of those deadlines are earlier than families expect. Cambridge's own key-dates sheet for the March 2027 series is the cleanest worked example available, because it shows the full chain in one place: the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries were due 27 November 2026, forecast grades 27 February 2027, results reach centres on Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June.

Read that backwards and the planning becomes obvious. If the paper is in early February, the final revision block starts in late November. If entries close on 27 November, the Core-or-Extended conversation has to happen in October at the latest, which means the diagnostic evidence for that conversation has to exist in September. A transferring student who starts a tutor in October for a February paper has already missed the decision that mattered most.

The June series works the same way with different dates, and the November series gives a resit route that few UAE families realise exists. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year, and the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, and revises them — which is exactly why this page links the official timetable rather than reprinting dates that may change.

One more mechanical detail bites UAE families specifically. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. A parent revising from a timetable found on a search result rather than from the school's own zone version is taking a risk the board has explicitly disclaimed.

sections.heading: Class 9 or Class 10: the two entry points, and what each costs in time
paragraphs: There are really only two sensible moments to move a child from CBSE into IGCSE, and the second one is more expensive in effort than it looks. The first is at the end of Class 8, into Year 9. The child arrives before the IGCSE course begins, before tiering, before entry fees and before any coursework component exists. A Checkpoint series in March, May or October gives the receiving school a proper scale score per strand, so placement is based on evidence rather than on an internal test written for children already in the system.

The second is at the end of Class 9, into Year 10, which is where most UAE transfers actually happen because it coincides with a parent's job move or a decision to abandon the Class 10 board exams. This works, but it compresses everything. The child meets a new mark scheme, a new command-term vocabulary and a tier decision inside one academic year, and the receiving school has no Checkpoint data on them at all.

Moving after CBSE Class 10 is a third option and a different animal: the child has a board certificate and is usually better served going straight into a sixth form, AS Level or IB Diploma route than repeating two years to collect IGCSEs. Families sometimes take one or two IGCSE subjects privately alongside, usually English or a language, to satisfy a sixth-form condition or to build towards the five accredited subjects MoE equivalency counts.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the tiering decision CBSE families have never had to make
paragraphs: CBSE has no equivalent of tiering. A Class 10 student sits the paper their school enters them for and the full grade range is available to everyone. Cambridge IGCSE works differently in most subjects: Core and Extended are separate papers covering different amounts of the same syllabus, and Core caps the achievable grade. A student entered for Core Mathematics cannot be awarded above grade 5 no matter how well they perform.

Schools make this decision for sound reasons. A Core entry protects a student who would otherwise sit a paper well beyond them and come away with a U. It is a kindness in the right case. In the wrong case — a strong CBSE student whose first term looked weak because they were learning a mark scheme rather than content — it quietly removes the top four grades from the table, and with them the A Level courses that ask for grade 6 or 7.

The practical defence is evidence and timing. A transferring family should ask, in October at the latest, which tier each subject is entered at, what evidence the decision is based on, and whether the department will review it before entries close. A diagnostic block that produces written topic-level evidence is far more persuasive in that conversation than a parent's confidence. If the evidence genuinely supports Core, accept it and plan the sixth-form route around it rather than arguing.

The table sets out what each tier actually changes. It is worth reading next to the subject your child is weakest in, because the decision is taken per subject and a student can sit Extended Maths and Core Biology in the same year.

sections.heading: Where a CBSE student loses IGCSE marks, topic by topic
paragraphs: Marks go missing in predictable places after this move, and the pattern is consistent enough to plan around. In Mathematics the losses are method marks and the non-calculator paper. CBSE habits favour an efficient route to the answer; IGCSE pays for the stated route. A student who writes three lines where they used to write one recovers most of this inside a term, once they believe the mark scheme means it.

In the sciences the losses sit in two specific components. The first is explanation: a six-mark question in Physics 0625 wants a causal chain in physics vocabulary, and a CBSE student's instinct is to give the formula and the number. The second is the practical or alternative-to-practical paper, which tests experimental judgement — identifying an anomalous reading, naming the control variable, explaining why a result is unreliable — that an Indian-curriculum practical record simply does not assess. This is learnable but it has to be taught deliberately.

In English the losses are structural rather than linguistic. Directed writing asks a student to transform a source into a new form for a named audience, and reading questions ask for inference and writer's effect. A student with excellent grammar can score in the middle of the band for two terms simply because they are answering a comprehension question that was not asked. In Biology the losses are definitional: the syllabus has preferred wording for osmosis, transpiration and enzyme action, and approximate wording earns approximate marks.

The honest version of this is that the first set of mocks after a transfer usually reads worse than the child's real ability, and the second set usually reads about right. Families who panic at the first set and buy four subjects of weekly tutoring often spend more than the problem required. One diagnostic block and one or two targeted subjects is the proportionate response.

sections.heading: What the move costs around it, in AED, with the rates attributed
paragraphs: Tuition is only one line in the cost of a board change, and families usually discover the others late. School fees are the largest: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. That freeze makes a mid-stream move cheaper to model this year than last, because the receiving school's published fee is the fee.

Supply is also moving in the family's favour. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools — four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate — creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. A transferring family looking for a British-curriculum place has more options than the same family had two years ago, which is worth knowing before accepting a waiting list.

On tutoring itself, the market rates below are what providers publish, not what IB Gram charges. Market rates in Dubai for a qualified subject tutor online run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour; Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 at the budget end; TutorChase lists AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 at the specialist and premium end. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 and specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 or above.

IB Gram's own position is simpler to state than to tabulate: a free trial lesson first, then a quote for the subject and level once a specialist has been matched. We do not publish a rate card on these pages because the honest number depends on subject scarcity and level, and a figure printed here would be a figure we had to defend rather than a figure you could rely on.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against a tutor in the room, for a transferring family
paragraphs: Parents searching for a home tutor in the UAE are asking a reasonable question, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a redirect. In-home tutoring is widely available in Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah, it costs more per hour than online because travel is priced into the rate, and the realistic tutor pool is whoever is willing to drive to your community at the hour you want. Bestimate's Dubai figures put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour, with independent tutors quoting up to AED 500.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons for UAE families are delivered one-to-one over live video, and the case for that is specific rather than general when the subject is a board transfer. A transferring student does not need a generalist near their villa. They need somebody who knows that 0620 qualitative analysis is examined as a descriptive bank and that 4CH1 structures its papers differently, and that person is unlikely to live twenty minutes away.

The second argument is scheduling, which matters more during a transfer than at any other time. A transfer term is the term when a child is tired, the school bus run is unfamiliar and the family is often still unpacking. A session that needs nobody to arrive can move by thirty minutes on a bad evening instead of being cancelled, and can shift to a post-Iftar slot through Ramadan without renegotiating a driver's route.

The third is continuity across a move. Families who transfer board often transfer emirate, country or both within a couple of years. A tutor relationship built over video survives a move from Sharjah to Abu Dhabi, or out of the UAE entirely, which a local in-home arrangement cannot.

sections.heading: Who enters your child for the exam, and what happens if nobody has
paragraphs: An IGCSE grade can only be produced by a registered exam centre, and a transferring family needs to know which centre that is. For a student at a British-curriculum school the school is the centre and handles entries, codes, zone timetables and forecast grades. For a student who has moved mid-stream, or who is taking a subject their school does not teach, the entry has to be made as a private candidate through a centre that accepts them.

This is the single most common administrative failure in a board transfer. A family assumes the school has entered the child for all the subjects they are studying, and discovers after the deadline that one subject was not on the form — usually a language, or a subject taken outside the timetable. Entries close months before papers, so the discovery comes too late to fix within that series and the student waits for the next one.

The fix is a short conversation and a piece of paper. Ask the school's exams officer for a written list of every syllabus code your child is entered for, at which tier, for which series, and in which administrative zone the centre sits. Check it against what your child believes they are studying. Do it before the final entry deadline, which for a Cambridge March 2027 series was 27 November 2026 — roughly ten weeks before the first paper.

If a subject is missing, private-candidate entry through an accepting centre is the route, and it carries its own fee and its own deadlines. Coursework-bearing subjects are harder to enter privately because the coursework component has to be produced and authenticated somewhere, which is why a transferring student who needs an extra English qualification is usually better directed to a fully examined route than a coursework one.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies do not change when the board does
paragraphs: Families planning a board change often forget that one part of the timetable is fixed by the regulator rather than the curriculum. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year starts in April. The federal position behind that is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

The organisational rules are specific and worth knowing, because they shape what tutoring can and cannot sensibly offer. KHDA requires that for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. For the mandatory UAE subjects, KHDA states that the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited — which means tutoring in these subjects has to work with the school's own material rather than substituting a parallel syllabus.

Two practical consequences for a transferring family. First, the timetable your child moves into already has these periods in it, so the hours available for IGCSE revision are fewer than a bare subject count suggests. Second, Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for MoE equivalency on the British track, so a strong Arabic grade does not substitute for a weak IGCSE one in that count.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency after an IGCSE route
paragraphs: Equivalency is the process that makes a foreign school certificate usable for a UAE university application or a government job, and it is the part of the move most families leave until too late. For the British track the published requirements are specific: a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade.

Two details inside that rule change how a transferring family chooses subjects. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, so the five have to come from the rest of the timetable. And the count is of accredited subjects, which is a question for the authority rather than for a tutoring page — if a subject's status matters to your plan, verify it with the attestation authority before building a two-year plan on it.

For completeness, the American track works differently: English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold appears in the source we read, so this page publishes none; a family on an IB route should read the figure on moe.gov.ae or ask the emirate's attestation authority directly rather than trusting a number found on a tutoring site.

IB Gram does not perform equivalency, submit documents or influence an outcome, and nobody should tell you that tutoring is required for it. What tutoring can do is make sure the five subjects a family is relying on are the five that will actually clear the grade threshold, which is a teaching question and a scheduling question rather than an administrative one.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and a family paying for lessons is entitled to ask about it. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published — Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties — so any page quoting an amount is quoting something unverified. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

There is a separate and more restrictive position for school staff. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. That was press-reported rather than read from the policy document, so treat the wording as indicative and verify against the current ADEK policy. Either way, the practical advice is the same: do not arrange for your child's own teacher to tutor them privately.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor. It needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE premises, and makes no claim of approval or accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

sections.heading: The line between teaching a student and producing their work
paragraphs: IGCSE has less assessed coursework than the IB Diploma, but it has enough — coursework routes in English, Geography fieldwork-style papers, Art and Design submissions, Computer Science programming tasks — for the honesty question to matter. A tutor may teach the skill, explain the criteria, model an approach on a different question, read a draft and give feedback on it. A tutor may not become the author of a piece of assessed work, and no family should buy that from anyone.

This matters in a transfer specifically because the pressure is highest exactly when the student is least sure of the standard. A child who has never written a coursework piece under a criteria-based mark scheme will often hand a tutor a blank page and an impossible deadline. The right response is to shorten the scope and teach the structure, not to fill the page.

There is a commercial dimension to this that parents should know about. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. Submitting that work is malpractice under board rules and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller. If a provider offers to produce assessed work, that offer is the clearest possible signal about everything else they sell.

Related rule, same principle: we do not reproduce or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads. We reference them and link to the official source — cambridgeinternational.org, qualifications.pearson.com, ibo.org — because that is both lawful and more useful to you, since the official version is the current one.

process.title: Tell us the series, not just the subject

That tells us whether this is a two-year plan or a ten-week one, and which specialist to look for. If you do not know the codes yet, ask the school's exams officer in writing and send what comes back.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the matched specialist
process.description: One lesson, no card details, no commitment, with the tutor who would actually teach the subject rather than a sales call. The trial is a teaching session with a diagnostic purpose: by the end you should have a view on whether the tutor can read your child, and we should have a view on where the real gap is.

process.title: A written gap list before the tier conversation
process.description: After the trial, and after a short diagnostic block where one is needed, you get a topic-level gap list against the real syllabus strands. This is the document to take into a conversation with the school about Core or Extended, because it argues from evidence rather than from a parent's confidence in their own child.

process.title: A plan dated backwards from the exam
process.description: Sessions are scheduled against the series: teaching finished before the final revision block, timed component work in the weeks before the papers, and the entry deadline marked as the point after which the tier is fixed. You see the plan as dates, not as a number of hours bought.

process.title: Reviewed each half term, changed when it should be
process.description: Every half term the question is whether the weekly session is still the right purchase. Sometimes the answer is to drop a subject because the gap has closed, sometimes to swap tutors because the match is wrong, and sometimes to stop. We will say so; a session a child no longer needs is a session that teaches them tutoring is permanent.

process.title: If no specialist is free, we say so
process.description: Some combinations are genuinely scarce — a Pearson 4PM1 Further Pure Maths specialist in a Gulf Standard Time evening slot, for instance. When we cannot match within a reasonable time we tell you that rather than offering a near-miss, and we say roughly how long a match is likely to take so you can look elsewhere if the exam will not wait.

faqs.question: Is IGCSE easier or harder than CBSE Class 10?
faqs.answer: Differently assessed rather than harder. A CBSE Class 10 student has usually met more content in Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry than Cambridge 0580, 0625 or 0620 require. What they have not met is a mark scheme that pays for stated method and for command terms, an alternative-to-practical paper that tests experimental judgement, and English papers that ask for inference and directed writing rather than comprehension. Expect the first set of mocks after a transfer to read worse than your child's real ability and the second set to read about right. The gap is roughly one term in Maths and two in Biology and English.

faqs.question: When is the best time to move a child from CBSE to IGCSE in the UAE?
faqs.answer: End of Class 8 into Year 9 is the cheapest in effort: the child arrives before the IGCSE course, before tiering and before any entry fee, and a Checkpoint series in March, May or October gives the receiving school a real scale score for placement. End of Class 9 into Year 10 is the most common in practice and compresses a new mark scheme, new command terms and the tier decision into one year. After the Class 10 board exams, a sixth-form or Diploma route usually makes more sense than collecting IGCSEs retrospectively.

faqs.question: What is the entry deadline for an IGCSE series, as opposed to the exam date?
faqs.answer: Months earlier, and this is the detail that catches transferring families. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series put final entries on 27 November 2026 against an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due 27 February 2027 and results on Direct on 13 May. The June and November series follow the same shape with different dates. Ask your school's exams officer in writing for the deadline, the syllabus codes and the tier for each subject, and check the list against what your child believes they are studying.

faqs.question: What does Core and Extended mean, and can we change tier later?
faqs.answer: Most Cambridge IGCSE subjects run two tiers. Core covers the core syllabus content and caps the grade at 5; Extended adds the supplement and reaches 9. The tier is decided per subject by the school at entry, so a student can sit Extended Maths and Core Biology in the same year. It is reviewable until the school submits final entries and effectively fixed after that. A transferring CBSE student placed on Core because a first term looked shaky can lose access to the A Level courses that require grade 6 or 7, so raise it in October with evidence.

faqs.question: After switching from CBSE, how many IGCSE passes does a UAE equivalency file need?
faqs.answer: Five. The published British-track requirement is that a student passes five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One competitor page ranking for these searches states six subjects, which does not match the published rule. Verify the current position on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation authority before you plan around it.

faqs.question: Which syllabus code should we buy books and past papers for?
faqs.answer: Whichever one the school has entered your child for, and the only reliable source is the school's exams officer. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel are different exams with different paper architectures: Mathematics is 0580 at Cambridge and 4MA1 at Pearson, Chemistry is 0620 and 4CH1, Physics 0625 and 4PH1. Buying for the wrong board means buying past papers that practise the wrong paper structure. Departments inside one school sometimes use different boards, so ask subject by subject rather than assuming the school has one answer.

faqs.question: My child did well in CBSE maths but is losing marks in IGCSE maths. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always method marks and the non-calculator paper rather than content. IGCSE mark schemes award marks for the stated route to an answer, so a correct final figure with one line of working above it scores below a partially wrong answer with full method. CBSE habits favour the efficient route. The other reliable losses are the topics Indian-curriculum courses treat lightly: set notation, vectors and transformation geometry. Most students recover this inside a term once they believe the mark scheme means what it says, which is a teaching job rather than a content one.

faqs.question: Does my child still have to take Arabic and Islamic Education after switching board?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the switch changes nothing about it. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's current requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes are strictly prohibited. Plan revision time around those periods, and note that Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the five subjects MoE equivalency counts.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with IGCSE coursework in English or Computer Science?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the skill, explain the assessment criteria, model an approach on a different question and give feedback on a draft your child has written. A tutor cannot become the author of assessed work, and a provider offering finished coursework is offering malpractice, with the consequence falling on the student. In practice the useful help in a transfer term is narrowing the scope and teaching the structure, because transferring students often arrive with an over-ambitious title and no sense of the standard. Fully examined routes are usually easier for a private candidate than coursework-bearing ones.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in the UAE need a permit, and is there a fee?
faqs.answer: They need one and it is free. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, under the service name Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Can my child's new teacher tutor them privately after school?
faqs.answer: Not for payment, if the child is enrolled at that teacher's school. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Teachers tutoring outside school hours need the permit regardless. That reporting should be checked against the current ADEK policy document before anyone relies on the exact wording, but the practical position is clear enough: use an independent tutor rather than your child's own teacher.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to our home in Dubai or Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. UAE lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time evenings. For a board transfer that is usually the stronger option anyway, because the help a transferring student needs is syllabus-specific — somebody who knows how 0620 examines qualitative analysis, or how 4MA1 splits its two papers — and that person is unlikely to live near your community. Market in-home rates run AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel priced in.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE tutor cost in the UAE at the moment?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in Dubai, as of October 2026, run roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget end, where Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65; AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, where Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150; and AED 200 to 450 or more for specialist exam-year support, where TutorChase lists AED 270. Bestimate's Dubai 2026 table puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350. Those are other providers' figures. IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson rather than publishing a rate card here.

faqs.question: What happens if the school did not enter my child for a subject?
faqs.answer: If the deadline has passed, that series is gone for that subject and the next one becomes the target — which is one reason the November series matters. Before the deadline, the fix is a written list from the exams officer showing every syllabus code, tier, series and the centre's administrative zone, checked against what your child thinks they are studying. Missing subjects can be entered as a private candidate through a centre that accepts them, with its own fee and deadline, though coursework-bearing subjects are harder to arrange that way than fully examined ones.

faqs.question: Does the Cambridge zone timetable actually matter for a UAE centre?
faqs.answer: It does, and Cambridge says so explicitly. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. A UAE parent revising from a timetable found through a search result rather than from the school's own zone version is relying on a document the board has disclaimed. Ask the exams officer which zone the centre sits in and work from that timetable only.

faqs.question: Is it worth moving board at all, or should we finish CBSE Class 10 first?
faqs.answer: It depends on where the child is going after 16, not on which board is better. If the plan is a British-curriculum sixth form or an IB Diploma in the UAE, moving before Year 10 makes the two years coherent and gives the receiving school time to place the child properly. If the plan is an Indian university or a move back to India, a CBSE Class 10 certificate is worth having. Finishing Class 10 and then entering a sixth form or Diploma directly is a legitimate third route that avoids collecting IGCSEs retrospectively.

cbse-to-igcse-transition.closingHeading: Start with the date, then the subject
cbse-to-igcse-transition.closingBody: If you are weighing a move from CBSE to IGCSE, the first thing to find out is not which tutor to hire. It is which series your child will sit, which syllabus codes the school enters for, and which tier each subject is down for — in writing, from the exams officer, before the entry deadline closes the question. Send us that, and a free trial lesson with the matched subject specialist follows, delivered live online wherever in the Emirates you are. If the honest answer is that your child needs one diagnostic block rather than four weekly subjects, we will tell you that too.

intro.heading: What a parent can actually verify about an IB tutor in the Emirates
paragraphs: Parents searching for a certified IB tutor in the UAE are looking for a filter. The word promises that somebody independent has already checked this person, so you do not have to. Part of that promise is real and part of it is not, and sorting the two takes about ten minutes of questions before any money moves. The real part is legal: private tutoring here is permit-regulated, and the permit is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The part that is not real is the implication that the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge or a UAE education authority hands out a tutoring licence to individuals. They do not. They license schools, approve exam centres and clear the teachers inside them.

That leaves four separate things bundled inside one marketing word. A permit to be paid for lessons. A teaching qualification from a university or an education ministry. A subject qualification, usually a degree in the thing being taught. And experience of the exact syllabus your child sits, which is a claim rather than a certificate and has to be tested instead of filed. Two of the four sit in a database somebody can look up. The other two are documents you should ask to see. None of them, on their own, tells you whether a person can teach Higher Level Chemistry to a sixteen-year-old who has stopped doing the homework.

The second half of the question is the system your tutor has to work inside, and it changes by emirate. Dubai's private schools answer to KHDA. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain answer to ADEK. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. The school's inspection report, published by whichever of those bodies holds its file, is the single most useful document a parent has before hiring anyone, because it is the only place a subject-level weakness is written down by somebody other than the school.

Running beside all of this are the subjects the Ministry requires regardless of curriculum. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever international programme the school is licensed to teach, with rules on language of instruction, on separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups, and on using content the Ministry has not permitted. Any honest page about Arabic and Islamic Education tutoring has to say that a tutor here works from the school's material, not a bespoke syllabus of their own.

On delivery, this page is blunt. IB Gram arranges online IB tuition in the UAE: one-to-one lessons over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen and the student's own files open. We do not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the Emirates. Visiting tutors are a service we run in India only. The trade is deliberate: instead of choosing from whoever can reach your community before 6pm, you choose a Physics HL or Economics HL specialist and the commute disappears from the bill. Last reviewed October 2026.

certified-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: IB Gram covers the four IB programmes, but the credential question changes as the stakes rise. A PYP parent is usually asking about literacy and number confidence. A Diploma parent is asking about marks, deadlines and whether outside help is allowed. Each programme below carries a note on how it sits inside the UAE regulatory picture.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is inquiry-led and has no external examination, so progress is reported through teacher judgement, portfolios and the exhibition in the final year. Tutoring at this stage is diagnostic rather than exam-driven: reading fluency, number facts, written structure and the habit of explaining an answer. A tutor working on PYP should be able to describe how a unit of inquiry is built, because that is the shape of everything the child is asked to do in class.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, PYP schools still deliver the Ministry's mandatory subjects from the earliest years, and KHDA requires separate Arabic classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils. A PYP parent asking about a certified tutor is often really asking about Arabic, where the school's stream placement matters more than the tutor's CV.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses against four criteria per subject, marked out of eight each, with no public examination unless the school enters students for eAssessment. This is where families most often discover a gap, because criterion-based marks do not convert neatly into the percentages parents are used to reading. A tutor who knows the MYP can explain why a child who understands the content is losing marks on criterion D, which is usually about applying knowledge to an unfamiliar context.
programmes.countryNote: Several UAE schools run MYP to Year 9 and then switch to IGCSE, so the transition year is the one that needs attention. The emirate regulator approves the curricula a school offers, which is why option blocks differ between a Sharjah school and a Dubai one even inside the same group.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internal assessment carries real weight in most subjects, and the written papers are set by the IB rather than the school. This is the programme where the certification question matters most, because a tutor is working alongside assessed coursework that must be the student's own and that the school's coordinator has to declare as authentic.
programmes.countryNote: The International Baccalaureate accounts for roughly seven in a hundred of Dubai's private-school pupils, a small share of the largest private-school market in the country. That scarcity, not price, is the real reason a Higher Level specialist is harder to book in the Emirates than a GCSE maths tutor.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a service-learning element and a language development component. It is offered by a small number of UAE schools and is frequently misunderstood as a lighter Diploma, which it is not. The Diploma courses inside it are examined identically, so tutoring for a CP student looks the same as tutoring for a DP student in that subject.
programmes.countryNote: Because the CP is rare locally, a parent cannot assume a tutor has seen one. Ask specifically whether they have taught the Diploma courses the CP student is taking rather than the programme label, and check with the school how the reflective project is supervised before anyone outside the school reads a draft.

certified-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: Subject descriptions below are written around where marks are lost, because that is what a credential cannot tell you. A tutor with a physics degree and a teaching qualification may still have never marked an IB-style data-analysis question. Ask which board, which syllabus and how many cohorts, for the exact subject and level your child sits.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency carry this course, and Higher Level adds a third paper that rewards students who can hold a long argument together. The exploration is worth a fifth of the grade and is lost on weak personal engagement and unexplained notation, not on difficult mathematics. Ask a tutor which exploration topics they have seen marked down and why.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use dominate. Students who moved from IGCSE often underestimate how much of the mark depends on interpreting output rather than producing it, and on writing a conclusion in context. Graphical calculator technique is examinable in practice, so a tutor who cannot drive the same model as your child is working at a disadvantage.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Marks are lost in two predictable places: uncertainty and error analysis in the scientific investigation, and the extended-response questions where a definition is given but not applied. Higher Level adds depth rather than breadth, so a student who is shaky on the core will not be rescued by extra content. Practical write-up conventions need teaching explicitly.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium account for most of the lost marks, and the investigation is where a strong candidate separates from an average one. The common failure is a method that cannot generate enough data to analyse. A tutor may question a student's method and point to the published criteria; choosing the investigation is the student's own job.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command terms decide the grade here more than recall does. Students who write everything they know about a topic score less than students who answer the verb in the question. Data-based questions on unfamiliar experiments reward comprehension rather than memory, and that skill is teachable in a handful of sessions with the right past material.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, evaluation and the internal assessment commentaries drive the grade. Commentaries fail on article choice and on word-limit discipline long before they fail on theory. Higher Level adds quantitative demands that catch students who chose the subject expecting an essay course. Real UAE and Gulf examples make evaluation sharper than textbook cases do.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application rather than tool recall is what the markers reward, and the case study at Higher Level punishes students who have not practised reading a long stimulus under time pressure. The internal assessment needs a real organisation and real evidence, which is where families in the Emirates have a genuine advantage worth using.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the Paper 1 guided analysis are the two components that move a grade fastest. Students lose marks by summarising a text instead of analysing how it works and by choosing global issues that are too broad to sustain ten minutes of speech. Timed writing practice with marked feedback is the whole intervention.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Script fluency, listening and the productive skills decide these courses. For students in the Emirates there is an added complication: the Ministry's mandatory Arabic lessons at school are a separate requirement from IB Arabic, with their own content rules. A tutor should be clear which of the two a session is addressing before it starts.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions, tracing algorithms by hand and the internal assessment product are the pinch points. Students who code well in Python often lose marks because the examination expects a specific pseudocode style rather than working software. The internal assessment needs a genuine client, documented, and the documentation is marked as heavily as the artefact.

certified-ib-tutor.regionsIntro: Regulation is the one part of UAE schooling that genuinely changes with the emirate, so the notes below are written around who holds the file rather than around commute times. Lessons are delivered over live video everywhere in this list, which is why the tutor pool does not shrink as you move north.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA oversees the quality of private education in the emirate and publishes the inspection reports families should read first. With 227 private schools and 17 licensed curricula, two schools a few minutes apart can run entirely different option blocks and assessment calendars.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools here, and its professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. That rule is the reason the obvious first choice of tutor is often not available.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Al Ain sits under ADEK alongside Abu Dhabi rather than under a separate authority. IB cohorts are smaller inland, so Higher Level groups can be tiny and a subject the school cannot staff is a common reason families look outside it.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Curriculum approval sitting locally is why a Sharjah school's subject offering can differ from a sister school in Dubai.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools in Ajman are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority, so there is no local inspection portal to browse. Ask the school directly for its most recent report and for which board it enters candidates with.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah and, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. Families here often drove to Dubai for tuition before online delivery made the drive unnecessary.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Fujairah's private schools fall under the federal Ministry of Education. Diploma cohorts on the east coast are small, which makes subject-specialist cover the main constraint rather than cost, and makes a video link the only realistic way to reach an HL specialist.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Umm Al Quwain also sits with the federal Ministry of Education. Many students commute to schools in Sharjah or Ras Al Khaimah, so a realistic session start time is governed by the school run rather than by anything the regulator does.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai IB schools
schoolClusters.note: Dubai holds the largest concentration of IB World Schools in the country, spread from Emirates Hills to Al Barsha and Dubai Silicon Oasis. Students we support sit the Diploma at schools like these, and their published KHDA inspection reports are the quickest way to see which departments are carrying the school.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain
schoolClusters.note: The capital's IB provision is concentrated on the islands and in the newer communities inland. ADEK publishes the inspection outcomes, and its staff-ethics position on teachers tutoring their own students is worth knowing before you ask the school for a recommendation.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah and the northern emirates
schoolClusters.note: IB cohorts thin out quickly north of Dubai, and a Higher Level group of four or five students is normal. That is the single strongest argument for a video link rather than a local search, because the subject specialist simply may not live within driving distance.

Most Diploma families start with one subject and add a second only if the first is clearly working. A written note after each session records what was covered, which also means a coordinator's question about outside support can be answered honestly.

sections.heading: What the word "certified" can and cannot mean for an IB tutor here
paragraphs: No UAE authority and no examination board issues a credential called certified IB tutor. The International Baccalaureate authorises schools to deliver its programmes; it does not license private individuals to tutor them. KHDA, ADEK and the Sharjah Private Education Authority license schools and set conditions on the people who teach inside them, which is a different thing from clearing a freelancer who teaches your child over video on a Tuesday evening. So when a provider calls a tutor certified, the only useful response is three questions: certified in what, by whom, and may we see it?

Four distinct things get bundled into that one word. The first is legal permission to be paid for private lessons in the UAE, which is a permit from MoHRE and which says nothing at all about teaching quality. The second is a teaching qualification such as a PGCE, a B.Ed or a national teaching licence, which proves training in how to teach but not knowledge of the syllabus your child sits. The third is a subject qualification, normally a degree, which proves content knowledge well beyond Higher Level. The fourth is experience of the exact course, board and option your child is entered for, and that fourth one is not a certificate at all.

The practical consequence is that two of the four can be looked up and two have to be shown or tested. Ask for the permit record from the tutor's own MoHRE account. Ask for the degree certificate with the awarding university and year. Ask which board, which syllabus and how many cohorts, then test the answer by asking for a trial lesson built on a question from the current syllabus rather than a get-to-know-you chat. A tutor who has taught the course will reach for the command term and the mark scheme without being prompted. One who has not will talk about the topic.

sections.heading: The one certificate UAE law does require
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the Emirates is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the federal portal states that it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so this page quotes no amount; a figure circulating online could not be traced to an official source.

The application itself is ordinary. MoHRE's service is listed as the issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, the website and the e-services system, with no fee shown and a stated completion time of two working days. The permit carries a code of conduct that bars a tutor from serving students affiliated with their own school. ADEK private school rules point the same way in Abu Dhabi: press reporting of its professional-ethics framework describes a prohibition on private and charter school staff providing paid tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that framing should be checked against the current ADEK document before anyone relies on its exact wording.

What this means for a family is narrower than it first looks. A private tutor permit in Dubai comes from MoHRE, not from KHDA, and it tells you the lessons are lawful rather than good. A tutoring business with premises and staff is a different legal animal again and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram operates no premises in the UAE and holds no such permit, which is exactly why we describe what we are instead of borrowing a status we do not have.

sections.heading: Which authority holds your child's school file
paragraphs: Five bodies regulate private schools across the seven emirates. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi, which includes Al Ain. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages reviewed for this project, and the Sharjah authority by one, which tells you how little of this reaches parents.

Two of those authorities do more than inspect. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's bodies approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so what a school is allowed to offer is settled locally rather than nationally. The federal baseline is lighter than parents assume: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, provided they adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That is the rule underneath every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement.

For a tutoring decision, the inspection report is the document that earns its reading time. A KHDA inspection rating is a judgement about a whole school, not about the department your child sits in, and the useful detail is inside the report rather than on the cover. Attainment describes where students have reached; progress describes movement from their own starting point. A school can be strong overall and still have one subject where progress is flat for two years running, and that single line is a better reason to hire a specialist than any grade on a report card. If you live in one emirate and the school is in another, the school's regulator is the one that counts.

sections.heading: Why a claim of regulator approval deserves a second look
paragraphs: The most dangerous sentence available to a UAE tutoring website is one that places a regulator's name immediately before the word approved. It reads as a licence and it usually is not. The permit KHDA issues in this space is an Educational Services Permit for a training institute, granted to an organisation with premises in Dubai, with initial approval first, a cap of six months to finish the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested ahead of expiry. It is a real document with real conditions, and a company with no premises in the emirate cannot hold it. Borrowing the name of it is a misrepresentation rather than marketing.

The boards work the same way. The International Baccalaureate authorises schools to deliver its programmes and trains teachers who work in them. Cambridge International and Pearson appoint exam centres and publish rules those centres must follow. None of the three issues anything to a tutoring platform. A page claiming otherwise is either confused about its own status or hoping you will not ask. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no affiliation with the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, the Sharjah Private Education Authority or the Ministry of Education, and holds no permit or accreditation from any of them. We run no office, centre or branch anywhere in the Emirates.

Three related habits in this market are worth treating with the same suspicion. A star rating a provider has written about itself, with no countable reviews behind it, is a self-serving number rather than evidence. A statistic without a sample size, a date and a method behind it is decoration, which is why no satisfaction percentage or average tutor score appears on this page. And a tutor described as a current examiner should be asked, politely, for the board and the year, because examiner status cannot be inferred and does not come with access to marking, boundaries or unreleased papers. What we publish instead is narrow and checkable: the permit position, the qualification, the board and syllabus taught, and the fact that lessons happen over video.

sections.heading: The UAE subjects that run beside the IB, and who may teach them
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed to deliver, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. This sits on top of a federal rule that private schools need not follow any specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations. A Diploma student in Dubai is therefore carrying six IB subjects plus a set of national requirements, and the timetable pressure is real.

The organisation rules are specific enough to be worth quoting to any tutor who claims to cover these subjects. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies is delivered in Arabic for Arab students and in the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises a minimum of 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson.

There is one constraint that reshapes what Arabic and Islamic Education tutoring can honestly offer. For the mandatory subjects, using any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. A tutor who advertises their own bespoke Arabic programme for these lessons is describing something the rules do not permit. The honest version is narrower and more useful: work from the school's own scheme and set material, build reading fluency, script control and answer structure, and leave the content selection where the Ministry has put it. Schools are also required to ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the KHDA approval those subjects require.

sections.heading: Where the honesty line sits on the IA, the Extended Essay and TOK
paragraphs: A tutor may teach the skill, discuss a plan the student has proposed, ask questions about a draft the student has produced, point at the published criteria, and mark practice work. A tutor may not supply sentences for assessed coursework, restructure the student's text, or hand back a version to submit. The student's work has to be their own, and the school's coordinator has to declare that it is. This is not a house rule we invented to be awkward; it is the line the IB's academic-honesty regulations draw, and crossing it puts the student's diploma at risk rather than the tutor's reputation.

That line has a practical shape in a session. The student opens their own file and shares the screen. The tutor reads what is there, asks what the method was meant to show, asks where the criterion is being met, and says plainly when it is not. The student makes the changes afterwards, in their own words, in their own file. Nothing is typed into the document by the tutor and nothing is sent back rewritten. A short written note of what was discussed goes to the family, which has a second use: if a coordinator asks what outside support was involved, there is an honest and specific answer rather than a shrug.

Supervision is the other boundary parents miss. The Extended Essay has an appointed supervisor at the school who signs the reflections, and a tutor is an additional reader, never a replacement for that person. The TOK essay belongs to the TOK teacher. One UAE-facing site in this market advertises finished internal assessments for sale at a four-figure price in dirhams; that is an academic-integrity breach and a malpractice trigger for the student who buys it, and it is the clearest possible reason to ask what a provider actually does before paying. We also do not reproduce or hand out syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. We reference the official sources and link to them.

sections.heading: The school system a tutor has to fit into
paragraphs: Dubai's private sector enrolled 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum taking 37 per cent of pupils, Indian curricula 26 per cent, American 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate about seven in a hundred. Read that last figure twice. The IB is a minority programme inside the country's largest private-school market, which is the real reason an experienced Diploma teacher is harder to find than a GCSE maths tutor, and why price is the wrong first question. Scarcity of people who have taught the course is the binding constraint.

The sector is also moving. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four following a UK curriculum and three offering the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places; six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. New IB places are good news for admissions. They do nothing for teacher supply in the short run, because new schools recruit from the same pool of experienced Diploma teachers everyone else is recruiting from.

What all of this means for a tutoring plan is specific. The subject your child needs help with may not be the subject the school is strongest in, and the inspection report is where that shows up. A school that is excellent in English and only acceptable in mathematics will produce exactly one kind of parent enquiry. Because delivery is online, the match is made on syllabus fit rather than on which community the tutor lives in, so a family in Fujairah and a family in Jumeirah are choosing from the same specialists at the same rate.

sections.heading: Which board sets the dates, and why the centre's zone matters
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after working from the wrong one. That single rule explains a conversation UAE parents have every year: two cousins at different schools sitting the same paper at different times, and both schools being right.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, so any plan should be built from the board's live timetable rather than from a date copied onto a tutoring page and left there.

On the IB this page deliberately stops short. UAE schools sit the May session, and the November session exists as a second route. We are not publishing an IB examination or results date here, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and an unverified date is worse than none: a family that plans six weeks of revision around a wrong week has lost the six weeks. Ask the school's IB coordinator or read ibo.org directly. One thing is constant across all three boards. The IB exam entry deadline, like the Cambridge and Pearson ones, is set months before the first paper, and it is the school that submits entries, not the family.

sections.heading: Equivalency: the paperwork that follows the certificate
paragraphs: Equivalency is the Ministry of Education process that converts a foreign school certificate into something a UAE university or employer can act on, and it is the step families forget until results day has passed. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which surprises most parents.

For the American track the requirements are tests rather than subject counts. English proficiency is shown by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT; mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. One page currently ranking for these searches tells UAE candidates they must take six IGCSE subjects. The published rule is five. Getting that number right is worth more to a family than any amount of reassuring prose, and it is the kind of error that should make you check everything else on a page.

On the IB, this page publishes no figure at all. The source that sets out both the British and American tracks states no IB points threshold, so a Ministry of Education equivalency certificate requirement for the Diploma has to be confirmed on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority before anyone plans around it. Two further points. Equivalency is not something IB Gram performs, submits or influences, and no tutoring is required for it. Any page suggesting that tuition smooths a regulatory process is selling urgency rather than teaching.

sections.heading: What to ask before the first paid lesson, and what we say when nobody is free
paragraphs: Five questions settle most of this. Which permit do you hold, and may I see the record? What is your teaching or subject qualification, from which institution, in which year? Which board and syllabus have you taught, and for how many cohorts? What will you not do with my child's internal assessment? And can the first session be built around a question from the current paper rather than an introduction? A tutor who has taught the course answers the fifth question with enthusiasm, because it is the part of the job they are good at. Hesitation there is more informative than any certificate.

The honest part most providers leave out is coverage. Some subject and level combinations have very few experienced teachers anywhere in the Emirates: Higher Level Physics, Computer Science, Economics HL in an exam term, and the smaller language B courses. When no UAE-resident specialist is available for the slot you need, we say so. The alternative we offer is an India-based IB specialist teaching the same syllabus over the same video link in the same Gulf Standard Time slot, and we tell you that is what is happening rather than hiding it behind a local-sounding phone number. If neither works, we will say that too.

One last thing, because enquiry forms about children collect more than people realise. We ask for the school, the programme, the subject, the level and the year group, because the match cannot be made without them. We do not need a photograph, a full report card or a medical history to arrange a trial lesson, and a provider asking for those without explaining why is worth a question. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on personal data protection sits behind this, and the privacy link on every page sets out what is kept and how to have it deleted.
