sections.heading: What a tutor may do with internally assessed work
paragraphs: Every IB subject carries an internally assessed component worth a fifth or more of the grade, and IGCSE coursework exists in some subjects too. There is a market in Dubai for finished work: one operation sells completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price. Buying one is malpractice under IB rules and the penalty lands on the candidate rather than the vendor.

The permitted support is substantial. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what each lettered criterion asks for and how marks are distributed across them, interrogate a research question until it is answerable, warn that a planned method will not generate usable data before weeks are spent on it, read the student's own draft and name the criterion not yet met, and teach the referencing convention the school requires.

The prohibited support is equally plain. A tutor does not author any part of the piece, does not supply sentences for insertion, does not rewrite a paragraph into final form, does not provide the data and does not hand over a finished example to be adapted. The authenticity test is conversational: a supervisor asks the candidate to explain their own method and reasoning, and a student who cannot is exposed whatever the document looks like.

In this district the risk is sharpened by system changes. A student who has just crossed from a board where coursework worked differently is exactly the one most likely to accept help that crosses the line without understanding that they have. Saying the boundary out loud, at the start of the first session, is part of the job.

sections.heading: Getting started when siblings are on different systems
paragraphs: Start with paperwork, one set per child: the most recent report, the latest marked assessment with the mark shown, and the subject list with syllabus codes where the system has them. In Al Barsha this third item frequently reveals that two children are on two boards, which means no resource, revision guide or past paper can be shared between them.

Then name the problem per child rather than the subject. For an IGCSE candidate it might be timing and tariff reading; for a transferring student it might be six-mark explanation questions; for a Diploma candidate it might be a criterion on an investigation. Three different briefs, three different tutors, and that is the correct answer rather than an inefficiency.

Book the trials in the block you intend to keep, allowing for the latest realistic arrival rather than the earliest. The most common reason tuition stops here after two months is that the slot was never survivable once the interchange, the food and a second child were accounted for.

Availability is finite and the pattern is consistent across Dubai. Higher Level Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Economics are requested in the same late-afternoon window everywhere, and a scarce combination narrows it further. If nothing suitable is free when you want it, the honest options are a different weekday, a weekend morning or a short wait. Lessons are online, one-to-one, over live video; there is no Al Barsha centre to attend and no tutor arriving at an Al Barsha address, because that service is not sold in the UAE.
bullets: One set of documents per child, including syllabus codes
A different named problem per child, even in the same subject
Trial in the slot you intend to keep so the logistics are tested too
Weekend mornings fill first; book ahead if the weekday evening has gone

process.title: Confirm the board before anything else
process.description: Read the statement of entry or ask the examinations officer. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are both IGCSE Mathematics and they tier and structure differently. In a district where neighbouring schools use different boards, this is the step that prevents a term of practice on the wrong paper.

process.title: Check the tier while it can still change
process.description: Cambridge Core and Pearson Foundation both cap the achievable grade, and entries are submitted months before the papers. For a transferring student placed cautiously on arrival, asking about the tier and the entry window in the first fortnight is the highest-value thing a family can do.

process.title: Name the problem, not the subject
process.description: Timing, tariff reading, six-mark explanation questions, a specific criterion on an investigation, or a misconception in electrolysis. A narrow brief lets a tutor start work in the first fifteen minutes instead of spending two sessions establishing what is wrong.

process.title: Take a trial in the slot you will keep
process.description: Test the time as well as the tutor. Al Barsha 1 households can usually hold 16:00; Al Barsha South and Heights households are realistically at 17:00. Discovering that in a trial is cheaper than discovering it in week six when the slot starts being missed.

process.title: Review against the school's own assessment
process.description: At the end of each term, set the tutor's view beside the school's marks. Where they disagree, that disagreement is the most useful information a parent receives, and in a mixed-system household it is often the first sign that a child was placed in the wrong set on arrival.

whyPoints.title: Matched by board, not by subject
whyPoints.description: A Cambridge 0620 entry and a Pearson 4CH1 entry need different paper practice even though the chemistry is identical. Matching starts from the code on the statement of entry, which in this district is the only reliable way to get the right preparation.

whyPoints.title: System changes treated as their own job
whyPoints.description: Crossing from an Indian board, an American programme or an IB continuum into something else is a format problem more than a content problem. The bridging block audits content, then works on question structure, which is where the marks actually sit.

whyPoints.title: A national tutor pool rather than a drivable one
whyPoints.description: Delivery over live video removes the drive-time constraint, so a scarce board, level or subject combination can still be matched properly. In a district with four systems running at once, that breadth is the difference between a specialist and a generalist.

whyPoints.title: Figures that can be traced
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is attributed to the provider or survey that published it. Nothing here is presented as IB Gram's own price, and a quote from any provider can be weighed against the published market rather than against a feeling.

whyPoints.title: Equivalency stated correctly
whyPoints.description: The British-track rule is five accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. A well-ranked competitor page says six; this page states the sourced figure and names where to verify it.

whyPoints.title: Nothing claimed that cannot be shown
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no permit, accreditation or partnership with KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and occupies no Dubai premises. Schools are named as context for boards and routes, never as relationships.

faqs.question: My two children are at Al Barsha schools using different exam boards. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: Yes, more than most families expect. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 are both IGCSE Mathematics, and they tier differently, structure papers differently and use command terms differently. Past papers and revision guides are not interchangeable between them, so buying one set for both children means one of them is practising the wrong format. Confirm each child's code on their statement of entry, then treat them as two separate plans with two tutors. The subject knowledge overlaps almost completely; the examination technique does not.

faqs.question: What is the real gap when a CBSE student moves into IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Answer format, not content. A Class 9 or 10 student from an Indian board has usually covered more mathematics and science than the IGCSE cohort they join, with more worked practice. What they have had less of is extended written explanation, graph interpretation against a mark allocation, and evaluation questions expecting a judgement. The visible symptom is a student who solves problems their classmates cannot and scores below them. Several weeks of format work with past papers from the correct board usually closes most of it, which is far quicker than content teaching.

faqs.question: Can a tier or set placement be changed after a mid-year transfer?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and only inside the board's entry window. Receiving schools place cautiously from a report they cannot interpret in detail, so a capable transferring student often lands on Cambridge Core or Pearson Foundation, which caps the achievable grade. Ask the examinations officer two questions in writing in the first fortnight: which tier is my child entered for, and when does the amendment window close. For the Cambridge March 2027 series, final entries were due on 27 November 2026, which shows how far ahead these decisions sit.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does a student need for UAE university equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five accredited subjects at a grade no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus either one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. That is the Ministry of Education's published clarification for the British track. At least one well-ranked tutoring page states six subjects, which is wrong. Confirm the current rule on moe.gov.ae before making option-block decisions, and note that no tutoring provider performs or guarantees equivalency.

faqs.question: What does my American-track child need for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: A different kind of requirement from the British track. The Ministry's published clarification sets English proficiency at a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics at a minimum of 450 in the SAT Mathematics test before applying. That makes standardised test preparation part of the route rather than an optional extra. Plan it into Grade 11 rather than Grade 12, and verify the thresholds on moe.gov.ae because they are the Ministry's to change.

faqs.question: Why does the same tutor help one of my children and not the other?
faqs.answer: Usually because the two children have different problems that look like the same subject. An IGCSE candidate whose issue is timing and tariff reading needs timed past papers marked against the published scheme. A Middle Years student whose issue is criterion literacy needs the criteria translated into what to actually produce. A Diploma candidate stuck on an investigation needs criterion feedback on their own draft. Those are three different jobs. Matching the format of help to the diagnosis matters as much as matching the subject.

faqs.question: Is a group class worth it, or should we pay for one-to-one?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether the gap is shared. A group of students from the same school and the same set, all weak on the same three topics because teaching moved too fast, does well in a shared class and pays much less per head. A student with a specific misconception, a timing problem or an internally assessed component with its own research question gets little from the same class. Al Barsha has plenty of centre provision, so the honest test is this: can you name the gap, and would seven other students have exactly it?

faqs.question: Does a tutor come to our villa in Al Barsha?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; home visits are offered only in India. Sessions run one-to-one over live video at a fixed slot. In this district that is also the more practical arrangement, because between three and half past five the roads around the Mall of the Emirates interchange carry school traffic, mall traffic and the Sheikh Zayed Road feed at once. An online session starts when the child is in the chair rather than when a driver arrives.

faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start in Al Barsha?
faqs.answer: It depends which part. Al Barsha 1 households, where many children walk or have a short run, are usually home by 15:10 and can hold a 16:00 start comfortably. Al Barsha 3 is typically fifteen minutes later. Al Barsha South and Al Barsha Heights households, where children commute outward and arrival depends on the bus and the building, are realistically at 17:00. Set the slot at the late edge of your arrival window rather than the early edge, because a late start pushes a second child's session and eventually the slot gets abandoned.

faqs.question: Should we change school to change curriculum, or stay and get tutoring?
faqs.answer: Three questions decide it. Is the child unhappy, or only underperforming, because unhappiness is a reason to move and underperformance usually is not. Is there internally assessed work already begun, since that is the most disruptive thing to carry across mid-course and may not transfer at all. And is the gap format or content, because format gaps close in weeks with the right past papers while a genuine curriculum mismatch does not. Budget for a transition either way: format sessions, a tier check and a confirmation of the English entry.

faqs.question: Which English syllabus should my child be entered for?
faqs.answer: Check it rather than assume, because mis-entry between first and second language English is one of the most common administrative errors after a transfer. Cambridge First Language English is 0500 and English as a Second Language is 0510 or 0511, and they have separate syllabuses and separate mark schemes. The second language papers have fixed word ranges and a required register for the extended writing tasks, and marks there are lost on register rather than grammar. A student in the wrong entry can be capped or over-stretched without anyone noticing until results.

faqs.question: How much does IGCSE tutoring cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market bands, attributed: one Dubai content provider advertises online tuition from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour and one platform from roughly AED 33 to AED 52; a Dubai agency publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200; a Dubai cost survey reports in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 and specialist exam-year tuition at AED 200 to AED 450 and above; one premium provider publishes AED 650. Monthly packages seen in the market run near AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are other providers' figures, not IB Gram's prices.

faqs.question: Can a tutor work on an Internal Assessment for an IB student here?
faqs.answer: Yes, inside clear limits. A tutor may teach the content, explain what each lettered criterion asks for and how marks are allocated, interrogate the research question, warn that a method will not produce usable data, read the student's own draft and name the criterion not yet met, and teach the referencing convention. A tutor may not author any part of it, supply sentences, rewrite a paragraph into final form, provide the data or hand over a finished example to adapt. Services selling completed Internal Assessments put the candidate at risk, not the seller.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do students in mixed-curriculum districts struggle with most?
faqs.answer: The pattern is consistent: Chemistry mole calculations and electrolysis, Physics electricity and waves, Biology six-mark explanation questions, and English writing register. For transferring students the sciences cause most trouble, because the content is familiar and the question style is not. Where a student is on Combined or Co-ordinated Sciences the difficulty is different again: everything is examinable and nothing is revisited, so a Year 10 gap persists untouched into Year 11. Confirming which award a child holds should come before any science tuition plan is written.

faqs.question: What should we ask before committing to a weekly slot?
faqs.answer: Four questions. Which syllabus code have you taught, and when. What will you fix first, stated in one sentence. What will my child do between sessions and who marks it. And for an individual tutor working privately in the UAE, do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is granted free of charge for two years. Any tutor who cannot answer the second question specifically after a trial has not diagnosed anything yet, whatever the subject expertise.

dubai/al-barsha.closingHeading: Confirm the board, then buy the help
dubai/al-barsha.closingBody: In a district running four curricula at once, the first useful step is administrative rather than academic. Read the statement of entry, note the syllabus code and the tier, confirm which English syllabus each child is on, and only then look for a tutor. Send the latest report, the most recent marked paper and the code list, and name one problem per child rather than a subject. Lessons run one-to-one over live video; no tutor is sent to an Al Barsha address. Every AED band quoted here belongs to the provider or survey that published it, and a rate for your household is quoted after a trial session.

dubai/al-barsha-south.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover the Diploma, the Middle Years Programme and both IGCSE boards. For a diagnostic session, send the most recent marked paper rather than the report, because the paper is the only document that shows where marks were lost.

intro.heading: Capable and underperforming is not a diagnosis
paragraphs: The most common sentence on a report from any school is that a student is capable of more. It is almost always true and it is almost never actionable. A mark is lost at a specific point for a specific reason, and there are only about five reasons that matter. Until a family knows which one applies, buying tuition is buying hope rather than a plan, which is why so many households in this district start in October and stop in January having changed nothing.

The five are these. Content that was never properly learned, which is the one everybody assumes and the least common in an able student. Content that was learned and has decayed, which looks identical on a mock and needs a completely different response. Question technique, meaning the answer is the wrong shape for the command term and the mark allocation. Timing, meaning the student knows enough and writes too slowly to show it. And coursework, where a fifth or more of a subject grade sits in work produced outside lessons and marked against criteria the student has never read.

Each of those can be tested in one session. A past paper under a clock and a marking scheme will separate timing from knowledge in forty minutes. Asking a student to mark their own answer against the published scheme exposes technique immediately. A blank-page recall test on a topic taught eighteen months earlier separates decay from absence. None of this requires expensive diagnostics or a term of observation; it requires somebody to sit with the student and the paper at the same time.

Al Barsha South makes the practical side of this specific. The district runs inland from Al Barsha proper through Arjan and Dubai Science Park towards Dubai Hills, and it was built later and taller than its neighbour, so most households here are in apartments and most children commute outward by bus. Arrival times are later and less predictable than on the Al Barsha 1 side, which is why 17:00 is the honest weekday floor for a session rather than 16:00.

IB Gram matches tutors online, one-to-one, over live video. There is no Dubai centre and no tutor is sent to an Al Barsha South address; home visits are offered only in India. For diagnostic work the format is an advantage, because a shared screen with a marked past paper on it is a better working surface than a kitchen table, and the session can be recorded so a parent can hear the diagnosis rather than a summary of it. It also widens the choice: the tutor is picked for knowing the paper your child sits rather than for being able to reach Arjan by five o'clock.

Everything below follows from that order of operations. The five causes with the test for each. The published component weightings, so four weeks of effort land on the paper that actually carries the marks. The marking exercise almost no student has ever done. Four realistic plans with session counts, and what to stop doing in each. How to read a mock paper in three colours. Then the local arithmetic of an Al Barsha South evening, because a plan that assumes a 16:00 start in this district will not survive half-term.

dubai/al-barsha-south.programmesIntro: The programmes below are described by where each one loses marks, which is a more useful frame for this page than a description of their structures.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Marks are lost in three predictable places: the extra Higher Level paper, which students practise least; the internally assessed component, assessed against lettered criteria most candidates never read in full; and timing on long papers.
programmes.countryNote: In an Al Barsha South household the Diploma's coursework load is the component that disappears from view, because it never appears on a homework diary. A student with two weak papers and an unstarted exploration should spend the first block of sessions on the exploration, since a paper can be improved in the final eight weeks and a missed internal deadline cannot be recovered at all.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Terminal examinations in a June or November series. Cambridge uses codes such as 0580, 0625 and 0620 and tiers several subjects into Core and Extended; Pearson Edexcel uses 4MA1, 4PH1 and 4CH1 and tiers Mathematics into Foundation and Higher. Marks are lost on tariff reading, on practical-method questions and on the tier decision made months earlier.
programmes.countryNote: The structural trap at IGCSE is that mocks arrive before teaching finishes, so a weak mock may be testing untaught content. Separating untaught from misunderstood takes half an hour with the mock and the syllabus side by side, and it changes the plan completely. Al Barsha South families often skip this and buy general subject tuition instead.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria marked out of 8 and converted to a 1-7 grade. There is no compulsory external paper, so mark loss shows up as a low criterion strand rather than as a low percentage, which most parents cannot act on without the task-specific clarification the teacher wrote.
programmes.countryNote: For families here the useful move is to read the criterion profile rather than the overall grade. A student at 6 overall whose Criterion D is 3 has a specific, nameable problem: they are not evaluating or reflecting. That is far more actionable than a general concern, and it is also the best early warning for how a student will cope with Diploma Higher Level.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: A transdisciplinary framework with no external examination, ending in the Year 6 Exhibition. Reporting is formative and framed against learner attributes, so number fluency and reading-age gaps can persist unremarked until a child meets criterion-referenced assessment in Year 7.
programmes.countryNote: The quiet risk in a newer district with many primary-age children is that the first hard evidence of a gap arrives in Year 7, when criteria are suddenly applied. A short fluency check in Year 5 or 6, on arithmetic speed and reading rate rather than on curriculum content, is a cheap and effective piece of prevention.

dubai/al-barsha-south.subjectsIntro: Each note below names where the marks are lost in that subject rather than what the subject contains, because the second is in every prospectus and the first is not.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At Higher Level the loss concentrates in Paper 3, worth a fifth of the grade, because it rewards sustained reasoning rather than quick correct answers. At Standard Level it is method marks on questions answered correctly but without working. The exploration is the third loss point and it sits entirely outside lessons.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Marks go missing in interpretation rather than calculation. A correlation coefficient produced without a sentence explaining it in context collects the calculation mark and nothing above it. Students who treat the graphic display calculator as the answer rather than as a tool plateau in the middle bands.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Uncertainty treatment and extended written explanation account for most of the loss, in that order. The scientific investigation is marked on research design and evaluation, so a technically sound experiment with a thin evaluation caps well below its apparent quality. Mechanics rewards diagram discipline more than algebra.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole arithmetic that is almost automatic is the single biggest silent cost, because it slows everything downstream. Energetics and organic mechanisms carry the Higher Level difficulty, and data-based questions expect a structured error analysis that is rarely taught explicitly.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command terms decide this subject. Outline, explain, distinguish and evaluate each demand a different answer length and structure, and a student revising by rereading answers everything at a uniform length. The six-mark questions are where that habit costs most, and it is visible in a single marked paper.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy earns more than additional prose, and most lost marks are unlabelled axes or a missing shift. The three internally assessed commentaries, each within 800 words, are often written late and under the limit. Higher Level Paper 3 is quantitative and the least practised paper of the three.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen analysis under time pressure and is where grades separate. The loss is usually structural: a response that moves through the text chronologically rather than arguing a reading of it. The Individual Oral loses marks on a global issue too broad to anchor in two specific extracts.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Three recurring losses: no working shown on multi-step questions, so method marks vanish with the answer; algebraic manipulation that is slow rather than wrong, which costs time across the whole paper; and a Core or Foundation tier entry that caps the grade regardless of performance.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and waves produce the widest spread of marks. The Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper is a written paper about experiments, and students who revise theory alone lose marks on apparatus reading and variable identification, which are a separate and learnable skill.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Electrolysis cases confused with one another, mole calculations attempted without a structured layout, and qualitative analysis results half-remembered. All three are memorisation and layout problems rather than understanding problems, which is why they respond quickly to drilling.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Transport in plants, homeostasis and inheritance carry the hardest questions. The loss pattern is fluent paragraphs without the required terminology, which scores in the lower bands however well written. Writing in named terms is a habit that takes about three weeks to build.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 / Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: The plateau at grade B is a register and structure problem rather than a vocabulary one. Directed writing is marked on audience and purpose as much as accuracy, and the reading paper rewards selective quotation while punishing narration of the passage.

The output is a written statement of which of the five causes is actually operating, with the evidence from the paper quoted. Families who buy this first spend less overall, because it is the cheapest way to avoid paying for the wrong intervention for a term.

This is the right format when the diagnosis is technique or timing and the wrong one when content is genuinely missing. sections.heading: Five causes of lost marks and how to test for each
paragraphs: A report that says a student could do better has described the symptom. The useful work is identifying the mechanism, and there are far fewer mechanisms than there are subjects. Almost every mark lost by an able student in Al Barsha South falls into one of five categories, and each is testable in under an hour.

Absent content is the one families assume and the rarest in a student with a decent attendance record. It is tested with a blank-page recall exercise: name everything you know about this topic, unprompted. A student who produces a thin page on a topic they were taught last month has a genuine knowledge gap. A student who produces a thin page on a topic from eighteen months ago has decay instead, which is a revision scheduling problem rather than a teaching one.

Technique is the most common and the most quickly fixed. Give a student a marked question and the published scheme and ask them to award their own marks. The ones who cannot see why their answer scored four out of seven are reading the content of the question and not the tariff. That realisation changes scores within weeks because nothing new has to be learned.

Timing is tested with a clock and nothing else. Set a section of a paper to its real time allocation and stop at the bell. A student who would have scored well with ten more minutes has a pacing problem, which responds to practice at speed rather than to further teaching, and which no amount of content revision will touch.

Coursework is the fifth and the one that is invisible until it is late. A fifth or more of each IB subject grade sits in work produced outside lessons against lettered criteria. The test is simply to ask the student to read the criteria aloud and say what each requires. Most cannot, which is not their fault and is precisely why the marks are sitting there unclaimed.

sections.heading: Which paper is actually worth practising
paragraphs: Students practise the papers that are easiest to find, which means Paper 1 and Paper 2 in abundance and the paper that decides their grade hardly at all. Published component weightings make this trivially checkable, and almost no family has looked at them.

At Higher Level in Mathematics, Paper 3 carries a fifth of the grade and consists of extended multi-part problems that reward sustained reasoning. In Economics, Higher Level Paper 3 is quantitative and carries a comparable share. In the sciences the extended-response and data-handling questions occupy the equivalent role. In every case the paper is the least practised and the most decisive.

The internally assessed component is the other under-weighted item. A fifth or more of each subject grade, produced outside lessons, marked against published criteria. A student spending every spare hour on Paper 2 practice while an exploration sits at half-finished has their effort allocated backwards, and the arithmetic says so clearly.

There is a second-order effect worth naming. Because the heavy paper is the least practised, it is also the one where a student has the least sense of the standard expected. They know roughly what a good Paper 1 answer looks like because they have seen dozens. They have no model at all for an extended multi-part problem, so the first attempt is not merely weak; it is formless. Three marked attempts changes that more than three weeks of content revision does, which makes it the highest-return work available in the last two months before a series.

sections.heading: The marking exercise almost no student does
paragraphs: Ask a student how they revise and most describe reading, summarising, or watching an explanation. Ask them when they last marked their own work against a published scheme and the answer is usually never. That single omission accounts for more lost marks in this district than any topic in any syllabus.

Marking your own answer is uncomfortable because it makes the gap between what you meant and what you wrote visible. A student who thought they had explained the mechanism discovers the scheme wanted three specific linked statements and they made two. That discovery is worth more than an hour of teaching on the same topic, because the content was never the problem.

The exercise is simple and it is the core of a timed-paper block. Answer a question under time. Put it down. Take the published mark scheme and award marks ruthlessly, including nothing for intention. Write the lost marks in an error log by category rather than by topic: missing terminology, no working shown, wrong command term, ran out of time. After twenty questions the log repeats itself, and the repetitions are the plan.

Examination boards publish mark schemes and specimen material through their own channels, and they should be used from there rather than from any third party. Reproducing or redistributing board material is a copyright matter, so a tutor references and links the official source and works from the student's own copy. That is also the honest version: the resources are public, and the value a tutor adds is the marking discipline rather than access to documents.

sections.heading: Hours to grade: what a realistic plan looks like
paragraphs: Families ask how many sessions it will take, and the honest answer depends on which diagnosis applies and how many weeks remain. A technique problem eight weeks out is a different purchase from a content problem with eight weeks left, and pretending otherwise is how tuition acquires a reputation for not working.

If the diagnosis is technique or timing, six to eight weeks of twice-weekly timed practice produces a visible change, because nothing new has to be learned. If the diagnosis is decay, one session a week across two terms with a spaced revision schedule works and a crash course does not. If the diagnosis is absent content, the requirement is proportional to the amount missing and there is no shortcut; a student missing a term of physics needs a term to recover it.

If the diagnosis is coursework, the calendar decides rather than the hours. An internal deadline in six weeks means a block of six to ten sessions now, finishing before that date, and everything else waits. A paper can be improved in the final eight weeks before a series. A missed internal deadline cannot be recovered at any price, which is why it takes priority over a weak paper even when the paper feels more urgent.

sections.heading: Reading a mock paper properly
paragraphs: A mock result arrives as a number and a comment, and the number is the least informative part of it. The paper itself is the document worth half an hour, and most households never see it because it stays in a folder at school. Asking for it back is the single cheapest intervention available.

Work through it with three coloured marks. One for questions on content that had not been taught at the time of the mock, which in a Year 11 January mock can be a third of the paper. One for questions where the content was known and the answer scored poorly, which is technique. One for questions left blank or rushed at the end, which is timing. Three colours, one paper, and the diagnosis is usually unambiguous.

The common surprise is how large the first category is. Schools set mocks before teaching ends because the calendar requires it, so a mock grade is not a prediction of a final grade; it is a snapshot of a part-taught course. Parents who read a disappointing mock as a verdict make decisions on bad information, and students who read it the same way lose confidence they did not need to lose.

The second surprise is how often the technique category is dominated by a single habit. Answers at a uniform length regardless of tariff. No working shown. Narrating a passage instead of arguing about it. Diagrams without labels. One habit, appearing in twenty places, costing a grade, and fixable in a few weeks once it is named.

sections.heading: Revision methods that work and methods that feel like work
paragraphs: Most revision in this district consists of reading notes, making new notes, and watching video explanations. All three feel productive and all three are weak, because they let a student recognise material rather than retrieve it. Recognition collapses under examination conditions, which is why a student who revised for weeks can sit down and find nothing comes back.

The methods that work are uncomfortable in the same way that marking your own answer is uncomfortable. Blank-page recall: write everything you know about a topic with the book closed, then check. Timed questions with strict marking. Spaced return to a topic a week later, then a month later. Teaching a topic aloud to a parent who asks why. None of these are pleasant and all of them produce retrieval rather than recognition.

Scheduling matters as much as method. A student with six subjects and two terms needs a rota, not a feeling about what to do each evening. Three subjects a week on rotation, each visited twice a month, beats intensive attention to one subject followed by six weeks of neglect. The rota also stops the common pattern where a student revises the subject they enjoy and avoids the one they are failing.

There is a Ramadan and holiday consideration here that the generic advice ignores. Dubai school calendars include a shortened day during Ramadan and a long summer, and revision that depends on uninterrupted weeks will break. Planning around the actual calendar, including the weeks that will be lost, is more useful than a plan that assumes they will not be.

sections.heading: Arjan, Dubai Science Park and the honest start time
paragraphs: Al Barsha South was built later and taller than Al Barsha proper, which changes the practical arithmetic of an evening. Most households here are in apartments, most children commute outward by bus to schools in Al Barsha, Motor City or Dubai Hills, and arrival depends on the bus and then on the building.

The result is that 16:00 is a fiction for most of this district and 17:00 is honest. Al Barsha South 1 and 2, nearest the parent district, can often manage 16:30. Arjan, Dubai Science Park and the deeper South sections are realistically 17:00, and households in Motor City or Dubai Sports City attending Al Barsha schools are later still. Booking at the late edge of the window rather than the early edge is what keeps a slot alive past half-term.

The second local factor is the apartment itself. A diagnostic session needs a quiet surface, a stable connection and a screen large enough to read a past paper on, and in a two-bedroom flat with two children at home the quiet surface is the scarce resource. Deciding where it is before the first session, rather than during it, removes the most common cause of a disrupted lesson here.

Delivery over live video means nobody is in traffic on the Umm Suqeim Road or at the single-lane entries into Jumeirah Village Circle. It also means a session survives a family trip, a Ramadan timetable change and a move further inland to Dubai Hills, which in a district with this much turnover is worth more than it first appears.

sections.heading: What a diagnostic-led plan costs in this market
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates span a wide range and it is more useful to name the sources than to average them. One Dubai content provider advertises online tuition from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour and one platform from roughly AED 33 to AED 52. A Dubai agency publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. A Dubai cost survey reports in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 and specialist exam-year tuition at AED 200 to AED 450 and above; independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to AED 500. One premium provider publishes AED 650. Those are the providers' own published figures, reproduced as market context rather than as IB Gram's prices.

A diagnostic-led plan is usually cheaper than an open-ended weekly arrangement for the simple reason that it ends. One diagnostic session, then six to eight sessions aimed at the named cause, then a review. That is nine or ten sessions rather than thirty across a year, and a family that knows the total before starting is far more likely to finish it.

The expensive mistake is buying the wrong intervention for a term. Content teaching for a timing problem does nothing, and it is not cheap. Paper practice for a student with a genuine content gap also does nothing. An hour spent establishing which problem exists is the highest-return hour in the whole sequence, and it is one hour.

IB Gram quotes a rate after a trial rather than publishing one here, because it depends on level, subject scarcity and session length. What this page provides is the market context, so that any quote from any provider can be weighed against something real rather than against a feeling about what tutoring should cost.

sections.heading: Coursework feedback without crossing the line
paragraphs: A fifth or more of each IB subject grade sits in internally assessed work, so a coursework block is often the highest-value purchase available. It is also the place where the line between support and malpractice is crossed, sometimes without the student realising. One operation in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price; buying one is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the candidate.

The permitted support is real and useful. A tutor may teach the content, explain what each lettered criterion requires and how marks are allocated across them, interrogate a research question until it can be answered within the limits, say that a planned method will not generate usable data before three weeks go into it, read the student's own draft and name the criterion not yet met, and teach the referencing convention the school requires.

The prohibited support is specific. A tutor does not author any part of the work, does not supply sentences to be inserted, does not rewrite a paragraph into its final form, does not provide the data, and does not hand over a finished example to be adapted. A supervisor tests authenticity by conversation, asking the candidate to account for their own method and reasoning.

Stated as a working rule: the tutor's output is questions and criterion references, and the student's output is the document. A session where the tutor talks more than the student is probably going wrong. That is slower than the alternative and it is the only version that is safe for the candidate, which in the end is the only test that counts.

sections.heading: Starting with a diagnosis rather than a subject
paragraphs: Send the most recent marked paper rather than the report. The report contains a judgement; the paper contains evidence. If the mock paper is still at school, ask for it back, because it is the single most useful document a family can hold and it is routinely left in a folder.

Book one diagnostic session before anything recurring. Ninety minutes with a timed section, strict marking and the student marking their own answers. What you should receive afterwards is a written statement naming which of the five causes is operating, with the evidence quoted from the paper, and a session count for the fix. That is a document you can take to a head of year.

Then buy the block that matches the diagnosis and nothing else. Six to eight sessions of timed practice for a technique problem. A term of weekly work with a spaced schedule for decay. A coursework block timed to an internal deadline. Resist the instinct to book four subjects at once; an overloaded student in February is almost always doing too many things rather than too few.

Availability is finite and the pattern repeats across Dubai. Higher Level Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Economics are requested in the same late-afternoon window everywhere, and this district's later start times compete directly with everyone else's. If the slot you want is gone, the honest options are a different weekday, a weekend morning or a short wait. Lessons are online, one-to-one, over live video; there is no centre to attend and no tutor arriving at an Al Barsha South address.

process.title: Retrieve the marked paper
process.description: Ask the school for the mock or assessment paper itself rather than relying on the report. A report states a judgement; the paper shows where each mark was lost. Families who hold the paper can have a precise conversation with a tutor in the first ten minutes instead of the third session.

process.title: Buy one diagnostic session
process.description: Ninety minutes with a timed section of a real past paper, strict marking against the published scheme, and the student marking their own answers. The output is a written diagnosis naming which of the five causes applies, with the evidence quoted. It is the highest-return hour in the whole sequence.

process.title: Match the block to the diagnosis
process.description: Timed practice for technique and pacing. A weekly slot with a spaced schedule for decay. Sequential teaching only where content is genuinely absent. A coursework block where an internal deadline is the binding constraint. Buying the wrong block for a term is the expensive error, not the hourly rate.

process.title: Set the slot at the late edge of arrival
process.description: Al Barsha South 1 and 2 can usually hold 16:30; Arjan, Dubai Science Park and the deeper sections are realistically 17:00. Book the later time deliberately rather than optimistically, because a slot that is missed twice stops being a slot.

process.title: Review against the next school assessment
process.description: The school's own next assessment is the test of whether the diagnosis was right. Compare it with the error log. If the logged categories have shrunk and the mark has not, the diagnosis needs revisiting rather than the plan extending.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before purchase
whyPoints.description: One session with a past paper, a clock and the published scheme separates content, decay, technique, timing and coursework. Buying the wrong intervention for a term costs far more than the diagnostic that would have prevented it.

whyPoints.title: Blocks that end
whyPoints.description: Six to eight sessions for technique, a term for decay, a coursework block to an internal deadline. A defined block with a target gets finished, and the family knows the total before starting rather than discovering it in month four.

whyPoints.title: Practice aimed at the heaviest component
whyPoints.description: Students practise the papers that are easy to find rather than the paper that decides the grade. Published weightings make that checkable, and a plan built on them puts the next four weeks where the marks actually are.

whyPoints.title: Marking discipline rather than material
whyPoints.description: Board mark schemes and specimen papers are published through official channels and should be used from there. What a tutor adds is the discipline of marking ruthlessly and logging loss by category, which is what changes a score.

whyPoints.title: Figures you can trace
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is attributed to the provider or survey that published it. Nothing is presented as IB Gram's own price, and a quote from anyone can be weighed against the published market.

whyPoints.title: No claim that cannot be evidenced
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no permit, accreditation or partnership with KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and occupies no Dubai premises. Schools are named as commute and board context, never as relationships.

faqs.question: The report says my child is capable of more. What do we actually do with that?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a symptom and find the mechanism. An able student loses marks for one of five reasons: content never learned, content learned and decayed, an answer shaped wrongly for the command term and tariff, writing too slowly to show what they know, or an internally assessed component under-scoring. Each is testable in under an hour with a past paper, a clock and the published mark scheme. Until you know which one applies, any tuition you buy is a guess, and the wrong guess costs a term rather than an hour.

faqs.question: How do we tell a timing problem from a knowledge problem?
faqs.answer: With a clock. Set a section of a real past paper to its actual time allocation and stop at the bell. Then let the student finish the same section untimed, in a different colour. If the untimed work scores well, the problem is pacing and no amount of further teaching will touch it; it responds to practice at speed. If the untimed work scores badly too, the problem is content or technique, and the next test is whether the student can mark their own answer against the published scheme and see why it fell short.

faqs.question: Why does my child revise for hours and score the same?
faqs.answer: Because most revision produces recognition rather than retrieval. Reading notes, rewriting notes and watching explanations all let a student recognise material they could not have produced from a blank page, and recognition collapses under examination conditions. The methods that work are uncomfortable: blank-page recall with the book closed, timed questions marked strictly, returning to a topic a week and then a month later, and explaining a topic aloud to someone who asks why. Hours are not the variable; what happens inside them is.

faqs.question: Which paper should my child spend the next four weeks on?
faqs.answer: Whichever heavy component is least practised, which is usually not Paper 1. At Higher Level in Mathematics, Paper 3 carries a fifth of the grade with extended multi-part problems. Higher Level Economics Paper 3 is quantitative and carries a comparable share. The internally assessed component is a fifth or more of most subjects and is produced outside lessons. Check the weightings for your child's cohort with the subject teacher, because subject guides are revised, then put the next four weeks into the heaviest thing nobody has been practising.

faqs.question: Is a bad January mock a reliable prediction?
faqs.answer: No, and it is often badly misread. Schools set mocks before teaching finishes because the calendar requires it, so a Year 11 January mock can contain a third of the paper on content not yet covered. Go through the paper in three colours: untaught content, content known but answered poorly, and questions left blank or rushed. The first group should be set aside entirely. What remains is the real diagnostic, and it is usually much narrower than the overall mark suggests.

faqs.question: What does a diagnostic session actually produce?
faqs.answer: A written statement naming which of the five causes is operating, with the evidence quoted from the student's own paper, plus a session count for the fix. Not a verdict on the child and not a general impression. It should be specific enough to take to a head of year or a subject teacher and have a concrete conversation. If what comes back is a description of how hard the subject is and an offer of weekly lessons, the session has not done its job and the match is probably wrong.

faqs.question: How many sessions will it take to fix question technique?
faqs.answer: Six to eight weeks of twice-weekly timed practice usually produces a visible change, because nothing new has to be learned. The work is mechanical: answer under time, mark ruthlessly against the published scheme, log the loss by category rather than by topic. After about twenty questions the log starts repeating, and the repetitions are the plan. A technique problem is the cheapest of the five to fix, which is why establishing whether that is what you have is worth doing before buying anything longer.

faqs.question: My child has an unfinished Internal Assessment and two weak papers. Which first?
faqs.answer: The coursework, without hesitation. A paper can be improved in the final eight weeks before a series; a missed internal deadline cannot be recovered at any price, and that component is a fifth or more of the subject grade. Clear the deadline with a block of six to ten shorter sessions, then move to paper technique. Doing both at once is how students end up finishing neither. It feels wrong because the paper feels more urgent, and the arithmetic says otherwise.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give feedback on my child's exploration without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes. A tutor may teach the content, explain what each lettered criterion asks for and how marks are distributed, interrogate the research question until it is answerable within the limits, warn that a method will not produce usable data, read the student's own draft and name the criterion not yet met, and teach the referencing convention. A tutor may not author any part of it, supply sentences, rewrite a paragraph into final form, provide the data, or hand over a finished example to adapt. A useful working rule: the tutor's output is questions, the student's output is the document.

faqs.question: When can a weekday session start if we live in Arjan?
faqs.answer: Realistically 17:00. Al Barsha South is apartment-heavy with outward bus routes to schools in Al Barsha, Motor City and Dubai Hills, so arrival depends on the bus and then on the building lift. Al Barsha South 1 and 2, closest to the parent district, can often manage 16:30. Households in Motor City or Dubai Sports City attending Al Barsha schools are later still. Book the late edge of your arrival window on purpose: a slot missed twice in a term stops being a slot at all.

faqs.question: Does a tutor come to our apartment in Al Barsha South?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; home visits are offered only in India. Sessions run one-to-one over live video. For diagnostic work a shared screen is a better working surface than a table, because the past paper and the mark scheme can be annotated together and the session recorded, so a parent hears the diagnosis rather than a summary of it. The practical requirement at your end is a quiet surface and a screen large enough to read a paper on.

faqs.question: Where can we get past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: From the examination boards themselves, through their official channels, and from the school. Cambridge, Pearson and the IB publish specimen material and past material through their own sites and through school access, and a tutor should reference and link those rather than circulating copies. Reproducing or redistributing board material is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, worse than that. The value a tutor adds is not access to documents, which are largely public, but the discipline of marking strictly and logging what was lost.

faqs.question: How much should a diagnostic-led plan cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Work out the total, not the hourly rate. Published market bands, attributed: one Dubai provider advertises online tuition from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour, one platform from roughly AED 33 to AED 52, a Dubai agency publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, a Dubai cost survey reports specialist exam-year tuition at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and one premium provider publishes AED 650. A diagnostic plus eight sessions is nine or ten hours in total. Those figures belong to the providers who published them.

faqs.question: Should we book tutoring in more than one subject at once?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and almost never four. An overloaded student in February is usually doing too many things rather than too few, and adding contact hours reduces the practice time between sessions that actually produces the improvement. The sequence that works is one coursework block if a deadline is binding, then the single weakest subject, then a second if the first is holding. A rota across subjects for independent revision is different and does help, because it stops a student revising only what they enjoy.

faqs.question: How do we plan revision around Ramadan and the Dubai school calendar?
faqs.answer: By assuming the interruptions rather than hoping against them. Dubai schools run shortened days during Ramadan and a long summer break, and a revision plan that depends on uninterrupted weeks will break at the first one. Count the weeks that will actually be available, schedule a subject rota across those, and shift sessions rather than cancelling them, which during Ramadan often means a later slot after Iftar. A plan built on the real calendar finishes; one built on an ideal calendar is abandoned in the second month.

Ask the school for the marked paper, book a single diagnostic session, and expect a written statement naming which of the five causes is operating with the evidence quoted from your child's own work. Then buy only the block that matches it. Lessons run one-to-one over live video at a slot set for the late edge of your arrival window; no tutor is sent to an Al Barsha South address. Each teaches a named syllabus rather than a subject in general, and each works to your child's own school deadlines.

intro.heading: Why the Al Furjan school run decides your tutoring timetable
paragraphs: Al Furjan sits between Jebel Ali and Discovery Gardens, with Sheikh Zayed Road to the north and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road cutting across the back of the community. Almost no family here attends a school inside the community boundary for the whole of secondary. Children leave on a bus at around 06:50 or in a car at 07:05, and they come back between 15:20 and 16:50 depending on which bus loop they are on and whether the driver clears Al Yalayis Street before the Expo-era interchange backs up. That one fact governs everything about a tutoring plan, and it is the fact most tutoring websites ignore entirely.

The practical effect is that a 16:00 lesson, which is what most agencies default to, lands in the middle of a bus journey. A 16:30 lesson catches a child who has been awake for ten hours, still in uniform, and has not eaten since a 10:40 break. A 17:00 lesson works. A 19:30 lesson works better for a Year 12 or Year 13 student, because by then the younger siblings are settled and the house is quiet. None of this is a scheduling preference. It is the difference between a session where a student can hold a Paper 2 question in their head and a session where they cannot.

The second Al Furjan fact is the spread of schools. Children from the same street go to The Arbor School a few minutes away, to Delhi Private School in Dubai Investments Park, to The Winchester School in Jebel Ali, to Arcadia Global School or Sunmarke in Jumeirah Village Triangle, and to Greenfield International School for the IB Diploma. That means neighbours sitting the same subject are often on different boards, different option blocks and different internal deadline calendars. A tutor who teaches Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 is not automatically the right tutor for a child on Pearson Edexcel 4PH1, and a parent comparing notes at the padel courts may be comparing two different qualifications.

Online delivery is what makes this solvable. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For Al Furjan that restriction turns out to be an advantage rather than a compromise. A family looking for a Chemistry HL specialist is no longer limited to whoever is willing to drive out past the Expo site at 17:00 on a Tuesday, and the forty minutes that would have gone on a tutor's travel stays inside the lesson. The tutor appears at 17:00 because 17:00 is when your child is ready, not when the traffic allows.

This page covers what tutoring actually costs in this part of Dubai in AED, how an in-home visit compares with a one-to-one online session for an Al Furjan address, which session length suits which student, how the mandatory KHDA subjects fit alongside an international curriculum, and the boundary a tutor must respect around Internal Assessment and Extended Essay work. Every rate is attributed. Every regulatory point links to the authority that publishes it. Nothing on this page is a promise about a grade.

dubai/al-furjan.programmesIntro: Al Furjan children are spread across three or four different stages at any one time, and a household with a Year 6 and a Year 12 is running two unrelated academic calendars. These are the programmes we support for this community, with a note on what each one looks like from an Al Furjan address specifically.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is inquiry-led and has no external examinations, which means a parent gets very little numerical feedback until the exhibition year. Tutoring at this stage is about number fluency, reading stamina and written expression rather than exam technique. Short sessions work better than long ones, and progress is measured against the school's own reporting cycle rather than a grade boundary.
programmes.countryNote: For Al Furjan families the PYP question is usually timing rather than content: a Year 4 child who gets home at 15:20 can take a 30 or 45-minute slot at 16:15 and still have an evening. We keep primary sessions early in the day's remaining window and leave the later slots for secondary siblings who need them more.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP assessment runs on four criteria per subject, marked out of eight each, and converted to a 1-7 grade by a published boundary table the school sets. Students who have never seen the criteria lose marks for structure rather than knowledge. The step from MYP Year 11 into Diploma Year 12 is where most of the difficulty sits, particularly in Mathematics and the sciences.
programmes.countryNote: Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens families often move a child from an MYP school into an IGCSE school or the reverse, because the practical choice is driven by the bus route as much as the curriculum. We map what the new school assumes a Year 10 arrival already knows, subject by subject, before the first lesson rather than after the first report.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment worth roughly 20 to 25 per cent of the final grade, submitted months before the written papers. HL sciences add a third paper. The workload is not evenly spread: Year 12 term two and Year 13 term one carry most of the internal deadlines.
programmes.countryNote: There is no IB Diploma school inside Al Furjan itself, so DP students here commute - most often to Greenfield International School in Dubai Investments Park, Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City, or further to Dubai Hills and Al Barsha. A 60 to 80-minute round trip after a seven-hour school day is why we treat 19:30 as the default DP slot rather than the exception.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: A two-year course examined by terminal papers, tiered in several subjects as Core and Extended or Foundation and Higher. Cambridge runs June and November series; Pearson Edexcel runs May/June and November. The syllabus code on the front of the paper matters more than the subject name, because two boards teach different content under the same title.
programmes.countryNote: The IGCSE cohort is the largest single group we support in the Jebel Ali and Dubai South belt, because British-curriculum schools dominate enrolment in Dubai and almost all of them examine at 16. We ask for the syllabus code from your child's exam entry before the first session so the tutor teaches the paper your child will actually sit.

dubai/al-furjan.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Al Furjan parents contact us about most, with a note on where the marks are actually lost rather than a description of the course. A tutor is matched to one named syllabus in one named subject, not to a general science or maths brief.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Marks go on proof technique, on calculus applied to unfamiliar contexts, and on Paper 1 where no calculator is allowed. HL students who coped with MYP extended maths often meet their first real wall in the first term of Year 12. We work from the student's own school papers rather than a generic question bank.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The calculator-heavy route, built on modelling, statistics and real data. The mark loss is almost always interpretation: a correct regression with no sentence explaining what it means scores badly. AI HL also carries a demanding Paper 3. Choosing between AA and AI matters for some university courses, so we check the intended degree before advising.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics account for most dropped marks at HL, and the Internal Assessment account for a fifth of the grade. Students lose points for incomplete uncertainty treatment far more often than for a wrong result. HL adds a third paper with extended data analysis, which rewards practised structure.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields, circuits and anything requiring a free-body diagram are the recurring weak spots. The command term drives the mark scheme: a question saying deduce needs working, one saying state does not. We teach the command terms explicitly because a student who answers the wrong question loses the mark regardless of their physics.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The content volume defeats students before the difficulty does. Marks are lost on process questions about experimental design and on applying a known mechanism to an unseen organism. Precise terminology is non-negotiable in the mark scheme, so vocabulary drilling has a measurable return in this subject.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: The two boards look alike and are not. Cambridge 0580 splits Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 splits Foundation and Higher with a different grade ceiling on the lower tier. A student entered for the wrong tier cannot reach grade 9 no matter how well they are taught, so tier confirmation is the first thing we check.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics and Combined Science
subjects.description: Electricity and waves produce the heaviest mark loss, and the alternative-to-practical paper catches students who have never been taught how to read a question about apparatus. Combined Science compresses three subjects into fewer papers, which changes what can safely be left out.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry are the pivot: a student who is secure there usually recovers the rest. Qualitative analysis tables are memorisable marks that students routinely leave on the table. We work through the specification point by point and keep a visible list of what is secure.

subjects.name: IGCSE English Language and Literature
subjects.description: Directed writing and the comparative question carry the most recoverable marks. Students lose grades for ignoring the audience and form instruction rather than for weak writing. Literature marks hinge on close textual reference, which is a trainable habit.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay support
subjects.description: The Extended Essay is a 4,000-word independent research piece and TOK carries an exhibition and an essay. Our role is to teach research method, question framing and referencing, and to give feedback on what the student has already produced. The work itself stays entirely the student's own.

dubai/al-furjan.regionsIntro: Al Furjan does not sit alone. The Jebel Ali and Dubai South belt shares bus routes, schools and traffic patterns, and families move between these communities often enough that we treat them as one operating area with different travel times.

regions.name: Discovery Gardens
regions.note: A short hop north and the nearest dense apartment community, sharing the Route 2020 metro link. Many Discovery Gardens children attend the same Jebel Ali and Dubai Investments Park schools as Al Furjan, so sibling groups and study partners cross between the two communities constantly.

regions.name: Dubai Investments Park

sections.heading: What a search for IB and IGCSE tutors in Al Furjan usually means
paragraphs: Almost nobody searching this phrase wants general academic enrichment. The search comes from one of four moments: a report card with a grade lower than expected, a mock paper that went badly, a Year 9 options form with a deadline on it, or a Diploma student who has realised in November of Year 13 that the Internal Assessment deadlines and the written papers are closer together than they assumed. Each of those needs a different response, and treating them identically is why so much tutoring produces no measurable change.

The second thing behind the search is a practical constraint rather than an academic one. An Al Furjan parent is not asking whether tutoring helps in general. They are asking whether an hour can be found on a Tuesday that does not collide with a 15:45 bus arrival, football training at 18:00 and a 21:00 bedtime, and whether the person teaching that hour knows the difference between Cambridge 0580 Extended and Pearson 4MA1 Higher. Those are answerable questions, and this page answers them.

The third is cost, and almost nobody in this market will tell you a number. Three of the six best-ranking pages for tutoring queries in Dubai publish no price at all, and two of the remaining pages quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family transacts in. Published market bands in AED are further down this page, attributed to who published them. Our own model is a free trial lesson and a consultation first, because the right session length and frequency cannot be set before someone has seen the student work.

sections.heading: The Al Furjan clock: when a lesson can realistically start
paragraphs: This is the part no tutoring site writes down, and it is the single most useful thing on this page for a family living here. Al Furjan's school population leaves early and returns late relative to communities nearer the centre of Dubai, because most secondary provision sits outside the community. The bus loop that serves Al Furjan South and Al Furjan North picks up between 06:40 and 07:05 and drops back between 15:20 and 16:50, with the later end of that range applying to anyone whose route includes Dubai Investments Park or Jumeirah Village.

Working forward from the drop-off gives a usable timetable rather than a guess. Twenty to thirty minutes to change, eat and decompress is not a luxury; a session that starts before it produces a student who is physically present and cognitively absent. That puts the first viable weekday slot at 17:00 for most secondary students, 16:15 to 16:30 for primary children on short routes, and 19:30 for anyone commuting from a Diploma school further out.

The table below maps the weekday as it actually runs in this community, and what a tutor can usefully do with each block. During Ramadan every row after 16:00 shifts, and we move sessions to sit after Iftar rather than trying to hold the same clock. Families who travel during the long summer keep their slot by time zone instead: a tutor delivering over live video can hold an Al Furjan student's 19:30 slot while the family is in London or Kochi, which an in-home arrangement cannot do at all.

sections.heading: Route 2020, the school bus and the Al Yalayis corridor
paragraphs: The metro changed Al Furjan's commuting arithmetic without changing its school arithmetic. Route 2020 put Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens stations on the network, which helps a parent working in Business Bay far more than it helps a Year 10 student, because school buses still run on roads and almost no Dubai private school is entered on foot from a metro station. Parents regularly assume the metro link means a shorter school day. It does not.

What the corridor does affect is the parent's own return home. A mother or father who finishes work in Media City or DIFC and relies on the metro is often back later than the children, which is why a tutoring slot that needs adult supervision to start is fragile here. Online one-to-one sessions solve that specific problem: the tutor joins the call at the agreed time whether or not an adult is standing over the laptop, and the session log shows exactly what was covered.

There is one further local detail worth planning around. Al Yalayis Street and the interchanges towards the Expo City site carry heavy construction and freight traffic through the working day, and a delay there does not announce itself in advance. A family depending on a tutor driving in from Mirdif or Al Nahda to reach an Al Furjan address at 17:00 is depending on that road behaving. Removing the drive removes the risk, and it is the reason we treat online delivery here as the sensible format rather than a second-best substitute.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs around Al Furjan in AED
paragraphs: Published rates in this market vary by a factor of roughly fifteen between the cheapest and the most expensive hour, and the variation is not random. It tracks four things: whether the tutor holds a subject degree and real classroom experience, whether they teach the specific syllabus your child sits, whether travel is included in the hour, and whether the session is one-to-one or shared. The figures in the table below are market rates published by other providers, not an IB Gram price list.

Two things in the table deserve a parent's attention. The first is that the in-home band carries the tutor's travel inside it, which is why a visit to Al Furjan from a tutor living in Deira is priced differently from the same hour online. The second is that the premium band exists because a small number of providers charge for scarcity rather than for a measurably better hour. A named examiner-led rate at the top of the range is not automatically a better choice for a Year 10 student struggling with moles.

For context, Dubai's school fees were held flat for 2026-27: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for that academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Tutoring is the part of the education budget a family can still control, which makes it worth setting the number deliberately rather than by default. We ask what the household wants to spend over a term before recommending a session length and frequency, and a free trial lesson comes before any commitment.

sections.heading: In-home tutoring in Al Furjan compared with one-to-one online
paragraphs: This comparison is the honest centre of the page, because the phrase most Al Furjan parents type includes the word home. In-home tutoring is a real service in Dubai and a reasonable thing to want. It also carries costs that are invisible until you book it: the travel is inside the price, the tutor pool shrinks to people willing to drive to your community at your time, and a single bad hour on Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road takes the first fifteen minutes of your lesson.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; that is an India-only service, and nothing on this page should be read as an offer to send someone to a UAE address. What we do instead is one-to-one live video, which changes the arithmetic in a way that favours a community sitting on the edge of the city. The pool of available Chemistry HL specialists stops being a map problem. A student in Al Furjan and a student in Al Barsha access the same tutor, on the same terms, at the time each of them can actually work.

The table sets both options against the things that decide an outcome. We have not scored the comparison in our favour on points where in-home genuinely wins: a very young child who needs a physical presence at the table, or a household with no reliable quiet space and no second screen, is better served by someone in the room. Those two cases are real, and when they describe your household we will say so rather than sell you a format that will not work.

sections.heading: Choosing between a 45, 60 and 90-minute session
paragraphs: Session length is the decision parents think about least and the one that most often explains why tutoring did not work. A 90-minute block with a Year 8 student produces forty good minutes and fifty expensive ones. A 45-minute slot with a Year 13 doing a timed Paper 2 question with feedback does not have room for the task. The right answer depends on the student's age, the work in front of them and the time the session sits in the Al Furjan evening.

There is a second constraint specific to this community. A 17:00 start and a 19:00 football session at the community courts leaves exactly enough room for sixty minutes plus the walk, and not for ninety. Families who book a 90-minute slot into that gap end up cutting ten minutes off each end, which converts a planned block into something shorter and less useful than a booked 60-minute session would have been. We would rather set the length to fit the evening you actually have.

Frequency works the same way. Two sessions a week in one subject beats one session a week in two subjects for a student heading into a terminal exam series, because the gap between contact points is what determines how much has to be re-established at the start of each lesson. A student eight weeks from a Cambridge June paper is a different planning problem from a student in October of Year 10, and the plan should say so.
