sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects running alongside IGCSE and the Diploma
paragraphs: Every private school in Dubai teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of the international curriculum it is licensed to deliver. KHDA published its mandatory-subject requirements with implementation from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, and they apply to The Arbor School, Sunmarke, Delhi Private School and every other school an Al Furjan child attends. Most tutoring websites in this market mention Arabic only as a subject chip in a list, and none of them explain the rules.

Two of those rules matter for planning. KHDA requires schools to organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. KHDA also sets the language of instruction: Standard Arabic for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

The instructional-time rule is worth knowing too: mandatory-subject time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should be at least 25 minutes. For the mandatory subjects, use of different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is not allowed, so tutoring here means helping a student with the school's own material rather than substituting a different scheme. KHDA also requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects - a credential question worth asking of anyone offering to help.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an Internal Assessment or Extended Essay
paragraphs: This boundary is worth stating plainly, because at least one provider ranking for these searches sells finished Internal Assessments at a fixed price. Buying one is an academic-honesty breach under IB rules, and the consequence lands on the student rather than on the seller: a malpractice finding can cost a Diploma. Any site offering to supply a completed piece of assessed work is offering your child a risk, whatever the page calls it.

What legitimate support looks like is specific. A tutor teaches research method and how to frame a workable question. A tutor explains each assessment criterion and the marks attached to it, so the student knows what a top band actually requires. A tutor reads what the student has already produced and gives feedback on structure, reasoning, use of evidence and referencing. A tutor runs a session on data handling, uncertainty treatment or citation style. A tutor helps a student plan backwards from the school's internal deadline so the piece is finished before the week it is due.

What a tutor must not do is contribute content to the submitted piece, restructure it into its final shape, or correct it line by line until it is no longer the student's own expression. The supervisor at your child's school signs a declaration about authenticity, and schools now routinely compare a student's written style across pieces. We tell students this in the first session on any core component, and we keep a record of what each session covered so a supervisor asking what support was received has a straight answer available.

sections.heading: The first four weeks, and what happens when no specialist is free
paragraphs: The honest version of getting started is less tidy than most tutoring pages suggest. The first conversation establishes four things: the exact syllabus code, the school's internal deadline calendar, what the last two assessments actually showed, and which evening slots in your Al Furjan week are genuinely free rather than theoretically free. We then run a free trial lesson with the proposed tutor before anything is booked, because a match that looks right on paper sometimes is not right in the room.

Weeks two to four are diagnostic as much as instructional. A tutor working with a Year 11 on Cambridge 0580 Extended will usually spend part of the first two sessions establishing which specification points are secure, because a student who says they find algebra hard is often fine with manipulation and lost in function notation. That mapping is what makes the remaining weeks efficient, and it is the step a cheap hour of homework supervision skips entirely.

Sometimes the answer is that nobody suitable is available at the time you need. A Year 13 asking for HL Further Mathematics at 17:30 on a Thursday is a narrow request, and we would rather say so than put a generalist in front of your child. In that case we offer a different time with the right specialist, a different specialist at your time with a clear description of what they do and do not cover, or a short wait with a date attached. No competitor in this market publishes a coverage limit; we would rather lose the booking than pretend.

process.title: Tell us the syllabus, not just the subject
process.description: Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 are both called IGCSE Chemistry and they are not the same course. The exam entry or a recent paper gives us the code, the tier and the board, and that single detail decides which tutor is the right one. Your child's school office can confirm it in a sentence.

process.title: Map the week against the Al Furjan school run
process.description: We ask when the bus actually arrives, what training or activities sit in the evening, and whether a parent is still commuting at 18:30. The slot we propose is one your family can hold for a whole term, because a slot that collapses in week three was never the right slot.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One full session with the proposed tutor, with no commitment attached and nothing to pay. You see how the tutor explains, your child decides whether they can work with them, and we get a diagnostic read on where the marks are currently going. If the match is wrong we propose a different tutor.

process.title: Agree a plan with a visible endpoint
process.description: Session length, frequency and the first four topics, written down against the school's own deadline calendar and the relevant exam series. For a Year 11 in October that plan looks different from one made in March, and the plan should say which it is.

process.title: Review at week four and adjust
process.description: We look at what the school's assessments show, what the session notes record, and whether the slot is still working against the family's week. Frequency goes up before a paper and down after one. Nothing is locked in for a year, because no honest plan can be.

whyPoints.title: The timetable is built around this community, not around a tutor's drive
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video, so the hour starts when your child is ready. For a community on the western edge of Dubai, with secondary schools mostly outside its boundary, that removes the single biggest reason a tutoring arrangement quietly stops after a few weeks.

whyPoints.title: One named syllabus, one matched tutor
whyPoints.description: We match on the exam board, the code and the tier, not on the subject name. A tutor who knows where Pearson 4MA1 Higher differs from Cambridge 0580 Extended saves a term of teaching content that will not be examined.

whyPoints.title: Rates in AED, with the source named
whyPoints.description: The bands published on this page are market rates with the provider who published them stated. We do not present them as our own prices, and we do not quote in dollars. Our own model starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation about what the household wants to spend.

whyPoints.title: A stated boundary on assessed work
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches the criteria, the method and the referencing, and gives feedback on what the student has produced. Content for a submitted Internal Assessment or Extended Essay is never supplied. Session notes exist so a school supervisor can see exactly what support was given.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits are disclosed, not hidden
whyPoints.description: If no specialist in a narrow subject is free at the time you need, we say so and offer alternatives with dates attached. A generalist placed in front of an HL student to fill a slot wastes the money and the term, which is worse than an honest no.

faqs.question: How much does an IB or IGCSE tutor cost for a family in Al Furjan?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in Dubai run roughly AED 45-150 an hour for budget online tutoring, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180-500 for an in-home visit with travel inside the price, and AED 200-450 or more for an IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist. Those are other providers' figures, attributed in the rate table on this page, not an IB Gram price list. Monthly bundles in this market run from around AED 799 for eight online sessions. We start with a free trial lesson and a conversation about what the household wants to spend across a term.

faqs.question: What time can a tutoring session realistically start in Al Furjan on a school night?
faqs.answer: For a secondary student, 17:00 Gulf Standard Time is the first slot that works. The Al Furjan bus loop drops back between 15:20 and 16:50 depending on route, and a student needs twenty to thirty minutes to change and eat before anything useful happens. Primary children on short routes can take 16:15 or 16:30. Diploma students commuting from Dubai Investments Park or further out are better at 19:30, when the house is quiet and a 90-minute block is realistic. During Ramadan every evening slot moves to sit after Iftar.

faqs.question: Do your tutors travel to villas and apartments in Al Furjan?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send a tutor to any address in the UAE; visits to a student's home are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video. For Al Furjan that works in your favour more often than against it: your child is matched to a specialist in the exact subject and syllabus rather than to whoever is willing to drive out past the Expo site at 17:00, and the thirty to forty minutes a round trip would consume stays inside the teaching hour instead.

faqs.question: Which schools do children living in Al Furjan usually attend?
faqs.answer: The community itself has The Arbor School, and families commonly travel to Arcadia Global School and Sunmarke School in Jumeirah Village Triangle, The Winchester School in Jebel Ali, Delhi Private School Dubai and Nibras International School in Dubai Investments Park, and Greenfield International School or Fairgreen International School for the IB Diploma. Nord Anglia International School Dubai and JSS International School also draw from here. These schools run different boards and different option blocks, so two children on the same street may be sitting genuinely different courses.

faqs.question: Is online tuition workable for a Year 11 student preparing for IGCSE papers?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the sessions are one-to-one and the tutor teaches the specific syllabus. Year 11 work is largely past-paper diagnosis, specification coverage and exam technique, all of which transfer well to a shared screen with an annotatable document. What matters more than the format is the gap between sessions and whether the tutor has the real mark scheme in front of them. For practical subjects we work through the alternative-to-practical paper explicitly, since that is where students who have never been taught apparatus questions lose marks.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Dubai need a MoHRE permit, and can we check?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through a MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask any tutor directly whether they hold the permit, and apply through the MoHRE smart app or website.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both IGCSE Maths and IGCSE Physics for an Al Furjan student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. A mathematician who has taught Cambridge 0625 Physics for several years can genuinely do both, and a single tutor across two subjects saves scheduling effort and builds a better picture of the student. The point at which it stops working is depth: a student aiming for a top grade in Extended Physics while also fixing algebraic weakness usually needs two specialists. We tell you which situation you are in rather than selling the convenient answer.

faqs.question: How quickly can you match a DP Chemistry tutor for a student in Al Furjan?
faqs.answer: Common subject and level combinations are usually matched within a few working days, and a free trial lesson follows soon after. Narrow requests take longer: HL Further Mathematics, a less common Group 2 language, or a specific slot like 17:30 on a Thursday can all reduce the available pool sharply. In that case we give you a choice between a different time with the right specialist, a different tutor at your time with a clear account of what they cover, or a short wait with a date attached. We do not fill a slot with a generalist.

faqs.question: Can lessons move to after Iftar during Ramadan for an Al Furjan family?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families here ask for it. School hours shorten during Ramadan, the whole household's rhythm shifts, and a 17:00 session stops making sense. We move weekday slots to sit after Iftar, usually between 21:00 and 22:30, and we often shorten them to 45 minutes while increasing the number of contact points in the week. Because every lesson is over live video there is no travel to renegotiate, which makes a temporary timetable change a two-minute conversation rather than a reason to pause tutoring for a month.

faqs.question: What happens to our sessions during the Cambridge November exam series?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, and every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version. Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct zone timetable and cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. We plan the final six weeks backwards from your child's actual paper dates, taken from the school's own entry confirmation, and we increase session frequency through the series rather than stopping.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help my child with the Mathematics Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor teaches what each assessment criterion rewards and how many marks it carries, helps the student find a workable exploration topic, explains mathematical communication and referencing conventions, and gives feedback on a draft the student has produced alone. A tutor does not supply content, restructure the piece into its final shape or edit it line by line. Your child's supervisor signs an authenticity declaration, and we keep session notes so that declaration can be made accurately. Any service selling finished coursework is selling your child a malpractice finding.

faqs.question: Do you support the KHDA mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons?
faqs.answer: We support students with their school's own material for these subjects. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum they are licensed to teach, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups and specified languages of instruction. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is not allowed, so the work is consolidation of the school scheme. KHDA also requires that school teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education hold appropriate KHDA approval, which is a fair question to ask any tutor.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week do Al Furjan Diploma families usually start with?
faqs.answer: Most start with one 90-minute session a week in the subject causing the most concern, then add a second subject or a second session once the first slot has proved it can survive the family's actual week. Two sessions a week in one subject generally beats one session a week in two subjects when a terminal paper is close, because the gap between contact points decides how much ground has to be re-established each time. Frequency should rise through the term before the papers and fall afterwards rather than staying fixed for a year.

faqs.question: What does my child need for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency after IGCSE?
faqs.answer: On the British track, the Ministry requires proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, plus passes in five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic Education are not counted among those five. One competing tutoring site states that UAE candidates need six IGCSE subjects, which is wrong. Verify your own child's position on the Ministry's own channel; equivalency is not something a tutoring service performs.

faqs.question: Is there a trial lesson before we commit to anything in Al Furjan?
faqs.answer: Yes. One full one-to-one session with the tutor we propose, at no cost and with no card details taken, before any booking exists. You hear how the tutor explains a topic, your child decides whether they can work with that person, and we get a diagnostic read on where marks are currently being lost. If the match is wrong we propose a different tutor rather than asking you to make the best of it. Nothing is locked into a term-length commitment at that stage.

dubai/al-furjan.closingHeading: Start with the clock, then the syllabus
dubai/al-furjan.closingBody: If you live in Al Furjan and you are looking for an IB or IGCSE tutor, begin with two pieces of information: the time your child is genuinely free on a school night, and the syllabus code on their exam entry. With those two facts we can tell you quickly whether a specialist is available in that window, what the market charges for that hour, and what a sensible first four weeks looks like against your school's own deadline calendar. The trial lesson is free and carries no commitment. If we cannot cover what your child needs at the time you need it, we will tell you that instead of filling the slot.

dubai/al-garhoud.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work the way this page does: from the student's own marked script, against the published criteria and command terms, in the subjects Al Garhoud families most often need, across the Diploma sciences, Mathematics, Economics and the IGCSE core.

intro.heading: A neighbourhood where the student has to be self-sufficient
paragraphs: Al Garhoud is an older, low-rise district wedged between Dubai International Airport, the creek and the Dubai Creek Golf Club, with villa plots, mid-rise apartment stock and a long-resident population rather than a transient one. A substantial share of its households are aviation households: pilots, cabin crew, engineers, airport and airline staff, many on shift patterns and many away for several days at a stretch.

That shapes what tutoring has to achieve here. In a household where one parent is away three nights a week and the other is on a roster, nobody is sitting over a Year 11 student every evening checking what was lost on the last paper. The student has to be able to do that themselves. Which means the most valuable thing a tutor can transfer is not content but diagnosis: the ability to look at a marked script, see why the marks went, and know what to do next.

So this page publishes the diagnostic apparatus rather than describing it. It lists the command terms and states what each one actually demands, because a well-written answer to the wrong command term scores close to nothing. It names the Internal Assessment criteria by letter with their mark allocations, which no competing page in this market does for a single subject. It gives the paper weightings at both levels, so a student knows which component is worth protecting. And it gives the word limits for every assessed component in one place.

A parent can hand this page to a sixteen-year-old and it does some work on its own. That is deliberate. The households here need a student who can self-correct between sessions, and the fastest route to that is giving them the specification's own language rather than a motivational summary of it.

Delivery is one-to-one online, over live video, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own script on screen. Tutors are not sent to addresses in the UAE; home visiting is an India-only service. In Al Garhoud that is also practically convenient, because a shift-pattern household needs a slot that can be set independently of who is home, and a video lesson does not require a parent to be present to open a door.

Every weighting, criterion and limit below should be confirmed against the current subject guide for your child's cohort, because the IB revises guides on a rolling cycle and your teacher holds the version that applies. No IB examination or results date appears on this page, because the IB's own site could not be verified for this project. What is published here instead are the things that do not move from year to year: what a command term demands, which criteria an Internal Assessment is marked against, how much each paper is worth and how many words a component allows. Those are the figures a student can plan around, and they are the ones competitors in this market leave out entirely.

dubai/al-garhoud.programmesIntro: Three programmes matter in the creek-side cluster, and each has a different diagnostic signature. These notes describe what a weak grade in each actually tells you.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, converted to a 1-7 grade. The diagnostic value is high because the criterion scores are written on the task sheet: a student can see exactly which of four things they did badly. The failure mode is nobody ever reading them, so the grade looks like a general verdict rather than four specific ones.
programmes.countryNote: For a self-managing Al Garhoud student this is the easiest programme to self-diagnose, precisely because the criterion scores are itemised. Teaching a Year 8 or Year 9 student to read their own criterion scores across three tasks is a twenty-minute job that pays for itself for years.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, with an Internal Assessment in every subject and markschemes behind every paper. A Diploma grade is an aggregate of components with known weights, which means a disappointing grade can always be decomposed into which component caused it. Most students never do that decomposition.
programmes.countryNote: The practical point for Al Garhoud families is arithmetic. If the science Internal Assessment carries 20 per cent and a student is sitting on a weak mark in it, no amount of paper practice recovers that 20 per cent. Knowing which component is the problem is what makes a revision plan rational rather than anxious.

programmes.name: Cambridge International GCSE
programmes.description: Terminally examined with syllabus codes that determine everything: Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, English First Language 0500. Core and Extended tiers exist in several subjects, with Core capped at a lower grade ceiling. Command terms carry explicit mark expectations, which is where most recoverable marks sit.
programmes.countryNote: The creek-side cluster has a broad curriculum mix, so a Garhoud household may have a Cambridge candidate and a Pearson candidate under one roof. Check each child's entry statement for the code, because Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 are different papers with different question conventions.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Single-tier in most subjects, with codes including 4MA1 for Mathematics, 4PH1 for Physics and 4CH1 for Chemistry, and a modular structure available in some subjects. Pearson runs May and June and November series, and publishes provisional timetables ahead of each, which can be revised.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Garhoud school enters Pearson, the modular option in some subjects is worth asking about, because it changes when the pressure falls across Years 10 and 11. Work from the live official timetable on the Pearson site rather than a date transcribed into a planner in September.

dubai/al-garhoud.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is described by where the marks actually go, not by what the syllabus contains. That is the information a self-managing student can act on without waiting for the next session.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Paper 1 carries 36 per cent and Paper 2 44 per cent, with the Internal Assessment at 20 per cent at both levels. Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms produce most of the lost marks at Higher Level, and in the data-based section students read a graph gradient correctly and then omit the units.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Same structure: Paper 1 at 36 per cent, Paper 2 at 44 per cent, Internal Assessment at 20 per cent. Extended-response marks go missing on the command term rather than the physics: a student describes a phenomenon where the question asked them to explain it in terms of a named quantity.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Paper 1 36 per cent, Paper 2 44 per cent, Internal Assessment 20 per cent. The highest-volume content load of the three sciences, and the one where command terms matter most: outline, describe, explain and evaluate have different mark ceilings and students routinely answer one when asked for another.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At Standard Level, Papers 1 and 2 are 40 per cent each with the exploration at 20. At Higher Level it is 30, 30, 20 for Paper 3 and 20 for the exploration. Paper 1 is non-calculator, and the commonest loss is an unjustified step, because method marks are itemised in the markscheme.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator permitted throughout, same weighting structure as Analysis. Marks are lost in interpretation: writing that a result is significant without naming the test, the variables and the significance level the question specified, which the markscheme requires explicitly.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: At Standard Level, Paper 1 is 30 per cent, Paper 2 40 and the Internal Assessment 30. At Higher Level it is 20, 30, Paper 3 at 30 and the Internal Assessment at 20. Each of the three commentaries is capped at 800 words, and marks sit in the link between diagram, theory and the article.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.description: At Standard Level, Paper 1 and Paper 2 carry 35 per cent each with the Individual Oral at 30. At Higher Level, Paper 1 is 35, Paper 2 25, the Individual Oral 20 and the HL Essay 20. The Individual Oral is where most grades actually move, because it rewards rehearsed, timed precision.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The Internal Assessment is a historical investigation of up to 2,200 words, structured in three sections: identification and evaluation of sources, the investigation itself, and a reflection. Students routinely under-weight the source evaluation section relative to the marks it carries.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1
subjects.description: Extended tier is needed for most post-16 routes. Bounds, surds, algebraic fractions and graph transformations appear every series. The commonest avoidable loss is a correct answer with no working on a multi-mark question, because method marks are allocated to steps.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics and Chemistry
subjects.description: The practical-skills component is where marks are cheapest to recover. Candidates asked to suggest an improvement to a method describe the method instead, and candidates asked to criticise a graph read values off it. Both are behaviours, not knowledge gaps.

subjects.name: IGCSE Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy and command-term sensitive. The six-mark extended questions reward a structured answer with the named terminology, and students who write fluent general prose score roughly half of what a bulleted technical answer would.

subjects.name: IGCSE English First Language
subjects.description: Marks are lost on form and audience rather than language quality. A candidate who writes an article in letter form is penalised under the form criterion however well it is written, and directed writing tasks specify the audience for a reason.

sections.heading: Command terms, and the cheapest marks in the building
paragraphs: Of all the recoverable marks in an IB or IGCSE paper, the largest single pool sits in command terms, and almost nobody teaches them explicitly. A command term is the verb at the start of a question, and it is not decoration. It specifies the assessment objective being tested, which determines what the markscheme will credit. A technically perfect answer to the wrong command term scores a fraction of the available marks.

The pattern is consistent across subjects and across boards. Students treat describe, explain, outline, discuss and evaluate as rough synonyms for write about this, and they are not. Describe asks for features without reasons. Explain requires a causal mechanism. Discuss requires more than one position. Evaluate requires a judgement supported by weighted evidence. Each of those is a different answer, and only one of them earns the marks on any given question.

This is the most self-serviceable thing on the page. A student who spends twenty minutes learning the command terms properly, and then goes back through a marked mock highlighting every question where they answered a different term from the one asked, will usually find several marks per paper. In a household where a parent travels and nobody is checking nightly, that is work a sixteen-year-old can genuinely do alone.

The table lists the terms that recur most and what each demands. The right-hand column gives the characteristic error, which is what to look for in a marked script. Confirm the exact definitions in the command-term glossary of your child's current subject guide, because the wording is set per subject group and the guides are revised.

sections.heading: Internal Assessment criteria, named by letter with their marks
paragraphs: Across the competitor pages fetched for this project, not one names a single Internal Assessment criterion. That is a striking gap, because the criteria are the specification. An Internal Assessment is not marked on general quality; it is marked against named criteria with fixed mark allocations, and a student who has not read them is guessing at a target that is published.

The sciences are the clearest case. The Diploma scientific investigation is assessed against four criteria, Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation, each carrying six marks for a total of 24, and the whole thing is worth 20 per cent of the subject grade at both Standard and Higher Level. That means a student who neglects Evaluation entirely has written off a quarter of the Internal Assessment marks and five per cent of the subject, regardless of how good the experiment was.

Mathematics works differently. The exploration is assessed against five criteria: Presentation worth four marks, Mathematical communication worth four, Personal engagement worth three, Reflection worth three and Use of mathematics worth six, giving twenty marks and 20 per cent of the grade. Use of mathematics is the heaviest single criterion, which is why an exploration with a modest mathematical core cannot reach the top band however nicely it is presented.

sections.heading: Paper weightings: which component is worth protecting
paragraphs: A Diploma subject grade is an arithmetic aggregate of components with published weights, which means a disappointing grade can always be decomposed. Most students never do that decomposition, and so revise the subject they feel worst about rather than the component carrying the most recoverable marks. Those are rarely the same thing.

The practical question is simple: for each subject, which single component carries the most weight, and how is the student currently performing in it? In the sciences, Paper 2 at 44 per cent is the heaviest component by a clear margin, and the Internal Assessment at 20 per cent is the one that can be improved before the examination rather than during it. In English at Standard Level the Individual Oral at 30 per cent is the largest single component and the most coachable.

The arithmetic matters because it changes the plan. If a student is sitting on a weak Internal Assessment mark in a science, no amount of paper practice recovers that 20 per cent, and the available improvement is capped before revision begins. Conversely, a student with a strong Internal Assessment has 80 per cent still in play and should be putting hours into Paper 2.

sections.heading: Word and page limits across every assessed component
paragraphs: This is a reference table nobody in this market publishes, and it causes real damage by its absence. Assessed components carry limits, and exceeding them does not simply lose a mark or two. Depending on the component, material beyond the limit may not be read at all, which means a conclusion written past the word count is a conclusion that does not exist as far as the marks are concerned.

The limits also shape the work. A Theory of Knowledge essay at 1,600 words cannot sustain four knowledge questions, and a student who tries produces four shallow ones. An Economics commentary at 800 words cannot carry both a full theoretical exposition and an article analysis, which is why the marks sit in the link between them rather than in either alone. Understanding the limit is understanding the task.

Students consistently misjudge in one direction. They over-write the descriptive sections and arrive at the analytical ones with no words left, because the descriptive part is easier. The fix is a word budget allocated by criterion before writing starts: if Evaluation carries a quarter of the marks, it gets roughly a quarter of the words. That single habit changes outcomes more than most content teaching.

Confirm every limit against the current subject guide for your child's cohort before relying on it. These are the widely published figures for current guides, and the IB revises guides on a rolling cycle, so the version your child's teacher holds is the authoritative one.

sections.heading: Where marks actually go in an IGCSE paper
paragraphs: IGCSE papers reward a narrower set of behaviours than students expect, and the losses are highly predictable across series. Four patterns account for most of them, and all four are technique rather than knowledge.

The first is unshown working. On a multi-mark Mathematics question, method marks are allocated to specific steps, and a correct final answer with no visible method scores a fraction of the total. This is the single most common avoidable loss in Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1, and it is entirely a habit problem. The second is command-term mismatch, already covered above, which bites hardest in the six-mark extended responses in Biology and Chemistry.

The third is the practical-skills component in the sciences. Candidates asked to suggest an improvement to a method describe the method; candidates asked to criticise a graph read values off it; candidates asked to identify a source of error name human error, which earns nothing. These questions appear in every series and the correct behaviours are a short list that can be taught in a couple of sessions.

The fourth is form and audience in English. A candidate who writes an article in letter form, or who ignores the specified audience in a directed writing task, is penalised under the form criterion however good the language is. All four of these are correctable from a marked script in a way that content gaps are not, which is why a mock paper is worth more than a term of general revision.

sections.heading: Reading a mock script in fifteen minutes
paragraphs: This is the skill worth transferring to a student in an Al Garhoud household, because it is the one that works when nobody is home to supervise. A marked mock script contains a complete diagnosis and most students look at the total and put it away.

The method is mechanical. First, go through the paper and mark every question where marks were lost, ignoring the ones that were correct. Second, for each loss, classify it into one of four categories: did not know the content, knew it but answered a different command term, knew it but showed no working, or ran out of time. Third, count the categories. The largest category is the problem, and it is usually not the first one.

That counting exercise is the whole diagnosis, and it is routinely surprising. A student convinced they are bad at Chemistry frequently discovers that two thirds of their lost marks were command-term mismatches and unshown working, which means they know considerably more Chemistry than their grade suggests and the fix is a fortnight of technique rather than a term of content.

Fourth and last, write the list down and bring it to the next session. A tutor given a classified list of losses can build a plan in ten minutes. A tutor given a grade has to spend the first paid hour producing the same list the student could have produced for free. Schools release scripts on request after mocks and internal assessments, and asking is entirely routine.

sections.heading: When a parent travels: what can be delegated to the student
paragraphs: A rostered household cannot run on parental supervision, and pretending otherwise produces a term of missed homework followed by an unpleasant February. The realistic approach is to delegate deliberately: decide what the student owns, what the tutor owns and what the parent checks, and write it down once.

The student can own more than most parents assume by sixteen. Attending the session, submitting the work set, classifying their own losses on returned work, and keeping the deadline list are all within reach of a Year 11 or Year 12 student, and all of them build the self-management the Diploma demands anyway. What a student cannot reasonably own is noticing a slow drift across a term, because they have no baseline to compare against.

That drift detection is what the parent should keep, and it needs almost no time. A written record from each session, stating what was set, what came back and what was corrected, can be read in five minutes on a layover. Three such records in a row showing homework not submitted is a signal that does not require anyone to be in the room.

The tutor owns the content, the plan and the honesty of the reporting, including saying when hours should reduce or stop. A plan that only ever recommends continuing is not being reported honestly, and in a household where nobody is watching closely, that matters more than it does elsewhere.

One more thing belongs on the student's side of the line, and it is the one most worth building: the deadline list. Internal Assessment dates, Extended Essay drafts and mock windows are set by the school, published in September, and almost never written down by the person they apply to. A student who keeps that list themselves, on a wall or a phone, stops being dependent on a parent noticing a date from a newsletter read in an airport lounge.
bullets: Student owns attendance, submission and self-classification
Parent owns drift detection from a short written record
Tutor owns content, plan and honest reporting including stopping
Write the division down once rather than renegotiating it monthly

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with coursework, and where the line sits
paragraphs: This page has spent a lot of words on criteria and limits, so the boundary needs stating precisely. Knowing that the science Internal Assessment carries six marks for Evaluation does not entitle anyone to write the evaluation. The criteria are a specification for the student's work, not a brief for somebody else's.

A tutor may teach the content the investigation rests on, explain each criterion in the subject guide's own wording, read the student's own draft and put the criteria to them as questions, teach uncertainty propagation and data presentation, teach referencing, and help narrow a research question until it is answerable within the word limit. All of that is substantial and all of it leaves the authorship untouched.

A tutor may not produce any part of the submission, including a rewritten conclusion, a supplied evaluation paragraph or an edit heavy enough that the words cease to be the student's. There are providers in this market advertising completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price in dirhams. The IB's authenticity requirement places the consequence on the student, so a malpractice finding can cost the Diploma while the seller carries nothing.

The practical protection is a word budget and an early draft. A student who allocates words by criterion before writing, and who has a review session two weeks before the school deadline rather than two days, never arrives at the point where the shortcut looks attractive. Ask any prospective tutor what they will and will not do with a draft; a clear answer is the signal to look for.

process.title: Send a marked script, not a report
process.description: A report gives a grade; a script shows where the marks went. Five minutes with a marked mock, or three MYP task sheets with criterion scores visible, is worth more than any description of the problem and it determines what the first session should do.

process.title: Classify the losses before the first session
process.description: Go through the script and sort each lost mark into content, command term, unshown working or timing. Count the categories. That list takes twenty minutes, costs nothing, and lets the first paid hour start on the fix rather than on producing the list.

process.title: Pick the component by weight
process.description: Target the component carrying the most recoverable marks rather than the subject that feels worst. A science Internal Assessment at 20 per cent can be improved before the examination; a paper cannot be improved after it. The arithmetic decides the order.

process.title: Set a slot independent of the roster
process.description: Lessons run over live video, so the session does not require a parent to be home. In a rostered household that matters: the slot is set once, against the student's schedule, and it holds whether or not anybody is in the country that week.

process.title: Written record after every session
process.description: What was set, what came back, what was corrected, in a few lines. It is the supervision mechanism for a travelling parent and it takes five minutes to read. Three consecutive records showing work not submitted is a signal nobody needs to be in the room to see.

process.title: Review against the next marked piece
process.description: The plan is tested against the next graded work rather than against how the sessions felt. If the classified losses have not shifted, the plan changes. If the subject has stabilised, hours reduce, and that is a legitimate recommendation rather than a lost sale.

whyPoints.title: The criteria named, with their marks
whyPoints.description: Four criteria at six marks each in the science investigation; five criteria at four, four, three, three and six in the Mathematics exploration. Across the competitor pages fetched for this project, not one names a single Internal Assessment criterion, and the criteria are the specification.

whyPoints.title: Weightings published so planning is arithmetic
whyPoints.description: Paper 2 at 44 per cent in the sciences, the Individual Oral at 30 per cent at Standard Level English, Paper 3 at 30 per cent in Higher Level Economics. Knowing which component carries the marks is what turns an anxious revision plan into a rational one.

whyPoints.title: Limits in one reference table
whyPoints.description: Extended Essay 4,000 words, Theory of Knowledge essay 1,600, TOK exhibition commentary 950, science investigation 3,000, Economics commentary 800. Material beyond a limit is not assessed, so a conclusion written past the count does not exist for marking purposes.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis transferred to the student
whyPoints.description: The script-reading method is published so a sixteen-year-old can run it alone. In a rostered Al Garhoud household that is the difference between a plan that survives a parent's absence and one that depends on somebody checking nightly.

whyPoints.title: Slots that do not need a parent at home
whyPoints.description: Teaching runs one-to-one over live video and nobody is dispatched to a UAE address, so a session does not require anyone to be present to open a door. For aviation households on rotating rosters that is a practical requirement rather than a preference.

whyPoints.title: The coursework boundary stated precisely
whyPoints.description: Knowing a criterion carries six marks does not entitle anyone to write that section. A tutor teaches, explains the criteria, questions the student's own draft and teaches referencing. Nobody authors a submission, because the malpractice consequence lands on the student.

faqs.question: What is the difference between describe and explain in an exam question?
faqs.answer: Describe asks for features or characteristics without requiring reasons. Explain requires a causal mechanism: why the thing happens, usually in terms of a named quantity or process. They are different assessment objectives and the markscheme credits them differently, so a thorough explanation on a describe question earns nothing extra, and a description on an explain question scores a fraction of the marks. It is worth twenty minutes with the command-term glossary in your child's current subject guide, because the pool of marks lost this way is usually the largest recoverable one.

faqs.question: How much is the Internal Assessment worth in IB Chemistry?
faqs.answer: The scientific investigation carries 20 per cent of the subject grade at both Standard and Higher Level, the same as in Physics and Biology, with Paper 1 at 36 per cent and Paper 2 at 44 per cent. It is assessed against four criteria, Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation, each worth six marks for a total of 24. That matters for planning: a weak Internal Assessment caps the achievable grade before revision begins, and unlike a paper it can still be improved while it is being written.

faqs.question: What are the criteria for the IB Maths exploration?
faqs.answer: Five criteria totalling twenty marks: Presentation worth four, Mathematical communication worth four, Personal engagement worth three, Reflection worth three, and Use of mathematics worth six. The exploration is 20 per cent of the subject grade at both levels. Use of mathematics is the heaviest single criterion, which is why an exploration built on a modest mathematical core cannot reach the top band however well it is presented or how genuinely personal the topic is. Confirm the allocations in the current subject guide for your child's cohort.

faqs.question: What happens if my child goes over the Extended Essay word limit?
faqs.answer: Material beyond the 4,000 word limit is not assessed, which in practice means a conclusion written past the count does not exist as far as the marks are concerned. The same principle applies across components: the Theory of Knowledge essay is capped at 1,600 words, the TOK exhibition commentary at 950, the science investigation at 3,000 and each Economics commentary at 800. The practical defence is a word budget allocated by criterion before writing starts, so the sections carrying marks get words in proportion to the marks.

faqs.question: Which exam component should my child focus on first?
faqs.answer: The one carrying the most recoverable marks, which is rarely the subject that feels worst. In the Diploma sciences, Paper 2 at 44 per cent is the heaviest component and the Internal Assessment at 20 per cent is the one still improvable before the examination. At Standard Level English the Individual Oral at 30 per cent is both the largest single component and the most coachable, because it rewards rehearsal. Decomposing the subject into weighted components and checking current performance in each turns an anxious plan into an arithmetic one.

faqs.question: How do I read my child's mock script usefully?
faqs.answer: Four steps, fifteen minutes. Mark every question where marks were lost and ignore the correct ones. Classify each loss as content not known, command term mismatched, working not shown, or ran out of time. Count the categories. The biggest category is the actual problem, and it is frequently not the first one. Write the list down and bring it to the tutoring session, because a tutor given a classified list builds a plan in ten minutes while a tutor given a grade spends the first paid hour making the same list.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks in Maths when the answer is right?
faqs.answer: Because method marks are allocated to specific steps, not to the final answer. On a multi-mark question in Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1, and equally in Diploma Paper 1, a correct answer with no visible working scores a fraction of the available total. This is the single most common avoidable loss in IGCSE Mathematics and it is purely a habit. It is also the easiest thing in this whole page to fix: the student writes every step, every time, including the ones that feel obvious.

faqs.question: What do students get wrong in the IGCSE practical skills paper?
faqs.answer: A short and repeatable list. Asked to suggest an improvement to a method, they describe the method. Asked to criticise a graph, they read values off it. Asked to identify a source of error, they write human error, which earns nothing. Asked for a control variable, they name something that was not held constant. These questions appear in every series and the correct behaviours can be taught in a couple of sessions, which makes the practical paper the cheapest marks available in IGCSE science.

faqs.question: Can lessons run when both parents are away on a roster?
faqs.answer: Yes, which is part of why online delivery suits this neighbourhood. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, so nobody needs to be home to admit a tutor, and the slot is set against the student's schedule rather than the household's roster. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses in any case; home visiting exists only in the India service. The supervision mechanism for an absent parent is the written session record, which states what was set, what came back and what was corrected.

faqs.question: How much of the IB Economics grade is the Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Thirty per cent at Standard Level and 20 per cent at Higher Level, delivered as three commentaries each capped at 800 words and built on a news article. At Standard Level that makes it the second-heaviest component after Paper 2 at 40 per cent, which is a strong argument for taking the commentaries seriously early rather than treating them as homework. The marks sit in the link between the theory, the diagram and the article, which is where students most often lose them by explaining theory correctly in isolation.

faqs.question: Is the Individual Oral worth preparing for separately?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the best returns available in the Diploma. At Standard Level in English Language and Literature it carries 30 per cent of the subject grade, and 20 per cent at Higher Level, assessed against four criteria worth ten marks each: knowledge and interpretation, analysis and evaluation, focus and organisation, and language. It is a timed, rehearsed performance built around a global issue argued across one literary and one non-literary text, which means it responds to practice far more directly than an unseen paper does.

faqs.question: What curricula do the schools around Al Garhoud offer?
faqs.answer: An unusually broad mix inside a small area. Al Garhoud itself holds full International Baccalaureate continuum provision at Deira International School, American curriculum provision at Universal American School, and British and Indian curriculum provision at Dubai Scholars Private School and Al Mawakeb School, with St Mary's Catholic High School and Dubai Gem Private School a short run away in Oud Metha. These are named as local context only; each school's curriculum licence and current KHDA inspection band should be checked on the KHDA site.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write the evaluation section of my child's IA?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody should offer to. Knowing that Evaluation carries six of the 24 marks in the science investigation is information for the student, not a brief for somebody else. A tutor may teach the content, explain the criterion in the subject guide's own wording, read the student's own draft and put the criterion to them as questions, and teach uncertainty handling and referencing. Producing any part of the submission is malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the person paid to write it.

faqs.question: My child says they know the content but still scores badly. Is that plausible?
faqs.answer: Very often, yes, and the script will show it. When lost marks are classified, a student convinced they are weak in a subject frequently finds that two thirds of their losses were command-term mismatches and unshown working rather than content gaps. That is a genuinely different problem with a genuinely different fix: a fortnight of technique work rather than a term of re-teaching. It also changes the student's own conclusion about themselves, which is worth something on its own.

faqs.question: How many sessions does technique work usually take?
faqs.answer: Less than families expect. Command-term discipline, working-out habits and the practical-paper behaviours are a finite list, and six to ten sessions with marked papers in between will usually shift the pattern visibly, provided the papers are actually done between sessions. Content gaps are different and more expensive, because the teaching has to happen before the drilling can start. That is exactly why classifying the losses first matters: it tells you which of the two you are buying before you commit to a term of it.

dubai/al-garhoud.closingHeading: Give the student the specification, not encouragement
dubai/al-garhoud.closingBody: Most of what separates a 5 from a 7 in Al Garhoud is not knowledge. It is command terms answered correctly, working shown, words budgeted by criterion and the right component targeted first. All of that is published, all of it is checkable, and a sixteen-year-old can learn to run the diagnosis alone, which matters in a household where a parent is away three nights a week. Mark the losses, classify them, count them, and bring the list. IB Gram arranges one-to-one lessons over live video, working from your child's own marked script.

dubai/al-habtoor-city.tutorsIntro: The requests from these towers are specific: a Year 11 student who has joined in November, a Diploma Year 1 student who has moved from an American high school, a Year 9 student whose previous curriculum covered half of what their new class already knows. The tutors below work on that gap rather than on broad revision.

intro.heading: A district of recent arrivals, and what that does to a school year
paragraphs: Al Habtoor City is a vertical neighbourhood. Three residential towers sit between Sheikh Zayed Road and the Dubai Water Canal, alongside hotels and a theatre, with no villa stock and no school inside the development. Almost everyone here is in an apartment, a good proportion on a corporate lease, and the average length of residence is shorter than in the villa communities a few minutes west. That profile, rather than anything about the buildings, is what shapes the tutoring the families here actually need.

The pattern is consistent enough to describe. A family arrives in September, or more awkwardly in November or February, having accepted a role in Dubai. A school place is found wherever one exists at the right year group, which in a city of 227 private schools still means compromise in the middle of an academic year. The child walks into a Year 11 IGCSE class that has already covered two thirds of the syllabus, or a Diploma Year 1 group that chose subjects in June and has been working since August.

That child is not behind in the ordinary sense. They have been taught a different syllabus, in a different sequence, assessed against a different scheme, and they now have to produce work on a timetable set by a course they did not start. The marks in the first term are therefore not a measure of ability, and treating them as one is the most common mistake a newly arrived family makes. The useful question is narrower: which specific topics have never been taught to this child, and how many weeks does it take to close that.

The second problem is paperwork, and it arrives later. A family that has moved countries will eventually need the Ministry of Education equivalency route for a certificate issued elsewhere, and the published requirements are specific about subject counts and minimum grades. Choosing an IGCSE option block in Year 9 without knowing those requirements is how families discover, two years later, that a subject they dropped mattered. This page sets out what the published rules say and where to verify them.

The third thing worth naming is timing. A household still unpacking does not have a car, a school transport routine or a reliable sense of how long Sheikh Zayed Road takes at 4pm. Online delivery solves a practical problem here rather than an educational one: sessions can begin in the first week, from an apartment with a laptop, before any of the rest of the logistics are settled. Nothing on this page requires a tutor to arrive at a UAE address, because IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai. That is a service offered only in India, and saying so plainly is more useful to a family three days into a tenancy than a promise that cannot be kept on a weekday afternoon in this part of the city.
bullets: No school sits inside Al Habtoor City; every family uses Sheikh Zayed Road or Al Wasl

dubai/al-habtoor-city.programmesIntro: What matters on this page is not what each programme covers in general but what happens when a student joins it late. The notes below describe each one from the point of view of a child walking into it in November rather than August.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. A student joining partway through Diploma Year 1 inherits subject choices made by somebody else's timetable, internal assessment deadlines already in motion, and a Theory of Knowledge course whose opening framing they missed. Each subject's internal assessment carries roughly a fifth to a quarter of the grade.
programmes.countryNote: A Diploma transfer into Dubai is only straightforward if the incoming school offers the same six subjects at the same levels, which is rarely the case. Ask the new school's IB coordinator, in writing, which subjects can be matched and what the internal deadlines already passed were, before the first week rather than after the first report.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessment is against four criteria per subject marked out of 8, converted to a 1-7 grade. A student arriving from a content-led curriculum has usually never been marked on process, and their first criterion task scores low for reasons that have nothing to do with knowing the material. The vocabulary of the mark scheme has to be taught before the scores mean anything.
programmes.countryNote: For a family new to Dubai this is the stage where reports are hardest to read, because a criterion score of 4 out of 8 does not map onto any grading scale the family has used before. Ask the school for the subject-specific grade boundaries it applies, since those are set at school level rather than centrally.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two distinct qualifications with different codes, paper structures and tiering rules. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended; Pearson does not do so in the same way. A student joining in Year 11 faces an entry that may already be locked, a tier decided on another school's evidence, and coursework components with deadlines that have passed.
programmes.countryNote: The practical first move for a Year 11 arrival in Dubai is to get the entry list from the new school's exams officer and compare it against what the previous school had entered. Cambridge sets final entries months before the papers, so the window to change a subject or a tier may already be shut by the time a family asks.

dubai/al-habtoor-city.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects that cause the most trouble for a student joining a Dubai course mid-year, with the specific reason each one is hard to pick up late rather than a general description of the syllabus.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: The hardest subject to join late, because the syllabus is cumulative and a missed topic blocks later ones. A student who never met vectors or circle theorems in a previous curriculum cannot access the questions that depend on them, and no amount of revision of familiar topics compensates.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and quantitative chemistry are the specific blockage for transferring students, because many curricula introduce them later or more lightly. Practical and data questions also assume a style of answer the student may never have been taught, which is faster to fix than the content.

subjects.name: IGCSE Business Studies
subjects.description: Looks accessible and is not. Marks come from applying terms to the case material rather than defining them, and the command terms behave differently from those in the equivalent American or Indian course. Transferring students routinely write correct content that scores in the bottom band.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Joining this late at Higher Level is the single riskiest transfer in the Diploma. Paper 3 asks for sustained reasoning through one extended problem, and the algebraic fluency it assumes is built over months. An honest assessment in the first fortnight is worth more than optimism.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The volume is the obstacle for a late arrival rather than the difficulty. The other issue is command terms: outline, describe, explain and evaluate carry specific demands, and a student from a curriculum with different conventions writes competent answers to the wrong question.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study application under time pressure, with a Higher Level extension that adds extended response. The internal assessment needs research planned early, so a student joining in the second term has to design something feasible with less runway than their classmates had.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries a large share of the marks, and the Higher Level paper adds quantitative work. The commentary portfolio is the transfer risk: each commentary must be anchored to a genuine published article within a word limit, and the earlier ones may already be due.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Students arriving from an English-medium school elsewhere are sometimes placed in English B and sometimes in English A, and the two are entirely different courses. Getting the placement right in the first weeks matters more than any tutoring that follows it.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: Conceptual rather than factual, and the engagement activity requires sustained independent work. A late joiner can catch up on content quickly but needs the assessment structure taught explicitly, because the marking rewards a form of argument most incoming curricula do not require.

dubai/al-habtoor-city.regionsTitle: Al Habtoor City and the districts its families use
dubai/al-habtoor-city.regionsIntro: This development sits on the boundary between Business Bay, Al Wasl and the Jumeirah districts, so a family here chooses schools across three different directions. These are the areas that actually feature in the week.

regions.name: Business Bay
regions.note: Immediately north across the canal, and where many of the working parents in these towers go each morning. Its office peak overlaps the school run, which is why afternoon appointments here are harder to keep than the map suggests.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Five to fifteen minutes along Sheikh Zayed Road depending on the hour. Shares the same apartment-household profile, so school choices and tutoring requests from Downtown and Al Habtoor City look closely alike.

regions.name: Al Wasl
regions.note: The inland corridor towards Jumeirah, and the route most families take to the Al Safa school cluster. It is the segment that adds the most unpredictable time in the evening.

regions.name: Al Safa
regions.note: The nearest dense cluster of British and IB schools, roughly ten to twenty minutes out. A large share of Al Habtoor City children are enrolled here, which makes the Al Wasl crossing part of the daily routine.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1
regions.note: Further west along the coast, holding several long-established British campuses. Places here are often full, which is part of why mid-year arrivals end up further afield than they expected.

regions.name: Za'abeel and Al Jafiliya
regions.note: East of Sheikh Zayed Road, with established schools that occasionally have mid-year capacity when the newer western districts do not. Worth asking about when a family arrives outside the normal admissions cycle.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Mohammed Bin Rashid City
regions.note: Fifteen to twenty-five minutes inland, where several newer British and IB campuses sit. These are the schools most likely to have space for a November arrival.

regions.name: Oud Metha and Al Jaddaf
regions.note: Across towards the creek, holding long-established schools serving a different demographic. Families from these towers sometimes look here specifically because the admissions pressure is lower.

schoolClusters.city: Al Safa, Al Wasl and Jumeirah 1
schoolClusters.note: The first choice for most households in these towers, reached by crossing Al Wasl Road. The cluster is predominantly British curriculum with IB continuum campuses mixed in, and its places are the hardest to secure mid-year because demand is steady all year.

schoolClusters.city: Nad Al Sheba, Mohammed Bin Rashid City and Oud Metha
schoolClusters.note: Where mid-year arrivals most often find a place. The drive is longer and the schools span British, IB and Indian curricula, which is also why transfer advice has to be school-specific rather than general.

dubai/al-habtoor-city.modesIntro: Three formats cover what these households ask for. All run over live video, which matters more here than in most districts because a family may be tutoring before the car, the school transport and the furniture have arrived.

modes.title: Arrival diagnostic and catch-up plan
modes.description: A short block of sessions in the first two or three weeks whose purpose is to establish what has and has not been taught. The tutor works through the new school's syllabus against the student's previous coursework and identifies the specific topics never covered. The output is a written list and a realistic number of weeks, which is what the family needs before anything else.

modes.description: A fixed slot with the same tutor working through the named topic list alongside the school's current teaching. The point is to cover the missing material without abandoning the live course, which means the session order follows the gap list rather than the textbook. Sessions carry written notes so the family can see what has closed and what has not.

The work covers what the criteria reward, how to design something feasible in the time left, and feedback on drafts the student writes. The text stays the student's own throughout, which is a requirement of IB academic honesty and not a preference.

sections.heading: Who actually lives in Al Habtoor City, and what it means for schooling
paragraphs: It is worth being concrete, because the generic area page that says a district is popular with families tells a parent nothing. Al Habtoor City is three residential towers of apartments on the Dubai Water Canal, with hotels and a theatre attached, no villa stock and no school on site. The households are therefore apartment households, a high share of them on corporate leases, and many of them newer to Dubai than the families in the villa communities a few minutes west along Al Wasl.

That has three consequences for schooling. The first is that school choice is made from a map rather than from a catchment: there is no local school, so the decision is which direction to drive, and that often gets made in a week. The second is that places are sought outside the normal admissions cycle more often than average, which narrows the realistic options considerably. The third is that a meaningful number of children in these buildings are on their second or third curriculum before they turn sixteen.

The academic risks follow directly from that profile, and they are different from the risks in a long-settled villa community. A child who has been in one school since Year 1 accumulates a stable picture of their own ability. A child who has moved twice accumulates gaps instead, and the gaps are invisible in reports because each new school reports only on what it has taught. The table below sets out the household types these towers actually contain and the specific risk attached to each.

None of this is an argument that mobile families do worse. It is an argument that they need a different first step. The first useful action for a settled family is usually choosing a tutor. The first useful action for a family in these towers is usually an honest diagnostic of what has never been taught, because tutoring aimed at the wrong gap is simply an expensive way to stay behind.

sections.heading: The mid-year joiner problem, stated honestly
paragraphs: A student who joins a Year 11 IGCSE class in November has missed around a third of two years of teaching. A student who joins Diploma Year 1 in February has missed a term of six subjects and whatever internal assessment work had begun. Schools handle this with varying amounts of care, and the better ones will tell you plainly what has been covered. Even then, the comparison that matters is between what was covered here and what was covered at the previous school, and only the family can assemble that.

The first-term report from a new school is therefore close to meaningless as a measure of ability. It measures the overlap between two syllabuses. A child with a strong record elsewhere can produce a set of 4s in Dubai in December and a set of 6s in June, having become no cleverer in between. The reverse also happens: a student arrives with high grades from a less demanding course and the Dubai marks come as a shock to everybody.

What works is mapping rather than motivating. Take the new school's syllabus or scheme of work, sit with the student's previous exercise books and marked papers, and mark every topic as taught, partly taught or never seen. That exercise takes a couple of hours with somebody who knows both systems and it changes the whole plan, because the never-seen list is usually much shorter than the family feared and much more specific than the school's general advice.

The last part is the timetable. A catch-up list of nine topics in mathematics does not take nine weeks if two of them are prerequisites for four others; it takes longer at the start and then accelerates. A family that understands the sequence can plan two sessions a week for a term and one thereafter, instead of booking indefinite weekly support with no end state in mind. The end state should be written down at the beginning.

sections.heading: Curriculum transition map: arriving into a Dubai course mid-stream
paragraphs: Dubai's private sector offered 17 different curricula to 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of students, Indian at 26, US at 14 and International Baccalaureate at 7. A transferring family is therefore almost always moving between systems rather than within one, and the gaps are predictable enough to tabulate. The table below covers the moves that come up most often in these towers.

Two transitions deserve specific warning. American high school into Diploma Year 1 is the one most often underestimated, because the student's English and general articulacy are usually strong and the mathematics and science depth usually is not. The second is British Year 11 into Diploma Year 1, where a student who has just finished IGCSEs meets Higher Level content that assumes an AS-level style of reasoning they have not yet been taught.

The move from an Indian board into IGCSE runs the other way in mathematics and the sciences, where the incoming student is frequently ahead on content and behind on written technique. The marks are lost in how answers are structured against command terms and mark schemes, not in whether the student can do the mathematics. That is good news, because written technique responds to focused work much faster than missing content does.

Whatever the direction, the sequence should be the same. Establish the gap in writing, challenge the subject and level placement in the first fortnight while it is still administratively possible, then work the list. The most expensive mistake available to a transferring family is accepting a Higher Level placement in the first week because it looks ambitious, and discovering in Diploma Year 2 that it cannot be changed.

sections.heading: Where a transferring student actually loses marks in the first term
paragraphs: The losses are rarely where parents expect. The first is command terms. Every board publishes a list of instruction words with specific demands, and they are not interchangeable between systems. A student who writes a strong description where the paper asked for an evaluation has demonstrated the knowledge and scored in the bottom band, and they will repeat the error until somebody shows them the list and makes them use it.

The second is mark-scheme shape. Marks in IGCSE and Diploma papers are awarded for specific statements and specific steps, not for the general quality of an answer. Students from curricula that reward a well-written whole response find this arbitrary at first. It is learnable in a few weeks of working through past papers with the mark scheme visible, which is a different activity from doing past papers and checking the final answers.

The third is pacing. A three-hour paper with a fixed mark-per-minute budget is a skill, not a test of knowledge, and a student who has only sat shorter or more frequent assessments will leave marks unattempted. This is the single fastest thing to fix in a transferring student, and it is routinely left until the mock results make it visible in the worst possible way.

The fourth, for Diploma students specifically, is internal assessment process. A late joiner has less runway for the research, the data collection and the drafting, and the deadlines are the school's rather than the student's. The right response is to scale the project to the time available at the outset. An ambitious investigation designed in February for a March deadline fails on execution regardless of how good the idea was.

sections.heading: What catching up costs in Dubai, and over how many weeks
paragraphs: Hourly rates are published across this market in a way that makes comparison hard, so the table below prices the scenario instead. The AED figures are market rates gathered in October 2026 and attributed to the provider that published them; none is an IB Gram price. The useful column is the last one, because a transferring family needs to know what a catch-up totals rather than what an hour costs.

For reference, the bands are these. Budget online tutoring, usually a university student, runs AED 45-150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor online is AED 150-300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An IB or IGCSE specialist is AED 200-450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and premium named tutors reach AED 500-650, with BartyED publishing AED 650. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240-600 at the budget end and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

The pattern that matters for a transfer is that a defined catch-up is usually cheaper than open-ended weekly support, because it has an end. Two sessions a week for ten weeks to close a mapped list of topics is a finite commitment with a testable outcome. Weekly support with no topic list attached runs for years, and the family never finds out whether it is working, because there is nothing it was supposed to close.

One piece of local context helps the budgeting. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. A family that has just relocated is therefore working from a known fee figure for the year, which makes a defined tutoring block easier to plan than it would be in a rising-fee year.
