sections.heading: Sheikh Zayed Road, the canal, and when a session can start
paragraphs: Al Habtoor City sits on a stretch of Sheikh Zayed Road where the school run overlaps the office peak, which is less common than it sounds. In the villa communities west of here the afternoon traffic is almost entirely school and household movement. Here it is school traffic plus Business Bay and Downtown office traffic plus hotel and theatre arrivals, and the three do not clear at the same time.

In practical terms that means the window between roughly 3pm and 4:30pm is not usable for anything that requires somebody to travel. A child coming back from Al Safa crosses Al Wasl Road in that window. A parent returning from Business Bay crosses the canal in the same window. An in-home tutor would have to arrive inside it, which is why in-home rates in this part of Dubai carry a travel premium of the order of AED 180-500 an hour against AED 150-300 for a qualified tutor online.

The reliable slot from these towers is after about 4:45pm, and many families here use later slots than the Dubai average because at least one parent is still travelling home at five. Older Diploma students often take a 7pm or 7:30pm session, which works when the student is self-directed and does not when they are not. The rule of thumb is that the slot has to suit the student's attention rather than the parent's convenience.

IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai; that is an India-only service. For a household in a tower with a laptop and a quiet bedroom, the online format removes the travel question entirely, and that matters more in the first month after a relocation than at any other time. A family can be three days into a tenancy with no car and still have a session running at 5pm.

sections.heading: Equivalency for a family that has moved countries
paragraphs: Equivalency is the Ministry of Education process that turns a certificate earned elsewhere into something UAE universities and employers can accept. It is a regulatory step a family completes through the official channel, and it is not something a tutoring company performs, accelerates or guarantees. What tutoring can do is make sure the subjects and grades the process requires are actually achieved, which means knowing the requirements before the Year 9 option block is chosen rather than after Year 11.

The British-track requirements are published and specific. A student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for that count.

That exclusion is where families get caught. A student who takes Arabic and Islamic Education plus four other IGCSE subjects has four counting subjects, not six. One competitor page ranking for these queries states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced requirement is five, and the composition matters more than the number. If an option block is being chosen in a hurry because a family has just arrived, this is the single detail worth slowing down for.

For the American track, English proficiency is met by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold appears on this page, because the source consulted states none and nothing could be read on the Ministry's own site. Any page publishing an IB equivalency figure without that citation is guessing with your child's application.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies for a child who has just arrived
paragraphs: A family new to Dubai is often surprised to find three subjects on the timetable that were not part of the decision to choose the school. Every private school in the emirate teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of the international curriculum it is licensed for, and KHDA's mandatory subject guidelines required implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The rules on how these subjects run are specific. KHDA requires separate classes by group for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for Arab and non-Arab groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

For a child arriving mid-year with no Arabic at all, the practical question is which stream they enter and what the school expects by the end of the year. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with KHDA advising at least 25 minutes for any mandatory subject lesson, so the load is real rather than nominal. Ask the school directly what is assessed and how it reports, because this is the part of the timetable families most often discover in the first report.

One constraint shapes any support in these subjects. For the mandatory UAE subjects, KHDA states that the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, and schools must ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate approval from KHDA. Support therefore works to the school's own material rather than to an imported scheme, and anyone offering a generic Arabic programme for a Dubai school is not describing something the rules allow.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when a student is behind and the deadline is close
paragraphs: This is the pressure point that makes transferring families vulnerable, and it deserves naming directly. A student joins in February, an internal assessment is due in six weeks, nothing has been started, and the parent is willing to pay to make the problem go away. The research for this project found a provider in this market selling finished internal assessments at AED 3,750. That transaction is academic malpractice under IB rules, the investigation falls on the candidate, and the consequence is to the whole Diploma rather than to one grade.

The boundary is not vague. A tutor may teach what the criteria reward and the marks each carries, scale a research question to the weeks that remain, explain how data should be handled, and read a draft the student has produced to say where it falls short of a criterion. A tutor may not supply text for submission, rewrite a passage into its final form, or hand over a model answer intended to be submitted. That applies equally to the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge, the MYP Personal Project and IGCSE coursework.

The honest route is also the more effective one under time pressure, which is not an obvious claim but is a true one. Criteria are published and specific, so a late-starting student can be pointed at the two criteria carrying the most available marks and work there first. A student handed finished text has no basis for the oral questions a teacher may ask, no understanding of the method, and no defence if the school queries the authorship.

There is a practical point for parents as well. Schools in Dubai are alert to this market, and a sudden jump in written quality between a classroom task and a submitted assessment is visible. If a provider offers to produce your child's coursework, the offer itself is the reason to decline. IB Gram's sessions on this work are teaching, questioning and feedback on the student's own material, and that is stated here because no price list shows it.

process.title: Tell us where your child has come from
process.description: The previous curriculum, the previous year group and the date of the move matter as much as the new school. A student arriving from an American high school into Diploma Year 1 has a different gap from one arriving from CBSE into Year 10, and the first session is wasted if we are told only the subject.

process.title: Send the old exercise books and the new syllabus
process.description: The most useful hour of the whole process is spent comparing those two documents. Marked work from the previous school shows what was actually taught and how it was assessed; the new school's scheme of work shows what is assumed. The gap between them is the plan.

process.title: Get a written gap list and a week count
process.description: You should receive a named list of topics marked as taught, partly taught or never seen, and an honest estimate of how many weeks the never-seen list takes. If a subject or level placement looks wrong, that is also the point at which to say so, while the school can still change it.

process.title: Trial the tutor at a workable time
process.description: The trial runs at the slot you intend to keep, which from these towers usually means after 4:45pm once Sheikh Zayed Road and the Al Wasl crossing have cleared. You see the specific tutor working with your child before committing to a block of sessions.

process.title: Close the list, then step down
process.description: A catch-up has an end. Two sessions a week while the gap list is open, one a week afterwards, and a review against the next marked school assessment. If the list is closed and the marks have moved, the right recommendation is fewer sessions rather than more.

whyPoints.title: We map the gap before selling the hours
whyPoints.description: For a child who has joined a Dubai course mid-year, the first deliverable is a written list of what has never been taught. Tutoring aimed at the wrong gap is an expensive way to stay behind, and the mapping takes an hour or two rather than a term.

whyPoints.title: Sessions can start in your first week
whyPoints.description: Delivery is online over live video, so a family three days into a tenancy with no car and no school transport can still have a session running. For a relocating household that is a practical advantage rather than an educational preference.

whyPoints.title: A catch-up with a stated end state
whyPoints.description: The plan says how many weeks and what will have closed. Open-ended weekly support with no topic list attached can run for years without anybody discovering whether it worked, because nothing was defined as the thing it should have fixed.

whyPoints.title: Equivalency rules quoted, not paraphrased
whyPoints.description: The British-track requirement of five accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the count, is quoted from the published guidance. A ranking competitor page states six; getting this wrong changes an option block.

whyPoints.title: The coursework line holds under deadline pressure
whyPoints.description: A late-joining student with six weeks to an internal assessment is exactly who the pages selling finished coursework are built for. We teach criteria, scale the question and give feedback on the student's own draft, and we say no to the rest.

whyPoints.title: We tell you when a placement looks wrong
whyPoints.description: Sometimes the problem is not the tutoring but a Higher Level subject accepted in the first week of a transfer. Raising that in the first fortnight, while a change is still administratively possible, is more valuable than a term of support.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our apartment in Al Habtoor City?
faqs.answer: No. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered online, one to one, over live video, and IB Gram does not make home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service offered only in India. From these towers the online format has a specific practical advantage: a family newly arrived, without a car or school transport sorted, can have a session running within days. The Dubai in-home market charges roughly AED 180-500 an hour with the drive priced in, against AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor.

faqs.question: My child has joined a Dubai school mid-year. Is the first report a fair measure?
faqs.answer: Not of ability. A first-term report after a mid-year move largely measures the overlap between two syllabuses. A student with a strong record elsewhere can produce 4s in December and 6s in June without becoming cleverer, because the December marks reflect topics never taught to them. The reverse also happens, where high grades from a less demanding course meet a harder one. The useful exercise is mapping the previous coursework against the new scheme of work and listing the topics never seen.

faqs.question: Which schools can an Al Habtoor City family realistically reach?
faqs.answer: There is no school inside the development, so the choice is a direction rather than a catchment. The nearest cluster is Al Safa, Al Wasl and Jumeirah 1, including Horizon English School, Jumeirah Baccalaureate School, GEMS Jumeirah Primary School and Jumeirah English Speaking School. Mid-year places are more often found inland, in Nad Al Sheba, Mohammed Bin Rashid City and Oud Metha, at schools such as North London Collegiate School Dubai, GEMS Modern Academy and Hartland International School. Those names are context for the school run, not relationships IB Gram holds.

faqs.question: We are moving from an American high school into the IB Diploma. What is the real gap?
faqs.answer: Usually mathematical depth and science volume rather than English or articulacy, which is why this transfer gets underestimated. Diploma Higher Level subjects assume sustained algebraic fluency and a quantity of content per subject that an American course spreads differently. The first fortnight should be spent testing whether the Higher Level choices are realistic, because a change is administratively possible then and not in Diploma Year 2. Expect a term of concentrated work in the Higher Level subjects rather than general support across all six.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a mid-year catch-up usually take?
faqs.answer: It depends on the mapped list, which is why the list comes first. Technique work on command terms and mark schemes is typically six to eight sessions. One IGCSE subject with a genuine topic gap runs ten to sixteen. A Higher Level science or mathematics catch-up is more often sixteen to twenty-four. At market rates of AED 150-300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor, or AED 200-450 and above for a specialist, those are finite commitments with a testable end, which open-ended weekly support is not.

faqs.question: What time can a session start from a tower on Sheikh Zayed Road?
faqs.answer: After about 4:45pm on a weekday, and often later here than the Dubai average. This stretch is unusual because the school run overlaps the Business Bay and Downtown office peak, so the window from roughly 3pm to 4:30pm is not usable for anything requiring travel. Many households in these towers use 6pm or 7pm slots because a parent is still coming home at five. Older Diploma students handle later sessions well; Year 9 and below generally do not.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge IGCSE the same qualification as Pearson Edexcel International GCSE?
faqs.answer: No, and treating them as one causes real problems for transferring families. They are separate qualifications with different syllabus codes, different paper structures and different entry arrangements. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended, with Core capping the grade available; Pearson does not tier in the same way. The code on a past paper is the quick check: 0580 and 0620 are Cambridge Maths and Chemistry, 4MA1 and 4CH1 the Pearson equivalents. Tutoring aimed at the wrong code wastes its first sessions.

faqs.question: My child joined after the internal assessment started. What can a tutor do?
faqs.answer: Teach the criteria, scale the project to the weeks left, and give feedback on drafts your child writes. A realistic research question designed for six weeks beats an ambitious one designed for six months and abandoned. What a tutor must not do is supply text for submission, rewrite a passage into final form, or hand over a model answer. One provider in this market sells finished internal assessments outright; that is malpractice, and the investigation lands on the candidate rather than the seller.

faqs.question: Why does my child's school teach Arabic and Islamic Education when we chose a British curriculum?
faqs.answer: Because every private school in Dubai does, regardless of the international curriculum it is licensed for. KHDA's mandatory subject guidelines required implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, so the load is real rather than nominal.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does my child need for Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One competitor page ranking for these queries states six subjects are required; the sourced figure is five, and the composition matters more than the count. Verify on the Ministry's own guidance before finalising a Year 9 option block.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram handle the equivalency or attestation paperwork?
faqs.answer: No. Equivalency is a Ministry of Education process that the family completes through the official channel, and no tutoring provider performs, accelerates or guarantees it. Treat any page suggesting otherwise with suspicion. What tutoring can do is upstream: making sure the five counting IGCSE subjects are passed at the grade required, and that the A Level or Diploma route chosen matches the course your child intends to apply for. Tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, admission or progression.

faqs.question: Do tutors working with families in Dubai need a government permit?
faqs.answer: Individuals giving private lessons in the UAE do. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's service page states a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website and e-services. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one faces fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: We may move again in two years. Which qualification travels best?
faqs.answer: That depends on the destination rather than on the qualification's reputation. The IB Diploma is designed to be portable and is recognised widely, but a mid-course Diploma transfer is genuinely difficult because subject combinations and internal assessment deadlines rarely match. IGCSE and A Level transfer more cleanly between British-curriculum schools in different countries. If a further move is likely during Years 10 to 13, ask the school directly what has happened to its previous mid-course transfers rather than relying on a general argument.

faqs.question: Is a repeated year ever the right answer for a transferring student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth considering properly rather than dismissing. A student moving from a national or bilingual curriculum into IGCSE Year 10 with a language gap as well as a content gap may be better served by entering a year lower, because running language and content catch-up together inside one year rarely works. Against that, a repeated year has social cost and a cost in fees. The decision belongs with the school and the family; what tutoring can offer is honest evidence about the size of the gap.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for a Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: You are told before booking rather than after. Some combinations have a genuinely thin specialist pool, particularly Group 2 languages at Higher Level and a handful of option subjects, and Dubai demand peaks between January and April as Year 11 and Diploma Year 2 families arrive together. The realistic choices are a different slot, a short wait for a named tutor, or a concentrated block closer to the papers. For a transferring student already behind, accepting a generalist is the worst of the options.

dubai/al-habtoor-city.closingHeading: Map the gap first, then book the hours
dubai/al-habtoor-city.closingBody: If you have just arrived in Al Habtoor City and your child has joined a course already in progress, the first useful step is not choosing a tutor. It is finding out, in writing, which topics have never been taught to them, and how many weeks that list takes to close. Send us the previous school's marked work, the new school's scheme of work, the year group and the board, and you will get that list plus an honest week count before any commitment to a block. Lessons run online over live video, so the work can start in your first week in Dubai rather than your second month.
